recent_reviews.author: Sophie Devoy
recent_reviews.text: I have a mixed review of Willow Green Surgery, as I’ve had a range of experiences with the telephone staff through to Dr’s themselves. Generally it’s been positive, however putting personal opinion of personalities and NHS / surgery red tape , I have now had TWO referrals missed / lost / not done, which to me is shocking and disgusting and pretty much sums up the demise of the NHS. Firstly for myself, I had a referral for a (fortunately benign) lump to be removed in 2023 and only when chasing late 2024 (extended time due to pregnancy in between), I found out it hadn’t actually been actioned by Willow Green and the lump is now 2x the size and I’ve had to go through all appt & scans etc again and still on a waiting list. And now most recently for my 10 month old baby, who has intolerances and was supposedly referred to a paediatric dietician at Worthing Hospital following an appt in February at Willow Green, I have found it it was never actioned!! A baby! Who has intolerances and is on a time frame for testing / next steps - disgusting!! So emails, calls, double scans, double appts, double blood tests because of incompetence / administrative laziness is what is bringing the NHS down, not the general public and larger populations etc. Anyway, if you’ve got this far, I hope this gives some insight to the surgery’s background and why I will be raising a formal complaint & switching surgeries (although I’m sure they’re all the same these days) but hey- strike cos you deserve more pay, right!?

recent_reviews.author: Lee Watts
recent_reviews.text: I wanted to take the time to leave a review because I feel it’s important to reflect my genuine experience, particularly in light of some of the low ratings currently visible. When I registered with St Mary’s Cray Practice after being moved into the area, I felt extremely anxious. I have been relocated multiple times by the council, and as someone with ADHD and complex health needs, that instability has taken a real toll on my mental health. Continuity of care has often been lacking, so I was bracing myself for another difficult experience. Instead, I was met with diligence, kindness, and genuine professionalism. From the outset, the staff were forthcoming, thorough, and compassionate. I felt properly listened to and taken seriously, rather than rushed or dismissed. What stood out most was how carefully my health was reviewed as a whole. My ADHD, mental health, and physical health — including the fact that I have one kidney — were all considered thoughtfully and with care. That level of attentiveness made a huge difference to me. After repeatedly having to explain my situation elsewhere, it was incredibly reassuring to feel that my history had been read, understood, and respected. I am very aware of the pressures facing the NHS, which is why this experience mattered so much. In a system that can sometimes feel fragmented and impersonal, this practice offered care that felt humane, patient, and genuinely supportive. I wanted to share this because my experience has been a positive one, and it deserves to be reflected here. Thank you to the staff at St Mary’s Cray Practice for your professionalism, kindness, and thorough care — it has made a real difference to my wellbeing.

recent_reviews.author: Steve Connor
recent_reviews.text: Thank you to the Greasby Group Practice GPs for helping my wife Julia. They have saved her life, it's that simple. She's been through a tough time in 2024 in particular and all the doctors have supported her incredibly well. Dr Pillitteri initiated emergency treatment at Arrowe Park, thank you so much. Dr Wright and Dr Patrick (who identified a DVT in my wife's leg) have also been a massive help with home visits and returning phone calls. Dr Carter has also been extremely helpful with advice and the admin team have also responded very swiftly to online requests or queries. I would strongly recommend using the PATCHS system, it works. We should be very grateful to have Drs like this in Greasby, so please support them. Remember also, they are like us, with families, and lives to live with all its day-to-day pressures. Being a GP is a huge responsibility and pressure and we need to consider that, so give them time and space to do their work. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- The last 2-3 years (21-23) has seen a significant drop in quality of service. I blame financial pressures (£ cuts - so called 'efficiencies') by central government. The staff are massively overloaded, are constantly hassled and it comes through on phone calls and enquiries. If you vote Tory this is what you get after 12 years. As doctor Coppock said to me before she retired 'the world has gone mad' meaning the unworkable booking system and more. Boris Johnson and his cronies have left a mess, but they don't care.

recent_reviews.author: M
recent_reviews.text: I have been registered at this surgery for over 20 years and never had an issue. All of doctors have been fine and getting appointments has never been an issue. The nurses are also helpful and provide a valuable service. However, there is an issue with the Reception. They are too quick to dismiss patient queries. They 'hear' what you are saying but don't 'listen', to the point where they are rude and dismissive. I asked a simple question, why my NHS app was quoting that my test results were saying, the Surgery had discussed the blood test results with me when they definitely hadn't. The receptionist started disputing what was on my phone, saying that what they had on their system was different, but would't listen when I suggested it was wrong to put statements on my medical records that were wrong. I was told it was nothing to do with her and if I wanted it changing to complain.

recent_reviews.author: Patrick Egan
recent_reviews.text: Rang today to get a future appointment for my wife. Receptionist told me that they do not book future dated appointments. This is not true and their website actually states a limited number of future dated appointments are available. I explained to her that my wife is a Head Teacher and can only attend an appointment when the school is shut for half term as she will not take a day off. This is a non urgent appointment and does not require her to miss school which she never would. I was told to put a request in online which I done and as per my own experience with this Surgery, the request was rejected within an hour. No wonder this countries productivity is poor when you need to miss a day off work to see your GP for something that can be planned in. I always thought that trying to plan such things in advance would be better rather than adding to high demand for services for sick people on the day....

recent_reviews.text: I had a fall and broke my shoulder and as a result I was house bound for 4 months , My shoulder was dealt with by the main hospital BUT as a result off my fall my legs started to swell because I couldn't raise the legs due to they were swelling and becoming blistered and ulcerated. Eventually after 1 month I phoned 111 on a Saturday a doctor visited whom contacted the practice and a kind Doctor from the practice finally visited me at home and I passed to District Nurse treatment who got my legs back to good health after 4 months. I'm back under surgery care and the nurse team are doing a wonderful job. My legs shouldn't have got this way I don't know if it's my emails or phone requests not being passed to the relevant person but I'm hoping the nursing team can sort my problem now I'm under there care.

recent_reviews.author: Shaun Saunders
recent_reviews.text: We all know that the NHS is under constant pressure. It must be very depressing, working in a service so underfunded and under pressure. What I don't understand is why the practice manager doesn't introduce some strategies that make it less likely that patients will become irritable. My partner collected my prescription today and was advised that they could not provide a vital medication and that I would need the GP to consider an alternative pill. I am writing this whilst waiting for the surgery to answer the phone. Frankly, I am getting bored and more than a little frusrated listening to a recording telling me how important my call us to them EVERY TEN SECONDS, for fifteen minutes so far! Why not some soothing music or even a system that advises you of your position in the queue? Why not a functioning facility for me to leave a text, email or voicenote. All I need to say is "NHS cannot obtain pregabilin". Can my GP suggest an alternative? See how easy that was. No stress. No pressure. No staff required to answer the phone. Please consider simple solutions. It will make life better for staff abd patient's.

recent_reviews.author: Dean Lawton
recent_reviews.text: Well after previously writing a good review of the surgery and of Doctor Tang i feel i need to make corrections. After suffering an incident in july 23 ive been left unable to work, sit, stand or walk. Ive had mri’s and xrays showing both l5/s1 disc bulge and osteoarthritis of the hips, oh then a month later apparently im clear of the latter. Ive begged for help to get me back contributing in society but to no avail. They offer me drugs i cant take, ive begged for injections in si joint but refuse and at best have been offered physio at the surgery, ive done physio the whole time. They have not offered me MSK physio, they haven’t even tried to get to the bottom of the source of my pain so that i can at least help myself to the correct exercises. The most alarming thing and was not going to go public with this but after a lot of reflection have decided to pursue through nhs complaints was, in february, dr harding thought he was doing the right thing taking me off a drug (gabapentin) which i had been on for 12 years and took me off it in 1 week!!! Causing me a whole load of mental trauma, night sweats, suicidal tendencies and probably a lot more pain from the mental anguish!! At best this was reckless behaviour by a dr! Im left with no faith in the surgery and after being compared to a knackered car that you wouldn’t chuck parts at by dr oxley this morning, my fairh in the nhs as a whole is a shambles!!!

recent_reviews.author: E M
recent_reviews.text: If you need to have continuity of care and need your shared care from a previous GP continued at this practice. They won't do it. I registered here recently and my endocrinologist sent them my report from previous GP practice. I had a perscrition written by ISCA, without seeing anyone. So I assumed all was well. They then cancelled upcoming important blood test and stopped my meds. With no bridging perscrition to help me whilst I run round asking other GP surgerys. I've had no proper explanation asides from a short 'no shared care'. They clearly dont follow standard GMC guidance on the matter. Instead whatever conflicting advice is spouted by Labours Streeting. And guidance from the Royal College of General Practitioners (RCGP) says that ‘’if you are already stabilised on hormone therapy, prescriptions should not be abruptly stopped, as this may cause physical or mental harm’’. So to avoid any self soul destroying. Do not even bother registering here, and try your luck elsewhere.

recent_reviews.text: Good Morning, On Tuesday 16th September, I made an appointment for my daughter Àlora Smith due to her stopping breathing and not being herself. I was seen to by Dr Kosi Onuorah who checked over my 8 week old baby and informed me that there was nothing wrong and I was being over sensitive. She did not form observation on her other then temp and listening to chest which she confirmed was fine. I expressed I still didn’t feel something was right and was informed to “keep an eye on her”. Later that evening I got a phone call from the surgery saying that due to my daughter being under the age of 3 months I need to take her to the children’s assessment unit which yes I’m thankful for the referral but I’m also not happy with the fact I was informed by a trusted doctor there was nothing wrong. When arriving at the assessment unit my child was rushed into a room to be put onto oxygen and antibiotics due to being on a Sepsis pathway. I’d like to say that the Dr who seen my child has robbed me off and needs action taken on her own actions for dismissing a child who was severely poorly to the point she could not leave the hospital for further 5 days. The evidence I had on my phone of Alora struggling to breath and head bobbing was enough for the CAU to take action so why did your doctor not take action? Regards

After reading some of the negative comments , all I can say is that these people don't appreciate what they have, which is : . Kind, polite and understanding reception staff, also highly experienced medical staff. . A ring back service that calls you if there are high call volumes. . All triage service that in most cases you get a call back within a hour, most often less than 30 minutes depending on the severity of your problem by a health care professional who will make a decision based on what you tell them , this often results in me getting an appointment on the same day and with the right person. This is a practice that gives me personally a high level of service and I appreciate what they do for me. Because you haven't got your own way or you think you may have been overlooked please just stop and think that there was probably a valid reason for this. If you want the world to revolve around you then maybe consider paying privately, I believe that companies like BUPA have very reasonable monthly plans. A satisfied NHS patient.

recent_reviews.text: Just had a good experience. Needed a dressing change and blood test within a week of heart surgery in London. Was told to book a blood appointment online (Swiftqueue) with instruction to email back if any problems. Earliest slot on Swiftqueue was 3 weeks away so emailed back and got another phone call saying the blood would be taken by Nurse Bayer at the same time as the dressing change. Nurse Bayer was very kind and reassuring. She even made another appointment for another dressing change 4 days later. Could get used to this…..

recent_reviews.author: Anna Dorant-Hayes
recent_reviews.text: Watling Medical Centre is the best run surgery in Barnet if not in the whole of North London. You can get an appointment relatively easy and if that's not possible you can rest assured that a doctor will call you back at least to discuss your issue over the phone and provide an advice. Receptionists are courteous and helpful and more importantly the medical staff really listen to the patients and take on board their concerns, and act promptly. The surgery always tries to improve its services and ensure patients have better experience - eg. introducing longer working hours until 20.00 on some days, accessing advice via e-consult. I've been registered in this surgery for close to 20 years and my experience has always been positive. I was particularly impressed by the way they quickly and successfully adapted their work during the Covid pandemic providing an efficient and prompt service in very challenging conditions. My thanks go to all the excellent staff but in particular Dr Patel and Dr Santhouse for their expert help over the years. Thank you.

recent_reviews.text: Along with others the receptionist is rude. I tried explaining something and just constantly spoken over, not listening to what I was trying to say about needing an emergency controlled drug prescription. I had phoned 111 the night before and they sent a request to the chemist but the chemist couldn't do it with it being a controlled drug. The chemist said someone would call within the hour to sort it which was 8pm so I could get there in time before it shutting as it's an important pain medication. I waited until 12 then went to bed in pain. I checked my phone at 6 and they'd tried ringing at midnight and 1am when most are in bed. I then rang 111 again at 8am and he said the gp would ring within 2hrs still no call at 12 so I've missed this morning's aswel. I tried explaining all this but the receptionist almost made me feel like I was lieing and wouldn't allow me to fully explain and said bye and hung up mid conversation. Exceptionally rude and not helpful. We are not allowed to speak like that to them or they can refuse treatment so why are they allowed to with patients that are ill with disabilities and certain diseases that need the pain medication??

recent_reviews.author: TRuthven
recent_reviews.text: My elderly mum contacted the practice on two consecutive days by telephone and encountered the AI assistant. She confirmed her landline was her preferred communication method for a callback, no callback was received. I contacted the practice on my Mum's behalf and spoke to a member of the reception team. It became clear that a text had been sent to my Mum's mobile phone for her to book an appointment. (1) My mum's mobile isn't a smart phone and therefore doesn't have the capability to book appointments. (2) This is not my Mum's preferred communication method. At no time has the practice identified with my Mum whether her mobile phone has the capability to book appointments. This appears to be a major system error for the practice to address immediately. I believe if I had not intervened my Mum would have been at serious risk of harm through the lack of care and poor administrative procedures employed at the surgery. Not everybody has or wants a smartphone. The AI receptionist will sadly fail patients and is making care more unsafe. We did finally get an appointment which is the only positive news that I can share about the surgery.

recent_reviews.author: Halax Strider
recent_reviews.text: ** This is the old review part, please see my newer comments at the bottom because I feel differently now about the surgery a lot but would like still to keep what was initially said for comparison sake / to show the improvement on previous vs. now, as they have improved massively: ** --- Old Review from 2024-ish from memory -- Extremely poor service. Put in prescription request over 72hrs, regularly they miss it then claim they have no idea about it. Ask for help with something and it's "so and so receptionist can deal with that, come back when they're here" when the person you just spoke to is on reception too. It has always been hit or miss whether my prescription gets picked up each month sometimes it does other times like now, they don't check emails or respond very rarely. I don't have an issue with the doctors.. Nancy Maningo especially is lovely. It's mostly the receptionist and really poor service when booking or trying to get your repeat prescriptions sorted. Nurses have always been good with blood tests, and very friendly - the GPs I see are all good. It is just awful reception and customer service side which is very frustrating to deal with. Also can echo the fact many times you ring even at 8am, you will not be answered until 9:50 sometimes, and then no appointments left. This has happened to my mother many times. NHS cuts are a problem but for me the biggest issue is how many times I put in my prescription every month for it to be missed and then I have to chase to a receptionist who says they know nothing about it. I am now out of my medication I take daily and again today, dealing with clueless receptionists who claim they haven't received anything... it was in writing to you via email the same way it is done every month..! -- Update from 2025 - Improvements made hugely -- I am updating my score as the service has improved considerably with no issues to my prescriptions anymore, plus they were majorly helpful in helping me with urgent care for an infection. I had seen the urgent care doctor at another clinic for a serious ear infection but no pharmacy had the antibiotics. When I rang Willows as my local GP they got me in to see a doctor immediately and change the antibiotic item to one in stock which has Seriously helped me as the pain was spreading to my jaw and face earlier and I feared it could get worse without any antibiotics. I was so relieved as I feared not addressing it today would have caused it to get worse. But overall my comments from 4 months to now are vastly different as the surgery seems to have improved a lot and I'm no longer having the same issues as I was having. I think theres still a bit of issues with getting appointments in the morning which seems to be a universal NHS doctor strain so not specific to the practice but overall I was really grateful they heard out what I had said and are improving a lot. Thank you -- More update as of March 2026 -- The service still is improving, and I think even getting in now is easier. I've had more opportunities to book in fairly quick as I have regular bloodwork done and check ups and it's been a lot easier to get everything in place. They also send me text reminders to book in which makes it simple as sometimes I have a lot of different check ups so I can keep track of it better. A few times I've rang in and been offered an appointment on the same day or few days later. I haven't a clue what they did but they definetly got the surgery to improve massively over the last year. Theres a lot more opportunity to feed back as well now with links to say how your experience was which we didn't used to have so this is allowing the management to look into people's issues more effectively. Overall I would stay with my current GP surgery as I have no issues anymore and everything has been going really smoothly for me.

recent_reviews.author: Lottie Treleaven
recent_reviews.text: If you’re offered an ultrasound here please reconsider where you have it done. The nurse and doctor are extremely rude and given the size of the surgery I doubt there are alternative staff. The nurse didn’t even bother saying hello before immediately by pointing out we were late and after we apologised and explained that we struggled to get there she continued to press the issue. My partner apologised three times explaining each time but the nurse still kept a scowl and continued to mention it. The doctor didn’t introduce himself or explain where he was going to touch before doing it and despite being a chaperone for the ultrasound I was told to sit in a corner of the room and then a curtain was put between us which does sort of defeat the purpose of having someone come in to make sure that you’re comfortable and nothing that shouldn’t happen happens. There was no goodbye only a scowl from the nurse as we left and the doctor returning to his desk. I don’t mind being treated neutrally but it seemed the minute we were late the nurse had it out for us and the doctor couldn’t seem to care less. We later watched that same nurse argue with another patient in the waiting room so I would say that unfortunately we got the preferable side of her which is saying something.

recent_reviews.author: Marta Staszek
recent_reviews.text: I have experienced multiple issues with this practice, but recently it has become beyond unacceptable. Two weeks ago, I called to book an appointment and was told the earliest available date was 31st March, which I agreed to and booked. While I was on holiday abroad, I then received a message confirming an appointment on 17th March — not only a different date, but also a different time. As I was outside the country and unable to call, I sent an email to clarify the situation and followed up again due to a lack of response. In my messages, I clearly asked for confirmation of my original appointment on 31st March and requested cancellation of the incorrect booking on 17th March if necessary. Instead, I received a message on the day stating that the appointment could not be cancelled and that I needed to call them. This was extremely frustrating, as I had already explained that I was unable to make phone calls while abroad. Additionally, there was no acknowledgement or confirmation regarding my original booking on 31st March. This is not the first time I have experienced disorganisation from the administrative team, but this situation has been particularly stressful. I arranged time off work based on the confirmed 31st March appointment, and now I am left uncertain whether that booking even exists. Overall, this reflects a serious lack of organisation, communication, and respect for patients’ time. I am extremely disappointed, especially as I chose this practice based on positive reviews. Once this issue is resolved, I will not be returning. The level of stress and effort required to manage even basic administrative matters is unacceptable. I would strongly advise others to avoid this practice.

recent_reviews.author: Stefan Rehak
recent_reviews.text: I recently visited West Green Practice ( 04.02.26) and was extremely disappointed with my experience. Since registering as a patient, my name has been misspelled in their system. During my last visit, when I noticed the error displayed on the screen, I politely approached reception to ask for it to be corrected. Instead of helping, the receptionist was dismissive and unhelpful. As I was rushing to my appointment, I explained I did not need an explanation and simply wanted my name corrected. I remained calm, did not raise my voice, and did not use any inappropriate language. Despite this, the receptionist refused to continue the conversation and issued me with a strike, even though I did not violate any patient conduct rules. Having incorrect personal details in medical records is a serious issue and could potentially lead to miscommunication, problems with treatment, or medication errors. Shortly afterwards, I received a letter stating I had been removed from the patient list — and the letter still contained the incorrect spelling of my name. There appears to be very limited opportunity for patients to raise concerns. When I contacted the call centre, I was told I would need to wait two weeks for a call back. I do not feel that I was treated fairly, which is why I felt the need to raise this issue publicly. While I understand that NHS staff need protection from abuse, patients should also feel safe raising legitimate concerns. Unfortunately, my experience felt dismissive and unprofessional. Furthermore, as my name was misspelled and never dealed with I now have difficulties in medical history matching and with registering at the new GP. On the positive side, my appointment with a male doctor went amazingly well.

recent_reviews.author: Omid Samari
recent_reviews.text: Dear Sherwood Rise Medical Centre, My name is Omid Samari (Date of Birth: 28/07/1983), and I am writing to express my sincere gratitude for the outstanding care I received from Dr. Badhe. In February, I visited your practice and was seen twice by another doctor. Unfortunately, my condition did not improve, and there was no follow-up. I consider myself very fortunate that Dr. Badhe later saw me. She listened carefully, arranged appropriate tests, and told me that if my symptoms persisted, she would write a referral letter to the hospital. When things didn’t improve, she did exactly that. Although the hospital initially rejected the referral, Dr. Badhe personally called me twice, showing great concern for my health, and advised me to go to A&E immediately. I followed her advice and was admitted to the hospital overnight. At first, the doctors suspected I had suffered a stroke, but it was later determined that the cause was spinal canal narrowing. I am truly grateful for Dr. Badhe’s professionalism, compassion, and decisive action. I believe her efforts played a key role in identifying the real cause of my condition and preventing further complications. I would also like to thank Dr. Eghbal, who has always been kind and supportive. Please kindly pass on my appreciation to both Dr. Badhe and Dr. Eghbal. Warm regards, Omid Samari

The morning of the appointment I receive a brief explanation of my results from the doctor and am asked why was the blood test ordered (all communication was done via app). I explain my concerns and express my need to speak to her.. After no reply and some time passing I call to inquire as to whether I will have my appointment only to find out it has been canceled. Hours later (after hearing nothing) I call and am told the doctor will call me around 5, she’s in a meeting. I have never felt so dismissed by a “medical “practice in al of my experiences. How can a doctor understand/make a determination without engaging with the patient? Are you a medical professional if a “meeting “ is more important than the public you have sworn to serve?? Or is the title of doctor more important?? There are many 1 star reviews for this practice, shouldn’t that be a wake up call for the entire staff?

recent_reviews.author: Dylan
recent_reviews.text: It's shocking how many bad encounters I've had with dantre medical practice. For an example 10 days ago I was told I must have an x-ray due to having heart and chest pains for over a year so they told me to come in the next day as to which I did only for them to be closed so I went in the day after that and had my x-ray and I was told I would get my x-ray results WITHIN 7 days. I called them 10 days later since they haven't even attempted to contact me only for them to tell me they haven't even bothered to look at my x-ray yet and to wait another 4 plus days. Oh and another thing they gave me a questionnaire to fill out to get diagnosed with ADHD, so I filled out the form and sent it to them and was told It will be passed on to a quicker private ADHD clinic and that I would be contacted within 6 months (this was 2 YEARS ago now) but of course it went well over 6 months and nothing happened so I emailed them around 3 times on separate occasions only to be ignored so I called them to make sure they actually sent my form to the clinic (as i know how forgetful they are) only for the person to actually tell me herself "to be honest I don't even know whats happened to the form" and that she will chase it up. Anyways fast forward a couple more months I had an appointment and in that appointment I asked for an update about the ADHD form only for her to say we've only sent it off about two months ago. Many months later I had another appointment and asked my Dr about the ADHD update yet again and this time he said I can see its been sent but I can't tell you how long it will take even tho the first Dr ( 2 years ago) said it will take no more than 6 months but now all the sudden 2 years later they can't tell me how long it will take. Also out of all the times I've been there not once has a Dr been on time for my appointment and one time I had to wait 45 minutes past my appointment time just waiting in the waiting room for my Dr to come out which is fine if it was a hospital but its not, its a quiet small Dr's practice with no more than 15 people in the waiting room whenever I go there. Also they said they CANNOT help me with my Insomia which has been happening since I was a child. Please do not take your children here or even yourself

recent_reviews.author: Sophie
recent_reviews.text: Called the surgery for an “on the day” appointment at 8am for my mum. We used the call back system which worked really well and were offered an appointment at 10:10am. Saw Mia, an Associate Physician, who gave Mum a thorough check over. Decided that there were some tests she wanted to perform and managed to organise them for us while we were there (partly due to someone else not turning up) ECG and blood test all sorted in no time at all. By the following morning Mum had heard from the surgery to tell her the results of her blood test and the details of some further tests that were needed. Not only was this visit extremely efficient, everyone was so kind - the receptionist on the phone, Mia and the nurses who did the ECG and blood test. So caring and reassuring at a time when we were worried about what was going on. Thank you so much.

recent_reviews.text: In my opinion, absolutely dire service, especially from the receptionist. They also made a point to inform me it was a 7 working day wait - to me that is irrelevant and entirely unhelpful as I still have to wait a total of 10 days to be seen, including the 7 working days. Serious room & need for improvement here I feel.

recent_reviews.author: M M
recent_reviews.text: I have been a patient at this surgery for over 30 years, dating back to when they were on the other side of Prince of Wales Road. It is incredibly disappointing to see how much the standards have fallen since the move to No. 52. The only reason we stayed so long was the clinical excellence of the long-standing doctors. Dr. Taylor was an absolute gentleman and was exceptionally good to my father; however, he and Dr. Major have now left the practice. It feels as though all the truly great, experienced doctors have either moved on or retired. While Dr. Pal and Dr. Postgate are still fantastic, it is now near impossible to get an appointment with either of them. The only remaining bright spot is Dr. Rose, who is lovely, but she cannot carry the whole practice alone. The biggest issue, however, is the reception staff. The attitude at the front desk is appalling the tone is often bullying and obstructive, creating a "my way or the highway" atmosphere. You are made to feel that if you don't submit to their rude temperament, you won't be allowed to see a doctor. It is stressful and completely unprofessional. Given the current CQC rating and the hostile environment created by the administrative staff, we have finally had enough. After three decades of loyalty, we will be moving to a GP surgery that values its patients and meets the required standards of care.

recent_reviews.author: Escape Normality
recent_reviews.text: This practice has treated me poorly on multiple occasions, and the issue is not a single mistake but a repeated pattern of failure. Across several interactions, my symptoms were dismissed or minimised without proper assessment. Concerns were not investigated thoroughly, and clinical curiosity was replaced with reassurance that was unsupported by evidence. When action was required, the default response was delay. There has been persistent inconsistency. Different clinicians have given different answers to the same issues, with thresholds and explanations changing depending on who I spoke to. This creates confusion, undermines confidence, and suggests a lack of coherent clinical decision-making within the practice. Follow-up has been weak. I have repeatedly had to chase appointments, prescriptions, or next steps, rather than these being managed proactively. Progress only seems to occur after escalation, which indicates a reactive approach to care rather than a responsible or preventative one. Responsibility is often deflected to “policy,” “guidelines,” or system limitations, rather than clinicians owning decisions and explaining them clearly. This leaves the patient carrying the burden of navigating problems that should be handled within primary care. The cumulative effect is a loss of trust. I now approach interactions expecting resistance rather than support, which is not how a patient–GP relationship should function. At no point should a patient feel they must fight repeatedly to receive basic, consistent medical care. In summary, this practice has managed risk for itself rather than prioritising patient outcomes. The repeated delays, dismissals, and inconsistencies fall below what I would reasonably expect from competent primary care. Based on my experiences, I cannot recommend this practice. Nothing more then another group of people lining thier own pockets and no regard for consumers health or condition management DISGUSTING and ill be getting a solicitor to deal with them

recent_reviews.author: Kaylum Gilbert
recent_reviews.text: I don't know why there are so many bad reviews about this place. Yes it can be quiet difficult at times to get an appointment but that isn't there fault. There's only so many appointments and time in the day. My only gripe with appointments is it's ring on the day. But there are always elderly patience waiting outside the surgery before half past 8 wanting appointments. In my own experience I have always managed to ring and get to see DR Lowe whenever needed. And Dr Lowe is hands down the best doctor I have ever dealt with. After years of struggling with my mental health and not knowing what's wrong with me or why I am like I am and using other doctors and nurses and getting absolutely nowhere I went to see DR Lowe, who was so understanding and could see how much I was struggling, he has helped me so much through many dark times. He got me reffered to a psychiatrist very quickly where after years of struggle was diagnosed with Bipolar. If it wasn't for Dr Lowe this would never have happened. So I cannot thank him enough for all his help and support over the last year or so, will only ever go to see him in future. The receptionists are always helpful and go the extra mile for me as they know how I struggle with social interaction. All in all I think it's a wonderfully surgery I won't be going anywhere else

recent_reviews.author: charlotte Lynn
recent_reviews.text: I have experience of the surgery for my step kids and everyone i dealt with was brilliant. Having now moved to the areas i have become a new patient and sadly the experience has not been good. Firstly a medical review appointment was booked without any correspondence or explanation - for a time i couldn't make. I called and rebooked - however all text communication didn't update and i had no idea which appointment would happen. The person who did the medical review had no idea what the appointment was for and seemed more confused than i was. The result of that review was 1 out of 3 meds required on repeat where approved and none were pushed through to the app as promised. The result being more work and confusion for myself and her colleagues. On speaking to the practice this was quickly resolved which was great. I haven't received any correspondence from the Practice explaining the patient onboarding process, steps to take or guidance. The staff seem to think we should know what happens and their default is to pop into the surgery which really shouldn't be necessary. Moving doctors is stressful, practices should own the migration and help patients with the process and most of all ensure repeat medication is migrated properly.

recent_reviews.author: Georgi Dimitrov
recent_reviews.text: They have good team in general, but the whole system.... First refused for nearly a month to give me a proper appointment, dismissed my request despite long term health issues which is complete medical negligence. After many requests finally was examined and confirmed that I actually was quite ill and need antibiotics, however because they kept me for so long now its very difficult for me to recover. Today I called again to ask for results and a follow up(1 hour before their closing time). First they tried to send me back to the hospital(which said that the GP has the results already). When asking about medication or a follow up appointment was told to put a request tomorrow - which I know is not true, as their system says it can be done on Monday, so I have to wait for 4 days without treatment again). When pointed this out to the receptionist, she confirmed but didn' t explain why she advises me to do something which I actually cannot do and she knows it.(pretty clear that she just wanted to get rid off me). And when I reacted with a sarcastic laugh she said 'Rude' and hung up. With this 'thin skin' and avoidance of constructive criticism no wonder the processes are ineffective. Processes and ineffective, cant blame just the surgery, its a system failure, educational failure... from a nurse(i believe) here, I was told that is not necessary the skin to be cleaned prior an injection... maybe you do not have it as a written policy to outline this good practice(elsewhere is a written MUST). And if you need to be legally obliged to adopt a great practice, which bear nearly 0 costs and quite a lot of benefits... then god save...what is critical thinking? Do you eat it, drink it? I know is not easy, but the people who work in a industry, organisation and/or system, and those who use the service provided, are the ones who can change these inefficiencies.

recent_reviews.text: They are very good. They have a system where you can fill out a form in the morning to complete an online consultation form and they will ring you back, forward you to the chemist for a prescription, or set up an appointment with you to come in. recent_reviews.author: Sean Elliott
recent_reviews.text: My wife and I have now switched surgery due to the poor service received here. Their desire to have everything done through Anima might make some sense, except that there is a window you can make a request the same as the phones, so no advantage there. And often things will get closed without a consult or resolution with the patient, so you have to wait until the next day to try again. When you do call, the reception staff often aren't very helpful (I think there's one in particular that's especially unhelpful), often suggesting that the patient sort problems the surgery has created e.g. sending a prescription to the wrong pharmacy, and suggesting to my wife that she just go there then (she can't drive due to a recent Caesarean section). My date of birth was entered incorrectly, and I've been in person with documents to get it sorted several times, but it still hasn't been fixed. Have heard similar stories from others and frankly wished I'd stayed away.

recent_reviews.author: Preya Ramey
recent_reviews.text: I had previously rated 5 Stars but that was only due to a prompt when completing registration that asked me how my registration experience was. Seems like a very shady and misleading method to fill 5 Star Reviews. That aside - I am not sure what has happened in the past few months, but this practice has gone down hill fast. You call first thing in the morning, receptionist now makes you triage online rather than taking a moment to speak to you, you then wait all day to hear back from them only to be told minimal information and that you now have to re-triage if you actually want an appointment. No matter what you are calling about, even if you were on the phone with your GP and the call got disconnected, the only thing the receptionist seems to say is “fill out the triage form online”. How does that make sense? I also have had similar experiences to others where blood tests were not completed properly. No follow up, no care for patients at all, receptionist literally says fill out the form and hangs up on you. Honestly appalling how little they seem to care these days when just months ago they were fine. I will not accept being busy as an excuse for providing no care and no empathy for your patients. I will say that the female physicians I have seen while visiting this practice have all been so empathetic and wonderful. My concerns are mainly with reception and overall organization and communication.

recent_reviews.author: Chanelle
recent_reviews.text: After having a scan at Purfleet medical centre where i was told something very concerning one weekend, I was then contacted by Peartree surgery on the Tues to say they had the report and I would be referred for an mri. I had a call from Basildon hospital the following day who booked me in for the scan to be done in less than 48hrs! Everyone at basildon were great, I had the scan done on the Friday and by Wednesday lunchtime Peartree surgery had text me to say everything was fine. I couldn't fault how fast everything was dealt with that week and Kathy & John were as reassuring as possible whenever i called during the wait. Im very grateful to Dr Reg for referring me so fast- he is always a great listener on the phone and i never feel rushed off the call when I have spoken to him in the past. The stress of the original incorrect findings at Purfleet caused myself & my family immense stress and fear across that week and so i would like to think the technician would maybe be contacted and offered further training as i feel somebody providing an ultrasound should be able to tell the difference between a cancerous tumour which is what he told me he thought i could have and what turned out to be muscle/tissue. I had an ultrasound at Basildon a few days later who couldn't see anything suspicious at all, which tells me the man at Purfleet wasn't really qualified enough to be telling me what he did. Im just grateful all came back ok, but I worry this could happen to other people in the future being scanned by that person

recent_reviews.author: Paul Saunders
recent_reviews.text: This surgery is failing its patients. Getting help here is incredibly difficult. Reception is often abrupt and dismissive, and you are made to feel like an inconvenience rather than someone seeking medical care. It is extremely hard to get clear information, timely appointments, or any sense that your concerns are being properly taken seriously. There is a serious lack of compassion, communication, and follow‑up. Patients are left chasing answers, repeating themselves, and fighting just to be heard. The overall attitude is undermining and patronising, with very little basic respect shown. The practice appears to be overwhelmed, with too many patients and not enough capacity. This leads to long waits, poor access to treatment, and worrying gaps in care, which is especially concerning for vulnerable people who rely on this surgery. Formal complaints have been raised and escalated to the ICB due to how these issues have been handled. From my experience, the problems here are systemic and ongoing, not one‑off mistakes. Peartree Surgery urgently needs to change how it treats patients and how it is run. Right now, it is letting people down in a serious way.

recent_reviews.text: This practice is fantastic. Having been a patient for seven years almost and going through a global pandemic, I have nothing but praise for the team. recent_reviews.author: Mark Winder
recent_reviews.text: Our experience, briefly: Written confirmation of 30 days’ continued registration. Discharged early anyway. Told written confirmation “didn’t matter.” Told removal could only happen if a new GP contacted them. No new GP had contacted them. Initially told this was “impossible.” Prescriptions eventually issued. Controlled drugs issued for one week only. Medication ran out. 111 contacted. Pharmacies declined. Three days without fentanyl. A&E attendance due to withdrawal. Separate occasions: Epilepsy medication not ready when due. Returned. Still not ready. Multiple seizures followed. Conversations with the reception manager often felt less like speaking to administrative support and more like entering a debate club — interruptions included at no extra charge. To be fair, once a GP became directly involved, matters improved. The clinicians were not the problem. If your healthcare needs are straightforward, you may never notice. If you rely on continuity and controlled medication being available when prescribed, pack snacks and patience.

recent_reviews.author: Valerie Ross
recent_reviews.text: Apalling system of obtaining an appointment. Phone at 8 am. haha you will be lucky to get through. I can understand the system to phone first thing in the morning for an appointment on that day if there is one available. But the curious one is; I am told that we all must phone on Monday 's for all appointments during the week. So, if on Wednesday I need to see a Doctor it's a no go situation; either phone each morning at 8 and seldom get any joy. (even if you get through there's no appointments available for about 4 - 6 weeks) or wait until the following Monday and hope you get through before all the bookings are taken. You can't win and it makes no sense. After spending 11 hours at A & E Saturday night, no sleep at all, monitors all night long etc., discharged and instructed to see my doctor for heart medications etc. So Monday, today; I start phone at 8 a.m. at 9.30 I walk to the surgery (walking is very difficult for me). I ask if report from hospital is through and if so I need an appointment to discuss medication and prescription that I apparently need. Ha, ha, ha, its funny if it wast so flipping stressful. I am told, no appointments available. Try tomorrow at 8 a.m. and so the circus will continues. She says she can see the report from the hospital has been received but there is nothing she can do. I tell her any doctor I don't care who. Once again I am told to ring at 8 tomorrow. So I shall get on the phone tomorrow at 8 a.m. and continue with this circus. Dealing with this sort of situation and guidelines laid down by who knows who is just so stressful. recent_reviews.author: Elara Rose
recent_reviews.text: Tried for months to get doctor appt. In the old days in the midlands and surrey, you pop in get seen same day. But now got to try endlessly on phone until get through. Not allowed to pop in or book online. Sure many like me need more care because problem not nipped in bud so to speak. I have given up officially now! My mum keeps saying go see doctor not understanding how impossible it is, because where i grew up, where she is, our doctor of many years will visit her, nurses call. Ive lived in 3 counties since left home, this has to be the worse for seeing a real human being whose profession is a doctor! When i did finally get an actual appointment, was 2 weeks time in marchwood doctors, different place, had a car then so didnt mind but they cancelled it on the day. Then i got feedback request re appt with no option to say you cancelled it so i didnt see anyone! Another time after 4 months trying to get appt. In desperation i went in, couldnt get appt, was told to phone. What would a person do if they've got no phone or cant phone because cant speak, lost their voice! Anyway finally got appt at hospital, did i see a doctor, no idea, he said go back to your doctor. I thought "but this is my doctor appointment!" So this, long term unknown medical problem is in Gods hands. The other simpler problem id been told i need antibiotics by pharmacists and chiropodist. This same person said quote "we wont give you antibiotics, we'll see if the black spreads up your leg"... In disbelief and shock i said nothing. No point going to a doctor. A few weeks later my toe nail fell off.... i still have the other issue nearly 2 years later. (Elaras not my real name)

recent_reviews.text: The staff are all friendly and well-meaning and overall I have no problem with the actual medical service, but everything else apart from that is third-rate. recent_reviews.author: Jacob
recent_reviews.text: From my experiences with this GP, there isn't anything you can say to convince me that the NHS's crisis with money and availability isn't at least 50% self-inflicted. When you actually get to see a doctor here, 9/10 times its fine and you get decent care. Personally I have seen a doctor in that 1/10 times who clearly did not understand the severity of my issue, and did not prescribe a long enough course of medication despite being given all the information needed to make that call (backed up by my own research after the fact), and this has ended up with a condition that could have been treated probably within ~8 weeks that I have now been battling for nearly a year and a half and have been waiting for ~4 months for different medication that nobody has except for online pharmacies. They order tests that will ultimately be nullified due to an unwillingness to effectively follow up with you, and if you try to follow it up, they just ignore you. Wasting time and money. They do not respond to emails, they just don't, no matter how straightforward the query is. It seems you have to waste both your time and their time to call them for everything; then calling them is invariably a slog, and you have a 50/50 chance of getting someone willing to take ownership of the call and be helpful. Wasting time. Shutting off the online request system after a handful of hours into the working day is just pitiful, when you also refuse to answer emails, and its a lottery whether a phonecall will end up with someone actually being helpful or just badly explaining how their terribly inefficient system works with useless internal jargon; being unable to read that they are speaking to someone in clear mental distress who is just trying to get a hold of some medication, and they are not willing or cognizant enough to offer a really simple solution of signing me up to electronic prescriptions. I only found out that you need to be signed up to electronic prescriptions to use online pharmacies on the weekend after being to the in-person pharmacy (telling me they released the prescription because they don't have it and nobody local is likely to have it), then the GP over the phone (telling me the pharmacy hasn't released the prescription and I should go back to them and then play 'drug hunt' around the pharmacies that won't have it), then the pharmacy again over the phone (who reiterated that they released the prescription and that I also need to play 'drug hunt'). Why do you not a system telling you local medication stock at nearby pharmacies? Seems like a no-brainer to ensure you either prescribe something that can actually be acquired, or proactively forward people to online pharmacies when they aren't. That would actually save everyone time and money. I sent them an email asking them to advise what it takes to get signed up to electronic prescriptions, its been 3 months and they haven't responded. I have since opened a complaint 2 months ago, and enclosed my ignored email into the complaint, they still have not responded to the original email nor the complaint. I don't even know what to say anymore, but it seems like I need to explore switching to a different GP to see if the grass is any greener elsewhere.

recent_reviews.author: Stefania Vati
recent_reviews.text: I have had an extremely distressing experience at this practice. I felt treated as a number rather than as a human being. Despite providing evidence that my most recent test in my home country was positive for a very high-risk virus associated with cancer, both the nurse and the GP refused to repeat the test. My medical records clearly show that I am in a higher-risk category: two women in my family have died from this condition, and over the past 15 years I have had both positive and negative test results. Although my last test with this GP was negative, that was almost nine months ago. Given my medical history (I had already two surgeries related to this issue) and risk factors, it is reasonable to consider that circumstances may change and that closer monitoring may be appropriate. I was told that protocol requires waiting five years before repeating the test. However, applying a blanket protocol without properly considering an individual’s documented medical history feels inappropriate and potentially unsafe. Clinical guidelines should allow for professional judgment and exceptions when a patient’s risk profile clearly justifies further investigation. I strongly believe that doctors should be able to exercise discretion in order to protect their patients’ health and, potentially, their lives.

recent_reviews.text: The doctors at this surgery are caring, professional, and thorough. Unfortunately, the newly installed phone system completely lets them down. I received a voicemail from a GP asking me to call back urgently about my sick child, but it has been impossible to reach anyone at reception. The phone system is a maze of confusing options, some of which only appear after waiting silently for a while. After multiple steps of verifying my details with the automated system, I’m then given another round of options, none of which allow you to speak to a receptionist or even leave a voicemail. Most selections simply end with “your response has been registered, goodbye” before hanging up. I’m relatively young and tech-literate, yet I still can’t navigate this awful system. It’s hard to imagine how elderly patients, people with special needs, or anyone unfamiliar with technology could manage it. This setup is actively hindering patient care. The surgery urgently needs to scrap this system and find an alternative that allows patients to reach reception easily. Especially for urgent or sensitive matters!

recent_reviews.author: Matt Nash
recent_reviews.text: Kingswood Surgery has been a superb GPs for me and my family over the years. We rarely have to wait long for appointments and they seem to have really thought through their scheduling system. On one occasion I was called within 40 mins to discuss the issue I had as - unbeknownst to me - depending on the type I had it was either a minor inconvenience or a potentially fatal development and they called quick as a result. When we compare stories to friends and colleagues in London it becomes apparent the stark contrast in quality and availability of Kingswood GPs versus what a lot of people have to face and deal with.

recent_reviews.author: Shahed Ahmed
recent_reviews.text: Been a patient here for around 40 years and I’ve never experienced behaviour like this before. The same receptionist (I believe her name is Shelly) has been rude and unprofessional on two occasions. The first time was when I brought my 91-year-old mother to the surgery and asked about home visits. My mother struggles to walk and it takes a lot of effort and stress to get her there, yet instead of just answering, the receptionist made condescending and unsolicited comments about it being “good” for her to get out, even speaking directly to her despite her being hard of hearing. Completely inappropriate and not her place. Today was worse. I arrived just before 8am to drop off a urine sample, saw people entering and the shutter open, so I politely asked if I could hand it in. She responded by shouting “we open at 8am!” at me — twice — in an aggressive tone. No one should be spoken to like that, especially in a healthcare setting. Very disappointing.

recent_reviews.author: Charis Leath
recent_reviews.text: Meadowell clinic continues to get worse. You can't book an appointment except at 9 AM or 3:30 PM, and the lines are immediately swamped by everyone else trying to book an appointment so you end up stuck on the line forever. If you try calling outside those times to make a non-urgent appointment you're left in a queue on a phone line that's not open, and nothing tells you that. It's difficult to book in non-urgent appointments that don't require immediate attendance (e.g. tests); good luck getting an appointment after you've been stuck on hold forever. There's no online booking system. You can't book in person; the receptionist refuses to help, says you have to call back at the set times, she can't do anything outside those times, and essentially tells you to like it or lump it. Using this surgery feels more and more like a waste of time. A shame given their purpose is specifically to help vulnerable service users.

recent_reviews.author: Denise Preston
recent_reviews.text: The Doctors and all of the staff at Terrington Surgery truly are remarkable and I simply cannot praise them enough. During the past, very tough couple of years due to the pandemic, I have never once found it difficult to obtain prompt medical advice, either by a same day telephone call with a doctor or by way of a face to face appointment with a doctor or nurse, I have also always found that ordering repeat prescriptions to be easy by way of ordering online or over the telephone. Whenever I have had cause to visit the surgery I have noticed the staff to be practically 'rushed off their feet' but they have always found the time to speak to me about my needs in a friendly, polite and professional manner and have always dealt with my medical problems very thoroughly and on a couple of occasions have gone above and beyond to ensure that I have received the prompt medical help that I needed at the time. I feel extremely lucky to be a patient of Terrington Surgery, many of my family and friends, who are registered with other practices in the Ryedale area, do not have the same excellent medical care which I receive, many of them are having to wait more than two weeks for a face to face appointment or a telephone call from their Doctor including my 80 year old mum who has several complex and painful medical conditions. I would like to say a very big thank you to every single one of the staff at Terrington Surgery and please please keep up your excellent work!

recent_reviews.author: James
recent_reviews.text: No change as of 2026......infact progressively worse. The receptionists at this practice are rude and make you feel like you are an inconvenience to their day. Poor communication and Appallingly managed. This has been like this long before covid came into our lives. 3 particular female receptionists are so dismissive and condescending that it really makes trying to get medical help stressful and occasionally makes you think twice about calling and having to face the Gestapo at reception..the practice manager is clearly an incompetent or else they are just as uncaring as the people they allow to work at the reception. It is disgusting that these women are allowed to conduct themselves in such a manner blatently abusing patients basic right to being treated with common courtesy and decency. They obviously believe they are above reproach, which is rather fool hardy considering each person they condescend and treat like a sub human inconvenience is only too well aware of exactly who they are. Each one of those ladies and especially the practice manager for allowing this conduct to go on for so long, should be investigated and removed. Looking at other reviews and knowing of actual complaints from family and friends on this very issue that have gone in make it very clear that there are serious mismanagement and staffing issues within that once great health centre. Sadly now it seems they are perfectly happy to allow these women at reception to treat sick and in need vulnerable people with disrespect and contempt. I for one have put a formal complaint into the scottish health board and will be taking matter as far as i have to , even if it involves the newspapers to have those receptionists and especially the practice manager, held accountable and hopefully removed from post for the consistant ongoing Appalling treatment patients are recieving . I have even had to change my name for this review in fear of spiteful repercussions from those receptionists as i have had such Appalling treatment from them in the past. The GPS present at this practice are not much better sadly, they too are dismissive, unsympathetic and have on numerous occasions failed to follow through on even the basic of communications. They seem reluctant to follow up or treat your concerns appropriately choosing to obsticate or deflect from doing any thorough investigation treating every prolonged ongoing illness as the patient over exaggerating. Not all but a good number of the GPS there are apathetic and uninterested past a quick Google search of your symptoms. They do not treat any ailment or need for medical assistance with any sense of urgency regardless of symptoms. There seems to be a general contempt towards patients. This has been experienced by more than just myself. I could name the main culprits on the practioner team but if you've attended this surgery you will be fully aware of who they are. It's long past time the health board acted on the numerous complaints about the running and conduct of this centre before they are the direct cause of serious health repercussions for a patient that could be easily be avoided with care, compassion, motivation and professionalism. Thankfully the nurse team at taybank are the light in the darkness there. The nurses are highly professional, approachable & caring. Sadly the rest of the staff at the practice are abhorrent

recent_reviews.author: Anne Williams
recent_reviews.text: The repeat prescription set up is an absolute joke! My husband has been on medication long term ie since the 1990’s therefore I believe I know what I am talking about. Anyway apart from the fact that in April 2024 he was hospitalized for a month and then had to attend hospital daily for 6 weeks to enable him to get intravenous medication, and even after that spent another few months on various medication until he was pretty much fully recovered. It is now very important to me that he gets his medication on time! Fair comment I’d expect but I have in the last 18 months especially (or maybe I’ve only noticed due to the severity of his latest illness) noticed that the system does not work! Used to be I ordered them on my phone ( his meds) repeatedly this did not work, I have for maybe 6 months now had to revert to “old school” and write on a chatty what is required and yet again I have lost count of the amount of times the script does not reach the chemist! To add insult to injury..I complained and then basically because I did I was threatened with being excluded from the practice! Okay I was a bit upset at the time but I did NOT shout at the receptionist nor did I behave in.a threatening manner! I explained in no uncertain terms that I am not happy about being mucked about 1 I do not have the time and 2 I do not want to see my husband that I’ll ever again, during the first week they were not sure he would survive and all this is down to not very good medical practice in the first place as in someone who is allegedly medically qualified should have realised that the diclofenac they put him on should have been stopped and not allowed to burn a hole in his colon and therefore allow bacteria to seep through to his peritoneal and allow 4 abcesses to grow and nearly kill him. To say I am not impressed is an understatement I am still awaiting a reply to my letter which was sent in before the end of November and yet it is still happening, no prescription- not ordered this is twice this week alone and I can assure you they were ordered. Does anyone have any suggestions on how to get prescribed medicine or should I consult a solicitor on what I have just realised might be a malpractice case?

recent_reviews.author: liam David Innes-Devlín
recent_reviews.text: DR riddle should be assessed to practice I am writing this review to express my dissatisfaction with one of the doctors at the Whins Medical Practice Alloa, Dr Graham Riddle. I have end stage renal failure and I have lost eight members of my immediate family in recent years. I called the practice today and received a call back from Dr Riddle, who was very rude and dismissive of my concerns. He made me feel like my reason to call was not worth his time. He asked me some questions that I felt were irrelevant and insensitive. When I tried to explain how I was feeling, he interrupted me and said that he understood, but the deaths did not impact my daily life. I told him that this was not helpful and that it actually made me feel worse. He said that I had misinterpreted what he meant, but he did not apologize or clarify. He also asked me three times what I wanted him to do, as if I was bothering him. I felt that he had no compassion or understanding for my situation. He also showed no interest in my health issues or how they affected me. I have heard from friends and family that they also do not want to see Dr Riddle as their GP, because he is arrogant and condescending. He acts like he is above his patients and twists their words to suit his excuses. I am a long-standing patient with many health issues and I now feel like I do not want to ask for any support from this practice. Dr Green at the Whins Medical Practice seems to be the only one who cares for his patients and is an asset to the practice. Dr Riddle, on the other hand, should not be allowed to practice medicine. I will be taking this matter further, as this is not the first time that I have had a bad experience with him. I think the Whins Medical Practice and the Scottish Health Board should consider assessing his competence and professionalism.

recent_reviews.author: Galaxy Plant
recent_reviews.text: Throughout my time in various Scottish locations, I've had the privilege of encountering consistently positive experiences with medical practices—until I interacted with the reception staff at Whinns Medical Practice. My numerous phone calls to the practice have been met with an unwelcoming attitude that is both rude and dismissive, raising questions about whether this is a result of insufficient training in customer service or an unfortunate hiring decision. The receptionists display a confrontational approach, aggressively questioning the necessity of speaking with a doctor and showing little patience for inquiries. Additionally, I had an experience where a staff member abruptly hung up on me, simply because I was uncertain about the parking situation, as I am new to the area. Despite these concerns, it's only fair to note that the medical professionals—nurses and doctors—I've consulted with at this practice have been nothing short of polite and helpful. However, due to the frontline reception staff significantly impacting the overall experience, I feel compelled to give this review a one-star rating.

Felt like being dragged in to another horror film. They told me over the phone: - People (other customers) are dying and no-one has time to solve my back pain issues. Disorganised, misleading, unprofessional

recent_reviews.author: Google User
recent_reviews.text: Very sorry to have to write this, but this practice is the worst experience I've had from GP's. I'm still do not know what my ongoing illness is, it's almost impossible to get an appointment and if it was possible to get one, the thought of having to visit this practice again leaves one feeling more unwell. As mentioned by some previous reviews, unfortunately the GP's can make you feel like you are wasting their time. The standard response from the the 3 GP's I've seen over the last 3 years is to stay in bed and rest. No blood test suggested, no other care possible it would seem, just stay in bed. The only way I've had any engagement was after I wrote to the practice manager. I got an appointment but was then unable to to get a follow up appointment, they were simply not taking any appointments at that point. It was post lockdown so in theory at least this should have been possible. I do not know where I'm going to go to try to get some medical support but I have no wish to return to this practice as I will feel more unwell when I leave. On a more positive note, the nurses at this practice have always been very helpful, friendly and professional.

THIS STILL HASN'T BEEN SORTED the lack of the right communication and the wrong information given is high ,at the end of the day we are just numbers and targets . To say my anxiety is high at the moment is a understatement

recent_reviews.author: Will
recent_reviews.text: Avoid this practice at all costs. They changed my long-standing asthma prescription without explanation, charged me for medication I did not receive, and completely ignored multiple attempts to resolve it. I have had asthma for 25 years and have always been on repeat prescriptions for my inhalers, paying for two of each as prescribed. After moving to Cotham last year, I registered with The Family Practice. Without any explanation or consultation, they reduced my blue inhaler to one while still charging me for two. This change has caused ongoing problems with managing my asthma. The prescription charge itself has not changed, so there is no justification for reducing the quantity supplied. I have emailed the practice three times and raised the issue twice via the NHS app. I have received zero response. Despite this, I continue to be charged for medication I am not being given. This is completely unacceptable. Ignoring a patient, mishandling repeat prescriptions for a long-term condition, and charging for medication not supplied feels dishonest and exploitative. Making money from someone’s chronic illness while refusing to engage is, frankly, disgusting. I would strongly advise others to think very carefully before registering here.

recent_reviews.author: Emese Eke
recent_reviews.text: ⭐☆☆☆☆ – Extremely Disappointed with Dr Jagdip Haer and Cornford House Surgery I have been a patient at Cornford House Surgery for over five years, and sadly, I feel compelled to write this review due to the consistently poor treatment I have received — particularly from Dr Jagdip Haer. On multiple occasions, Dr Haer has spoken to me in an extremely rude and dismissive manner. The most recent incident was especially distressing: I was in severe pain, literally crying out and asking for help, yet his tone was cold, unkind, and lacking all empathy. I honestly cannot understand how a medical professional can behave this way towards someone who is clearly suffering. As a foreigner who has lived and worked in the UK for 20 years, I strongly suspect that part of the disrespect I’ve received may be due to my background. If that is the case, it is completely unacceptable. Every patient deserves to be treated with dignity, compassion, and professionalism — regardless of nationality. Overall, this GP practice has repeatedly let me down. The lack of care, basic humanity, and respect is shocking. If I could give zero stars, I would. I urge the staff — especially the doctors — to reflect on how they speak to people, and to treat all patients equally. I do not recommend this surgery to anyone seeking kind or respectful healthcare.

recent_reviews.author: Amit Lodhia
recent_reviews.text: I wrote this review a few years ago, and it is based on my experience here when I was a patient. I hope they've improved for the sake of the patients, but who knows. The surgery used to be one of the best, but their interest in patient care has lessened over the years, and especially since they've taken on the new appointment booking system. The number of times I would be on the phone from 8am in a queue and then by the time someone answered at 8.15 or 8.20, the appointments would be all booked, is far too many to count. When I did have an appointment, the doctors were barely interested in seeing me. I had one appointment where I was seen by a locum. He organised a full blood test and then I heard nothing after. I still had the issues and had to book another appointment when it again became too much for me. I had to send photos in, rather than actually being seen and more than 6 months later, I've still got the issues. In 2021, I had a blood test, which showed that my vitamin D was deficient. I wasn't told and it wasn't picked up in subsequent visits. I have just been through my past blood tests after being told by my new GP that I am deficient and seen that I was deficient back then too! I've recently moved to another surgery, they've noticed straight away that I'm deficient and immediately advised me of what to do. Looking up the symptoms, I have been suffering from Vit D deficiency for the last few years! Why was this not picked up in the blood test in 2021? Another time, a doctor advised me during a visit that if a patient has a cough for more than 3 weeks, they need to be seen. My wife had filled in the online form a few weeks before this and explained she had had a cough for more than 3 weeks. She received a text message to say it wasn't deemed urgent and wouldn't be seen! I said this to the doctor and he apologised and said to try again?! There have been more incidents where they weren't interested in patient care but I haven't got the space to write it now, but they really need to have an audit. My mother needed to be urgently referred to Addenbrookes for further support, it took about 6 months for the referral to be sent!! One day, she was having a very bad episode, so I called and asked what the situation was with the referral (after about 2 months) and for her to be seen, I was spoken to in a way that they seemed offended that I was asking for help for my mother! Several times, it was found that a doctor had seen my mother, said they were referring her and nothing had been done about it!! As I said, this surgery needs to be audited and checked. They seem more intent on turning patients away and less interested in helping them, even after seeing them (if they're lucky enough to actually be seen)! I have now been diagnosed with arthritis and my current surgery sent the referral to the hospital within a couple of days! So it really is disgusting that it took Firs House nearly six months to send my mother's referral to an already busy clinic!!!

recent_reviews.author: Ny Warmington
recent_reviews.text: The doctors at this practice are excellent — particularly Dr McCrea and Dr Collins, who demonstrated professionalism, empathy and an extremely thorough approach during what was a difficult diagnostic process. Unfortunately, the administrative side of the practice is deeply problematic. Booking an appointment is unnecessarily difficult, and the reception experience is often chaotic and confrontational. During one visit I witnessed a red haired male employee openly shouting “I’m only doing my job” at the receptionist. I stepped away from the chaos, only to be later confronted outside on the pavement by the same red haired male member of the administrative team in a way that felt entirely inappropriate and unprofessional. I had removed myself from the ensuing chaos. Despite following the eConsult process and the advice given to me by hospital doctors & consultants after an A&E visit, I repeatedly received unsolicited and contradictory medical advice from receptionist who was not familiar with my medical history. This was frustrating and concerning, particularly given that it contradicted guidance from hospital doctors. I struggled to stand or walk, due to chronic back pain. Yet the receptionist advised I could travel to hospitals in Kent or Redhill for medical care. The clinical care here is strong, but the behaviour and omnipotent presentation by the receptionist significantly undermine patient confidence in the practice. I was specifically advised to monitor my blood twice, daily by doctors at Croydon University Hospital. Yet the attached photo is the unsolicited contradictory advice given by receptionist. A omnipotent paramedic working as a receptionist does not have more authority than actually qualified doctors? This repeated abysmal behaviour constitutes medical negligence.
