recent_reviews.author: Hani Soltani
recent_reviews.text: My experience with this GP has been extremely disappointing. My older son suffered for a long time with recurring ear and throat infections. Every single time I brought him here, I was told everything was “normal” and no further action was needed. No proper investigation, no referral to a specialist. Eventually, I took him to a private doctor, where it was confirmed that his tonsils and adenoids needed surgery, and both ears were affected due to repeated infections. His hearing was already at risk. This could have been prevented with earlier diagnosis and referral. Now my younger son is showing exactly the same symptoms. I have taken him to this GP more than ten times. Each visit results in a different opinion one doctor says asthma, another says allergies, another says it’s viral. Still no clear diagnosis, no proper tests, and no specialist referral. It feels like under the NHS system, as long as a child is breathing, everything is considered “normal.” This level of inconsistency and lack of concern is unacceptable. I would not recommend this GP practice to any parent who is serious about their child’s health.

recent_reviews.text: This GP Surgery is getting worse. Not only can you not get a GP appointment if you are unwell, it seems now that you are not even able to order a repeat prescription with the Receptionist's now. I tried this morning to order a repeat prescription and I was told that I have to order this directly with the Pharmacy now. My concern is that if you have ongoing health problems and you are not even able to get an appointment to see a Doctor anymore just how unwell do you have to be to be able to get an appointment? This Surgery is absolutely useless and seems to be getting worse by the day. It maybe masquerading as a GP Surgery in bricks and mortar only. I don't see the point of this GP Surgery even being open anymore because you cannot get the help that you need. I was very unwell a couple of years ago and despite calling this GP Surgery I was told to go to A&E, I went to St Helier A&E three times without getting any better. It was only because of a Receptionist called Pauline that I was able to get an appointment a month after becoming ill. Thank you very much Pauline, you are the only Receptionist that helped me when I was unwell, all the other Receptionist's were useless. I hope the GP Manager reads this email and takes on board what I have said in this message and that moving forward changes are made to improve the GP appointment system. What will it take before this appointment system is changed someone dying. Whatever happened to patient care? There is no patient care at this Surgery!!!!

recent_reviews.author: Meredith P
recent_reviews.text: Cricket Green Medical Practice is genuinely one of the best GP surgeries around. They are consistently able to help me in a timely manner, which is crucial for managing my family's health. The doctors are fantastic—they are attentive and take the time to actively listen to my concerns regarding both myself and my children. The care provided is always high quality. The reception staff are the unsung heroes here, regularly going above and beyond when they can. They were able to sort out an urgent prescription in under an hour the day before a surgery, and they patiently guided me through my children’s multiple vaccine appointments without ever being condescending. The only time I've had any confusion was due to my own lack of understanding that the NHS has a rigid structure that the receptionists simply aren't able to change. I also want to praise their efficient online system. It's clearly necessary; if everyone called in, no one would be seen. The process takes less than five minutes, and I typically receive a call back to schedule an appointment in two hours or less. Overall, the practice offers a superior quality and quantity of doctors that is simply unmatched by other GPs in the Mitcham area, even those who operate with a traditional phone booking system. This is a top-tier medical practice.

recent_reviews.author: Dawn Haffner
recent_reviews.text: I am extremely disappointed by the standard of care my 92-year-old grandmother has received at this practice. Despite a BNP result of over 4000 and a hospital echocardiogram showing serious cardiac issues, no one from the surgery contacted us to explain the findings or arrange any follow-up. When we saw Dr Steve Allen to discuss the results, he told us “GPs don’t go through echocardiograms,” refused to explain the report, offered no reassurance, and didn’t carry out any observations or medication review. The consultation lasted 7 minutes and left my grandmother upset and humiliated. We only received an urgent referral because I personally chased the hospital directly — the GP hadn’t sent one, despite knowing the result. It was only after a hospital manager intervened that the referral was finally made. Dr Allen routinely declines phone consultations and instead sends vague, grammatically poor one-line text messages, even for serious clinical findings. One example was when a chest X-ray revealed fluid on my grandmother’s lungs — he sent a single text instead of calling or reviewing her in person. This kind of communication is completely inappropriate and shows a lack of care or urgency. Confidential results were also sent to my personal email without consent, and we received a fit note text for an unrelated patient — clear administrative failings. Reception staff have behaved unprofessionally on several occasions. I have a recording of two staff members speaking rudely about me after forgetting to hang up the phone. We also received a vague text on a Sunday evening about an appointment the next morning — no details, just a time. My grandmother woke early and got herself ready, only for us to arrive and be told by the receptionist it was a “reassurance call” she had booked herself — despite the results not even being back. It caused needless stress and upset. I submitted a detailed complaint weeks ago, which has been completely ignored. We’ve now moved my grandmother to a new GP practice, and I’m escalating this to the Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman and the GMC. If you’re caring for an elderly or vulnerable relative, I would strongly advise avoiding this surgery.

recent_reviews.author: ADTD TD
recent_reviews.text: If I could give zero stars, I would. I recently moved to Coventry and, like most people, registered myself and my family with the nearest GP surgery—Walsgrave Health Centre. The registration was done online, and the next day we were called in for what they described as a "check-up." To my shock, the so-called check was done by a receptionist—not a nurse or doctor. She stepped out of reception and took our blood pressure, height, and weight using one of those automated machines on the wall. With the machine fixed in place, you couldn’t even stretch your arm properly for an accurate blood pressure reading. I have hypertension and am on medication, yet my reading came out as 120/60—the same for all family. Clearly, this was inaccurate and not handled properly. The following day, I returned to sort out medication for myself and my mother, book a proper GP or nurse appointment for a medication review, and get blood tests done with forms I had from my previous surgery. I also had health concerns I wanted to discuss. Unfortunately, the receptionist was incredibly dismissive and rude, telling me, “Computer Says Noo!,” and that no appointments could be booked, just because we want to as a new patients. When another staff member stepped in, instead of helping, they told us, that with our demands we were no to be a long time patients at their surgery and asked us to leave NOW, instead trying to solve the issue and book an appointment. This has been an absolutely appalling first impression of healthcare in Coventry. It’s no surprise at all, this practice receives such poor reviews. I’m sharing this because sharing is caring, and I genuinely worry about the quality of care current and future patients might receive here. Avoid this surgery if you can.

recent_reviews.author: Bob Kelso
recent_reviews.text: Needs serious improvement. Some doctors are good, but the reception and process issues let this place down. The check-in PC has been broken for months, phone queues are often 20+ long, and the front-desk staff can be unhelpful or slow. There’s poor communication when delays happen, inconsistent sample handling, and random closures for training with little notice. Additionally, the online triage form frequently shuts off once they hit their daily quota, even a 111 doctor couldn’t get through on my behalf, saying the system wasn’t good enough. Even when it works, the wait can still be up to two weeks. It’s not the worst surgery ever, but the bar is way too low, and things could be much better with basic fixes.

You have to fill out their silly online form, then wait for their call. In one occasion we did the online form and they referred us to pharmacy. When the pharmacy called they referred us back to surgery. Then wait for their call again. If you miss the call they will send you back online. At the end they send you to emergency care because you missed their call. This is a circus not a surgery.

I can certainly understand the frustration you have from this experience. We are under a lot of pressure in general practice, and have to have processes to send patients to get the care that we believe is most appropriate, as quickly as possible. If the pharmacist, following assessment believes this must be referred back to the surgery, then we follow the process to get you seen. I of course understand that this may feel like being sent in circles, but is a part of our triage process, where our clinicians will send patients to what they believe is the most appropriate service based on the symptoms and information provided.

recent_reviews.author: Vincent Raimondo
recent_reviews.text: Just an update on my review, I rung up the surgery. I found out I was number 36 in the queue, so I pressed 1 for the option for them to call me back. After waiting over an hour I rung the surgery back, to find out I was still number 36 in the queue. Utterly appalling long gone are the days when you could rely on your GP service. Well I am just editing my review because now you have to do a appointment request online!!!!!!! I did put in all the details about a serious condition & instead of them getting back to me, saying yes you can have a appointment on such and Such. They have just fobed us off to A&E again putting more pressure on the NHS. GPs are a JOKE!!!!!!!! Well I've been here about a Yr now, and the receptionist are rude don't even say please, when they're asking for your name date of birth, or first line of address. Had an operation on my back, that left an open wound, the surgery was meant to dress it every day. However after the worst experience ever from a nurse, who barely done nothing for the wound, put a long dressing that came off within a matter of mins. So my wife had to do it, now my wife is away for a week, and the surgery won't understand that I'm having panic attacks about them putting a dressing on. Tried to explain that I'm now petrified to go back. They have not cared just said if you want to complain send an email!!! No patient care or understanding at all...... Put 1 Star as can't put 0. First few times had a great service, treated amazing. Had my yearly check up, and because of family health history, was advised to do blood test. It's been over 2 weeks, and still nothing, so I rung up todayto be given results, by the receptionist, not a doctor. Now no disrespect to the receptionist, but for something serious as a health problem I was expecting a qualified medical professional to inform me of the results.

Therefore, we do not contact patients if their results are normal, and instead ask that patients contact the surgery or use our online portal (SystmOnline) or the NHS app to retrieve test results. We do however contact patients if their test result is abnormal or requires follow up. We completely understand that it would be far more convenient if we could contact every patient about their test result, and we would love to do this if we had the capacity and staffing to do so. recent_reviews.author: Bahri Ozbek
recent_reviews.text: Why did you only prescribe one pack of Venlafaxine 75 last month? I previously used Cocodomol, which didn't work, and I don't want Cocodomol anymore. I didn't buy it from the pharmacy, and instead, I want morphine 60 mg and the transdermal patch 10 mg that I'm currently using. I brought 12 boxes of special medication from another country for my athlete's foot, including Itraconazole 100 mg. Normally, if you were a GP, you would have given me an appointment when I requested one, but you just wanted to sit back, relax, and make money, not wanting to be bothered. And I paid 145 pounds for these medications. My finances are already very bad; I couldn't shop this week and only ate cheese and yogurt because of your responsibility. And now you're sending me to my old GP for physical therapy. I'm afraid to go to GPs because of them. You're happy about that, aren't you? Now I've come and asked your employee to write my doctor's name and address on the form, and she told me not to. It's as if I don't have the authority; I asked her to save the world, of course she wouldn't. When I arrived, she was on her phone, busy with social media. Who am I, madam, that she should disturb her own comfort? It's a shame, a great shame. Is this how you manage the trust my government has given you? You go to a GP, you get a prescription, three days pass, five days pass, and it's not written. You go and ask, and not only do they not write the prescriptions, but they also humiliate sick people by shouting at them in front of other people. You request an appointment from a GP, I have a fungal infection on my feet, but they won't give it to you. To avoid disrupting their conversation, they say, "We'll send you a link, you can make an appointment there." We request an appointment, you send pictures on the NHS app, you send them on another app, but the app doesn't work, and what happens here? That fungal infection spreads throughout the patient's entire body. The reason is very simple: so that someone's conversation isn't disrupted, so that someone's social media activity isn't blocked. Shame on you! Go look in the mirror and ask yourselves, "What are we doing?" Although, God has taken away your sense of shame. Now you happily eat and have fun with the money the state gives you, which you don't deserve. Look, I told the hospital I have a cyst in my palate and I'm in pain, they sent me for emergency surgery. Five months will pass, I'll be entering the sixth month, and nobody cares. Because of the hospital's irresponsibility, I've already lost all my teeth on the upper right side, only two are left. They're waiting for me to lose all my teeth before they operate. Because of your responsibilities, I've forgotten how to smile, I've learned to hate myself and people. Are you happy now, you and Chesfarm Hospital, playing hand in hand?

recent_reviews.author: Alicia Kingsland
recent_reviews.text: Update 19 March 2026. I thought I should change my review from 1 star to 4 star. Since the implementation of their accurex system, this practice has done an incredible turn around in relation to its care and organisation. Same day response, helpful receptionists, no stray referrals, caring gp and nurses, who seem very thorough in their consultations. Face to face appointments where needed and telephone consults where not. They are definitely a practice I would recommend now. The only reason for keeping it at 4 star rather than 5, is that the majority of appointments (especially same day) are held at the hospital (Rolle) which is really really challenging to park at (or anywhere near). Also they use the pharmacy in the hospital for the pharmacy appointments which wasnt a good experience for my child. Disorganised. Chaotic. 3 weeks for a telephone consultation, longer for face to face. lengthy hold times on phone Dont do actions they say they will multiple times over, think they are so time pressed they don’t actually have time to read any clinical history or study other professionals clinic letters. Prescriptions written wrong multiple times (or sometimes not written at all!), many many phone calls to resolve - each time you have to hold 15 mins + for them to pick up the phone. No one takes ownership of problems or mistakes , you’re just added back to the pile and the process starts over again . Who knows where your personal information will be sent. Randomly referred one of my children to Torbay hospital although we live in Exmouth. Other child needed referral sent 3 times to rd and e for them to receive information. Receptionists are gatekeepers. They say they are not medically trained… Incredibly stressful, multiple times for multiple family members. Literally the worst possible service imaginable. Pick another gp practice. Anyone! We thought we had signed up to a local practice. Actually pretty much all appointments are by hospital where there is no parking whatsoever.

recent_reviews.author: Ella D
recent_reviews.text: I was extremely disappointed by the lack of empathy and professionalism displayed by the staff. A woman arrived in severe pain, to the point that she fainted and collapsed to the floor. Rather than showing concern or offering assistance, the receptionists exchanged inappropriate looks with one another and with me, as if expecting agreement with their reaction. Shockingly, instead of checking on her wellbeing, they chose to involve the police. When the doctor finally came out, he physically dragged the woman off the floor and forced her to sit down, despite her being visibly distressed and crying in pain. The treatment she received was not only lacking in compassion but was deeply dehumanising. The behaviour demonstrated by the staff showed a serious lack of respect, empathy, and basic patient care.They also fail to diagnose people correctly, and tell you too take paracetamol when your in excruciating pain no help given at all these people should not be getting paid so much money, they do nothing apart from sitting there and judging you.

recent_reviews.author: Krist
recent_reviews.text: Incredibly unprofessional, rude and neglectful surgery. If you can get to see a Doctor then they are not actually that bad in person but it is near impossible to get that far and on the phone they are so rude. Since moving to the Wilson they have become an exercise in frustration, I was caller number 2 for 48 minutes and when I finally got through the receptionist asked me very personal questions and I had to near beg to speak to a Doctor. When the Doctor finally called me back several hours later I was working and couldn't answer so had to go through the whole thing again, this time I was caller 18 in the que. Hence I called them during my break when I had the time to do so, then was told a GP would call me back 'whenever'. Did finally talk to a Doctor who was very off with me from the start (just said hello then we waited in silence for 10-15 seconds until I took the initiative and continued the conversation) and monosyllabic and just asked me the exact same questions I had already told the Receptionist and then prescribed antibiotics for no reason I can figure out (Research how GP's get cash incentives for every prescription they sign off and it'll suddenly make sense). Everything is on their terms, us Patients seem like an inconvenience to them. Been with them for years and used to be able to call and book an appointment in 10 minutes during my lunch break, now it's hit-or-miss to even get through to them same day. On top of this they have messed up my repeat prescription 3 times on the trot, it being registered as sent but the Pharmacist never recieves it. Cannot get contact details for the Practise Manager and the Secretary is never there, leave a message and then never hear back. Nice new Surgery yes, but unbelievably neglectful Practise just doing anything to boost their profit margins it seems at the expense of Patients' health, which is why they exist in the first place. We are all finding it hard nowadays in a post-covid, mad World and many professions are hit hard but to these prescious clowns it seems they have forgotten the importance of their chosen profession, we are not cash-cows for them and I have never known a financially poor GP. The Hippocratic Oath means nothing, they are a danger to their Patients.

recent_reviews.author: Purvi Kirticumar
recent_reviews.text: If I could 0 stars I would. I don't normally write reviews but after the amount of problems my family and I have encountered with this incompetent service I feel forced to leave one. My family have been patients with Eagle eye surgery (good service back then) for many years and then the surgery was merged and became GP pathfinder clinics and since then the service has been atrocious. It is impossible to get an appointment. You have to fill out an online questionnaire for EVERYTHING. They tell you they will contact you and then I've had no call back/contact! I've had to chase them up. (My sister is still waiting for a callback for a rash from 4 weeks ago!!!) - and no we should not have to chase up appointments all the time. They don't bother taking your availability into account (apparently we're all sitting at home twiddling our thumbs so can answer their callback phones at the drop of a hat). I've spoken to a pharmacist before for blood results and he told me to start iron tablets. I asked him a very specific question related to my medical history that needs to be checked to ensure I actually require them. (The GP has prescribed me iron tablets in the past by mistake for the same reason and then called me back to stop taking them). The pharmacist quite obviously had no clue what I was talking about but maintained I should start the tablets anyway (Clearly the question was out of his scope). On a separate all the doctors I have encountered at the Eagle eye surgery have been amazing! This purely seems to be a management issue in how the surgery is run and I could go on and on about the incompetency of this place.

recent_reviews.author: Kez B
recent_reviews.text: I’ve lived around the country and needed a lot of medical care over the years. I’ve almost always received excellent support from previous surgeries and have been very grateful for this support. I was encouraged by the good reviews for this practice, but sadly, my experience so far has been very disappointing. I have several chronic health conditions and am currently awaiting hospital appointments for some of them. As a new patient, I expected at least a basic health check or a review of my medical history, as this is standard practise at all surgeries in my experience, but this hasn’t been offered. It's been a very odd start at this surgery, and I've felt dismissed and unsupported. I was given one appointment at the walk-in centre but as I was new to the area, got lost as it's poorly signposted and in a very niche location. I arrived a few minutes late and the doctor refused to see me, and recorded that a hadn't turned up. I'd gone to great lengths to attend - even calling in for directions prior which obviously didn't help! I offered to wait until the end of surgery but they just refused. Since then, I've yet to secure an appointment for anything. The dismissive attitude seems to prevail throughout: for example, I’ve had a long-standing mild allergic asthma diagnosis for over 20 years. This has been managed as necessary without issue by numerous GP surgeries. However, for some unknown reason, on receipt of my notes this was dismissed as ‘just a bit of wheeze’ by a doctor who has neither seen me nor conducted any form of asthma review, and I was told this diagnosis could not be recognised by this surgery. I didn't diagnose it myself! If anything, my previous doctors have suggested that I don't seek enough support for this, rather than trivialising the condition in this way. I have tried to get an appointment but this appears to be an impossible task here. Every time I’ve contacted the surgery, I’ve been fobbed off, or requests are simply ignored. I feel like I still don't have a doctor. It's the worst experience I've ever had at any practice and I really don't understand how this surgery attracts so many positive reviews. Update: The response from the surgery asked me to contact them via the general admin and routine care form. I did this over a week ago and still haven't had a reply, which is why I left this review in the first place in the hope of receiving a response. Yet more 'fobbing off'! I've also emailed them via their feedback form and I haven't received a response to this message either. I'm so pleased for the patients who receive good care at this surgery, I'm just very disappointed that I'm not one of them. I am at a loss to understand what the disconnect is here.

recent_reviews.author: Andy Lloyd
recent_reviews.text: I had an absolutely terrible experience at this doctor's practice. There for I left the surgery around six months ago. Reception staff where inattentive and dismissive, arrogant and believed it was fare play to snigger, laugh and giggle to each other while I was on the phone. The reception staff are so trained in the medical field they apparently no more than the doctors even before an appointment due to super human body scanning skills while over the phone. This places Practice Manager is just beyond trying to reason with, who ignores the concerns of patients to save face with her abrupt reception colleagues. My mother died a year and a half ago from Septic Shock as she had Leukemia. My mother was fobbed off over and over again as this pathetic practice, well they would not request or carry out relevant tests each time my mother attended the practice, there for it was to late once it was diagnosed! (The doctor in question, well she no's who she is) who let my mother down as she called up over and over again' checking in' most likely worried about a lawsuit! It's a real shame her husband left the practice as he did his job properly. I had to argue for six months for a scan for my back after I landed in A&E with sever back pain and temporary paralysis. Turned out however, I had two Herniated Disks in my lower spine. My daughter had from what I can gather Flu A before Christmas. This left her with sever pain breathing in from her left side, she was also coughing up fluid. She attended an appointment and low and behold no scan or referral for any investigation (What a surprise) Go the walk in she was told for when needing a second appointment, despite the walk in not having the equipment to test for the problem at hand. They will not refer for investigation without a battle of wits, risking further and prolonged sickness or in my poor mothers case - Death! When I was finally seen during my time here, the doctors seemed rushed and uninterested in listening to my concerns complaining over appointment timeframes. The examination felt superficial, and I left with no clear answers or helpful advice. To make matters worse, I had difficulty getting my test results and had to follow up multiple times. Overall, this was one of the worst healthcare experiences I've ever had. I would strongly advise looking elsewhere for medical care.

recent_reviews.author: Ayla Dyett
recent_reviews.text: Since moving I have had a lovely experience with this surgery. All of the receptionists are kind and lovely. When I was really ill on one occasion, one of the receptionists went out of her way to go and get water to give to me in the waiting room. The doctors, nurses, and midwives are all so friendly as well. It’s such a nice feeling to feel supported, especially during pregnancy. My only feedback is to the surgery’s overall booking system. I had moved from a surgery in which you were able to book appointments via the NHS app. Both telephone and in-person. It really simplified the process and the system seemed to work really well despite the surgery being so busy. Here, if I request an appointment via the NHS app, it isn’t done like that and you are told to call in. This can be hard when you may be busy, with a newborn like myself, or if the surgery is closed on the only days you are free. I assume the centre joined the NHS app due to the national contractual obligations to have an online booking system but I only wish it was made more use of.

recent_reviews.text: Johnson Medical Practice is an absolute disgrace when it comes to communication and patient care. I have repeatedly called regarding an ongoing prescription query, and every single time I have spoken to a doctor or receptionist, I have received conflicting answers. The lack of consistency and professionalism is shocking—it’s as if they make it up as they go along. They do not make any effort to help their patients in any way, shape, or form. When I tried to book an appointment to get some clarity, they initially told me there was availability within two weeks. However, when I decided to take that appointment, they suddenly changed their story and claimed there were no appointments available at all. It’s beyond frustrating and completely unacceptable. I genuinely have no idea how this practice is still registered with the GMC. The whole operation is an absolute shambles, and it’s clear they are only interested in taking advantage of patients rather than providing any real care. Avoid this place if you actually value your health!

recent_reviews.author: Violet Sobacka
recent_reviews.text: I want to offer a different perspective to the one star reviews which often seem to be based on a single negative encounter. I have been with this surgery for just under 10 years and I predominantly get to see same clinician (Dr Umar who is an excellent doctor ⭐️) I work in healthcare myself and believe me when I say this I am incredibly particular when it comes to my own care. Over the years I have received a lot of support from the practice team for both minor and more significant health issues. I have been treated by APCs, GPs, physiotherapists, practice nurses, had my travel vaccinations here as well as various screening tests. You name it, I have probably experienced it. I have always found the care to be very good and competent. My prescriptions and admin requests are dealt with quickly, phone calls are answered. I can always get appointment when I need it, the triage process is reasonable and the reception staff have been helpful. The surgery also continues to make improvements in care and service delivery which is great to see.

recent_reviews.author: Serhat Atess
recent_reviews.text: Absolutely appalled by the treatment I received from this practice, particularly from Dr Swati Shukla. After years of being prescribed Tramadol, Naproxen, and Sertraline to manage my arthritis, chronic pain, and mental health conditions including OCD, depression, anxiety, and personality disorder, I had a single phone consultation with Dr Shukla — who I had never spoken to before — and was abruptly cut off, accused of being an addict without any medical assessment, and had my long-term medication stopped immediately with no tapering plan or review. I felt deeply discriminated against, stigmatised, and racially profiled. I had made it very clear that I was mentally unwell and vulnerable, and that routine is critical for my mental stability — yet I was treated with no compassion, no care, and no professional courtesy. Instead, I was judged and dismissed in a manner that has left me traumatised and more mentally unwell than before the call. Calling a vulnerable patient an “addict” without a proper review, and terminating care without warning or discussion, is not just unprofessional — it may breach NHS guidelines, GMC standards, and legal protections under the Equality Act 2010. I am in the process of filing formal complaints with the practice, NHS England, and the GMC. No one should ever be treated this way — especially when already struggling with long-term mental and physical health conditions

recent_reviews.author: Lyra Thompson
recent_reviews.text: If you need visa forms filled and are going to have to pay anyway, It might be more expensive, but just go private. I asked for an appointment about the visa form in early November. First, I got a telephone appointment where the conversation was pretty much the doctor telling me "Well, I don't know why they booked a telephone call this needs to be an in person appointment." And books me an in person appointment. I clarified that I needed it by January 1st, and she said that would be fine. Then, at my in person appointment the man prints off the referrals for what I need (he needed to call a woman in to help use the printer, and while she was trying to show him how he started weighing himself???). So the receptionist really helped me more than the doctor did. I also asked this doctor that he was sure it would be done by January 1st, and he said yes. But when I go to get my walk in X-ray, after a 2 hour wait, I'm told my referral isn't filled in properly and I have to go back to the doctor to get him to properly fill out my paperwork and return another day for my X-ray. So I do that, get my blood test, and after that, I ask for the appointment to finally get my paperwork signed that I took the tests. And they tell me the earliest available is the 22nd of January... Receptionists were nice and tried to help, but those doctors are useless.

recent_reviews.author: Precious Carol Sibanda
recent_reviews.text: Worse service I have ever experienced in my whole life.Told a paramedic does the same thing as a GP, went to see a paramedic with a obvious chest infection only to be told am ok just continue drinking fluids and taking paracetamol. In less than 24hrs I got more poorly and I was taken to hospital, GP then asks why was I not given antibiotics to begin with...so my condition worsened all because of wrong diagnosis...What does it really take to be seen by a GP in this practice or the practice is run by paramedics only??
recent_reviews.raw_card_text: Precious Carol Sibanda2 reviews11 months ago Worse service I have ever experienced in my whole life.Told a paramedic does the same thing as a GP, went to see a paramedic with a obvious chest infection only to be told am ok just continue drinking fluids and taking paracetamol. In less than 24hrs I got more poorly and I was taken to hospital, GP then asks why was I not given antibiotics to begin with...so my condition worsened all because of wrong diagnosis...What does it really take to be seen by a GP in this practice or the practice is run by paramedics only??Like Share Response from the owner 10 months agoThank you for your review. I am sorry you found your experience of care unsatisfactory. Primary care nationally has had to evolve over recent decades as there are nowhere near enough GPs to see all patients about all problems. We have a number of paramedics employed by the practice and PCN who are highly trained professionals. They work under the supervision of a GP. The receptionists work to a protocol as to which problems are suitable for the paramedics. This helps to free up appointments with the GPs to deal with more complex problems and management of chronic conditions. From your description you were appropriately assigned an appointment with a paramedic. We work to a policy of only prescribing antibiotics where clearly needed. This helps to prevent the development of antibiotic resistance. It is not uncommon for patients to be seen at a stage of illness where assessment does not indicate antibiotics are needed. In this situation patients are advised to seek medical attention should they get worse- which sounds like what happened in your case. If you are unhappy about the care you received I would encourage you to contact the practice directly with a view to making a complaint. This will allow us to thoroughly investigate what happened and make any changes necessary to improve patient’s experience of care in the future. Regards. Dr Alex van den Bos. GP partner

recent_reviews.author: Bethan Amber Bradshaw
recent_reviews.text: I had my first appointment with the practice today and was pleasantly surprised by the overall experience. I called at 8am and, despite a 20-minute wait on the phone, I was able to get a same-day appointment. I also submitted a request through their website, which the doctor mentioned was very helpful in preparing for the consultation. I saw Dr. Khan, and she was incredibly attentive and respectful. She listened carefully, didn’t dismiss any of my concerns, and approached everything with empathy and understanding. For the first time in a long while, I left a GP appointment feeling heard, supported, and optimistic. It’s one of the most positive experiences I’ve had with a GP, and I feel confident continuing my care with this practice.

recent_reviews.text: If GP practices were competing in the Olympics,Woodview Medical Centre would definitely take the gold medal!🥇 I can honestly say this is one of the best GP practices I’ve ever experienced in my life. From the moment you walk in, you feel like you’re in the hands of people who genuinely know what they’re doing—and actually care while doing it. The doctors are highly qualified, incredibly knowledgeable, and wonderfully patient. They listen carefully, explain things clearly, and treat you with respect. It’s the kind of place where you leave the consultation thinking, “Wow… that was actually a pleasant visit to a GP!” — which is something I never thought I’d say about a medical appointment. The staff deserve a special mention as well. They are extremely professional, organised, and always helpful, even when things are busy. Somehow they manage to keep everything running smoothly with calm efficiency and a friendly smile. In short: 1)Professional doctors 2)Well-trained and supportive staff 3) Excellent patient care 4)A practice that genuinely values people Woodview Medical Centre sets a high standard for what a GP practice should be.I’m extremely satisfied with the care and service I’ve received, and I’m truly grateful to the entire team. Highly recommended! 👏

recent_reviews.text: Used to be wonderful. Then the regular GPs left and patients weren't informed (only discovered when trying to book appt. with usual GP). So patients were left without continuity of care and practice failed to inform patients of this change. Very badly done. Replacement locums were brusque, patronising and dismissive, unable to cope with long term health matters. 2 locums failed to make a diagnosis of a common condition, and dismissed me without any treatment, because they couldn't be bothered to ask any proper investigative questions. Complete failure in duty of care.

They prescribed cream without even seeing a photo, it was wrong so that’s a waste of money. These are not hard things for them to do better, but they keep doing things badly.

recent_reviews.author: Debbie Cottrill
recent_reviews.text: Very disappointed with this practice. We moved from Lancaster where our doctor’s practice was very caring and helpful . I get the feeling if you join Garstang Medical Practice as a new patient that they don’t care as our neighbours have been with them for a while and seem to get better treatment. My husband has multiple medical problems and needs some advice but apparently the new online triage system wants one problem at a time . What if several symptoms are due to one problem though? He went with a list on his phone this week when had been asked to go for a “ health check”, thinking it would be with his GP but it was an NHS nurse from Lancaster who hadn’t even read his notes and wasn't prepared to help with any of his problems. She put the needle in him to take blood and it was only after it was spurting out that she asked was he on blood thinners! All she was interested in was does he eat fruit and veg., what is his waist size and does he run( he can hardly walk as gets short of breath, which was something he wanted to discuss). It disgusts me that patients are being so badly treated as I am a trained physio and would never have dismissed my patients in this way. When people are ill they want to be listened to and cared for, not put under more stress and give up. All my husband gets told is to go to A and E, which really isn’t the role of A and E. I have asked our MP about the problem but she seemed to concentrate on 4 good reviews for the practice. I give up too. What has happened to the NHS?

recent_reviews.author: P C
recent_reviews.text: Useless, obstructive and rude. Staying away on holiday, left a medication at home and needed an emergency prescription sending to a local pharmacy. Local pharmacist and local GP both pointed us in the right direction; simply to call our GP at home, ask for a prescription to be emailed or faxed to the local pharmacy. Called Garstang medical practice, twice, both times met with the same obstructive approach of "that's not what we do" and "we won't do that". Asked how we were meant to get otherwise vital meds apart from driving 5 hours home and were met with no response. After the uselessness of the local pharmacy, who lose your meds as often as they can find them (if they've actually got them in stock at all) and the ever deteriorating service at GMP, where you can't get an appointment unless you're a regular it seems, we've had enough and after being happy to leave us without meds that NEED to be taken every day, will be making formal complaints. Done with this practice, its terrible attitude and the general air of uselessness that seems to be accepted just because it's in Garstang and that there is no other choice. Having moved away from Garstang in August 2025, I'm ecstatic to be out of the 'care' (I use the word loosely) of GMP, albeit I have avoided them unless utterly necessary, when the experience has been as expected; awful, frustrating and depressing. Useless to the end, on a mission to outdo themselves in providing less each year and nothing short of a stress you don't need. Having heard the mantra 'everywhere is under strain' so many times, I'm now registered with another practice who are, apparently, terrible, yet they literally apologise because they take 48 hours (not working hours, or working days), just 48 hours to process and dispense a repeat prescription. Appointments with GP's and physios are available on request, it's actually a functional practice. Quite why GMP need a full week to get a repeat processed, using an electronic system and having a robot in the pharmacy beggars belief, let alone trying to get an appointment and/or referral. Having made multiple complaints over years, the attitude is unrepentant and their responses are standard customer service denial and/or doublespeak. This is not, in any way, a 'standard' medical practice, under the usual strains, it's a dysfunctional mess of a private business that has, bizarrely, only two full time GPs and 13 part time ones, earning an average of over £80k/yr. Bearing in mind your junior doctors (residents) in the NHS hospitals are on less than half that, this is utterly atrocious and isn't something that anyone accepts. One of the highlights of moving house is knowing that from now on, I don't have to deal with GMP any more.

Done with this practice, its terrible attitude and the general air of uselessness that seems to be accepted just because it's in Garstang and that there is no other choice. Having moved away from Garstang in August 2025, I'm ecstatic to be out of the 'care' (I use the word loosely) of GMP, albeit I have avoided them unless utterly necessary, when the experience has been as expected; awful, frustrating and depressing. Useless to the end, on a mission to outdo themselves in providing less each year and nothing short of a stress you don't need. Having heard the mantra 'everywhere is under strain' so many times, I'm now registered with another practice who are, apparently, terrible, yet they literally apologise because they take 48 hours (not working hours, or working days), just 48 hours to process and dispense a repeat prescription. Appointments with GP's and physios are available on request, it's actually a functional practice. Quite why GMP need a full week to get a repeat processed, using an electronic system and having a robot in the pharmacy beggars belief, let alone trying to get an appointment and/or referral. Having made multiple complaints over years, the attitude is unrepentant and their responses are standard customer service denial and/or doublespeak. This is not, in any way, a 'standard' medical practice, under the usual strains, it's a dysfunctional mess of a private business that has, bizarrely, only two full time GPs and 13 part time ones, earning an average of over £80k/yr. Bearing in mind your junior doctors (residents) in the NHS hospitals are on less than half that, this is utterly atrocious and isn't something that anyone accepts. One of the highlights of moving house is knowing that from now on, I don't have to deal with GMP any more.Like Share

recent_reviews.author: Leonard Allaway
recent_reviews.text: Dr Haroon at the Chatham Street Surgery in Reading has been brilliant at helping me with my health concerns. He is thorough and efficient, thus enabling me to cover a lot in each appointment. He got all the tests, diagnoses, and medicine that I needed quickly and efficiently, so I wasn't having to suffer any difficult Waits or anything like that. I also really like the complimentary approach he takes as well alongside traditional medicine. The surgery itself is also very efficient, and waiting times for my appointments and tests have always been within just a few days or maybe a week. There is an online Appointment Booking system on their web site, but I think it might only work during their opening hours. Good doctors often run a bit late, so you might find yourself having to wait in the waiting room for a while if your appointment is later in the day. At first this was a bit of a put off, but then I quickly figured that if I let a few of my To-Do outstanding tasks build up over the days leading up to my appointment, I can quite happily sit in the waiting room, carrying out these tasks to pass the time. There is usually plenty of seating available in the waiting area, but I would advise wearing a mask just in case. Back in last August 2024, Annalise at the reception was a great help in getting me started and registered at the surgery. She made me feel totally at ease, was very professional, and didn't make me feel under pressure in any way whatsoever. I was very happy with the conveniences that she explained, that makes contacting and booking easy and user-friendly. I was offered an introductory health check with the nurse, and was advised that I could have "a full MOT" if I discuss this with the doctor. It was also pleasant and reassuring when Annalise identified with me about the importance of proactive healthcare, to reduce future problems and less future burdens on the NHS.

recent_reviews.author: Agnieszka Sobon
recent_reviews.text: I want to share my personal experience at Chineham Medical Practice in Basingstoke to help others make informed decisions about their care. Over the past years, my family and I have faced repeated difficulties in accessing safe and timely GP care. Critical events, including severe illness in my youngest daughter and my own chronic and autoimmune conditions, were not adequately monitored or followed up. Prescription issues and inaccuracies in medical records also caused additional challenges. Despite raising concerns directly with the practice, the problems persisted, leaving my family without continuity of care. This experience has caused significant stress and worry, and in some cases required emergency medical attention due to the lack of appropriate follow-up. I am sharing these facts so that other patients can be aware of potential challenges and take steps to ensure their care needs are met.

After insisting I needed sleeping pills, the doctor gave me a prescription for Promethazine. Last night I took one and was tossing and turning for 4 hours before I eventually feel asleep. I check on the internet and apparently this drug can paradoxically cause alertness and restlessness which is exactly what I experienced. I phone the duty doctor, tell her about this unpleasant side effect, asks for something that actually does the job and not the opposite, and she says they can't help. Make it make sense.Like Share

recent_reviews.text: Every time I or my family have a need to contact our local GP surgery - St Paul’s in Winchester the service is outstanding! I have been a patient here for 5 yrs now and can’t fault it. Very well done and thank you. Hilary Maurice and family

recent_reviews.author: Jessie Tsao
recent_reviews.text: I had a very disappointing experience with this surgery. I booked an online consultation last week and waited for a very long time today. It was already the afternoon and no one had called me. Later, I received a message from the doctor assuming that I no longer needed the telephone consultation because I also have a face-to-face appointment at 6pm. I replied immediately to explain that I still needed the telephone consultation, because I will be leaving the UK tomorrow and might not be able to get my medication after the 6pm appointment when most pharmacies are closed. After that, the doctor never replied. I called the surgery for help, but the receptionist kept saying they could not do anything. In the end, they simply hung up on me. The lack of communication, responsibility, and empathy was extremely disappointing. The attitude and efficiency of the service were far below what I expected. Honestly, without comparison, you really don’t realise how poor the medical service and attitude can be here.

recent_reviews.author: Scott Cowell
recent_reviews.text: If I could leave zero stars I would. I have been suffering with severe mental health for a while now and I've been trying to get a doctors appointment for as long as I can.... This means unfortunately though that I have better days than others. When I'm motivated I call up and I can never get an appointment. When I finally got through and managed to speak to someone, I only wanted to tell the doctor what the issue is because I've sat in this doctors surgery before and heard the receptionist talking to her colleague about patients. Don't want my personal information shouted out. So after I told the call handler 3 times that I did not want to share the information and ith her and only with the doctor. She became rude. So I simply told her that she's not a doctor, she is a receptionist/call hand ler... it's my personal information and I can choose to only speak to the doctor if I wish. She decided to blacklist me from the surgery for not wanting to tell her this information. Out data is protected under gdpr and I can tell who I want only and specifically if I wish. Over the recorded phone call I have requested a SAR (subject access request) of the call to take this further. If it isn't provided within 30 days the ICO are taking this further. Disgusting that a large percentage of our taxes go these doctors when they can't even get call handlers that understand there role in there job.

recent_reviews.author: Yvonne Hilton
recent_reviews.text: Since Covid this practice has gone down considerably in my opinion. Trying to get an appointment is harder than meeting the King. Your so called Health Care Professionals have a very uncaring attitude. They do not try to help at all. When asking for specific GPs the wait is generally 4 weeks or more, no emergency appointments which there used to be. Your receptionists don’t even offer appointments with an alternative GP. Ringing at 8 am in the morning is useless, by the time the phone is answered all appointments have gone. Once I was even told to go to a walk-in centre! Both myself & partner have terminal illnesses and only see a GP when necessary, but it is still virtually impossible to pre-book with anyone. According to recent information from the Government, we should be able to book appointments on-line but this surgery never has on-line appointments available with anyone on any date. Of all the times I have been in your waiting area over the last few years, there are rarely more than 2 or 3 other patients waiting to be seen, the number of waiting area chairs has been reduced by at least half. It’s as though you don’t want patients in the surgery at all. I’ve been with this surgery for almost 11years, it used to be somewhere I would recommend. No more. • Al Overview NHSH+4 The government has issued a mandatory instruction for all GP practices in England to offer online appointments. This change was implemented as a contractual requirement from October 1, 2025. • Key Requirements • Online Consultation Tools: GP surgeries are required to keep their online consultation tools open for the entire duration of core working hours (8am to 6:30pm, Monday to Friday). • Purpose: The tools should, at a minimum, allow patients to submit non-urgent appointment requests, medication queries, and administrative requests. • Choice: This online option is intended to complement, not replace, traditional methods of contact (phone and in-person visits), providing patients with more choice and convenience. • Goal: The aim of this instruction is to "end the 8am scramble" for appointments and ease pressure on phone lines, making it easier for patients to access care. • The change is part of a broader government plan to bring the NHS into the digital era, with nearly all GP practices (98.7%) now offering online access.

recent_reviews.text: The receptionists, staff and drs are always very pleasant and understanding. The communication system such as e consult really needs looking into, im pretty good with technology but it is so complicated to work through. All I wanted to do was to ask for guidance on getting a specific test done and was lead down a dead end each time, despite following the receptionists instructions (not their fault). The process for requesting medical appointments is relatively good but I really do worry for those people who cant deal with technology. The e consul usually opens at 8:30 and quite often by 8:50 it is closed due to high demand, can this not be open throughout the opening hours for non urgent requests? When having tests and referrals across the different services, surely all the documents should be linked to the patients portal. Ive had tests carried out at different hospitals and the results dont appear to get linked to my GP account.

recent_reviews.author: Krisztina Majerik
recent_reviews.text: Had a wonderful experience before with a nurse. Today that experience was shadowed by a phone experience with a receptionist who did nothing to help. I was asked by my doctor to not go call in till April to give time to the medication to work but a fit note was not provided. When I asked for one in January, that request was ignored, I asked for it again and got a message to book an appointment. I called in to explain that I was told this isn't necessary but was happy to do so with someone I have spoken with already. I mentioned that the link provided to book did not show the doctor I was hoping to see but the receptionist did not check if she could do this over the phone just said the link should work and indeed, she does have appointments available, still didn't book me I wonder why? I also mentioned that I don't want to see someone new as I knew this would trigger my anxiety but she just said they're all capable of conducting the appointment completely disregarding what I just told her. I had to repeat myself multiple times as to why I'm calling but still didn't manage to book an appointment. I was clearly a nuisance to her. Shame as I never had an issue with anyone there. You should consider retaining her as to what it means to people to deal with these situations if they suffer from anxiety and panic disorder.

recent_reviews.author: Sidra Saeedzada
recent_reviews.text: I’ve had several bad experiences with the reception staff at this GP practice. They are often rude and unhelpful when patients try to book appointments, showing little empathy or patience. There have also been repeated problems with prescriptions not being sent to pharmacies on time. On one occasion, I was told the pharmacy’s system was down, but this turned out not to be true — the prescription simply hadn’t been sent from the practice. This kind of dishonesty and lack of accountability is really disappointing. Communication from the practice is also very poor. Patients rarely get updates about their health or test results unless they keep calling back themselves. It shouldn’t take multiple phone calls just to get basic information. Overall, the standard of service and professionalism here needs serious improvement. Patients deserve to be treated with respect and to trust that their prescriptions and care are handled properly.

recent_reviews.text: UPDATE I have changed my rating from 4 stars to 5 stars. During the last 18 months, the surgery have been fantastic supporting me during my treatment. I can’t thank them enough. recent_reviews.author: Edyta
recent_reviews.text: I rarely write reviews, but I felt this one truly matters. This morning’s appointment with dr Constantinos Regas made me hopeful:) After years of struggling with complex symptoms and feeling unheard, I finally met a doctor who genuinely listened. From the very beginning, he approached my case with curiosity, respect, and an open mind — something that has been incredibly rare in my experience. What stood out most was not just his knowledge, but his ability to connect the dots. He took the time to understand the full picture, rather than focusing on isolated symptoms, and acknowledged links that others had previously dismissed. That level of insight and critical thinking made a huge difference to me. He treated me as a person, not just a case — and that alone restored a lot of my trust in the medical profession. It’s truly unfortunate that he is leaving the practice, as his combination of empathy, intelligence, and willingness to think beyond the obvious is something every patient deserves. I am incredibly grateful to have been under his care, even for a short time.

recent_reviews.author: Анастасия Горбач
recent_reviews.text: Today I had this situation — and it’s not the first time my GP can’t help me. I know I’m an immigrant, so maybe there’s no help for people like me — I get it. But sometimes it’s really hard to accept: I’m here alone with my ten-year-old child, and if something happens to me, no one will step in. Today my head was killing me. I called the GP, they said: “Sorry, no appointments — call tomorrow.” I told them: “My headache is really severe, I’m vomiting, I feel awful right now!” — and they said: “Go to the pharmacy, they’ll help.” So I went, got some pills — but they don’t work straight away. I took six — still hurting, I could barely walk to the pharmacy. I’m just hoping it eases up, because tomorrow I have work, I need to take my kid to school — so many things I won’t manage if it stays like this. To get properly checked out, I realise: I’ll only get real help back home, not here. And it’s terrifying — I came here to save my child’s life and mine, and now I have to go back to war. Then people will say: “Look, Ukrainians are returning — things must be fine there, safe.” But really, most of us go back just to survive. The pain was so bad I could hardly make it to the pharmacy. I need help now, not tomorrow. But I’m scared — what if it doesn’t get better? Thank you for attention.

recent_reviews.author: Kate Logan
recent_reviews.text: I've been a patient of Crewe Medical on and off for around 35 years, completely for the last 18, since the surgery was in one of the houses opposite Scotmid. My dad and daughters growing up were also patients there. There have obviously been big changes in all areas of the NHS during this time, 99%not fir the better, but this is no fault of the surgery itself. During those 35 years I can count maybe a dozen times when I've felt that things could've been handled better, not negligence, just handled better. And given that I'm speaking about 5 ppl I think that's incredible. My dad recently passed away due to terminal cancer. He refused hospice care and would not go into hospital, so it was pretty much the GP service that we were left with. The care and compassion shown to my dad and family by the Dr's, reception staff, nurses ( both practitioners and district) was second to none. Dr Cooney , more than once, visiting after surgery closes as my dad was unwell. Dr Scarlet writing a prescription, taking it to chemist herself, waiting on it being dispensed then taking it back to my dad as no family member was available, on her own time. Reception staff taking prescriptions over to chemist too, NOTHING was too much, with a special thanks in that respect to Shirley, Lianne and Neil who were incredible and a lifeline at times. Dr Lang, coming up to me asking after my dad when I was at a nurse appointment for myself, this is my experience of the surgery, a whole team of people who are both professional and compassionate. Dr Scarlet also took the time to call me after my dad passed away...... he could not have had better treatment had he been in the private sector. I understand that is not the norm, but not everyone is terminally ill and reliant almost solely on their GP, and I am trying to convey the care and compassion that was shown, to counteract the terrible reviews that have been left, some of which ( with all due respect) I struggle to comprehend , as in grammatically. I can obviously only speak from personal experience, but I would not go past Crewe Medical Centre if looking for a GP. I genuinely don't know what people expect from a GP surgery given the size of the population as opposed to the infrastructure that is in place. I've heard of ppl waiting weeks for an appointment elsewhere, it never happens here. Yes, we all get fed up of the "call at 8am fir an appointment", but if you are genuinely unwell then you will be seen that day , I've experienced it and have no complaints. As a side note, the GP is not there if you have a cold or wake up with a bit of a sore throat that morning, and I would hate to see the amount of appointments wasted for these matters that could be put to good use for people who are genuinely in need. Also the amount of appointments taken up by people with self inflicted health problems who moan the GP can't see them is bizarre. Stop blaming the GP and take some responsibility for your own health, that would probably free up even more appointments than the ones who go with a cold , or even worse , don't attend at all.

recent_reviews.text: If I could give no stars, I would. I'm at a loss for words about this surgery. If you are new to this area, I would look for an alternative surgery. This one is not fit for purpose and the Doctors are still in hiding as getting an appointment is impossible. I saw a nurse there once and she was lovely. I wish they would all treat their fellow humans with kindness and respect by taking a leaf out of the nurses book. Just recently i asked to see a Doctor due to sudden loss of vision and was told to see an optician, nothing like seeing a patient to ask if they have other symptoms, no just go to the optician. Quite a few Doctors do not want to know and it's a disgrace. I remember a time when they used to care. These days are gone..... especially with this surgery. recent_reviews.text: Sent for blood tests before a heart check up at the hospital. I spent 25 minutes scraping the snow off the car to get to towers for my blood test. I was told if i go up to the surgery now and get the doctor to put the test through again, they will still do my blood test today. Drove all the way to the surgery to be told no doctor can authorise this today. No apology given at the surgery. A doctor did call in the afternoon, again no apology. I now have to wait another 10 days to have these blood tests, cutting it very fine with my hospital visit. Furthermore, in September my Son enquired about the flu vaccine for me. They said they will be making phone calls in November. Never happened. Went back in November to be told they are fully booked until December. In December i was told they had "run out of vaccine" and to seek help at "local pharmacy". This place has become beyond a joke. They need investigating immediately. At 75 years old they wonder where the stress comes from. This is not the first time this has happened. Very disappointing.

recent_reviews.author: Karen Fleming
recent_reviews.text: I have been a patient at this practice for 16 years and I am so glad I am. I have been lucky and enjoyed good health up to about 4 years ago. I have been off work since September with severe arthritis pain due to bone on bone in knee and hip complicated by Spondylitis in my spine this was complicated by stress and anxiety due to a lot of external factors. Trilinks is a training practice so newly trained doctors come and go and it was Dr Mosabbeh who initially helped me when I first became ill. He arranged for urgent referral for my arthritis, counselling, sick notes etc and spent time talking with me to understand what was going on and to ensure I received the correct ongoing treatment....lovely man who I have no doubt will be an excellent GP. Since then I have received excellent support and help from the doctors and some of the reception/ practice team. Had a bit of a blip when my first operation was unexpectedly cancelled and I spent 2 weeks trying to get a new referral but once he knew what was going on, Dr Singhu soon sorted it out. My sincere thanks goes to everyone at the practice and all of the doctors there. It's always easy to criticise but Dr Singhu gives newly trained doctors the much needed opportunities to get general practice experience and he runs an excellent practice. They have been instrumental in my recovery to go back to work. I should imagine not many people know it's a training practice and the turnover of doctors can be annoying BUT my advice would be to be patient , make sure you explain exactly what your issue is and they will sort it.

She did not review my medical records or take the time to listen thoroughly. Instead, she dismissed my symptoms by saying, “Oh darling, you’ve had a very bad experience; you’re just panicking.” I found this extremely unprofessional and patronising. To put this into perspective, I have been hospitalised three times for the same infection: • Once for 30 days • Once for 10 days • And another time for 7 days Despite this serious medical history, she didn’t even order a basic blood test. Her only advice was to “take paracetamol and drink water.” The reception staff were polite and helpful, but I have nothing positive to say about the doctor. I will not be returning.

recent_reviews.author: Anne Hinchliffe
recent_reviews.text: I had been with my previous doctors in Leeds for almost 40 years. However, 4 years ago I moved to Bradford and even though I was still in the catchment area of my Leeds doctors, I was referred to the Bradford mental health services team and was advised I should change my doctors to one in the Bradford area. Reluctantly I did so. I needn’t have worried at all. What can I say about this practice?… Well, where do I start… - What a fabulous modern, clean, easily accessible practice. - What lovely staff. The receptionists I have spoken to, the doctors I have had telephone consultations with, the nurses I have had blood tests with… every single one of them has been fantastic, they listen to you and nothing is too much trouble. - I have made requests for repeat prescriptions and letters and they are done promptly. Far quicker than I could ever ask. My experience over the last few months at this surgery has been excellent and they are an absolute credit to the NHS. Thank you very much to every single one of you, you are making this very distressing time in my life far easier with your kindness and professionalism. I am forever grateful

recent_reviews.author: Kirsten Birkett
recent_reviews.text: Genuinely sick of this GP now. I’ve been suffering from all sorts of illnesses over the last year; liver problems, lung infections, you name it. Not once have I received proper care. I suffer from such urgent issues and the best they can give me is a phone call appointment a month after getting into contact with them about my issue. When I first moved to Bradford about a decade ago, this GP was amazing. Lovely staff, quick appointments, overall just really great and I felt well looked after. Now I’m seriously considering switching GPs so I’ll actually be taken seriously. Honestly, it feels like I’ve got ‘mug’ written across my forehead every time I try to speak to a member of staff here, especially the receptionists. The amount of times I’ve had to ring 111 to get an out of hours appointment because this GP never has availability for urgent issues is genuinely ridiculous. I shouldn’t have to be doing that. This morning, for example, I rang 111 because I’ve been suffering from all sorts of fevers, colds, chest infections since August and this GP basically dismissed me every time, saying “it’s that time of year for colds and flu”. It’s not normal at all for me to be sick this long!! I got some answers from a different doctor out of hours and they asked me to contact this GP to schedule a chest x-ray after being diagnosed with an upper respiratory tract infection, and the best they can do is a telephone appointment in a months time? Stupid. Absolutely horrific service.

recent_reviews.author: Mrs H
recent_reviews.text: I genuinely cannot recommend this practice enough. We have been patients for 20+ years and they've been there as our family has grown. recent_reviews.author: Annmarie Archer
recent_reviews.text: Dr Moore is one of the most condescending and dismissive doctors my family has unfortunately had to deal with, both in relation to my own care and my child’s. Incorrect and, at times, dangerously inaccurate information was recorded in my medical notes, by him, which later had to be formally corrected. This is particularly concerning given that I now have multiple formally diagnosed, complex health conditions after years of being dismissed and gaslit within the NHS. Despite these confirmed diagnoses, I am still treated as though my conditions are not real or not medically established. Out of three doctors we have encountered at this practice, only one, a male doctor who attends intermittently from London, has provided competent and respectful care for my daughter. The rest of our experiences have been extremely poor. One female doctor, I think named Dr Galan, told me that she had never heard of palpitations being associated with anaemia and suggested the symptoms were “in my head.” This is not only dismissive but factually incorrect. Palpitations are clearly listed as a common symptom of iron deficiency anaemia on the NHS website, in addition to being associated with several of my other diagnosed conditions. Even a receptionist at the practice was aware of this. Imagine being told it is in your head when the last time my Transferrin saturation was checked it was 7% and just before 4%. This is very low, and would account for many symptoms, no one needs a doctorate to figure that out. On multiple occasions, letters have been sent from A&E requesting follow-up or support, yet I have received no response. As a result, I am now managing aspects of my health independently simply to avoid further distress from interacting with this practice. I am actively hoping to move and no longer be registered here. I would not recommend this surgery to patients with complex or chronic health conditions who require informed, compassionate, and accurate medical care. These are just the main points.

recent_reviews.author: M VPI
recent_reviews.text: From the bottom of my heart, I want to express my deepest gratitude to the entire team at the surgery. After being unwell for over 10 days, I contacted the surgery during what I know is one of the most difficult and pressured times of the year for GP practices. From the very first moment, the reception team were absolutely exceptional. They listened to me with kindness, patience, and genuine care, making me feel heard and supported when I was feeling at my weakest. I had already been advised by a pharmacist and by NHS 111 to seek urgent GP advice, and the receptionists acted quickly and compassionately to ensure a doctor contacted me as soon as possible. Their calm reassurance and efficiency made an enormous difference and immediately gave me confidence that I was in safe hands. The doctor then asked me to attend the surgery, where I was thoroughly assessed and diagnosed with pneumonia. Thanks to their professionalism and prompt action, I was able to start antibiotics straight away, and I am now on the road to recovery. I truly believe that without the care, understanding, and swift response from this surgery, my condition could have been far worse. The kindness shown to me was not just medical care — it was genuine human care, and it meant more than words can express. Thank you for being there when I needed you most. I will always be deeply grateful for your support, compassion, and dedication.

recent_reviews.author: Alexandra Angela Mititely
recent_reviews.text: With a GP like this, we end up being afraid that something might happen to us, because we are not taken seriously at all! Today, my 2-year-old daughter was stung by a bee at nursery. Even though, thank God, she did not have an anaphylactic shock, her little hands were swollen and, as a mother, I was terrified. I rushed there quickly and waited more than 20 minutes in the hallway without even a nurse coming to see her… This is the level of professionalism of this GP, from A to Z. For 2 years I have constantly been facing their ignorance and lack of care – from receptionists who never have available appointments except for elderly patients ( friends of them ) or immigrants from the hotel, to doctors who respond with “I don’t know what it could be” when I tell them that my legs hurt and I suspect circulation problems. Tests? Just a dream… and if I do manage to get some tests done, I never even get the results. It’s a nightmare. I lived in London for 5 years before moving here, and even though it was very busy because of the large population, at least the staff there really cared and did their best. recent_reviews.text: Excellent medical centre! I have been with this practise for more years than I care to remember and have never had a bad experience from my GP, Dr Evans and any other doctor I have seen. My only upset has been that although I have been out of their area for the last 32 years, it is in the last fortnight that I have been asked to find another practice as I’m out of their area?! I spoke with Dr Evans who agreed many years ago that I could stay but I wouldn’t be able to have a home visit. I have never requested one because I was allowed to stay in a practice where I felt looked after so well as a patient. Would love to know why, after all this time I am being asked to leave? I am so upset by this because I have always been respected and looked after by gps, nurses and reception staff. It is with great sorrow that I am trying to find a practice that can come up to this standard, not an easy feat I’m afraid.

recent_reviews.author: Mitchell Olford
recent_reviews.text: I had a medical condition at the beginning of 2025,so I went on the Hamilton Practice weblink to book an appointment. The website was very user friendly and I managed to get an appointment to see a GP 3 days later. He referred me to Princess Alexander Hospital,and a week later I was examined. I then received a follow up phone call from the GP at the Hamilton Practice to ask a few questions on my condition which was under control.However several months later the medical condition had got worse,so again I made an appointment and received a phone conversation with a GP. I was again referred to the Princess Alexander Hospital, only to receive a letter stating the could on see me in January 2026. I was not happy with the length of time to wait. Contacted the Hamilton Practice to see if they could do anything to speed up my medical appointment. They managed to get referred to the Rivers Hospital under the NHS, and I am seeing a doctor in early September. All I can say is I am very happy and appreciate everything the Hamilton Practice has done over the last 8 months to help me

recent_reviews.author: Sonya Howarth
recent_reviews.text: This has taken me over a year to build the confidence to write this review but it still troubles me after my experience. I was deeply disappointed and hurt by my experience with Dr. Dosanj. I came to him after a crisis and was met with no understanding or sympathy. I eventually had to transfer to another clinic to get the support I needed. When I returned, I again felt unheard — I left the appointment in tears, and was told we were no longer in the area despite living just minutes away. Having known him since childhood, I was shocked by how different my experience with him was. I truly hope he can reconnect with his patients in a more compassionate way. I am now relieved to be with a new surgery where I feel listened to and treated with understanding and compassion.

recent_reviews.author: T S
recent_reviews.text: I just wanted to write a review as people always leave one to state the negatives but hardly the positives. I have been at this gp surgery for about 9 years and have always had a positive experience. The econsult is quick to complete and I have always had a call back within the stated time. My children are also registered here and the doctors have taken care each time they have been unwell and always offer to see them face to face to examine them properly. They had all their injections by Josephine who is amazing with the children and completed their vaccinations without any problems (they came out laughing). I recently had my cervical screening with Sandra and she was really friendly and professional and made me feel comfortable. I have never had a problem with appointments and the patient access app means I can look at everything on my file whenever I need to. Really don’t have anything negative to say. I wonder if those who have also had the same experience as me just haven’t left a review! Anyways I am more than happy with the surgery and defo wouldn’t want to change!
