recent_reviews.text: I appreciate your service, but I am very disappointed about receiving two PCNs. I was running late for my wife’s appointment, which is why I parked in the consultant’s parking aa consultant parking was empty. After the appointment, I went out on my own to move the car while my wife was waiting in the pharmacy. At that time, the warden had already taken pictures, but I arrived at the parking area immediately afterwards. Since the parking was full, I waited briefly in the ambulance bay, making sure not to cause an obstruction for other cars. However, the warden took another picture and issued me a second PCN. I believe this is unfair, as the warden could have simply warned me since he had already taken evidence the first time. We were not there casually; we were attending a medical appointment with a patient. I kindly ask you to review this situation, as receiving two fines under these circumstances does not feel resonable. Could you do something for the pcn.

recent_reviews.text: Update: The new online-only booking system is inefficient and dangerous. You're required to request medication, and its taken 4 DAYS to get a GP to approve it. recent_reviews.author: Veronica Ortega
recent_reviews.text: I’ve been registered at this surgery for several years, and my experience has been very mixed. About five years ago I had a very negative experience with a doctor who, in very dismissive terms, essentially blamed my symptoms on my weight. Later it turned out that the issue was actually a stomach bacteria, completely unrelated to my weight. That experience made me very anxious about booking appointments for quite a long time. Then in May 2024, when I found out I was pregnant, I called the reception because I genuinely didn’t know how the process worked. The person on the phone was quite hostile and simply told me to “check on Google” and choose where I wanted to give birth, saying I needed to do a self-referral myself. As a first-time pregnant woman asking for guidance, I found that response very unhelpful and quite discouraging. However, I want to be fair. During my pregnancy and afterwards, with my baby, I’ve had several interactions with the surgery and the experience has been very different. I don’t know if the management or staff have changed, but the attitude and care have improved significantly. The staff I’ve dealt with more recently have been helpful and kind, and overall the service now feels much more supportive. For that reason I’m giving four stars. The beginning of my experience was not good, but I do feel things have improved a lot and today I’m generally happy with the care provided.

recent_reviews.text: After reading the reviews seems like I was treated the same way as Simon and Paula. After Lakenheath pharmacy (great bunch of people and very helpful) not having my prescription in I was told to go to the doctors and explain my situation. Go there and explain, almost immediately I'm being spoken to in a rude, snotty tone by someone, believe her name was Hayley, bearing in mind this isn't the first time this person has spoken to me like that before, unfortunately I had a run in with this person last year after being spoken to in a rude manner but ignored it. Then to make matters worse she starts arguing with me bearing in mind they're the ones who haven't sorted my prescription out properly so it's their fault. She calls the manager over, who's looking at me in a puzzled/confused way like I'm the one in the wrong. Still explaining my point and her colleague (Hayley) next to her starts laughing and still arguing with me bearing in mind her manager is standing next to her, absolutely speechless, no words. I've dealt with some unpleasant/unprofessional people before but this takes it to another level. Manager says to me, "why didn't you collect your prescription earlier if you put it in weeks before hand" why? Because as explained, you're so incompetent I have to put it in a few weeks in advance so I know when I go collect it, it's definitely ready to collect, but lo and behold, no prescription to collect today. Appalling service from this surgery, and to add, trying to get an appointment to see an actual doctor is like trying to draw blood out of a stone, unless your arm is hanging off or you're on deaths bed you may as well go to hospital. numerous people are unhappy with Lakenheath surgery, just go on Facebook to see for yourselves. The only positive to this surgery is the receptionist, really kind and lovely lady who has been there years, she's a credit to your abysmal practice, as for the rest especially Hayley who has a chip on her shoulder, you need retraining in how to deal/speak to members of the public. Lakenheath surgery has never been great, but in the last few years they've really gone downhill unfortunately.

recent_reviews.author: Reiji Yamazaki
recent_reviews.text: It’s a shame there isn’t an option to give zero stars. In the past, Canbury Medical Centre lost my urine test sample and the issue was effectively brushed aside without any proper accountability. On another occasion, I asked reception to book two appointments because I needed two completely different issues examined. I was told that one appointment would be enough. However, when I saw the doctor on the day, I was told that two separate appointments were actually required, so I was only able to discuss one problem. To make matters worse, I am still dealing with muscle pain that I first raised with a doctor seven months ago, and it remains unresolved. My GP, Dr Manson, advised me to stop running, effectively restricting my daily activities. When the problem did not improve, I was told to “use this app to exercise that area”. However, the link I was given does not even include exercises for the affected area. When I asked Dr Manson whether there was a physiotherapist available, she finally started to take action, but by that point all that had happened was a significant waste of my time. Once I was referred to the physiotherapist, Ms Kemila, she quickly arranged the necessary tests. After the results came back, I tried to book a follow-up appointment, but the earliest available telephone consultation was more than two weeks away — despite the fact that the conversation would likely take less than a minute. Reception then told me to resubmit the online triage form and mark it as urgent. However, the result was exactly the same appointment date. This clinic is clearly not functioning properly. Mistakes of this kind can lead to delays in treatment and, in some cases, could potentially put patients’ health at risk.

recent_reviews.author: Richie Mills
recent_reviews.text: This practice is a continual let down in my honest opinion. Incredibly hard to get appointments, and when I do manage get one, I often end up with a doctor that just says "Well, I'm stumped about this...let me speak to another doctor and we'll call you back". I've been having an issue with my spine for over 2 or 3 years, and have jumped thru every hoop that's been held up in front of me to get them to take me seriously, and still getting nowhere. Today, I phoned in at 8am on the dot as i have a raging ear-infection, and I get told i will get a call back with an appointment. 4 hours later and I had heard nothing, so I called them back only to be told "well, there's no appointments today". If I hadn't called back, then i would've never known there were none! The receptionist was polite tho, but struggled to find my initial query from first thing this morning on their system, and bumped me on to the next day. On top of this, their telephone queuing system message is telling us how they are accepting new patients. I simply can't see how they can cope with any more. I'm kind of at my wit's end with them. I cannot recommend The Molebridge Practice.

recent_reviews.author: Shakir Hassan
recent_reviews.text: Medical staff are generally friendly and helpful and will try to get to the bottom of an issue whether it’s a follow up for prescriptions or a clerical error. However, some administrative staff and front desk personnel should consider a different career considering they take issue with simple questions asked and are immediately offended when asking follow up questions although they are quite literally customer facing most of the time. My information for some reason had gotten muddled up with another patients (major breach of data protection but we will park that for now) and I had essentially been deregistered from the GP practice without knowing. When I expressed my concern I was quickly told there’s nothing that can be done and to fill out a form (although I had already reregistered online I was told that’s irrelevant) and nothing more can be done - no apology nothing. I came back a few days later, form in hand and the lady at the front desk retold me what I already knew. When I tried to explain she abruptly told me to let her finish and once again repeated everything I already knew (hence why I had come back with a filled form). I was told once again that I had been deregistered and after saying that this is beyond me how do I get reregistered, she went off in a huff to who I assume is her manager and mumbled to her saying that “he doesn’t understand” haha. Any way the manager came over and was far more cordial and polite (perhaps she should be front of house instead) with my original online registration in hand (the same one I had been told wasn’t processed - shocker) and that my written form was the one that was redundant, all the while frustrated lady who said I don’t understand remained silent the whole time. Pretty poor management of patient information and even worse effort to rectify a situation that should never have happened. Although, and I stress the lady I ended up speaking to was lovely, very patient and actually resolved the issue within minutes.

recent_reviews.author: Stephen Mackley
recent_reviews.text: They do not take appointment bookings over the phone and instead require patients to use a system called Total Triage on their website. However, the website is cluttered, confusing, and lacks intuitive navigation. I spent around 15 minutes trying to find the booking system, as it is not clearly labelled. Rather than simply calling it “Book an appointment”, it is listed as “Total Triage”, which makes it unnecessarily difficult to locate. On every occasion I have tried to use it, the system has been unavailable, meaning I have had to call the receptionist anyway. This then involves waiting on the phone for a long time before getting through. My longest wait was 45 minutes. Additional note: I have just received a text message. "We have reached safe working limits today, so are no longer able to safely assess your request or able to offer you an appointment at this moment. If you feel you are unable to wait until appointments become available tomorrow morning, please attend a local Urgent Treatment Centre."

recent_reviews.author: Diane Giacomelli
recent_reviews.text: I have been registered with the Glebe practice for 4 years . I have had exceptional service. The reception team are always extremely helpful and knowledgeable, I’ve sadly witnessed patients becoming stressed and being rude to the front of house team and they have dealt with it professionally and with empathy. They are a friendly face and voice on the phone, understandably there are those who become frustrated at the time it takes for the phone calls to be dealt with but with the high levels of need they are doing their utmost to assist and prioritise appointments. The dispensary team, nurses and GP’s are also exceptional. Where necessary I have been referred to hospital, specialists and other health care providers. I have always been given follow up appointments and had notifications and calls for bloods and inoculations. This has been my experience from day one and I speak as I find. Thank you all at Glebe Surgery 10/10

recent_reviews.author: Ross Jennings
recent_reviews.text: Hope that the partners of this surgery are fully aware and happy about the predatory parking charges they are inflicting on people in a cost of living crisis. I visited Kippax for the first time to pick up a takeaway on a dark evening and found what I thought was a reasonable place to park - it was late after all and the building in front (unbeknownst to me, a doctors surgery was clearly shut). It just looked like a normal shared car park, and I was nipping into the coop facing as well the surgery so I thought nothing at all of it. Until I got a letter charging me £60 because apparently the doctors surgery is enforcing a 24 hour ban on parking in front of the surgery. I have read and understand the reasons for enforcing the rules during opening hours - but why after? Only to cause pain to innocent people like myself and others online. Remember- First, do no harm.

recent_reviews.author: Sarah Burton
recent_reviews.text: This is such an appalling surgery it's unbelievable if I could give it no stars I would. As someone who has been here a couple of times from a decent local surgery for blood tests it is very clear the whole place is totally mismanaged. The receptionists need better management and retraining for a start. It is ridiculous to have a queue of people waiting while all receptionists are on the telephone making people late for their appointments. Not everyone can sign in for their appointments on the electronic one if they aren't from practise, they should know this as they have blood tests for everyone. Everyone in the queue is agreeing how completely awful the practise is. My mother sadly is signed up here. She has been completely unable to get an appointment, they make it completely untenable for people. They probably kill off more people this way tbf. When my dad was poorly they made it difficult until consultants got involved when he had heart failure. While I was there 3 people came in and complained about something. As someone who is at a good surgery, this seems almost third world. I wouldn't sign up here unless you absolutely have to because once you do no other better local one will take you as you're in area.

recent_reviews.author: Francesca Reynolds
recent_reviews.text: I am extremely disappointed with the lack of care and support from Swan Practice during a critical time for my newborn. Following my planned C-section at Stoke Mandeville, my baby sustained a cut to her head. Hospital doctors specifically advised us to book an appointment with our GP to have this checked. This request was also formally sent to the practice in writing while we were still under hospital care. Despite this, the surgery refused to even discuss the issue until my baby was registered. Once registration was completed, I submitted an appointment request via the online triage system. Instead of being seen, I received a text message redirecting me back to the midwives and advising that the issue should be checked before discharge from their care. This directly contradicts the advice we were given by a hospital doctor, who was clear that our GP should assess the injury. The experience felt dismissive and uncaring, as though every effort was made to avoid seeing us at all. At a time when parents should be able to rely on their GP practice for basic care and reassurance, we were left feeling ignored and unsupported. If I could give no stars for a review I would.

recent_reviews.author: T J
recent_reviews.text: DO NOT RING FOR AN URGENT APPOINTMENT. I have a lot of respect for the NHS; we’re very lucky to have it. However, since the Swan Practice introduced this online booking system, it’s been an utterly useless GP service. On their website, it says to book an appointment, use the online form OR call (provides a number). Now, if you call, you’ll wait in a queue for 20-40 mins before someone picks up to tell you they cannot book appointments and you should use the online form! What a waste of time and money. The only thing they can do is fill in the form for you. They’ve completely removed the ability to urgently get an appointment. The online form is too long, possibly confusing for non-tech savvy people and not accessibility friendly. The practise’s website should say ‘Please fill in the online booking form or, if you have trouble completing it, or have other accessibility requirements, please ring the number and a staff member can do it for you. A couple of Docs are great and the staff are generally fine (if you ever physically get there), but bedside manner needs improving.

recent_reviews.author: Ae R
recent_reviews.text: I only can give 3 starts for the new AI system. The staff is absolutely brilliant but this AI system is a nightmare. Waste of money I would say whoever made profits to force onto GP practices or onto the NHS. Same day call back or to be seen by a person is gone through the window. Only got a text onto the day that is not definitely not good. Instead of making a quick call to agree on a day that works for everyone they make you call them and if you are having bad luck with wait in line for well over 45 minutes. I get it NHS is trying to save money but elderly who lives on their own with no family near by will struggle to get in touch for sure and with that when receptionist have to fill in the form for them takes time away from the lines for other phone calls for a form that still not provided an appointment a that stage. Waste of time. The previous online form was way better than this AI. Also no option on rejection of collection of cookies about your data. Whatever the reason I never share it. And don't feel comfortable on any level with AI getting involved when we try to reach out for medical help. When we need to talk to humans not robots. With no AI system this surgery could get 5 stars from me but unfortunately I don't have positive experiences with it. We can tell our government is hell bent on blead out all health services and this how it shows. Get an AI so you don't have to hire actual humans. This practice struggled with rent for so long and these wonderful people deserve to be recognised instead of replacing them with an AI system.

recent_reviews.author: A B
recent_reviews.text: I wanted to share our experience with Hilary Jones because she has been such a help to our family. My five year old son has had a really tough time with health issues and constant trips to the doctor, which left him feeling very scared of medical appointments. Hilary was so patient and kind from the very first moment. Instead of rushing through the appointment, she took the time to talk to him and build a real connection. It made a world of difference. While other visits have left him feeling like just another patient on a list, Hilary made him feel safe and comfortable. Seeing him go from being terrified to actually feeling happy to see a doctor is a huge weight off our shoulders. Hilary’s ability to listen and her genuine care have completely changed how he views his appointments. We are incredibly grateful for the way she looks after him.

recent_reviews.author: Sarah Djedovic
recent_reviews.text: Absolutely awful medical practice called them for an emergency prescription due to my asthma and the receptionist gave me the response of “what are we supposed to do about it” I had spoken to 111 and the confirmed that they would’ve been able to do so. A year later now and had another horrible experience furthermore it’s deeply concerning the lies that spew out of your responses to people online, who tells someone that they confirm you’ve misheard them??? Clearly did not listen to the phone call as it was said loud and clear but obviously trying to cover your back. Had an asthma review booked in not even three months later where the Dr (Shaikh) complained the entire 5 minutes claiming it wasn’t his job and that he doesn’t have the time to do it even though when making my appointment I made clear I needed an asthma review done also after getting a text message from the GP themselves claiming I needed one, to ensure I was seen by the correct medical staff whose job it is to do it ended up having to book another. Had another emergency appointment made initially I had called to ask for advice if it’s worth just going to the A&E they reassured me to come in. I did and the same Dr did not want to deal with my situation and told me to have just gone to the A&E. Not only wasted my time coming an hour in from work for 10 seconds but wasted an appointment for a patient that may have needed it more! To make matters worse all staff including the manager and Dr decided to have a meeting slandering my situation in the reception where I was sat and could hear as well as everyone else sat in there. Once called over no apology was made at all from their side for the mistake which they had mentioned was theirs as well as for the fact that I was staring at them the entire time they had this tea party for all to hear. Furthermore the Dr gave me zero time or input on what I should do to sort my situation out since he again didn’t want to do it and instead wrote into my medical record that I refused to go to the A&E which was not the case because not even 5 seconds after telling me to go he then tells me to just wait a week for symptoms to pass. His behaviour was erratic and he kept yelling. What makes matters worse is after speaking to the receptionist about this they had rolled their eyes and explained that this is a normal occurrence of a response from this particular doctor. Consistently have had an extremely bad experience with this GP don’t bother. Either unprofessional, lack of care or miserable.

recent_reviews.author: Calvin Mcintyre
recent_reviews.text: I have had an extremely frustrating experience with Abbey View Surgery. Calling reception is nearly impossible—either you can’t get through, or you’re on hold for ages. Because of this, I’ve often had to go to Spalding Walking-in Centre just to be seen. The doctors are dismissive and rarely listen, often just prescribing medication rather than addressing the underlying issue. After a car accident, my back was in severe pain, yet I couldn’t get an appointment for two weeks. When I asked the receptionist what I should do, she told me to go to A&E if it was that bad. When I finally saw a doctor, I was told an MRI scan would be booked. Checking the NHS app later, nothing was scheduled. I called reception to follow up; they said they’d call me back but never did. My pharmacy even contacted me to ask about coming off gabapentin, despite the surgery having made no effort to manage my back properly. Most recently, I had another issue with gabapentin, which was logged, yet the receptionist falsely told me the doctor said “MSK” instead of an MRI, which I clearly remember him stating. Overall, the surgery is disorganized, dismissive, and unhelpful. The repeated delays, lack of communication, and poor patient care have made this experience extremely stressful.

recent_reviews.author: s j
recent_reviews.text: These people are so unprofessional it's actually comical now. So what they are doing now is pushing patients to download the livi app, because obviously it benefits the creators and I dare say someone in the health centre probably gets a nice brown envelope. Despite filling out the triage and saying I wish to be called they want you to do a 'video' call, even though they know it's not necessary as it was in my case, they know you will have download the app to do it, it's basic stuff but they insist on insulting our intelligence. Anyway, I have refused this because you do not need to download apps and make other people rich to make a doctors appointment, just like you do not need to do a online 'triage' to make a appointment despite what they try and tell us, although sometimes its more pleasant then speaking to the rude receptionist as I find (by law you CAN make your appointment via phonecall, they will begrudgingly admit this if you ask) so upon calling them and saying you clearly didnt read my triage correctly and that I asked for contact to be made via a phoncall, not a video call which involves downloading a app, I was told the doctor deemed it necessary for my symptoms (overly tired, that needs a video call doesn't it lol, even the receptionist didnt think a video call was necessary for that when I asked her opinion) to have a video call (obviously nothing to do with having to download a app whatsoever) and that I will have to start making a second triage if I refused the livi video app call. And when I asked which doctor thinks I need a video consultation for my 'tired' symptoms I was told I dont think you need that information, to which I said I do, eventually she passed it on after probably remembering not to make the same mistake twice. So I make a second triage and insisting on receiving a phone call only 'please' what do they do? Yup you go it, they msg me and tell me to travel 10 miles for a blood test, and if I don't like it to call the surgery and wait one month for a blood test locally. Which is a odd time to wait since they are apparently sending everyone to plymouth, but hey they know the games they play and management knows it as well, essentially they are playing with people's lives, how long before someone passes away due to their 'morning attitudes' or maybe it's not how long maybe it's how many more...It's not as if they would tell any of us is it. Look at the reviews, they clearly have absolutely no interest in listening to the customers, and obviously they think we are all lying. The town councillors and local mp's need to take a long hard look at this place.

recent_reviews.author: Diana S
recent_reviews.text: Absolutely shocking! Absolutely disgraceful service. My partner's appointment was cancelled at the very last minute while he was already on the way to the practice. He had taken time out of his day, arranged everything around this appointment, booked holiday and wasted his time travelling for nothing. Instead of any genuine apology or consideration, he was simply told to “reschedule” as if patients have unlimited free time to fit around their poor organisation. This practice clearly has no respect for people who rely on them. The lack of professionalism and basic courtesy is shocking. Cancelling appointments is bad enough, but doing it when someone is literally on route and then dumping the inconvenience back on them is completely unacceptable. I expect far better from a healthcare provider. Sort out your scheduling and start treating patients with the respect they deserve. This is now the SECOND time this has happened to him, which shows it is not just “unforeseen circumstances” it is clearly terrible organisation and total disregard for patients’ time. The last time he attended, he wasn’t even seen by the person who was supposed to be dealing with his care. He was pushed onto someone else “due to unforeseen circumstances,” meaning he had to sit there and explain everything again to a different doctor who had no idea about his situation. That is not proper continuity of care, it’s lazy and unprofessional. He has been taking blood pressure readings and submitting tables as requested, yet they have basically left him hanging from last year until this year with medication that doesn’t even work. He was given two weeks’ worth of tablets that are clearly ineffective, and nobody here seems remotely interested in following up or changing them. It feels like they’ve just handed out medication to shut him up rather than actually treat him. No proper monitoring, no adjustments, and no sense that anyone cares whether the treatment is helping. I will be leaving this joke of a practice! Avoid AT ALL COSTS !

recent_reviews.author: emkay dee
recent_reviews.text: The practitioner took photos of a skin abnormality, and did some data entry about them. She absent-mindedly shone the instrument light directly into my eye for a sustained period while doing the data entry. When I asked what the light source was, she had no idea and only knew the name of the instrument. I looked it up and it is safe, but was surprised that they don’t understand the instruments they use here. Also regarding answers to the survey of the skin conditions, I have wrong answers sent to the dermatologist because of miscommunications. When I pointed this out, I was told “Well I already sent it” then “thanks, goodbye” Please, please protect yourself: remember when you are dealing with this group that they are not trained to the level of doctors, or equivalent European practitioners. They will get through patients as fast as possible and are not particularly interested in making sure things are done correctly - whether this is apathy or time-pressure is unclear, but you cannot expect professional service, and there must be a surprisingly low bar for training.

recent_reviews.author: Younis A
recent_reviews.text: On 02/09/25, I called the GP surgery to request a call back from a doctor. The receptionist told me that a doctor would call me. I waited until 4:00 pm, but no one contacted me. I called the surgery again, and the receptionist said that the GP was open until 6:00 pm and that I should just wait for the call. Unfortunately, no one ever called me back that day. The next day, I phoned again to ask what happened. The receptionist told me that “someone tried to call” but I didn’t pick up. When I asked what time this supposed call was made, she could not give me an answer. I explained that at 4:00 pm the previous day, I had already spoken with reception and was told to keep waiting, so clearly no attempt had been made. During this second call, the receptionist was very rude and dismissive. She asked, “Do you want to book today or not?” and avoided discussing what had gone wrong the day before. When I said yes, she immediately hung up the phone. I do not feel that this is acceptable service. Patients should not feel like they are a burden or that staff are trying to avoid them. Not all receptionists are rude, but the person who answered at 9:05 on 03/09/25 made me feel like I was not being listened to or treated with respect.

recent_reviews.author: A A
recent_reviews.text: As a patient of this surgery for over 15 years i want to share my experiences at Gaumount House Surgery. Unfortunately, I have repeatedly encountered issues that have left me extremely disappointed with the level of service provided. The reception staff have often come across as rude and unprofessional, showing very little customer-service awareness or compassion toward patients. On several occasions, I felt spoken to in an abrupt and unhelpful manner, which only added to the stress of trying to get medical support. I have also experienced long waiting that caused real inconvenience and left me feeling that patients’ time is not valued. Another ongoing issue is the difficulty reaching the practice by phone.There have been many times when calls go unanswered for long periods, even during working hours. This is especially frustrating when you need urgent guidance or when you can see that there appear to be several staff members present but still no response. I have also become increasingly concerned about the lack of diversity and representation within the practice. It often feels like the staff team does not reflect or understand the diverse community they serve, which affects communication and trust. This is not about anyone’s background individually, but about the importance of having a staff team that is inclusive, varied, and able to connect with all patients. Over the years, I have consistently experienced rude and dismissive behaviour from both reception staff and management, with very little empathy or willingness to help. This is not what patients should encounter when seeking medical support. Overall, these repeated experiences have made accessing care far more stressful than it should be. I hope the practice seriously reviews its customer-service standards, appointment-management processes, and communication with patients, as these issues are preventing people from receiving the support they need. The management team has also been disappointing, as their communication and attitude have felt similarly unprofessional. Rather than addressing concerns or offering solutions, interactions with management have often left me feeling unheard and disappointed. I regret not taking actions in the past and taken my complaint further maybe this service would be better now. If anyone is unhappy like me about the service at this GP surgery and would like a formal investigation to begin, you have the right to make an official complaint. You can send your concerns directly to the Practice Manager most problably is ignored or dismissed considering the unprofessional approach they have you can skip this and take it to those who would listen. Take it higher for an independent review, you can complain to your local NHS Integrated Care Board (ICB). They are responsible for overseeing GP services and can look into issues such as poor communication, unprofessional behaviour, appointment problems, or concerns about patient care. Care Quality Commission (CQC) – to report concerns if the response is not satisfactory, you can escalate your complaint to the Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman for further investigation.

recent_reviews.author: Boe Omunnawke
recent_reviews.text: My experience at Gaumont House Surgery has been mostly negative. On many occasions when you enter the reception waiting area the staff often do not acknowledge me at all, even when I was standing directly in front of them. Their attitude often came across as rude, and I felt they would benefit from retraining. I repeatedly felt a complete lack of empathy, and I often felt like I was being treated as just a number rather than a patient with genuine concerns. When speaking with clinicians on the phone, they regularly sounded rushed, as if they wanted to end the call as quickly as possible. This added to the sense that empathy and professionalism were lacking throughout most of the practice. For a long time, I hesitated to move to a different surgery because many reviews of other practices mentioned similar issues. However, I eventually found a new surgery where every member of the reception team has been polite (I have visited them a couple of times), respectful, and caring. For the first time in a long time, I feel properly listened to and not dismissed. I do want to make an exception for a few individuals at Gaumont House Surgery: Dr Mary, Andrew (the practice manager), and Remi (if I have her name correct). They have always treated me with courtesy and empathy, and they deserve recognition for that. They would receive five stars from me and if all members of the team followed their example I would not even be writing this review. But then fact that GHS has an overall rating of 2.3 speaks for itself (in comparison the surgery I’ve just joined has 4!). To be honest if I could give zero stars for GHS I would however in have to at LEAST check 1 star. I am now in the process of leaving this surgery!!! Lastly, for those who feel that they have to put with GHS please know that you don’t. Look for a surgery with staff that are all trained to deal with people in a polite, empathic and professional manner. There are still some out there!

recent_reviews.text: I have been registered with this GP surgery since August 2025, and from the moment you walk in, it feels welcoming and professional. Overall, the standard of care is very high, and the environment, staff, and overall patient experience have completely changed my expectations of what NHS care can and should be. recent_reviews.author: Stacey
recent_reviews.text: I’ve never written a review for a GP before, but I feel like I have to after my recent experience with this surgery. About a month ago, I called regarding some ongoing health issues, and they told me I’d get a telephone consultation at a specific time. I waited, but no one ever called. I ended up having to call the surgery myself for 3–4 days in a row just to chase up the appointment. Only after the fourth day did someone finally call me back. During that call, they said they’d booked me in for an ultrasound. I waited three weeks and still hadn’t received any letter, phone call, or text about an appointment, so I called the GP again. They told me to contact the hospital myself — which I did — and when I spoke to the hospital staff, they told me I wasn’t even booked in for a scan at all. Thankfully, one of the hospital staff kindly booked me in themselves, and I managed to get my scan done two days later. What’s also upsetting is that some of the staff over the phone sound rude and completely unbothered, as if they don’t want to be there. Not all of them — there are some helpful staff — but most of them really let the practice down

recent_reviews.author: Aimee Vozzo
recent_reviews.text: This is a very important review that should be read and acknowledged assertively. “I’m extremely annoyed at this surgery as a women in a same sex relationship. I went to the GP like instructed by multiple resources to see Dr Anita Nathan. I’m ready to start a family and have a history of cancer and infertility issues. I was not supported or referred to a specialist or hospital after seeing the gp twice. The doctor claimed I had not failed enough times to receive any NHS funded support. This is ludicrous. My partner and I were ignored in so many aspects and I had to defend my position of wanting a biological baby (my eggs) through IVF with my partner as the carrier. This seems extremely simple to refer me to the next step. I am writing to express my deep concern regarding the treatment I received from Dr. Nathan in relation to my fertility care. recent_reviews.text: ** Updated 18 July 2025** Just to update this review – I find it astonishing how inefficient Sheen Lane Health Centre continues to be. recent_reviews.author: Michael Hasnip
recent_reviews.text: I think the many one-star reviews already make it clear how poorly this surgery is run. Unfortunately, my own experience over the past two years has been just as disappointing. The reception staff are consistently rude and dismissive, both in person and over the phone. Patients are forced to use the Anima online system rather than being allowed to make straightforward requests by phone. Even then, responses often take days — or never come at all. My most recent Anima request went unanswered for over a week. When I eventually called to chase it, the receptionist was rude, gave no meaningful update, and simply told me to “wait for a doctor to respond.” I’ve raised multiple complaints and repeatedly requested a call from the practice manager, Haley S, but despite several attempts, she has never contacted me. When I developed significant breathing problems in late 2024, the handling of my care was appalling. After several appointments and conflicting advice, I was told an urgent ENT referral had been made on a two-week wait. The letter I later received showed a 19-week wait instead. I called the practice multiple times, was promised the referral would be expedited, and was even told I’d receive an urgent GP call — which didn’t happen until much later, only for the GP to deny what I’d previously been told. I eventually had to contact the hospital myself to get the referral treated as urgent (which advised I needed urgent corrective nasal surgery). To make matters worse, a third-party rehabilitation provider I’ve been dealing with following a major accident contacted the surgery for information. I was informed the practice had been completely unresponsive to their repeated requests. I’m now facing the same issue with my solicitor, whose information requests are also being ignored. Overall, my experience with this surgery has been defined by poor communication, false assurances, and a complete lack of accountability. I’ve lost all confidence in their ability to manage patient care. Absolutely disgraceful service.

recent_reviews.author: Bonge
recent_reviews.text: Been with Norton Brook for most of my adult life, Doctors, Nurses and Pharmacy staff have always been professional and compassionate when appropriate. Also I have rarely struggled to make a timely appointment. But the reception staff have always been the weak link. There have been a few instances of minor oversights on their part, not putting prescriptions through to Day Lewis when requested was a repeated inconvenience a few years ago but admittedly hasn’t happened lately; or the time that instead of checking me in for my appointment the receptionist cancelled it, I sat waiting for 45mins beyond my appointment time before approaching the desk and being told, without apology, that my appointment was cancelled. That also happened a good few years ago. The reason I’m writing this now is because one, some but certainly not all of the reception staff there are just rude, prone to making snarky judgements and providing commentary that I find unprofessional and off putting. I am definitely someone who has sat on symptoms for longer than I should because of the ‘don’t waste our time with this sort of thing’ attitude I have received during some calls over the last 10 years, including today. I know thats silly, but I can’t be the only one put off my these off putting gate keepers.

recent_reviews.text: I’ve had a very poor experience with Havelock Grange Medical Practice regarding my care. I should not have to chase my own treatment like this, especially when it has already been approved by clinicians. The whole situation has been frustrating, stressful, and completely avoidable. Very disappointing experience.

recent_reviews.author: Stephanie Paterson
recent_reviews.text: Formal Complaint Regarding Repeatedly Disrespectful and Unprofessional Conduct by Reception Staff at Feltham HMC GP To the Practice Manager and Senior Partners of Feltham HMC GP, I am writing to lodge a formal, urgent complaint regarding the unacceptable and unprofessional behaviour of two receptionists at your practice. This is not an isolated incident but a pattern of dismissive, arrogant, and disrespectful conduct that severely undermines patient trust and access to care. My most recent experience occurred on weekend, when I called to request an urgent appointment for my daughter. I was spoken to by a male receptionist who introduced himself as "VEJAY". His manner from the outset was abrupt and devoid of empathy. When I explained the need for an urgent appointment, he dismissed my request immediately without any attempt to explore clinical need or options. Upon asking for the next available appointment, he simply said "no." I politely asked if he could kindly check the system or advise on the protocol for urgent matters, but he was utterly dismissive. His tone was consistently arrogant and lacked any basic courtesy. When I asked for his name, he stated it in what I can only describe as a boastful and confrontational manner, spelling it out unnecessarily. Alarmed by his attitude, I asked to speak to a manager or supervisor. He responded by claiming he did not have one and stated, "I don't care if you complain," before suddenly terminating the call. This behaviour is utterly reprehensible for any NHS frontline staff member. It creates a direct barrier to healthcare and causes significant patient distress. This pattern indicates a serious cultural or management problem within your reception team. Such staff members are making the GP experience in the UK worse and are a disgrace to the NHS's core values of respect, compassion, and professional service. My requests for action are urgent and clear: 1. Immediate Investigation: I demand a formal investigation into the conduct of the receptionist "VEJAY" on the weekend. 2. Accountability & Training: These individuals must be held accountable for their unprofessionalism. If they cannot adhere to the fundamental standards of patient interaction, they must be replaced. Mandatory retraining in customer service, communication, and NHS values for the entire reception team is essential. 3. Management Structure: The claim by "VEJAY" that he has "no manager" is alarming. Please clarify the management and supervision structure for reception staff and provide official contact details for escalating issues. 4. A Formal Response: I expect a detailed written response to this complaint, outlining the steps you have taken, within the standard NHS complaint timeframe. I will be escalating this matter via a DATIX complaint report to the NHS urgently, as this represents a clear patient safety and experience concern. I will also be forwarding this complaint to the local Integrated Care Board (ICB) if a robust and satisfactory resolution is not provided by the practice. The wellbeing of patients and the reputation of your practice depend on professional, compassionate staff. The current behaviour of this receptionist is damaging. I await your urgent response. Yours faithfully, Steph

recent_reviews.text: Booking system is diabolical and not suitable for chronic illness sufferers with multiple symptoms. I have been investigated for complex symptoms since January 2025. More staff training is needed for some call takers, who are abrupt and defensive. A little empathy will go a long way. I'm currently going through a series of appointments, spaced out over months. Most of the GPs are knowledgeable and understanding, but it would be hopeless if I was seen by a random GP every time, it would take 10 mins for me to explain my issues. I try to see the same GPs but it's not an easy task. The sooner I can get my referrals the less I need to stress about contacting the GP which is a real shame. Finance constraints and business models have taken over patient care and safety. I have a rare chronic condition that requires urgent attention if I have a fever. Although I have not been acutely ill recently, the option to go to Ashford Acute if there are no more appointments at the GP practice is a welcome additional assurance. Otherwise, it'll be A&E for me maybe?

recent_reviews.author: Olivia Gornall
recent_reviews.text: ⸻ I have been suffering with ongoing back pain for over two years, and the care I have received from this surgery has been nothing short of dismissive and unacceptable. Despite repeatedly attending appointments and explaining how severe the pain is, I have been continually fobbed off with the same response – physiotherapy. No scans, no proper investigation into the cause of the pain, and no real effort to actually diagnose what is going on. Just the same cycle of being sent away again and again. My most recent appointment with Dr Sword was particularly concerning. My back was visibly swollen and red hot to the touch, yet he did not even examine it. No physical assessment whatsoever. Instead, he simply told me to see a physiotherapist again. I left feeling completely dismissed and shocked that a doctor could ignore such obvious symptoms without even checking them. After this appointment I contacted the surgery to complain because I felt my concerns were not taken seriously. I was then booked for physiotherapy, but the next available appointment was three weeks later, leaving me to continue suffering in pain with no treatment or support while waiting. After waiting those three weeks, I arrived 10 minutes early at 8:20am, checked in on the screen at the surgery, and sat waiting. After 45 minutes, I went to reception only to be told that my physiotherapy appointment was actually at a completely different location. This was never communicated to me when the appointment was booked. The app stated the appointment was at the surgery, and the check-in screen at the surgery also showed my appointment there. So after waiting weeks for help, my time was completely wasted due to yet another communication failure. Sadly, my experience is not the only concerning one within my family. My nan attended this surgery complaining of chest pain, dizziness, headaches, nausea and problems with her eyesight. These are extremely serious symptoms, yet her blood pressure was not even taken during the appointment. Just one week later she suffered a major stroke and has now lost movement and speech. When she was later assessed in hospital, doctors also discovered she has Aortic stenosis, a serious heart condition that had also been completely missed. Situations like this make it feel as though patients at this surgery are simply being dismissed rather than properly assessed. When serious symptoms are not investigated and basic checks are not carried out, the consequences can be devastating for families. This surgery used to have a good reputation, but the standard of care now feels like it has drastically declined. Patients are being dismissed, not examined properly, and left waiting weeks for help while serious conditions are overlooked. At this point I have completely lost confidence in the care being provided here. If these issues are not taken seriously, I will have no choice but to escalate this further through a formal complaint to NHS England and the Care Quality Commission, because patients deserve far better than what is currently happening here

recent_reviews.author: Alex Duckworth
recent_reviews.text: Over the last couple years I've slated Standish medical practice it's no where near as good as it used to be. However recently it seems like it has improved. The text system they have is good and the my gp app has improved in some ways it's good that you can see your medical history now. There's a few helpful tools on there. Therefore I have upped my review from a 1 star to 3 stars, never really had a problem with the staff, sometimes I feel they don't dig into things deep enough but that's just my personal opinion. Lastly I think the way you make bookings is still appalling you shouldn't have to wait 4+ weeks for an appointment, if you have a bad memory like me you just forget about it, even if you get the reminder sometimes you still miss it or have made plans. You can't plan for 4 weeks from now. Also the fact you can only book between 8.30 and 10am is terrible I go months without making appointments waiting for a day off work to text in or ring and then not having late appointments for after 5pm is just as bad. Also the fact they aren't open on the weekend as a doctors makes 0 absolutely 0 sense to me. Youre never gonna fix a back log of patients by doing this for an expanding village more like a town now. Overall it's improved, the booking system is awful and I suppose there's always GP alliance that are open late that can be used so not a massive issue there

recent_reviews.text: Was a patient here for 25 years and it’s fair to say they’ve really gone downhill so I’ve had to leave the surgery. The doctors are not great here, they’re very lazy. recent_reviews.author: Taparati
recent_reviews.text: I injured my index finger and attended A&E in Wolverhampton, where I received only a basic check-up and no medication. Initially, I thought things were fine, but about two months later I developed an infection. I visited my GP twice - the first prescribed antibiotics that didn’t help, and during the second appointment, the doctor mentioned he was unsure whether it was even an infection. The condition worsened to the point where I had to travel back to my home country, where it was confirmed to be a serious infection, and I finally received the correct treatment. I wish the issue had been investigated more thoroughly earlier, as it could have prevented a lot of pain and an operation. The staff is overall good with behaviour, but the diagnosis capability is not good.

recent_reviews.author: Alison Gillies
recent_reviews.text: I have been a patient of this practice for over 30 years, and its treatment of patients is now so appalling that I assume it must be in some sort of crisis situation. Patients are required to phone at 8am for a telephone call-back appointment, and all of my attempts have been at precisely 8am. After listening to the recorded message, another automated message then tells me that I am 28th or 35th in the queue for receptionist to speak to me. By the time receptionist becomes available, it can often be mid-morning, and the message is inevitably that there are no routine telephone appointments now available for this day - ‘try again tomorrow’. This can go on for days or weeks. Some of the receptionists have advised me to try logging on at midnight to try to book a phone appointment for the next day. But often the online response at midnight is that there are no appointments available. I imagine that many people just give up trying to speak to a doctor. It feels like a really worrying and unsafe situation when there is a concern about a potentially serious health issue. Receptionists tell me cheerily that this is a telephone practice. Face-to-face appointments are certainly not the norm. When a telephone appointment is available, the most common response appears to be a suggestion that the patient should make an appointment with a nurse for bloods to be taken, and that a prescription may be issued, depending on results. It is several years since I managed to see a GP on a face-to-face basis, and my rarely-achieved phone appointments tend to be with GPs who have never met me. By contrast my partner is a patient of the wonderful Colinton Medical Practice just along the road in Colinton Village, and he is ALWAYS seen by a GP on the day he phones for an appointment. The GPs there know him well, and treat him on the basis of this knowledge and his face-to face presentation, as opposed to described symptoms from a stranger on a phonecall, NHS records, and subsequent blood results. GPs at Colinton Medical Practice do not hurry their patients, and discuss and agree treatment options and plans with them. I’d really so much welcome an explanation for the dreadfully poor and deteriorating treatment of patients seeking attention from GPs at Craiglockhart Medical Group. I have obviously tried to move from this apparently failing medical practice to another more successful and ‘safe’ local practice, where it’s viable to see GPs, and does not feel so difficult to access even a phone appointment. Any local practice would seem preferable. But sadly - in common with lots of other Craiglockhart Medical Group patients - I have found that it’s impossible to escape unless I move to a new address in a catchment area for a better medical practice.

recent_reviews.author: Michelle M
recent_reviews.text: Poor service & attitude… I have family at Glenwood Health Centre & although they have the same limitations in terms of pressures & finances within the NHS service. Their attitude & manner is second to none. The amount of times I & other patients I know have gone into the practice & stood without a simple acknowledgement, while staff stand blathering, is appalling. I have found the training lacking as at times have gotten differing answers to the same questions or been given conflicting information. Unable to get an appointment in advance, on the day only, if you manage to get through on the phone. The cost to get a simple stamp, signature & a few boxes ticked for a claim form for an airline form (due to being ill & unable to fly), was astronomical & made it impossible to do the claim. I have since moved practice to Glasgow, what a difference. Friendly, helpful, appointments available to book, professional manner. I thought the NHS had just gotten so bad that in general this was how most practices operated. Not the case at all, restored my faith in the system.

recent_reviews.author: Mischa Pereira
recent_reviews.text: I'm a tourist visiting lovely Scotland and Fort Augustus/Loch Ness. Unfortunately my daughter became rather ill on the bus ride from Edinburgh. She was coughing badly and was an asthmatic and had started to break down in tears so I was concerned. We googled and followed the directions to the clinic. Unfortunately and sadly, the receptionist/assistant was extremely dismissive. She informed me that the doctor was out to lunch. When I asked if I could put my daughter's name down to see him at 2pm, she checked reluctantly and told me that the earliest my daughter could be seen was 3pm. She then proceeded to dismiss my daughter's symptoms, informing me that my daughter should go to the hospital if indeed she was suffering from an asthma attack. She also suggested that my daughter had covid, and then proceeded to tell me she was heading for lunch. I'm not sure why and where all these assumptions came from and I can only hope that it was not because we were Asians. While I'm sure that this review will have no bearing on the business of medicine, I'd like to express my disappointment at the service of this establishment especially since in the last week I have met many lovely people from Scotland who have been warm and friendly. It is unfortunate that given the opportunity to represent her country with kindness and compassion, she represented Scotland with rudeness and dismissiveness. Should she ever find herself in need if ever she was in Singapore, I can almost guarantee that she would have been treated with respect and kindness, especially when it came to someone who was unwell.

recent_reviews.author: W
recent_reviews.text: We have been waiting to write this review. This is undoubtedly the worst surgery we have ever been unfortunate to use. The staff are combative with their approach and that's not just the receptionists who seem to think they are god. Getting past the Receptionists is a challenge within itself. Each time I had to call the surgery they were just negative and combative. In the end, I took it personally. The receptionist M would just lie about appointment availability even though I could blatantly see an empty surgery. Also I had on occasions sat there for up to 40 mins after my appointment time and not a soul would walk in. I could hear the receptionists whispering etc at times. When I asked why I had not been called in, I would be told "they know you're there". No apology, nothing. My time is just as important as the GPs. My most recent encounter with this surgery was with Ev where she threatened to sit on transferring my medical files to my new GP as she communicated she had a deadline time to do this and if she wanted to be awkward, she could wait until last minute to do it. I asked her to repeat what she said and put her on loud speaker so that my husband could hear. This was regardless of me stressing that I needed my urgent medication which couldn't be prescribed by my new GP until my historical files had been received. They had even been contacted by the new GP requesting this. On another occasion I had to wait weeks for my smear test to be carried out only due to the incompetence of the nurse, GP and another GP. In the end I was asked to wait until they obtained a particular device. I have and always had a tilted pelvis but this is the first GP/ Nurse I have come across who struggled to get this done. Fortunately, after waiting a month longer my final result was clear. I could continue to write so much more but I don't wish to spend too much of my time thinking about this place which gave me anxiety at every encounter with them. My penultimate comment has to be documented because I found it disgusting. I was refused my repeat prescription which should have been adjusted on a patient by patient basis according to symptoms. The NICE guidelines say exactly this. In the end I had to go private to get this prescription because the pharmacist for this clinic said "now I'm not prescribing anything because I know you'll use more than what the NHS Highland guidelines say". Let me be specific, I am referring to estrogen hrt patches which are body identical and should be prescribed after a consultation with the patient to discuss symptoms. It is documented as so by the NICE guidelines. It should not be on the GP or pharmacists personal interpretation. She literally left me with nothing and as a punishment stopped the prescription altogether. When I told the GP what their pharmacist said to me, her response was "you must have misunderstood what was being said'. She basically gaslit me. The GP approached the pharmacist to clarify what was said she realised what I said was accurate, nevertheless she proceeded to defend what was said instead of apologising. Lastly, when we first moved to this area, my husband had to do a stool sample test. The receptionist refused to take the sample saying it was in the wrong bag. We complained to the GP who apologised and said it was not in the wrong bag and that my husband should do another one. My husband works offshore so there was a 3 week delay before he could get another sample to them. This was a typical example of the Receptionists playing god. They are not medically trained so how dare they take such a risk. Thankfully, the second sample was negative. We now have another GP in an area outside of the Highlands and I can honestly say, the care, attention and service is AAA. In my opinion Dr La and the staff need more training. What a disappointment. I must say though, the male GP is very good. I'm also sending a copy of this to the Highland Health Board.

Each time I had to call the surgery they were just negative and combative. In the end, I took it personally. The receptionist M would just lie about appointment availability even though I could blatantly see an empty surgery. Also I had on occasions sat there for up to 40 mins after my appointment time and not a soul would walk in. I could hear the receptionists whispering etc at times. When I asked why I had not been called in, I would be told "they know you're there". No apology, nothing. My time is just as important as the GPs. My most recent encounter with this surgery was with Ev where she threatened to sit on transferring my medical files to my new GP as she communicated she had a deadline time to do this and if she wanted to be awkward, she could wait until last minute to do it. I asked her to repeat what she said and put her on loud speaker so that my husband could hear. This was regardless of me stressing that I needed my urgent medication which couldn't be prescribed by my new GP until my historical files had been received. They had even been contacted by the new GP requesting this. On another occasion I had to wait weeks for my smear test to be carried out only due to the incompetence of the nurse, GP and another GP. In the end I was asked to wait until they obtained a particular device. I have and always had a tilted pelvis but this is the first GP/ Nurse I have come across who struggled to get this done. Fortunately, after waiting a month longer my final result was clear. I could continue to write so much more but I don't wish to spend too much of my time thinking about this place which gave me anxiety at every encounter with them. My penultimate comment has to be documented because I found it disgusting. I was refused my repeat prescription which should have been adjusted on a patient by patient basis according to symptoms. The NICE guidelines say exactly this. In the end I had to go private to get this prescription because the pharmacist for this clinic said "now I'm not prescribing anything because I know you'll use more than what the NHS Highland guidelines say". Let me be specific, I am referring to estrogen hrt patches which are body identical and should be prescribed after a consultation with the patient to discuss symptoms. It is documented as so by the NICE guidelines. It should not be on the GP or pharmacists personal interpretation. She literally left me with nothing and as a punishment stopped the prescription altogether. When I told the GP what their pharmacist said to me, her response was "you must have misunderstood what was being said'. She basically gaslit me. The GP approached the pharmacist to clarify what was said she realised what I said was accurate, nevertheless she proceeded to defend what was said instead of apologising. Lastly, when we first moved to this area, my husband had to do a stool sample test. The receptionist refused to take the sample saying it was in the wrong bag. We complained to the GP who apologised and said it was not in the wrong bag and that my husband should do another one. My husband works offshore so there was a 3 week delay before he could get another sample to them. This was a typical example of the Receptionists playing god. They are not medically trained so how dare they take such a risk. Thankfully, the second sample was negative. We now have another GP in an area outside of the Highlands and I can honestly say, the care, attention and service is AAA. In my opinion Dr La and the staff need more training. What a disappointment. I must say though, the male GP is very good. I'm also sending a copy of this to the Highland Health Board.Like Share

recent_reviews.author: Michalina Bujak
recent_reviews.text: I am sharing my personal experience following recent contact with this GP practice and specifically my communication with Dr Calum Forrester-Paton. I am currently 8 weeks post laparoscopic gynaecological surgery. When I was assessed earlier this month, I was still able to walk and manage basic daily activities. Over the last 5 days, my symptoms have significantly worsened to the point where I am now struggling to function normally and my pain has become severe and constant. I contacted Singleton Hospital, Swansea, and spoke directly with the gynaecology department. After I described my symptoms and explained that my condition had clearly deteriorated, I was advised that my GP must urgently refer me to the gynaecologist on call for further assessment. I relayed this information to my GP practice. However, following communication with Dr Calum Forrester-Paton, I was informed that my case was not considered an emergency and that I should wait for a gynaecology clinic appointment. I was also advised that if I felt worse, I should attend A&E. When I attended A&E, I was informed that they only assess for immediately life-threatening conditions and do not manage post-operative gynaecological complications unless they are life-threatening. I was advised that ongoing post-operative issues should be managed by gynaecology or via GP referral. This resulted in a situation where the hospital advised urgent GP referral to gynaecology, A&E advised that they do not manage post-operative gynaecological complications, and my GP did not arrange the referral despite clear worsening of symptoms. I explained that my condition had significantly deteriorated compared to my earlier assessment and that I am now unable to carry out normal daily activities. I did not receive clear guidance on how to manage my worsening symptoms while waiting, despite the serious impact this has had on my physical and mental wellbeing. I am sharing this review to accurately reflect my experience and the difficulties I faced in accessing appropriate post-operative care.

recent_reviews.author: Charlie Moritz
recent_reviews.text: I was born in this village and Potterals was always great. Compared to friends that lived in other places and when I lived elsewhere and overseas, I always thought the doctors here were professional and it was easier to get an appointment than other NHS GPs, even post-Covid when I moved back. Recently they have changed their appointment system so now you have to share a lot of personal and private information in a form, rather than getting an appointment. They make you play 20 questions before they permit you to see a GP. You can't choose which doctor you go to. Why is it not just a calendar so you can book yourself in at a convenient time with a doctor you trust who knows your medical history? The answer? They have created the system to discourage people from booking an appointment. It is a form of friction that discourages people from seeking medical help, simply put. That isn't the only reason I am giving this 1* review. Dr. Ridout botched a vaccination for flu on my mum, causing her severe pain and disability in both arms that required prolonged steroids use to bring under control. It is clear based on symptoms that the injection was put into the wrong part of the arm, leading to near paralysis at the site (upper shoulder) later on the same day. He also insulted my dad after we finally got him to go to the doctor and he was so humiliated by the experience that he never went to the doctor again, and his condition worsened. He died in August 2023 from heart failure. It's such a shame to see this once reliable institution succumb to the same poor care we see everywhere else in the NHS. Really sad. But what can we do? Nothing, it's the NHS. Just hope you don't get sick.

Not just are they extremely dismissive in regards to any issues raised to them, they make you feel a burden or rushed when seeking support especially within the mental health area, being from outside of the asian community and them being mainly an asian run surgery I’ve noticed the difference in treatment with different cultures and it’s absolutely disgusting to say the least the way I feel I’ve been treated here. During my pregnancy I was facing some issues which I seeked support from the surgery and I was appointed to see one of the midwife’s at the surgery I was very visibly upset and conveyed for my unborn baby’s safety to which I was told to go in a very cold manner “go home and bleed out and if you then still need some help call back” so in no other words told to go home to potentially loose my baby and I asked if she could simply do a reassurance test with the hand held machine to just ensure baby’s heartbeat is at least stable but I was denied any suggestion I’d made. I was later prescribed with medication again during this same pregnancy which on the label clearly mentioned I shouldn’t have been taking during pregnancy so again MAJOR concern as this could have costed me my beautiful sons life. I’ve also had a few encounters where I’ve found the front of house staff very hostile, cold, unapproachable and just rude which makes things extremely difficult. I’ve since had few more issues happen which has made me finally leave. I only stayed with them this long as I was new to Birmingham after having just left London and where I live I’ve found it hard finding a GP as they all work with post codes over here and this was the only one available to me at the time. So if highly reconsider getting any treatment from here especially if vulnerable.Like1 Share

recent_reviews.author: M
recent_reviews.text: They are always 30mins late (at least) for an appointment. Even if it's the first one of the day. They should compensate patients for wasting their time. Receptionists don't answer the phone in time. Can walk to the place quicker than they answer sometimes (45mins). No privacy when talking to receptionists as everybody is staring at you with all chairs looking in same direction. Uncomfortable chairs. Some receptionists are quite rude, while others are friendly. Doctors are friendly, when you can see them... When you try to call, you're sometimes waiting a stupid amount of time. I rung them and started to walk to them at the same time. The walk is 45mins. I walked there quicker than they answered the phone. When I walked in (still on hold) the reception staff were doing nothing. Not busy at all. I told them I was calling them (and had been for 45mins) and they had nothing to say. Useless. I've found out that a better way of doing it, is calling 111. And telling them something to make the doctors at the GP ring you back. Saves so much time. Cut out the GP receptionists all together. When you do get through, they never have any appointments anyway. Just call 111 once the surgery is shut. If the call while the surgery is open, 111 will tell you to call the surgery. The NHS is a joke. Call 111 after the surgery is shut, and you'll be able to speak to a doctor within an hour. Give me back by NHS tax money so I can just go private.

recent_reviews.text: I had an appointment this morning with Sophie The Nurse for blood test results and home blood pressure monitoring but I had to go into work due to a colleague being off sick. Sophie was very thorough, informative and professional during my initial visit. I rang the surgery and spoke to Helen The Receptionist she was very understanding and cancelled my appointment for this morning and rearranged it. She kindly sent me a text message to confirm the rescheduled appointment. Helen was very professional, she had a lovely cheerful voice and a great telephone manner she is without an element of doubt an absolute asset to the medical practice and our NHS. Keep up the marvellous work Helen. Sadly, individuals are very quick to come online to complain about something but not often to compliment and acknowledge a great service. As a fellow healthcare worker within the field of independent pharmacy I totally understand the daily pressures and value/appreciate the NHS.

recent_reviews.author: farah manir
recent_reviews.text: I was referred to the practise for an appointment following a call with 111. I was told I would receive a call after 9:00 AM however I got the first call from the GP at 8.43am so was not expecting the call and therefore missed it. I called the GP immediately and was told will get a call back received a further call however as I went to answer the call the phone went dead. I then called the practise again and was told the GP would call me back. I am literally holding the phone in my hand now and have my sister as a witness, The phone call came through and before I even have a chance to answer it the phone goes dead. The calls were made by Dr Azeem and it appears that he did not allow the phone to ring long enough for me to actually have a chance to answer it and has recorded failed attempt three times. My message to Dr Azeem, people have appointments for a reason for help care and support because they are suffering, if you are going to call patient and not allow them to answer the call and discuss what they are struggling with there was no point actually training to become a GP because this is not actually helping people. This is not my first encounter with Dr Azeem where he has been a professional and proficient practitioner and therefore I will now be raising this formally. The main thing that I want you to understand Dr Azeem is there are many vulnerable people that you are supposed to provide care for, You might have a long clinical list that you're trying to get through however there are people in serious need of help and support and you're clearly not the right person to provide this support, you need to be called out on this making out like your calling patients when your clearly doing a tick box exercise.

recent_reviews.author: Ahmed Khan
recent_reviews.text: This GP surgery should be investigated for the way they treat patients. They removed my mother from their register without informing her, even though she was unwell. When I tried to book an emergency appointment, I was told she was “not registered” — despite our entire family being registered there. They claimed she was removed because she hadn’t attended the surgery for a few years. How can you remove a patient without notifying them? This is unacceptable and unsafe. The same thing was previously done to my brother, who was also removed without notice from Pak Health Centre for the same reason. We contacted NHS 111 for my mum, and they confirmed she was still showing as registered on their system and said they would pass the details to the GP. However, when I called the surgery again, I was told we must come in person and fill out forms to re-register her. This shows a complete lack of care, respect, and responsibility toward patients. A GP surgery should protect patients, not abandon them — especially elderly or unwell patients. I would give zero stars if I could. We will be reporting this surgery to the appropriate authorities so this does not happen to anyone else.

recent_reviews.author: princess omavowan
recent_reviews.text: I have generally had positive experiences with this GP surgery, and several doctors here are kind, professional, and empathetic. However, my recent consultation with Dr. Mark Jones was extremely upsetting. I felt that my symptoms and pain were downplayed despite explaining in detail how my condition affects my daily life, work, and even causes episodes of collapse. Some information documented in my medical notes did not accurately reflect what I said, which left me feeling dismissed and concerned about my care. During the consultation, I was also told that I was disturbing the emergency line, even though I had followed the process advised by the reception staff to speak to a doctor about my concerns. I hope the practice reflects on this experience to ensure patients feel heard, supported, and that medical records accurately reflect consultations. Empathy and accurate documentation are fundamental to patient care, and no one should feel discouraged from seeking help.

recent_reviews.author: m p
recent_reviews.text: My Dad was taken to the gardens Neurological centre in 2013 from having a serious bacteria infection, so this caused a serious brain injury, spinal cord injury and got cognitive impairment from this. He was there for 2 years. We got greeted by Rita McCarthy- General manager of the Jacobs and Gardens and Rita Applin- clinical services lead of the Jacobs and Gardens. We was promised a brilliant quality of care for my Dad, which we hoped it would be but this was all lies. They didn’t care one bit about anyone’s welfare and quality of care, all they wanted was the money. They promised physio everyday for 3 times a week for an hour but just about got 20 mins for 2 days a week. We spoke to Rita McCarthy about this as we wasn’t happy and all she did was come outside and say to my dad in a wheelchair ‘if you don’t like it here, you know where to go’ (pointing at the exit). Disgusting behaviour for someone who manages the whole place. Dr Roberts was putting my dad in strong drugs so he was sleeping all day and couldn’t go physio as he had no energy, We wasn’t happy about this, so we spoke to him and he took us outside so no one could hear him and said to us ‘I’ll drug him up as much as I like’. This is a Dr saying this, someone you would hope you could trust. He was more like a murderer! This is when we called for a meeting With Rita Applin and she stuck up for Dr Roberts and lied for him, she lied constantly in the meetings and was a bully like the rest of them. The behaviour of these people in charge was so scary to know that my Dad was in their care. They don’t care about the patients at all which is so sad, there was other families who had the same experience as us. Many Patients were just left alone when they needed 1:1 care and they were still getting the money from these people. Some of the staff that did want to help didn’t have a leg to stand on, they was either suspended or left because how badly they was treated. Unfortunately there’s not many Neuro Rehabs in the country so they have a lot of patients go there, but if there’s one thing they need to do is get compassionate people to be in charge instead that actually care about the patients and want to see the people get better. Not just for the money. The trauma we had there we will never forget for the rest of our lives.
