recent_reviews.author: Kieran
recent_reviews.text: I would give this surgery half a star if I could. Sometimes you need to be half dead just to be able to get an appointment to see a doctor the same day, Otherwise you have to book a week in advance. if you're able to call in at 8am and get an appointment the same day then you should try your luck on the Euromillions. Admittedly this surgery is the workplace of the best doctor in Herne bay/Beltinge and one of the highest regarded and skilled in the whole of Kent. (Mr) ( Dr. Q. Mangi ) But the surgery has many more good doctors there so I just don't understand why it's so difficult to be seen within 48 hours. Especially as there is another very large surgery just round the corner. I never had an issue with the surgery mentioned ( Park Surgery ) in regards to booking appointments and being seen quickly, I just wasn't happy with the level of care I was receiving so I decided to do a switcheroo. So yes, that is my review and opinion. Brilliant Doctors, Shout-out to Dr Mr Mangi, Boo to the borderline rude receptionists, And hopefully the rate of which people can get appointments and start receiving treatment improves significantly! TaDa Kiza

recent_reviews.author: Phill Morgan
recent_reviews.text: I wanted to take a moment to express my sincere thanks and appreciation following my appointment today, Friday 16th May. Nurses Starmer and Wood were outstanding in their professionalism, care, and, above all, their ability to put me at ease. I freely admit I’m probably one of the worst patients when it comes to needles, yet both nurses handled the situation with such calm reassurance and genuine kindness that the experience was far less daunting than it might have been. Their excellent listening skills and patient-centred approach made a real difference. It’s clear they are not only highly skilled but also deeply compassionate professionals who take great pride in delivering quality care. I would also like to take this opportunity to praise the entire team at St Anne’s Practice. The service I received on 16th Mar, and consistently in the past, reflects the dedication, efficiency, and empathy that define outstanding NHS care. Please do pass on my gratitude to Nurses Starmer and Wood and my thanks to the wider team. Warm regards, P Morgan

recent_reviews.author: Rozina Asghar
recent_reviews.text: I wanted to leave a really positive review after my recent appointment. I was previously registered at another surgery where it was very difficult to get appointments, even when something felt urgent. I was rarely offered appointments in a short space of time and never managed to be seen on the same day. This practice has been completely different from the start. They actually contacted me themselves to arrange my new patient check-up, which already made me feel very welcomed. During my visit, I was seen by Dr Javeria Ikhlaq who was incredibly kind, professional and reassuring. She explained everything clearly and handled what was quite an uncomfortable situation with real care and respect. The nurse who saw me in my first visit (I’m sorry I didn’t catch her name) was also wonderful – very gentle, supportive and made me feel at ease throughout the appointment. I’m genuinely so happy that I’m now registered here. It really feels like I’m in the right place and in very good hands. Thank you to the whole team for the care and professionalism you showed.

recent_reviews.author: Jake Williams
recent_reviews.text: Recently my partner and mother left a review that has been denied by the practice who continue to shelter nurses who harm people deliberately. Our information is 100% correct and from the first hand, not information that has been passed through an office of people and combed over. Yes I shouted in the reception, I only shouted in the reception after my complaint was refused and the manger raised their voice at me to leave, then I raised my voice in return. Because it's a human right not to be assaulted by a doctor and then verbally abused for trying to complain. ive had an ear irrigation several times and on only one of those occasions was the water jet almost forced through my ear drum. I had the same procedure at a different practice mere weeks afterwards and the nurse was excellent and I barely felt a thing. The practice is trying to suggest that I am violent when the only violence that occurred was towards myself. The practice are trying to suggest I am too stupid to tell the difference between deliberate harm and an uncomfortable procedure. I tried to file a complaint and I was given a form and ushered out of the door. On that form it said complaints can be taken in person. Negligence under oath is a serious complaint and deserved to be heard immediately. Instead what the practice chose to do was outright refuse an immediate complaint and then blame the victim when they are shocked and outraged at the blatant disregard. The fact you do not take complaints seriously and choose to victimise your patients should be a screaming red flag of how dangerous this practice is. This is a silencing and defamation tactic of a patient to preserve the practices legitimacy when in reality they would maintain their legitimacy if they took action against malpractice instead of telling people they are violent for being upset that malpractice is being ignored. Having an instrument forced into you ear canal incorrectly and then being tutted at while being treated like scum, then also being dismissed by management is a complete abuse responsibility and any human being with a sense of morality would be disgusted. Clearly the intent of this procedure is to reduce people's capacity to complain and be heard because we are just scummy civilians. The fact that I'm being forced to leave a review like this is that is embarrassing goes to show how much disregard the management has for people who have a complaint. Quite a few years ago I experienced a collapsed lung, during the process of having needles and syringes put inside my chest cavity I requested another nurse to hold my hand because I was terrifird and believed i was going to die as I hadn't been able to breath properly for over two hours. I was extremely grateful to the hospital staff. Even though I had to have the syringes reapplied I was extremely courteous, trying to stay still etc. For anyone not aware collapsed lings are easily life threatening. So what we are saying is I am kind to people on my potential death bed in agonising pain, but apparently one day I decided to just turn up to a GP and start causing a scene? Just dosent add up really does it. Or maybe what happened is there is a serious problem with accountability at this practice and they prefer to use their elevated status in society to try and silence people. Which in turn makes people with poor intentions realise just how much they can get away with because of their title. Pure facist behaviour.

Always professional, friendly and willing to help if possible. From the reception staff who manage anxious patients and juggle appointments with consumate ease (all of them, not just one) to the nursing team (shout out to Jackie and Jenny here) to the GPs. They are always honest, even if telling you something you don't want to hear! I am alive now because of their skills, and am very grateful.

recent_reviews.text: Have visited this place a couple of times will start with the positive. Got appointment relatively quickly and everyone is friendly and respectful. Sunarun gave me and blood test, which was quick and very personable. Safia at reception was also incredibly helpful in sorting out an issue with additional samples and explaining what was needed. However, if the GP/physician’s assistant/nurse doesn’t type up their notes at lightning speed there may be an issue with info for the samples not being printed out. But thankfully today had Safia and she was on it and sorted out some printouts and new sample pots for me.

recent_reviews.author: Lavinia Cotosevitz
recent_reviews.text: On July 18th, I had an appointment with Dr. Z Ahamed, booked for 3:00 PM at Romford Rd, E15 4BZ. I had a referral from my GP. I've been suffering from back pain for a year. Since the healthcare system here only performs MRIs for severe cases (i.e., when you can no longer walk), I decided to go to my home country for an MRI. I came back with the results, which were explained in English by a doctor, and the report was registered with my GP. I know already the result, explained by 2 doctors before him. My appointment with Dr. Z Ahamed was the worst experience I have ever had. He was completely disinterested and bored, showing no interest in listening to me. He described my condition as "muscle spasms," even though the MRI mentioned something completely different. He said there was nothing to worry about and recommended I take paracetamol and ibuprofen and do a few daily exercises, nothing extensive. That was pretty much the whole consultation; he just wanted me to leave. I told him I had a few questions. I've had this pain for a year, and I came to this appointment looking for a way to help myself, as my back hurts 95% of the time. What about massage? What kind of massage is recommended for me? He rolled his eyes and clearly stated that massage wouldn't help, saying it was just a trick! He said the same about acupuncture and cupping—that they don't help and he doesn't recommend any of them. If these are just "tricks," then what does ibuprofen do? You're just filling me with pills for a year, yet you don't know of a single solution! I came to this appointment for help and received an unconcerned attitude, with no compassion or interest in a patient's needs. It was a complete waste of time! If you do a simple Google search for what is recommended for "muscle spasms," it clearly says MASSAGE in big letters!!! Thank you, Dr. Z Ahamed, for wasting my time! If you don't like this profession, change it—stop wasting people's time! Let other doctors do their job! I do not recommend him, and I hope I never have to deal with you again!!!!!!

recent_reviews.author: Luna Century
recent_reviews.text: Many times — maybe more than ten, around twenty times — I have been unable to get an appointment. The system closes very early, probably around 11 a.m. I cannot book an appointment at 8 a.m. because I am working and simply do not have the time. At all other times, the system is closed. So what am I supposed to do in this situation? At the reception desk, I am told that I must do this at 8 a.m. But how is that realistic if I am working? At the same time, when I call the phone number, the automated message says that if I cannot make an appointment, I should contact the reception and they will help me. However, the online system states that appointments are available until 6:30 p.m. Why is this information provided in the system or on the voicemail if this service is not actually available? What is the purpose of this? How am I supposed to get an appointment if there are no real options for working people? I simply want to see a doctor. I work, I pay taxes, and I have the right to see a doctor occasionally. This is a basic human right.

recent_reviews.author: Dennis A Hall
recent_reviews.text: I have been a patient at Eldale Street Surgery for over 20 years, and during that time my experiences have been mixed. In the past, some consultations left me feeling more like a number than a person, with appointments feeling rushed and my concerns not always fully listened to or explored. However, my more recent experiences have been a marked and welcome contrast, reflecting the standard of care that patients should reasonably expect. In particular, the doctors I have seen lately, especially Dr. Natasha King, who in my estimation exemplifies what patient-centred care truly looks like. Dr. King is personable, attentive, compassionate, and genuinely engaged. She listens carefully, takes concerns seriously, and responds with empathy and clarity, creating an environment where a patient feels heard, respected, and reassured. These recent consultations have restored my confidence in the practice, to the extent that I would now be happy to recommend Eldale Street Surgery as my own GP surgery in any setting or conversation. My latest experiences reflect professionalism, care, and humanity at its best. Kind regards Dennis

recent_reviews.author: Tony Pink
recent_reviews.text: My 11 yr old daughter was seen by the Asthma nurse who got stroppy and rude when questioned as to why she was prescribing Steroid tablets to her after inhalers did not work. I asked if she was diagnosing Asthma, she said NO just trying things!! I asked if it could be an allergy and if she could have an allergy test! She was even more angry I had questioned this! I took her to allergy Uk London who did an 13 point skin prick test , lung function which was 111 (should be no more than 50!) tests were all in one appointment and she was diagnosed with allergy to grass pollen , horses dogs and cats !! I wrote to surgery to complain, Dr Head, and received no reply. Why didn’t the surgery not refer for lung function tests/allergy tests?? They are either not qualified to do the job or just don’t care! You are just a number!! How many more children are just a guinea pig trialing steroids and guessing a diagnosis for this surgery ?

recent_reviews.author: Nabid
recent_reviews.text: I've been with this surgery for 15 years now. It's all I've ever known - I thought the way they operated and their sub par quality was just the norm, all anyone could expect from an NHS GP. After enrolling my wife to the same GP, it really opened my eyes to how poor this GP is. I've looked at other reviews to find that other people have experienced the same thing - appointments that have not been noted down on my record (so it is as if they never even took place - this was with Dr Khanom), extremely slow responses and regular delays with appointments and overall poor practise from the GPs and nurses. I've had several appointments with Dr Khanom and it seemed like I was better off not having any appointment at all - I'd leave the appointment with no resolution - I hate to say it but she seems very incompetent - and I actually try to avoid having an appointment booked with her - it gives me anxiety. I've had several occasions where I've brought an issue up to Dr Khanom and she asks me what I think the issue is, and I'm just there like "??? idk? that's why I've booked this appointment" which is followed by a lot of her umm-ing and ahh-ing and not coming to any conclusion or next steps, I went about ear pain one time and she said there's not much that can be done, the ear seems fine. My wife raised other issues with her and she did not seem to understand the issue at all. Dr Ade-Alade always seems like she's in such a rush (no wonder since they're always behind schedule) and very dismissive of mine or my wife's issues. The male doctor that comes every other Friday is very good. And the nurse Dr gulev (who I believe has left now) was also great - they would listen and actually respond to what you're saying and inspire you with confidence regarding the next steps. The receptionists are hit and miss, they seem to have hired some more friendly helpful ones recently - but the original staff are still quite unhelpful and standoffish. Anyway, we've been considering leaving - and experiencing some other GPs for some other appointments have really opened our eyes to how bad this one is - would not recommend to anyone. Will be leaving this instant. Edit: can't even complain to the surgery via online as they've removed the online complaints form lol. Sums it up.

recent_reviews.author: Gemma anderson
recent_reviews.text: Disappointed by the lack of support and care shown by this GP practice regarding my father’s urgent health concerns. My father has been waiting over 18 weeks for an MRI scan. I contacted the surgery out of serious concern, particularly as he had already been sent directly to the hospital on appointment by this very GP due to dangerously high blood pressure which triggered this whole experience. While in hospital, doctors discovered he had also suffered a heart attack, and he was admitted for further care. This is especially alarming given that only a few weeks prior, my mother—also under this practice’s care—tragically passed away from a heart attack. One would expect heightened vigilance and compassion in light of this family history, especially with an ongoing, unexplained delay in crucial diagnostic imaging. When I reached out, I was told by a receptionist to complete an eConsult on his behalf which I did. I was assured that an appointment would be made for my father to see doctor aktar, instead he received a dismissive written response stating uncertainty about whether they could help or refer him for an MRI, with no follow-up call, no attempt to discuss the matter further, and no offer of support or alternative solutions. But they could see an appointment with the hospital for the 20th. (Talk to them) Exactly words. News to my father..no such correspondence has been sent and no such letter for an appointment has been received. This response falls far short of the GP’s duty of care. General practitioners are responsible for advocating for their patients' health, especially in urgent or deteriorating cases. They should coordinate with secondary care services, provide clear communication, and ensure vulnerable patients are not left in limbo. A refusal to help—without any further dialogue—is not only negligent but potentially dangerous. Patients and their families deserve proactive, compassionate, and accountable care. In this case, the GP practice failed us profoundly, and I sincerely hope they reflect on the seriousness of their responsibilities moving forward.

recent_reviews.author: Miron Barteczko
recent_reviews.text: Headline: Exceptional individual care marred by inconsistency and professionalism gaps. ​My experience with Ivory Street Medical Centre has been a 50/50 mix. On one hand, there are staff members who are "above and beyond." Specifically, the nurse responsible for blood tests and heart rate monitoring is excellent—thorough, professional, and highly recommended. The reception team is generally helpful, and some doctors provide a great standard of care. ​However, there are significant issues regarding professional standards and "lazy" diagnostic assumptions: ​Diagnostic Tunnel Vision: I had a health assessment where breathing issues were dismissed almost entirely as "anxiety." Despite my attempts to explain other factors, my input was ignored. It has since been confirmed that there were other sources for these symptoms beyond just anxiety. ​Professionalism & Accountability: I have encountered staff who openly admitted to being "under-qualified" for a standard request after I had waited a month for the appointment. To make matters worse, I felt mocked when raising concerns, and my attempts to complain were met with denials or being called a liar by the individuals involved. ​Communication Failures: My social prescriber requested a psychiatric evaluation based on a misunderstanding of my needs, yet admitted she does not read the emails sent to her—despite providing the email address herself and asking for contact via that method. ​It is frustrating to wait a month for an appointment only to be told the professional cannot help and must refer you elsewhere, leading to another month of waiting for a "reasonable request." While the good staff are great, the lack of professional accountability and the tendency to default to mental health labels rather than listening to the patient is a major concern.

recent_reviews.author: Andreea Dumitrescu
recent_reviews.text: I am currently 8 weeks pregnant and self-referred for antenatal care in early September. At my GP appointment on 22 September, I was told that if I hadn’t heard back from the midwives, the practice would chase the referral on my behalf. Today (14 October), I followed up exactly as instructed. The receptionist dismissed my concern, stating that booking appointments happen at 12 weeks and that they “can’t do anything.” This directly contradicts both NHS guidance and the advice I received from the GP. For reference, the official NHS website clearly states that the first midwife (booking) appointment should take place between 8 and 10 weeks, not 12. By providing incorrect information, your staff risk delaying essential blood tests and early screening potentially putting expectant mothers at risk. The attitude and misinformation I experienced demonstrate a serious lack of training and empathy from the reception team. It’s not acceptable to tell a pregnant woman misleading information when the NHS’s own published advice says otherwise. I strongly urge the practice to review its staff training and ensure receptionists understand the basic antenatal care timeline. Expectant mothers deserve accurate information and proactive support, not dismissive and uninformed responses.

recent_reviews.author: Naomi Mayer Baker
recent_reviews.text: I have been with this surgery for 3 years, first arriving in the non face to face era and masks. Even then, if we needed to be seen face to face, we were. All of my family have visited over the 3 years at some point and I can hand on heart say that we received great care. Reading all the reviews, I agree that sometimes reception can be a little abrupt but I have also seen first hand, how busy they are and I would imagine I might also be like that sometimes, in their shoes. The Drs we have seen have always been kind, caring and considerate. Dr Chapman, Dr Firth, Dr Sultana and Dr Franklin, all very different in personality but also very good at what they do. I am truly grateful for them and the services they offer. Having spent many years living overseas and paying for healthcare and every Drs visit, you appreciate the NHS that bit more and we need to do all we can to save it. Lastly, if you use the surgery's website and register to use their services online, it's very easy to book non urgent appointments, without even having to go through the reception booking system. Edit: I want to add to my review that I managed to see a Dr on Saturday that was fantastic and I felt very cared for. Brilliant surgery.

recent_reviews.author: Tasha Law
recent_reviews.text: Formal Complaint Regarding Treatment and Staff Conduct I am writing to formally complain about the treatment and behaviour I experienced at Priory Gardens GP Surgery in Dunstable. On Friday 16th January 2026, I attended a pharmacy as I was concerned I may have a urinary tract infection (UTI). The pharmacy explained that they were unable to test my urine sample. After I described my symptoms, which included abdominal pain and feeling nauseous, I was advised that I could potentially have pyelonephritis and was strongly signposted to attend my GP surgery as a priority. I was also advised to contact 111, but told to attend my GP first. I was given documentation to take with me. I attended Priory Gardens GP Surgery with this paperwork. At reception, the receptionist looked at my notes and then went to speak to her manager. The manager then came out and spoke to me in a very rude and unprofessional manner, raising her voice at me. I tried to explain that the pharmacy could not test my urine and that I had been advised to attend my GP urgently, but I was repeatedly told there were no appointments and that I must call 111. I explained that every time I call 111, I am directed back to my GP surgery, meaning I am being passed back and forth without receiving any care. I tried to explain this calmly, but the manager dismissed me and continued to speak over me. The manager then stated that I could not be seen due to my “medical history.” This was extremely upsetting, as she did not review my medical history in front of me, does not know me personally, and provided no explanation for this comment. I found this remark inappropriate and unprofessional. I also explained that I had called at 8am and again at 1pm, and on both occasions was told there were no appointments available. Despite clearly being unwell and presenting with concerning symptoms, I was refused any form of assessment or support. This experience is not isolated. During my pregnancy, I repeatedly contacted the surgery and struggled to be seen. I was only seen once, and later found out I had Group B Strep, yet no appropriate action or support was provided. This has left me with a complete lack of trust in the care provided by this surgery. The behaviour of the reception manager was unacceptable. Shouting at a patient, being dismissive, and refusing to listen is not acceptable under any circumstances. This is not appropriate customer service or patient care. Due to the repeated poor treatment and lack of support, I will be moving both myself and my daughter from this GP surgery. However, I feel it is important to formally raise this complaint so that this behaviour can be addressed and does not continue to happen to other patients. I would like this complaint to be formally investigated, and I would appreciate a written response outlining what actions will be taken.

recent_reviews.text: After Covid booking appointments are difficult in most surgeries and there is no exception here however when you call at least you know what number you are in line.I always found that receptionist are very professional and they only can do what they were told. They are fast and efficient. Regarding GPs. Dr.Stacey will be greatly missed.New doctors I dealt with so far since Dr.Stacey left was very disappointing.I have many unclear symptoms and being a carer of 3 disabled people full time calling surgery was very challenging for me at 8.30. Once I spoke to a doctor I was told we do not do routine health check. You must have symptoms if you want to have blood test I was told.Filling under the weather does not qualify to have a blood test. No doctor ever said this to me as long as I live. Blood test is the first basic test to find out if you have any problems with health. I had no choice but to do the blood test privately and and I was right I have a problem. I am speechless that my request for general health check was denied. Four stars are for receptionists only.

recent_reviews.author: E Y
recent_reviews.text: This clinic is a fascinating case study in how disorder can be institutionalised. The administrative staff demonstrate an impressive consistency in getting things wrong: appointments that mysteriously never existed, cancellations that were allegedly never made, and warning letters sent with great confidence to patients who did exactly what they were supposed to do. Responsibility, regrettably, does not appear to be part of the workflow. The doctors are a lottery. Some are competent and reassuring; others are clearly very new, frequently having to leave the room to consult a more senior colleague before making any decision. This arrangement manages to waste time while simultaneously eroding any sense of professionalism or confidence. As for management, they deserve special mention for their commitment to silence. Complaint forms can be filled in carefully and conscientiously, with the comforting assurance that they will be met with absolutely no response whatsoever. One can only assume these forms are filed directly into a drawer marked “Ignore”. The clinic’s sole redeeming feature is that if you begin phoning repeatedly from 8:20 a.m., with the persistence of someone who has nothing else to do, you may eventually secure a same-day appointment. Overall, this clinic offers not so much healthcare as an extended exercise in frustration, lowered expectations, and administrative disbelief.

recent_reviews.author: Talita Emmanuela
recent_reviews.text: It's been months that I can't get any appointments. The owner below said there are other ways to book, I went to check the NHS app and you can't (screenshot attached). Today I called at 8am sharp as they ask. The line was busy, kept calling until I got through at 8:02, sit and listen and chose the options, "We are unable to answer your call at the moment". Kept calling non-stop and at 8:20 finally manage to be put in the queue. They give you the option to retain your position in the queue and get a call back, after a few times when they called me way later just to say all appointments have been filled I was told is better to stay in the line or even go in person. recent_reviews.author: Gemma Rowell
recent_reviews.text: Why do I get so anxious about going to the doctor for anything? Oh I don’t know, maybe because when I get a UTI and call the doctors I get told to go to the pharmacy to get the normal 3 day course of antibiotics (Nitrofurantoin), but when I explain that I have a history of UTI’s and know from past experience that they don’t work, that I need and have previously always needed a stronger longer course, that I have a history of kidney infections (that’s on my doctors notes), I’m now taking medication that is known to cause and worsen both UTI’s and kidney function (I have yearly blood tests to keep an eye on them) and need to actually talk to a doctor to discuss this I just get told to bring in a urine sample and fill out a form… that has no space to explain why it’s not a straight forward issue. I then get a text saying a prescription has been sent to my pharmacy… of Nitrofurantoin… a 3 day course. No phone call. No contact. Nothing. I don’t know what the point is anymore.

recent_reviews.text: My name is Anita Simsek I’m the owner of Global Getaways Travel Agency. Previously Eden Travel Company Check my reviews ! They are 100% Fantastic! Much better than their 3.1. I was really ill and in hospital and they referred me back to my gp. I asked him to please refer me back to my respiratory consultant as my condition had worsened and he said it wasn’t possible and refused to refer me back! recent_reviews.author: Alexa Druga
recent_reviews.text: This review has been a long time coming, and today was the final straw. I have been dealing with multiple health issues, one of them for over a year, and this GP practice has completely failed to provide proper care. I am in ongoing pain, yet my appointments are repeatedly cancelled, sometimes on the same morning I am supposed to attend. This has happened multiple times. There is no continuity, no ownership, and no clear plan. I am constantly being sent back and forth, wasting time and energy while my symptoms remain unresolved. Communication is extremely poor. Different members of staff say different things, often contradicting each other. I am told to attend appointments that then do not go ahead, including being sent for tests or procedures that are later not carried out despite being clearly indicated. Recently, I contacted them again regarding a separate, new issue. I was sent back and forth between different services. This caused completely unnecessary visits, all while I was in pain and the test or procedure was medically justified. While the staff are generally polite, patients are not treated as people with real pain and real urgency. There is a clear lack of understanding of how severe and persistent symptoms can be, and despite being in significant pain, I am repeatedly left without timely help or follow-up. I am constantly told to use the eConsult form, but even when I do, I might wait up to two weeks for an appointment, which is then sometimes cancelled anyway. During this entire time, I am left in pain, unsupported, and without any clear next steps. Overall, I cannot recommend this GP practice at all. I do not feel listened to, taken seriously, or cared for in any meaningful way. If you are looking for a GP who will actually investigate symptoms and understand the impact of ongoing pain, I would strongly advise looking elsewhere. It isn’t even 1 star…

recent_reviews.text: I got a severe health issue recently. My fingers are becoming swollen and they get numb sometimes randomly. And I am finding it difficult to walk properly as my feet pains as well. Filled up e-consult last month and they gave me appointment for yesterday. I waited patiently for the appointment. The doctor was very nice , he understood my problem and advised blood tests. But when I went to book in the blood tests, I got a date in Dec. I waited so long for an initial appointment and then almost a month now I need to wait for bloods. Update: Luckily for me, I got a call and my bloods were collected within two days. Many Thanks to Dr. Atalla who was very kind. He personally looked into my problem and arranged for blood collection and got them sent for tests. Once the reports are out, he called me and explained the results and started me on necessary treatments right away without any further delay. He also recommended for further steps to get a few more things looked into. I can’t thank him enough for helping me by diagnosing my problems. I have been with this practice for over 10 years now. And the main reason why I never think of moving to different GPs - despite the long waits for triage calls etc over here, because at the end of it all I feel when they start looking into a patient, they do provide the best treatment care possible.

recent_reviews.author: Annette Blackett
recent_reviews.text: I belong to Royal Primary Care with Grassmoor. Forget about getting seen in Grassmoor, all my appointments are booked with Clay Cross. This is only a minor inconvenience. The problem with Clay Cross is GP availability and any constistancy. I recently had tests done at the hospital. I was told by reception that I must book an appointment two weeks in advance with a GP to get my results. Fair enough, I booked my appointment. The morning appointment offered between 8 and 12, phone call that I expected never came. I phoned to only be told it was a mistake from the GP who thought I was after another test that the results were not in yet. "Sorry, we will have a GP phone first thing in the morning." Frustrated, I was forced to accept the doctor had gone home for the day. Next day, came. No morning call came as expected. So, I phoned the office at 11. I was told, yes you're on our call back list. So much for another morning appointment. I went to work. At 5:30 p.m., my husband called. He asked if I got a phone call yet. Upon learning the answer was no, he took it upon himself to call and form a complaint. Within a half an hour, I got a call from the nurse. She listened to my complaints and said she would book me in to see a regular doctor. Great! So, I thought. It was another week before I was seen. 20 minutes past my scheduled appointment. Only to be told that another MRI of my neck was going to be ordered. It had been several years since the last one. Yes, I've been suffering for over 8 years. Sent to physio therapy and told by them "I must, learn to live with my pain." The GP refused to do an MRI of my shoulder years ago and still refuses today and this is where my pain is located. He told me, I may have to learn to live with my pain also. He refused to refer me to an orthopaedic when I asked. My shoulder muscles are gone. I've lost all strength in my dominate right arm. I'm so depressed and broken. Thanks Royal for years of chronic pain and depression. 19-12-23 Edit* I've since moved over to Hasland Medical. Wonderful, caring doctors there ❤️! I finally got my shoulder tested and found that my tendon is damaged beyond repair. Awaiting a new shoulder in 2024. Looking forward to a better year than these past years of misery have brought to me. 04/11/2025, I got my new shoulder just over a year ago and in asking great. The surgeon couldn't believe the amount of damage in the shoulder joint. All of this should never have taken years to get fixed. I'll never regret moving from Royal Primary to Hasland, never!

Absolutely disgraceful!

recent_reviews.author: Claire Mc
recent_reviews.text: I have been with Clifton surgery for years and have never had any problems at all . The reception staff are lovely ,the GP,s and nurses great . I work at a different surgery in Rotherham not connected to Clifton and totally understand some of the frustration and anger the patients encounter , the waiting times for calls, the lack of appointments to offer and having to use the online services. Unfortunately this is the NHS. and surgeries have little choice when things change. We can't go back to the old ways queuing up in the morning , demanding an appointment with a particular gp.for a sniffle. It upsets alot of patients but im sure Clifton surgery is doing its best to help everyone at a difficult time. It is not the receptionists fault if there are no appointments left or they ask you what the appointment is for, it is to make sure you see the right clinician. Due to some people wanting an appointment a minor cough, cold, sore throat that they only had a couple of days, or hay fever or back pain that a pharmacist or physio can deal with is one of the reasons there are no appointments left for you or your family the genuine unwell patient. In addition to this the people who book appointments and do not attend anyway! again they are wasting an appointment that could be yours. This is across the whole of the Nhs GPS and hospitals . Clifton medial centre are trying their best to help everyone.please have a little more understanding, they are doing the best to help you ! Keep up the good work Clifton .

recent_reviews.text: As far as doctors’ surgeries go this one is towards the bottom of the list in most, if not all aspects, the main thing that i find nice and redeemable about the surgery is how clean and modern it is inside. recent_reviews.author: Caitlin Barnett
recent_reviews.text: If you’re looking for a GP surgery that treats mental health as an inconvenient afterthought, congratulations — you’ve found it. Appointments are rushed, concerns are minimised, and anything related to mental health is met with the same enthusiasm you’d expect for a stubbed toe. I left feeling unheard, dismissed, and frankly embarrassed for having bothered to ask for help in the first place. There’s plenty of lip service about “taking mental health seriously,” but when you actually need support, you’re brushed off, redirected endlessly, or made to feel like you’re overreacting. Apparently struggling mentally only counts if it’s easy, quick, and doesn’t require any effort from them. If you’re already vulnerable, do yourself a favour and look elsewhere. This surgery seems far more comfortable dealing with physical symptoms than acknowledging that mental health is, in fact, health. One star, and that’s being generous.

recent_reviews.text: NOT IMPRESSED! Re visited today for re dressing after having a dressing placed last week by a different nurse. (Ok I’ve not visited the practice after the previous GPs retired who I had a good relationship with) and I know I should have kept up with should have my health checks) I had to come out of work for this appointment- first thing I was greeted with was I’d not been for a while, get on scan scales, blood pressure high ( which I knew it would be a bit) informed high, I said one of the reasons because I’m under pressure to get back to work. Tried to take bloods - couldn’t find vein - not had a problem before - nurse had to seek assistance from GPA as to where the cannula should have been placed in a better bigger vein - left with 3 attempted cannulas - 3rd success but cannula wasn’t held in correctly so had to be repositioned as no blood let!so cannula had to be re adjusted. Left with bruising I’ve never had before!!! Was finally re dressed with the nurse a lot of faffing as their dressings/treatment rooms aren’t obviously properly stocked - the member of staff cleaned my wound carefully and gently but was advised I need the correct dressing for which she had to write a script for , so I have to now pay for this. This was before the above mentioned - near the beginning of my appointment, a member of staff knocked and came in ( seemed like they were having a sharps/clinical waste collection but they didn’t have the right size containers- to sort this issue, so was left in treatment alone for a few minutes- of which it sounded like but can’t substantiate - the person that was treating was talking to an apparently new mother with her baby! Before coming back to me ! I don’t feel I was given 100% care - although I’m expected to comply with tests imposed on me when I was extremely time limited! I get it - NHS establishments HAVE TO BOX TICK! But consent should have been asked for! EXTREMELY DISAPPOINTED!!!!!!!

recent_reviews.author: Ray Santi
recent_reviews.text: This is, quite simply, an exceptional GP surgery. At the front of house, all of the receptionists are consistently friendly and helpful. The doctors — Dr. Komal, Dr. Derwent, and Dr. Gill Snr — are caring, considerate, and empathetic, always willing to go the extra mile to resolve any health concerns. I’ve never felt rushed during an appointment; each doctor listens attentively and takes the time to understand any issue in detail. It’s clear that patient care is their top priority, and that ethos extends to every member of staff at the practice. A significant bonus is that Dr. Gill Snr can perform minor surgery, and from personal experience, he is an absolute master of his craft. The nursing team is equally exceptional — professional, kind, and reassuring. The gradual and sensible introduction of technology — such as the phone system, repeat prescription ordering, and email reminders for blood tests and vaccinations — has further enhanced an already excellent service. I consider myself extremely fortunate to have been a patient at this practice for almost 25 years.

recent_reviews.author: Sue Willington
recent_reviews.text: Like many I joined this medical practice recently. They use the e-consult software system to request an appointment which is used as a triage system for this extremely busy practice. During my limited time with Saxonbury this is the only area of concern I have encountered and, as they have only recently transferred to the system back in March’25, I am sure the hard working practice manager will be working on improving the process(the reason for giving 4 rather than 5 stars). Once through that first process I have found the Centre itself to be extremely clean and well organised. The staff are some of the best I have ever come across in the NHS - they are extremely caring, professional, and knowledgeable individuals who obviously care deeply about the care they provide their patients - from Health Care workers to Phlebotomists, GPs to Practice Nurses; Wonderful. Once that bit of AI technology gets refined it’ll be the best - please be patient with the reception staff until then. Front of Office staff often bare the brunt of our frustrations.

recent_reviews.author: Eliano Addis
recent_reviews.text: I’ve never left a GP appointment feeling so invalidated. Dr. Azam, Naveed showed no compassion or willingness to listen. Instead of supporting me through what was already a difficult and vulnerable time, he was cold, dismissive, and more focused on questioning my choices than actually offering help or support. It felt like he was trying to catch me out rather than understand me. What’s even more concerning is that I know others—including my own family—have had similar experiences with him. This doesn’t seem to be a one-off. Patients deserve to be treated with empathy, especially when they’re already struggling. That was completely lacking here. To be clear, I have no issue with the other doctors at this practice. Even when I haven’t heard what I wanted, I’ve always felt respected and heard. But Dr. Azam’s entire demeanour was so poor that it massively worsened the situation. I wouldn’t feel safe seeing him again—only judged and disrespected.

recent_reviews.author: Ioana Elecfi
recent_reviews.text: I’m writing to share my disappointment regarding the experience I had at the first-floor reception today, April 11th, at 11:30 AM. Unfortunately, the two ladies present were unhelpful and displayed a lack of basic empathy and problem-solving skills. I arrived at 11:20 AM for my scheduled appointment at 11:30. At 11:40, I received a message on my phone stating that I had missed my appointment due to not checking in. However, in the past, I’ve been called in without needing to check in, so this was unexpected. When I approached the reception to explain I had been there on time, one of them was unable to locate my name in the system. The other simply told me I would need to rebook. There was no effort to accommodate me—even though I was only 10 minutes late, the area was not busy, and the situation could have easily been resolved with a little understanding and initiative. A more human response would have been: “No worries, you’re only 10 minutes past, let me see what I can do.” Instead, I was told to rebook, with no consideration of the circumstances. That response turned a small issue into a frustrating and disheartening experience. I’ve always had good interactions in the past, and this is the first time I’ve encountered such unhelpful behavior. I won’t name anyone, but I hope this feedback helps highlight the need for better communication and empathy from the team. Whoever was working the reception desk on April 11th at 11:30 should be encouraged to reflect and improve. Otherwise, it becomes difficult to distinguish a human interaction from an automated system

recent_reviews.text: Avoid - I'm making an official complaint to the NHS, as what this GP did is damaging my health. Have been with this practice for the last 6 years and get regular prescription. Suddenly one day they deleted all my files and profiles from their system, and no longer include me as a patient, because I moved address. I understand they prefer not to see patients outside of their coverage area, but before they deleted all my info, they didn't call, email, send physical mail or anything to give me a heads up and transition period. As a medical practice, you should at least make sure patients are registered with a new GP before you suddenly delete them. As a result, I missed 3 weeks of medication and suffered from withdrawal effects.

recent_reviews.author: tuana hayfavi
recent_reviews.text: Stay away from this practice. I had a blood test on 29 January and was told the results would be ready within 1–5 working days. More than three weeks later, I still couldn’t access my results on the NHS app. I had to call the practice dozens of times. Every time, the reception staff gave different and contradictory information. One said the results weren’t downloaded, another said everything was normal. When I finally spoke to the GP three weeks later, I was told my cholesterol was actually high, which directly contradicted what the reception team had told me before. The hospital confirmed they had sent the results to the practice within five days. So the delay was clearly at the GP surgery. After all this time, the stress, and even a formal complaint, my results are still not uploaded to the NHS app and I still cannot view them myself. This level of administration and communication is completely unacceptable.

This level of administration and communication is completely unacceptable.Like Share Response from the owner 6 days agoDear Patient, Thank you for taking the time to review our practice. We were also very disappointed about the circumstances you describe, which were due to an IT change external to us that we were not aware of. Our management team was already looking into this issue before you submitted your complaint and your review. Your blood tests were ordered initially by a clinician working outside of the practice; all results normally go back to that clinician or to the patient’s registered practice. Unfortunately the results in your case were not loaded onto your patient notes by the Imperial lab in the normal way. When you contacted the reception team, they informed the doctors. Two different doctors downloaded the results, on two separate occasions, to try and get them onto our system and available for you to view. This is how the process has historically been done for thousands of patients. In addition, to reassure you at the time of trying to get them into your clinical record, the doctors reviewed the results, and then ensured that the results were communicated to you. In this case, however, the download system did not work, because of an Imperial hospital IT upgrade. We were not aware that this had happened or that the results would not come directly onto your clinical record. Once the problem had been discovered, we did manage to get a copy of your results emailed to the Practice and this version was uploaded to your patient notes. Our staff tried hard to resolve this for you: they contacted the doctors to resolve, they contacted the lab to resolve and they contacted the NHS North West London IT teams to find the source of the problem. We will be logging this as a learning event and we have escalated it inside and outside the practice, to ensure everyone is aware of this change, and to see if an IT solution can be found. We are very disappointed to receive such a poor review and such reviews significantly affect our staff morale. It is particularly upsetting when the source of your complaint is not due to the team at Grand Union but due to an IT change external to our practice, that we were not aware of. We are sorry for the upset that this delay caused you. Grand Union Health Centre

recent_reviews.author: Roman D
recent_reviews.text: Dear Grand Union Health Centre team, I wanted to leave a heartfelt thank you for the care and support you provided while I was coming in for wound dressings after my surgery. I had regular dressings in September for around a month and a half, and then again from December to February for almost two months. Throughout this time, every appointment was handled with professionalism, patience, and genuine care. A special thank you to Practice Nurse Jihanne! Her expertise and attention to detail made a huge difference to my recovery. She always took the time to explain what to do, gave clear and practical advice on wound healing, and helped with every little thing! Thanks to her timely recommendations and the consistently excellent dressings, my wound healed much faster than expected. Honestly, without that guidance, I believe I would have needed at least another month of dressings. Jihanne, it’s rare to meet someone who is such a true professional — skilled, kind, and incredibly supportive. It’s a little sad that my dressings are coming to an end, but it’s also reassuring to know that patients at Grand Union Health Centre continue to have someone like you looking after them and making the world better through your care and expertise. Thank you again to the entire team for everything you do, you are amazing people!💚

recent_reviews.author: Happy Grump
recent_reviews.text: In the last year C'fields has become scary, especially for those with chronic or complex illness. Communication throughout entire setup is awful. Every contact I have with them I'm finding some form of stress. Critical medicines removed from repeats with zero explanation. You can tell even the empathetic helpful staff have less options or power to assist. It's so easy, as a patient of C'fields today, to just give up. I dread needing them. I do everything I can to hold off making contact. A recent visit with a GP highlighted why demand on A&E grows. You can leave GP appointment without any attempt at addressing even serious issues. Made to feel an inconvenience. Made to feel you can't say exactly what you've waited 5+ weeks to say because it'll take more than one sentence. So you get worse and emergency medicine ends up being needed. It was totally avoidable. Notice GPs demand to see you (must be some incentive), yet unashamedly clock watch the entirety of an appointment. Patient's only crime is perhaps having quite the history. I was growing more concerned with each visit, or 2 sentence text message GP input, but the most recent visit shocked me.

recent_reviews.author: xEx xCx
recent_reviews.text: 1st appointment. I had an appointment with Dr Bruce, she was very kind understanding and had read my econsult prior to my appointment which meant we could get things dealt with quickly, even though I had further difficulties which were additional to my original appointment request she reassured me and I felt she took everything into consideration and helped me put things in perspective. xEx 03/02/25 2nd appointment. Follow up appointment with Dr Wong. She was absolutely wonderful she was extremely knowledgeable about my condition and seemed genuinely kind and understanding, she is a locum GP. She, like all GPs in every practice was running about 30 minutes late but this doesn’t bother me one bit because in my opinion it shows that they are taking the necessary time with patients rather than rushing one in and out as quickly as possible. Reception staff, I know the administration and reception staff have a hard time when it comes to dealing with the public but I have never had a bad experience, yes it can be frustrating sometimes when one is not well but credit must also be given to these individuals who have a difficult job. I had gone to the chemist to get my prescription but realised I had forgotten to ask for the other medication I need so I went back to the practice which was technically closed. I spoke to a lovely receptionist who popped an emergency request through to another Dr so I can hopefully collect my other medication tomorrow. I tried to do it online but apparently there is a limit as to how many patients can submit forms. All in all I think we are lucky to have such a nice practice and staff team. Keep up the good work I STILL APPRECIATE ALL YOU DO! Thank you all! And for those who moan about the practice and staff maybe try treating others the way you would like to be treated. RESPECT OUR NHS! 💜 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 xEx 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿💜

recent_reviews.author: Rudolf Berki
recent_reviews.text: I recently joined Portlethen Medical Centre in Portlethen (Aberdeen), but I wish I had not. Although the doctors I met seem to be quite friendly, the administration part is hopeless. Some of the staff are helpful, but I find most of them unkind, even quite arrogant. I am off work due to a hand injury and need fit notes, but when it comes to it, it is a terrible nightmare to scramble one from them when needed. They take their time, which should not take more than a few minutes to write, and if you ask questions, they can be quite rude, and they shake you off as if you were nobody. So, unless they improve their attitude toward their patients (to whom they should be grateful that they are in a quite comfortable practice) and are more caring and professional, I do not recommend them.

One time I was in dire pain due to my back - I was upset on the phone and the people guiding the call were nothing short of empathetic and helpful. Do you get appointments straight away always? No. That's once again not the fault of the staff but overburdened and underfunded services. However, whenever I've had a small query or something wrong they've almost always immediately gotten back to me on the phone and have been helpful.

recent_reviews.author: Yeung Chan
recent_reviews.text: Last Wednesday morning, I returned to this clinic because I had a trigger finger surgery earlier. After the stitches were removed, I found that the wound healing was not ideal, so I returned to the clinic to seek their advice. This time, when I returned to the clinic, a nurse carefully helped me observe my wound first. There was also a nursing student on the scene. Because my English communication is not very good, they tried to help me call a translator, but the call was not connected. Fortunately, they were very patient and explained it to me carefully using the translation app on their mobile phone. In addition, there was a more experienced nurse who helped to understand my situation. So I feel very relieved to leave my wound to you to take care of it. Thank you very much, and the front desk staff. Every time I go to this clinic, they are all very polite and helpful. 👍🏻 I also want to praise the nursing student that day. I can feel your enthusiasm. You really want to help people. You will be a good nurse in the future. 👍🏻

recent_reviews.author: Kasia
recent_reviews.text: My regular GP is Dr Fawcett. I have been with her for many years and I feel lucky to have come across a doctor who is competent, skilled, open minded and also caring. My medical issues are acute and disabling. I haven’t once felt invalidated by her. I dread the day she decides to take a break or move practices. It’s hard to describe but before I had her as my GP I spent years going to various doctors trying to figure out why I am in constant and acute bladder pain. The blank faces of some doctors (in other surgeries) and lack of interest and hope for resolution was hard to take. This doctor encouraged me to research and I finally started reading and educating myself which led to finding out about a drug which helped. This has improved my condition making my life less unbearable. This week I met two new doctors. Dr Nelson who was just fantastic and sorted out my problem with dosette box and Dr Henderson, another brilliant doctor who wrote a letter for me and put a lot of effort into wording it just right. My experience is that this surgery is unique in the high level of attention and quality of care they provide. It’s outstanding.

recent_reviews.author: Amélie May
recent_reviews.text: Had nothing but horrible experiences with this GP surgery since moving to university nearby. Every time I have called the reception staff have been consistently rude, dismissive and unhelpful. Every time I order my prescriptions to a local pharmacy they never arrive and I, or the pharmacist, have had to chase them up multiple times. This has often meant I go without important medication, even though I order them with plenty of time. An exception is Dr Jessica Lynas, who when I saw her was lovely - extremely understanding and receptive to my issues, listened to everything I had to say and discussed solutions in depth with me. However, I was made to feel extremely uncomfortable by one of the male GP’s I previously saw and his comments to me. He repeatedly asked me if I needed birth control and asked about my sexual activity though it was completely unrelated to my problem and denied at the beginning of the appointment. As a 19-year-old girl, this seemed very inappropriate and understandably made me uncomfortable leaving me very confused and angry. Overall a poorly run and insensitive practice which provides less than the basic standard of care and human respect and needs an extensive review. A wholly unpleasant experience which has caused me to switch surgery.

recent_reviews.author: Margaret Morrison
recent_reviews.text: Dr Gibson's consulting style was paternalistic, not a good choice. The appointment went on longer than necessary. I felt I knew what would help given my limited options. I'm extremely resilient despite everything. I've coped with my struggles for 50+ years yet she didn't seem to appreciate that. Could have got the appointment completed in under 5 minutes but she proceeded to press me on my reasons for wanting my Summary Care Record. She did not respect my boundaries when I told her my reason for requiring my Summary Care Record wasn't any of her business, just her way of asserting control and gathering information. Yet, she still pressed me multiple times for further details, not respecting patient boundaries. This further antagonised me and given that the reason I required the Summary Care Record was due to multiple dismissals for a diagnosis now privately acquired it didn't go down well. She's dismissed me in the past when I was perimenopausal, progesterone intolerant which I didn't realise at the time, and undiagnosed ADHD. I was refused any hrt input at the appointment, she dismissed my concerns as being down to "anxiety not hormones". 🤔🙄. Give me strength. I was early 50s with no hrt, progesterone intolerant and undiagnosed ADHD. The issue was most certainly hormones as I later discovered I was progesterone intolerant. Five stars for the ability to antagonise the patient so badly it impacts their mental health.

recent_reviews.author: CroissantKid
recent_reviews.text: We've been registered with Burvill House for nearly 8 years, and I have never had trouble getting an appointment. Yes, the old system was a pain, but the new system allows you to put your request through quicker and for the doctors to triage you quicker. The doctors have been friendly and respectful and helped me through a myriad of health problems. A big thanks in particular to Dr Elder, Dr Bateman, Dr Tangang who have all been considerate and professional each time I have seen them. My only qualm is the hygiene of the practice - you have to use a touch screen to check in (considering people who visit are sick!). Additionally, to get out of the surgery, you also have to use touch buttons and also not wearing gloves when checking over babies (I also didn't see any visible hand sanitiser on the nurses desk either!) And there is no sanitiser near the check in touch screen every time I have visited! However, locking the surgery toilets feels like a sensible hygiene precaution as the surgery is located in a heavy footfall traffic area, I can imagine a lot of random people wanting to just use it!

recent_reviews.author: Margaret Newbold
recent_reviews.text: This surgery has changed beyond recognition sadly from having fantastic doctors when i joined- every one of them was outstanding:- Dr Edwards, Dr Machin, Dr Kavi, Dr Evans, and all those at this teaching practice. However after they all retired post pandemic, I have only ever seen locums and no continuity of care. I rarely go now as I don’t see any point going to be told you look healthy!! This after feeling poorly for many weeks and having several health conditions with no regular follow ups or anything. Getting older isn’t good at the best of times but to be judged because I’m not overweight, non smoker or drinker is beyond me. My dad’s incurable cancer was undiagnosed many years ago by another local surgery as was my mom’s heart attack because both were slim and “healthy” Sad that this surgery isn’t a patch on how it once was when I first joined and was taken seriously then referred to a cardiologist specialist who diagnosed my conditions. I will lifelong be grateful to Dr Kavi and to Dr Edwards for referring my aunt and catching her cancer very early and also for walking to another elderly aunt’s in snow and ice when I was concerned about her breathing. He kept her going into her 90s and was so good caring for her and my dear mom’s palliative care. Doctors like these are a rarity today sadly. Receptionists are still good but previous retirees were something special.

recent_reviews.author: Helen Wright
recent_reviews.text: I always find the service at BoA to be outstanding - through every touch point - Reception Team, Phone Team, Pharmacy Team, Health Care Assistants, Nurse Practitioners, GPs, Mental Health Practitioners and Practice Management. Sorry if I've missed anyone out! The system itself has also improved massively since being reviewed a few years ago. Your BoA team are efficient, timely, professional, supportive and very friendly. I use the surgery a lot for several long term health conditions. I've had a particularly tough few years health-wise. Without your service and staff I would have found it impossible to navigate and manage. Thanks so much to the whole team! I'm incredibly grateful :) Having lived abroad, I never take our free point of access to primary healthcare for granted. We are incredibly privileged and lucky to have primary health care trusts, NHS etc. when so many others less fortunate abroad do not. Great staff and service in challenging circumstances is not easy. Please know that you're all doing fantastic work :) Thank you all at BoA Health Centre.

recent_reviews.author: Virginia Tolomei
recent_reviews.text: If I could give 0 stars I would. I haven't been their patient in years but I just found out that their horrible treatment of my partner caused a delay in diagnosing him correctly. When he went complaining about certain symptoms he was dismissed as being fat while those symptoms were signs of multiple sclerosis. Had they treated him like a person and run some tests he could have been diagnosed years before he actually did and he might not have lost his eyesight in one eye and be in a way better condition than he is. As for me they used me as a practice dummy by taking my blood 4 times for one simple test that they ended up never performing (they lost the first sample, didn't take enough blood the second time, tested me for the wrong thing the third time, took my blood the fourth time only to admit they didn't know what kind of test I needed) and I had to go private. They also promised me a phone call to discuss my fertility struggles and I took time off work to be able to have that conversation only they never called. When I called them myself I was told in a rude and patronising tone that I was never scheduled for a phone call despite me having a text from them confirming the phone appointment and when I started crying out of frustration and stress for my situation they hung up on me. Avoid them like the plague.

recent_reviews.author: M C
recent_reviews.text: This surgery is the most unprofessional uncaring doctors I have been to yet. I have had numerous issues regarding appointments, the fact they do everything in their power to not speak to you over the phone, sassy unprofessional receptionists the list goes on. - I had made a request for an appointment 2 weeks ago. I heard absolutely nothing back not even a phone call to ask details about the issue. I understand nhs gets busy but that’s just lack of care. - I’ve had medications in the past that I’ve had to take myself off due to a dr here stating they put through refill prescriptions and upon going to the pharmacy they would not have done this. This happened 4x before I took myself of the medication. - I called today to inform them that I would no longer be looking for an appointment (the one I put a request in for 2 weeks ago) and that I would be looking at finding a new surgery due to the lack of response. I couldn’t even get an apology from the women on the phone. - not to mention I paid £40-60 for a doctors note that had to be chased over a period of 3 months. For a surgery that is partnered with a university and an nhs practice in general this place has let me down regarding both mental and physical health and should be utterly ashamed. It’s not just a job this is people’s real lives and real wellbeing’s and health. This place needs to seriously look at how it currently handles appointment requests and needs to immediately put receptionist staff into training on how to come across kind and caring rather than sounding like your asking for something silly or as if they aren’t just sat their working a job they don’t want to be at. I totally understand it can be a rough job for both receptionists and drs.

recent_reviews.author: Joseph Fort
recent_reviews.text: My experience with Elm Hayes Surgery has raised serious concerns about the way the practice manages patient care and complaints. I want to share this so others can be cautious and, ideally, avoid similar issues. During a consultation, I clearly communicated a history of a serious condition, yet I was misdiagnosed and left to manage the situation alone. No referral was made, no written contact details were provided (contrary to their stated clinical process), and no follow-up occurred. Red flags consistent with NICE Guidance were missed. This resulted in a delay in accessing appropriate treatment and caused unnecessary distress. I was led to believe I had a minor issue, when in fact it was a recurrence of a much more serious condition. The practice appears to lack sufficient knowledge and training related to conditions like mine and should not be managing such cases. Several opticians later told me the GP’s actions were deeply concerning and showed what appears to be a fundamental misunderstanding of these conditions. When I submitted a formal, professionally written complaint, the process was slow, dismissive, and lacked transparency. A senior review I specifically requested was only carried out after repeated follow-ups, and when it finally arrived, it simply reiterated the original explanation without engaging with the evidence I had provided. It was clearly rushed and showed no meaningful engagement from the senior GP. Most troubling of all: in response to a subject access request, the surgery confirmed that the practice holds no documentation whatsoever regarding how my complaint was assessed or triaged. There were no internal notes, no formal consideration, no correspondence, and no record of escalation. According to their own words, the complaint was considered in “a passing conversation” (their words), which reflects a complete lack of care and respect for a patient raising legitimate concerns. The response also confirmed that what amounts to a restriction had been placed on my future care—without my knowledge—via a system note that effectively blacklisted me from seeing the GP in question. This was seemingly because she did not want to see me again after I questioned her judgement, and reception staff were instructed to conceal this from me. All of this suggests the complaint was never properly investigated or taken seriously. The practice seemed more focused on self-protection than accountability—raising serious concerns about governance and responsiveness. Their handling of the Subject Access Request was evasive and breached ICO compliance requirements, with deadlines repeatedly missed. Although my condition is now being managed, the experience has left me with a complete loss of trust in the practice. I believe the GP I saw demonstrated a serious lack of judgement and care, resulting in a delay in treatment that has affected my life. While the practice has committed to some process changes, these were not directly related to my case. No sincere apology has been offered. In fact, their response felt spiteful—punitive, simply because I raised concerns. I strongly urge others to be cautious when dealing with GPs at Elm Hayes, especially if you have a complex or recurring health issue. Patients deserve to be listened to, supported, and taken seriously—not left to chase their own care or complaints. My experience is that GPs at this practice seem to operate with a sense of entitlement and status, believing this shields them from the concerns of the very people they are meant to serve. Elm Hayes appears unwilling or unable to learn from its mistakes or show empathy. Their priority seems to be self-preservation. If you question them, their instinct is to become defensive and retaliatory. My advice: find another practice, even if it means going out of area. The review scores here speak for themselves. Find a practice that believes in caring for patients.

recent_reviews.author: Tom Caton
recent_reviews.text: PART 1: I’m not one for knocking the health services normally, but when someone close has had a bad experience I guess the need is there to speak up. A family member, who would prefer to remain nameless went into the surgery earlier today with an issue that had previously saw him see a doctor immediately; receive injections (in the surgery) due to what was potentially a life-threatening condition and have the doctor immediately call an ambulance for him. However, earlier on today the madam behind the counter took it upon herself to declare that said family member would not be seeing a doctor, in what would by all accounts sound like a ‘greater-than-thou’ voice of authority. We all know the type. The one’s who let a little bit of power go to their head. The one’s who think they’re being forthright and accurate but sound like complete and utter swines. Of course, diplomatically speaking, tough decisions are part and parcel of these jobs and the folk in that role will no doubt rise and fall based on their decisions. However, we’re not talking about a landlord’s decision as to whether someone drinks in their pub or a shopkeeper’s decision as to who is served on their premises. These are lives we’re dealing with. Surely any doubts should be cast aside even if it’s in the ‘just in case’ category. But Cruella’s actions had consequences which meant that a situation which could have made my family member’s day a lot less stressful turned into a bit of a nightmare which ended up with him in hospital, subjected to numerous tests and (at present) at least one overnight stay. You could argue these things would have happened anyway, but a little bit of consideration, kindness and thought would have made things much easier. Would it have been too difficult to call for a doctor, just in case? Just for a second opinion? I highly doubt it. The arrogant so and so who made the call: Does she have the medical knowledge to send someone packing and so nonchalantly tell them to call 111 or at best go straight to A&E, especially after she was advised of what happened the previous time such a thing occurred? Would a ‘better safe than sorry’ approach have been more appropriate? It’s easy stamping down your authority, being direct when you’re in that position, but where’s the empathy? The compassion? The commitment to the patient? Maybe it will take a worse outcome next time for the receptionist to change her attitude, but next time it might be too late for the person on the receiving end of her authoritative ways. recent_reviews.raw_card_text: Tom Caton1 reviewEdited a year ago PART 1: I’m not one for knocking the health services normally, but when someone close has had a bad experience I guess the need is there to speak up. A family member, who would prefer to remain nameless went into the surgery earlier today with an issue that had previously saw him see a doctor immediately; receive injections (in the surgery) due to what was potentially a life-threatening condition and have the doctor immediately call an ambulance for him. However, earlier on today the madam behind the counter took it upon herself to declare that said family member would not be seeing a doctor, in what would by all accounts sound like a ‘greater-than-thou’ voice of authority. We all know the type. The one’s who let a little bit of power go to their head. The one’s who think they’re being forthright and accurate but sound like complete and utter swines. Of course, diplomatically speaking, tough decisions are part and parcel of these jobs and the folk in that role will no doubt rise and fall based on their decisions. However, we’re not talking about a landlord’s decision as to whether someone drinks in their pub or a shopkeeper’s decision as to who is served on their premises. These are lives we’re dealing with. Surely any doubts should be cast aside even if it’s in the ‘just in case’ category. But Cruella’s actions had consequences which meant that a situation which could have made my family member’s day a lot less stressful turned into a bit of a nightmare which ended up with him in hospital, subjected to numerous tests and (at present) at least one overnight stay. You could argue these things would have happened anyway, but a little bit of consideration, kindness and thought would have made things much easier. Would it have been too difficult to call for a doctor, just in case? Just for a second opinion? I highly doubt it. We appreciate your feedback and are sorry for the frustration caused. We are genuinely sorry to hear about your experience and understand how distressing it is to be without medication. For reasons of confidentiality, we are unable to discuss individual cases on a public platform. Our GPs frequently work well beyond 6.30pm, after the reception team have gone home, in order to manage clinical workload and patient requests. We regret the frustration this situation has caused and welcome direct contact so concerns can be addressed properly.

recent_reviews.author: Nonnie Fox
recent_reviews.text: The staff at this surgery are so kind. Unfortunately their decision to move to an AI appointment booking model, with no alternative via phone or in person, has impacted my ability to access my GP severely. I live with chronic pain and other disabilities, this booking system keeps telling me to call myself an ambulance and that no appointments are available for me to book. If these symptoms occurred in a generally healthy person they should absolutely go to hospital, but A+E would not be able to help me as it's not an acute condition. I tried calling to explain this situation and was met with "we can no longer book appointments over the phone", the lonely receptionist told me to try their Ask A Question option instead. I did so, however you only get 300 characters (including spaces) to ask said question. Trying to fit the relevant information, that would explain the need to see my GP and not A+E or yet another Physio referral, is impossible without it reading as hysteria. I can't go to another GP, the other Vernon St surgery also uses this system and I simply cannot consistently walk/bus) to further surgeries (I don't drive and taxis are not in the budget). I can't imagine that I am the only one being negatively impacted by this god awful system so if you need a new GP and are disabled? Look elsewhere if you can.
