recent_reviews.author: Nigel
recent_reviews.text: Wilson St Surgery is not the easiest to get an appointment at, you have to make sure your ready as soon as the appointments go online at 8am. Then its a race against time to read the times and which Dr is which for each appointment so you have to be quick and I've seen it many times where by 08.01 ALL the appointments are gone ! Sometimes theres 8 or less appointments, occasionally more but not loads. And if you try to ring up the receptionists give you the standard answer " I'm afraid all the appointments are gone you'll have to try again tomorrow". The appointment system is shockingly stressful, I know many surgeries have similar issues but it needs sorting. You used to be able to ring up and the receptionist would say they can book you in at the end of surgery, but they don't even offer to do that now. Also if you ring to try and make an appointment the receptionist's will ask what the problem is, I'm pretty sure they've been instructed to say that but that is really none of their business and the reason usually given is so they can put you with the right Dr, I know Drs have specialties but I would like to think that ALL Drs have the capabilities to diagnose most ailments. Another problem is consistency, every Dr has a slightly different opinion about treatment etc so to not be able to see the same Dr when you have an ongoing health issue that you've seen them before with makes no sense and can be stressful for elderly patients like ourselves. My wife and I are in our 60's and we try and see the same Dr for the above reasons, Dr Richards is a very understanding Dr as are several at the practice and he has a fantastic 'bedside' manor same as Drs Daniels and Fyle before they retired from the practice. The practice itself is not a bad practice but the appointment system is a lottery as to whether you can get an appointment, also their doesn't seem to be many appointments available at Taddington Road when you go online. which is within walking distance for us. We aren't stupid people and are aware the N.H.S in general is under pressure. But Drs surgeries are mostly private partnership's with a growing number run by private corporations, much like vets. So patients need more availability for appointments, the online system is a good way to access these along with repeat prescriptions, but while we are quite savvy with the internet some elderly patients are not, so appointments should also be able to be booked ' easily' over the phone. Thank you Nigel M Cooper

recent_reviews.author: Maeve Smyth
recent_reviews.text: The GPs here are really dismissive and make you feel like you are wasting their time. I had an allergic reaction which resulted in facial swelling and hives breaking out all over my body - despite not having any known allergies. When I told my GP about this she said that 'we cannot do an allergy test for every person that has an allergic reaction, everyone has these reactions at some point'. On the NHS website it states that an allergy test is appropriate if you have had a reaction with an unknown trigger. I don't feel that I can trust the GPs here with my safety and wellbeing anymore. I book an appointment for medical advice, not to be told 'everyone gets sick sometimes, get over it'. Just an update on this - I have now had three separate allergic reactions where I have to been rushed to A&E with serious facial swelling and hives. They are clearly serious as I was put in the resuscitation area as soon as I got to A&E. I still do not know the trigger and I have still been denied an allergy test by my GP so I will be changing to a different surgery as this unacceptable and dangerous.

recent_reviews.text: I think this GP has resigned from helping people. The doctors and staff are simply going through the motions of NHS guidelines and not really interested in helping people approaching them. I’ve paid £3000 to the nhs for a £3 pound service in the last two years, the least they could do is be a little bit helpful to those who are new.

recent_reviews.text: I am writing to express my disappointment regarding an unpleasant experience I recently had with one of your new receptionists, Muskaan. This kind of behaviour is completely unacceptable, especially in a healthcare environment where patients deserve courtesy and respect. I understand that everyone can have an off day, but as a new employee representing your practice, her conduct left a very poor impression. If the centre is hiring new staff, I would urge you to ensure they are trained not only in administrative duties but also in professionalism and patient interaction. I hope this feedback is taken seriously and addressed appropriately, as I would like to continue receiving the high standard of care I’ve always experienced at Harley Grove Medical Centre.

recent_reviews.author: Parveen Rani
recent_reviews.text: UPDATED REVIEW: A SERIOUS WARNING TO PARENTS I am genuinely horrified by what this surgery has put my family through. I requested a straightforward referral to a general paediatrician months ago, yet instead the GP added something to my son’s records that led our private insurance to reject the referral completely. This has now blocked him from being seen privately for years. After I complained, Trowbridge said they had sent an NHS referral, but the letter they gave me contained no details at all. When I contacted the referral team myself, I was told it had been dismissed because it was irrelevant, and the request they sent was not even for the issue my child actually needed help with. It was completely the wrong referral. Because of these mistakes, delays, and confusion, my child has still not been seen by a basic paediatrician. My concerns were dismissed when he was younger by the GPs at Trowbridge, and now that the symptoms are still there, he still has no proper path to care, privately or through the NHS, all because of this surgery’s errors. PLEASE do not take your infant or child to this surgery. In my experience, their incompetence has directly blocked my son from getting crucial medical support.

recent_reviews.author: Mya & Amelia
recent_reviews.text: I’m extremely disappointed with the way I was treated by the receptionist at this health service. I called today to check where I was on the waiting list for an implant removal – something I’ve been trying to arrange through the NHS for over a year. After being promised call backs and follow-ups, I finally received one today, only to be told I was never on the waiting list at all. I was essentially accused of lying. I was then told to go back to my GP, as there was apparently nothing they could do. However, my GP had already referred me to Forest Health Care (FHC), and even gave me their number. FHC could have easily referred me to appropriate services for this issue, but chose not to. What’s even more frustrating is that the receptionist confirmed they do offer an implant removal service and even mentioned that the women's health clinician would be in on Friday. Despite this, she refused to add me to the waiting list or offer any real help. This level of care is unacceptable for a health service that is meant to be supportive and compassionate. My GP is now trying to arrange for a nurse to come in specifically to address this issue – something that shouldn't be necessary if FHC had simply done their part.

recent_reviews.text: Takes several weeks to get an appointment and at my most recent appointment I had two issues I needed to discuss, I was told in no uncertain terms that I could only discuss ONE, so pick !!…. When you finally make an appointment with the doctor you ask for by name, the surgery changes that doctor for the appointment and doesn’t tell you! When you are on life long medication you can only get one month at a time on repeat prescription, you have to allow one week from ordering so in effect you have a 3 week cycle of requesting - collecting. I use the practice because I have to, and because of the one amazing gp I found, if it wasn’t for her … I would have lost my mind, and probably been very poorly!

recent_reviews.author: Laurie
recent_reviews.text: If I could give minus stars, I would. The standard of care and service from this practice has been extremely poor. Since the introduction of the online consultation system, patients were told it would improve access to appointments and reduce waiting times, as well as ease the difficulty of getting through by phone each morning. Unfortunately, this has not been my experience. I submitted an online consultation form and was only told that my request had been triaged and that an appointment would be arranged when available. When I finally received an appointment date — three weeks after the initial consultation — I received multiple reminder texts, only to arrive at the surgery and be told the appointment had been cancelled. This level of delay and disorganisation is unacceptable, especially given the nature of my symptoms and the fact that I have been raising these concerns for over two years. During this time, I have been prescribed various medications, including antidepressants, without a confirmed diagnosis or any proper investigation into the underlying cause of my condition. This approach has left me feeling ignored and unsupported. I have now requested to transfer to another GP practice as the the care I’ve received has been an outright failure on the practice’s part. However, I believe it’s important that this feedback is shared so the practice can review its processes, particularly around triage, communication, and follow-up for ongoing health issues. I would strongly advise anyone considering this practice to look elsewhere.

recent_reviews.author: David Glover
recent_reviews.text: I was promised a telephone call from one of the doctors at Ixworth Surgery following an NHS 111 scare about a blood test that showed an abnormality with my troponin levels. These indicate the possibility of a heart attack. Two weeks later I telephoned the surgery and said I was still waiting for the call. I was told that there was no record of any telephone call booked for a doctor to call me and the receptionist said that a forthcoming appointment with the diabetic nurse would explain all the symptoms of the blood test. I tried to explain to her that the treponin levels were nothing to do with blood sugar levels. She told me that she didn’t know what treponin is. I have total admiration for W.S. Hospital but I have lost all trust with the Ixworth surgery, sadly. I feel frightened and worried about something that NHS 111 considered to be of concern and Ixworth Surgery have failed to react.

recent_reviews.author: Raul Bermudez
recent_reviews.text: I am writing to formally raise a complaint regarding my recent experience when attempting to register and access services at this GP surgery. When I attended in person to register, two reception staff members were engaged in a personal conversation while several patients were waiting in the queue. After waiting several minutes, I politely asked for the registration forms. I was told to wait while they continued their conversation for several more minutes. When I was eventually called, I was given the form with a very poor and dismissive attitude. When I returned with the completed paperwork, the registration process was repeatedly delayed without clear justification. I was asked for an excessive number of documents, one after another, despite already providing valid identification, including my driving licence and immigration status. I was required to attend the surgery twice, with no clear explanation for the repeated requests. In addition, I have been unable to access the surgery by telephone. I have been calling for over four consecutive days from 8:00am, as instructed. Before 8:00am, the message states calls open at 8:00; after 8:00am, the line is either unavailable for over an hour or, when answered, I am told that the urgent appointment window has already passed and that I must call again another day. Given that I am suffering from ongoing and severe pain and urgently need GP care, this lack of access, poor communication, and unprofessional behaviour is extremely concerning. I would appreciate this complaint being reviewed and appropriate action taken to ensure patients are treated with respect and are able to access care in a reasonable and fair manner.

recent_reviews.text: This practice has put my personal safety at risk. I am now contacting the Information Commissioner to make a formal complaint. If my details end up in the wrong hands because of their negligence, I will press charges.

recent_reviews.text: My elderly parents and I attended an appointment on a cold and rainy morning. Despite arriving only 7 minutes late and apologising, we were met with no empathy from either the GP or the receptionist. The receptionist was dismissive, unfriendly, and argued about whether we were 7 or 10 minutes late, showing no understanding of the circumstances or my parents’ needs. The GP reluctantly agreed to see us and repeatedly commented that our lateness would impact the next appointment, even though the waiting room was empty. The consultation felt rushed, despite no other patients waiting. My parents have attended this surgery for years and have never been treated so abruptly or disrespectfully. Overall, the experience lacked courtesy, compassion, and basic customer service — particularly disappointing given the vulnerability of elderly patients.

recent_reviews.author: Christianna Hemmings
recent_reviews.text: Absolutely appalling experience and complete lack of professionalism. I called on Monday to ask about booking a blood test and was told to call back on Wednesday at 8am, which I did. The appointment was booked. On Friday, I called again just to double-check where the blood test would be done, and I was clearly told it would be done at the GP practice at 12:40. Based on this, I cancelled my plans and arranged my day around the appointment. Then, at 4:48pm on Friday, I received a call from the practice. First a receptionist told me I apparently needed to see a doctor first. Then the phone was passed to another woman whose attitude was extremely rude and dismissive. She told me I cannot have the blood test because I’m “too young”, which is ridiculous as I am 24 years old. When I explained that the last time I had blood tests was when I was 12, she said it “doesn’t matter” because it wasn’t done with them — which makes absolutely no sense. I explained I’m concerned about my health and that I feel like I might faint when getting out of bed. Instead of showing any care or reassurance, she interrogated me with “what are you concerned about?” in a tone that made me nervous and uncomfortable. She then said she would need to see me first to check my blood pressure something that was never mentioned in any of the previous three phone calls. The lack of communication is shocking, but what made this experience so upsetting was the dismissive and rude attitude. I was made to feel like I was wasting their time for simply wanting to check my health. Cancelling an appointment at the last minute after repeatedly confirming it, then speaking to a patient this way, is completely unacceptable. This experience caused me unnecessary stress and left me extremely upset. I have lost all trust in this practice.

It may be beneficial for her to receive additional training to reinforce the importance of her role and the responsibility she has in providing a professional and supportive service to patients.

recent_reviews.author: Ben
recent_reviews.text: This is an exceptional GP practice. I’ve been with them for many years and have always felt fully supported and genuinely cared for. Dr Kalimatu, Dr Patel, and the wider team, including specialist doctors such as Dr Ferris, have supported me consistently over the course of many years, particularly in relation to a long-term chronic illness. Throughout that time, they have provided the right guidance, tools, and reassurance to help me manage my condition with confidence. Over the last year, I went through what could have been a potentially life-changing situation, and once again the care I received was outstanding. The doctors, along with the nursing team and wider staff, looked after me with real compassion and professionalism. You are never treated as just another patient hereyou genuinely feel like a valued individual, almost like family. The doctors and nurses take time to listen, understand, and care. Their empathy is real and never rushed, and they consistently go beyond basic clinical care to focus on your overall wellbeing. Having received healthcare in different parts of the country, I can honestly say this practice represents the very best of the NHS. I would not hesitate to recommend the Beaumont Practice to anyone looking for a GP surgery where care, empathy, and professionalism truly come first.

recent_reviews.text: Registered with the High Road surgery since 2003 the service I received has been amazing (first class) I would like to sincerely thank Dr Munazza Ahmad at High Road Surgery, Stuart Crescent, Wood Green for the excellent care she provides. Dr Ahmad is a wonderful doctor who truly listens to her patients. She takes her time during consultations, pays attention to detail, and makes you feel comfortable and respected. It is clear that she genuinely cares about the wellbeing of the people she treats. When I asked for a referral, she handled everything professionally and arranged it without delay. Because of her support, I am now being seen by specialists at North Middlesex University Hospital, which I really appreciate. Dr Ahmad clearly takes her profession to heart. Her kindness, patience, and professionalism make a real difference. Doctors like her remind us how important it is to have compassionate healthcare professionals. Thank you, Dr Ahmad, for your dedication and for treating your patients with such care and respect. This review below is over one year ago Dr Wijeyekoon is a very kind, good listener, assuring and very caring. when it is examing time he never rush. All i can say he is the best Doctor I know. About 3 months ago I requested a referral for NHS OVIVA path to diabetic remission. Dr Wijeyekoon referred me without hesitation and made me feel listened to I also felt that my opinion matters. After 3 months of being on the program the outcome of that referral was very successful and mind blowing . My diabetic is now in Remission. I'm not taking any type of diabetic medication since December 2024. Big up to Dr Gelly as well who is a very good listener, patient and never rushing during physical examination after I recently been diagnosis with new scarcely health issue. Dr Gelly clearly explained and elaborate to me about my new diagnosis and prescribed the best medication 💊 which unfortunately was no more manufactured according to the pharmacist. But Dr Gelly go ahead and referred me to go and have MRI for further investigation. and promised to get to the bottom of this new health scary and find a solution. This made me feel better already and hope for fully recovery while I'm waiting for MRI appointment date. Lastly Dr Gelly make sure and explained to me very clearly about not prescribed other oral medicines for the new diagnosis which could have interfered with my currently medication or worsen the situation, of my other longer time diagnosis. This is professional to the highest level 👌 I'm grateful & thank you Dr Wijeyekoon and Dr Gelly for listening. "KEEP UP THE GOOD WORK". YOUR THE BEST Doctors at High Road Surgery. (Sayda Eunice Noor ) 💪 💪 💪

recent_reviews.author: Madalina-Ramona Ripa
recent_reviews.text: Look, I’ve been with this GP for over 7 years now and have switched between 3 or 4 different ones in that time. I have a family, and I’ve heard all sorts of stories, but this is different. The reason I chose this GP is because it’s right across the street, so it’s incredibly convenient for us. I registered myself and my family there, and I was told it would take about 5 days to complete the process. On the second day, I tried to book an appointment online as I needed, and they called me right away. Two days later, they called again to follow up and check if the issue had been resolved. I’ve never encountered a GP that genuinely cares this much. I’ve spoken to several people there, and every single one of them was professional, helpful, and polite. I honestly don’t understand how this practice has a 3.3-star rating – they deserve nothing less than a 10/10. They truly deserve better reviews, and I wanted to share my positive experience. We need more GPs like this one! Thank you!

recent_reviews.author: Salman Aybars
recent_reviews.text: They have the worst appointment system I’ve ever seen. I seriously want to change my GP as soon as possible. I haven’t experienced any rude behaviour from the staff so far, so I can’t blame them — but their appointment system is absolutely rubbish. You have to fill out a very long online form, and then it says someone will call you in a few days. You can’t even fill out the form at just any time or day — it only works during business hours on weekdays. It’s not like you’re getting an appointment right away, so why restrict access to the form? Ridiculous. And if you happen to miss the call for any reason, nothing happens afterward — it just ends there. Once, I filled out that long form again because I had no other choice, and after a few days, I got a text saying they booked me an appointment for a specific date and time. Why don’t you ask me first if that day and time work for me? How can you randomly assign appointments without checking with the patient? What a ridiculous system. My previous GP was so much better — I could log into the online system whenever I wanted, answer a few quick questions, and then see all the available dates and times. I could choose the one that suited me best. But this place is a total disaster. You have to go through so much hassle just to book a simple appointment…

recent_reviews.author: Paul Burton (aura_paulb)
recent_reviews.text: I feel very lucky to be a patient at Roseworth Surgery. I fact, I’ve had to stop telling people how good it is because they generally don’t believe me!! We are all used to the “hasn’t there been a terrible decline in the quality of general practice” conversation. In my involvement with such conversations, I have found that Roseworth Surgery seems literally to be the only practice (anywhere in the country!!) where you can still get all the things that everyone else complains don’t exist anymore. And in my own objective comparison with the general practices that look after members of my own family (eg my 90 year old father) Roseworth is way out ahead. If you phone at 08:30 in the morning you are very rarely in a queue longer than 5 callers and you are usually through in less than 10 mins. If you need to see or speak to a GP that day you virtually always can. The receptionists are all pleasant. They will be assertive when that is necessary but, in my experience, never rude or aggressive. The GPs are excellent. At present there are four I see regularly. All are very knowledgable, clinically strong, sensible, and if they aren’t sure about something they’ll ask a colleague. They are all nice and friendly to interact with. The practice nurses provide a very valuable service which allows the practice to provide excellent health monitoring programmes, prompt vaccination schedules and to remain on top of regular blood test monitoring. In fact I owe my life to the practice’s routine blood test monitoring mechanism for cardiovascular disease that picked up my Leukaemia in 2022 just as the malignant cells were about to break out of the bone marrow. The IT systems are up to date and work well and, in particular, repeat prescriptions and access to your own personal medical information run very smoothly. In my case, I interact very effectively with the practice via their interface with the NHS app. In summary, I can wholeheartedly recommend Roseworth Surgery at every level.

recent_reviews.author: Emily Godfrey
recent_reviews.text: ⭐ 1 star Absolutely appalling behaviour from the doctors and staff. My father rang simply to enquire about his medication — a basic, reasonable question that any patient should be able to ask. During the call, staff clearly believed he had hung up, and proceeded to speak about him in a disgusting and unprofessional manner, including calling him an “arsehole” and making other derogatory remarks. This wasn’t a misunderstanding or a poor bedside manner — it was outright disrespect. Hearing medical professionals speak about a patient like that is shocking and completely unacceptable. It raises serious concerns about how patients are treated when they’re not “on the line.” Healthcare staff are meant to show compassion, professionalism, and basic human decency. What we experienced was the exact opposite. No apology, no accountability — just behaviour that would be unacceptable in any workplace, let alone a medical setting. I would strongly advise others to think twice before trusting this practice with their care or that of their loved ones.

recent_reviews.text: For anyone considering joining this practice I would look elsewhere. They are clearly so over subscribed that they are totally negligent to the point of dangerous. recent_reviews.text: Dear Sir or Madam, I am writing to submit a formal complaint regarding my experience at the GP clinic located at 77 Sandy Lane, Mansfield, which occurred today. I had a pre-booked appointment for my 3-month-old baby at a specific scheduled time. We arrived on time and checked in at reception, where I was informed to wait. After waiting for 30 minutes without any update, I approached the reception desk to ask how much longer the wait would be, as I was holding my infant. I was told to continue waiting, without any explanation or estimated waiting time. In total, we waited for 1 hour and 30 minutes. When I approached reception again, I was informed that I would need to book another appointment for a different day. My child was not seen at all. I find this situation unacceptable, especially considering the age of my child. No explanation, apology, or alternative solution was offered. After an excessive wait with a young baby in my arms, I was forced to leave without receiving any medical care. I request that this complaint be formally reviewed and that I receive a written response explaining how this situation occurred and what measures will be taken to prevent similar situations in the future.

recent_reviews.author: Sarah-Ellen Wooller
recent_reviews.text: I am very impressed with the new appointment system. I just filled in a form and within a few hours I receive a phone call to book me in for an appointment. Gone are those stressful days being on hold and number 30 in the queue! For me this new system is fabulous. Sadly, I don't think it caters for all, e.g the elderly who are not confident using ICT. I feel there should be an independent phone line for the elderly so they can still call up as opposed to needing a device to fill in a form. UPDATE - 20/06/25 My elderly parents-in-law were struggling to navigate the new online system. After I assisted them, we discovered there appeared to be a technical issue. When we contacted the surgery, we spoke with Sam Busby, who provided outstanding customer service. Sam was incredibly helpful and even invited us to visit the surgery to resolve the problem in person. During our visit, Sam demonstrated exceptional patience and understanding with my parents-in-law, and we successfully resolved the issue. Sam's dedication to patient care was remarkable - they were prepared to work beyond their scheduled hours to ensure we left satisfied. Fortunately, this wasn't necessary as Sam efficiently resolved the problem. THANK YOU Sam :-)

recent_reviews.author: Andrea Devonport
recent_reviews.text: I'm reviewing Spilsby Doctors pharmacy on behalf of two clients that I care for . In the last week I have visited the pharmacy 6 times before being able to obtain all the medication that had been ordered each time being told if you can call back tomorrow we will have the stock in , this didn't happen at one point I was told if you would like to wait 2hours until we have checked the delivery you can . This morning on my 5th visit I was given what I thought was the remaining items only to find when delivering them to my clients that one item was missing , apparently it was in the fridge and the pharmacy assistant failed to include it with the order . My clients who are housebound and pay £20 an hour for care services are seriously out of pocket this week due to the incompetence of Spilsby Doctors pharmacy. I'm sure I'm not the only person who is so frustrated with the service provided as two people in the queue in front of me rolled their eyes and were clearly unhappy . I've advised my clients who live 6 miles from Spilsby surgery to change to Horncastle GP as I know the service there is excellent. I would have awarded zero stars for this review however the system doesn't allow this

recent_reviews.author: Karl Turner
recent_reviews.text: You have more chance of winning the lottery than getting an appointment here. If I want an appointment I can’t book one for date X at a time of my choosing, no matter how many weeks in advance it is. I have to be ready to call at 8am, sit in a queue, and have to accept a same-day appointment. This isn’t possible for me, I have to work. And what if you can’t connect Woosehill to your NHS app? You’ll get a ‘computer says no’ when you seek help from the receptionist who’ll tell you to ‘pop in’ to their workshop on a Wednesday from 1pm - 3pm. Sorry, love, but I work that day. Oh, and did I mention the day I drove there to book an appointment in person as I couldn’t get through on the phone? Well, guess what - I was sent away and told I have to call them at 8am the next day if I want an appointment! UPDATE: Very pleased with the new booking system; very easy to sign in upon arrival; VERY unhappy with my interactions with the asthma doctor. She was abrupt, repeatedly interrupted me (which required me to repeat myself on more than one occasion to continue communicating what I wanted to say) and didn’t listen to my questions. In particular, when I asked a question about how her diagnostic machine worked, she gestured at a piece of paper and told me to “find the answer there”. RUDE, RUDE, RUDE. I came within a hair’s breadth of telling her how rude she is. (Think: Emma Thompson (the nurse) from Bridget Jones 3.)

recent_reviews.author: Fred Parker
recent_reviews.text: Dr. Baxter has been our family doctor for probably the last thirty years. He was extremely kind to my mother when she came to us for the last few months of her life and is always very friendly, easy to talk to and has seen us through the highs and lows of family life. I recently developed rheumatoid arthritis and saw Dr. Devlin who is, I think, quite new to the practice. She was very thorough and concerned and referred me to a specialist. I was impressed with the way she dealt with me but even more impressed when she followed up the appointment with a telephone call. I explained that the appointment was six weeks away and she told me to leave it with her and she would see if anything else could be done. Within a few minutes she rang back to say that she had consulted with another doctor and if I came straight in she could give me a steroid injection. Yesterday morning I could hardly move but this morning I was able to lie on my back in the boot of my old car and refit the boot lock which had gone wrong! Both boot lock and my ancient body are now working perfectly and it is all down to Dr. Devlin, who, really put herself out to help as much as she could. Thank you very much!

recent_reviews.text: I needed to visit the GP surgery this morning to request an appointment for an issue that is causing me pain and affecting my sleep. On entering the GP surgery in Staveley there's a large seemingly hand written sign saying that you won't receive an appointment straight away as it needs to go to a 'clinician led triage team'. On approaching the receptionist she seemed more interested in fobbing me off and telling me it would be quicker for me to do it myself online. I'm not tech adverse, far from it but I don't want another app on my phone and I'm not signing up to use another web portal when, quite literally, there are people being paid to sit there and deal with the public. A 'clinician led triage team', what exactly is this? I have no idea, is it a team of clinicians or just one and several other people who just follow a script? Again, no idea, the receptionist didn't seem able to tell me either. After the information was reluctantly taken, I was informed that someone would be in touch, when exactly no one could tell me, great and not really a problem if you don't work, not so great if you work and have to notify people and potentially move appointments, meetings, etc. All this happened just after 8am this morning, it's now 10:20 and guess what, total silence from the GPs, nothing, NADA. This system is a joke.

recent_reviews.author: Sian Brookes-Wilde
recent_reviews.text: I just wanted to say a huge thank you to everyone at South Park Surgery. Every doctor we’ve seen has been kind, professional and really helpful, and we’ve always felt listened to and well looked after. As a family it makes such a difference knowing we have a GP surgery we can trust. A special thank you has to go to Nurse Rachel, who has been absolutely incredible with both of my children. She has been so patient, gentle and reassuring with them, and has such a lovely way of putting both kids and parents at ease. It’s clear she genuinely cares about the families she looks after, and we’re so grateful for the support she’s given us. I also want to mention the reception team, who are always so helpful, friendly and understanding. They often deal with a lot, but they’re consistently kind and do their best to help however they can. We’re really lucky to have such a caring and supportive surgery. Thank you to the whole team — it’s very much appreciated.

recent_reviews.author: Laura Mobey
recent_reviews.text: (Laura Kenyon) I felt compelled to leave a review (as a former Elmwood patient) after my recent interactions with the staff at Stewart Medical Centre. Although I have no axe to grind regarding my historical dealings with Elmwood, I always received professional and timely help during my 40 plus years with them, I have noticed a marked positive difference since Stewart medical centre acquired the Elmwood practice. The administrative staff will go above and beyond to ensure that enquiries are dealt with swiftly and this helpful attitude is always accompanied by a cheerful disposition. It makes ringing the practice a pleasure, knowing that you will receive efficient yet empathetic advice and resolutions! It is much easier to find an appointment now, whether that be prebookable or on the day. I admittedly have struggled before the takeover when trying to get appointments for ill children with tonsillitis, ear infections etc. My daughter, who has suffered with tonsillitis has been seen by the pharmacist (and prescribed antibiotics) more times than a GP or Nurse during her time at Elmwood; I could never get her an appointment. This problem appears to have been well and truly resolved as my son needed antibiotics for an extended period and easily secured several appointments at Stewart. Well done Stewart Medical Centre staff. You run an efficient and customer friendly operation which is truly appreciated!

recent_reviews.author: Katie Bai
recent_reviews.text: Since the GP practices merged, it has become almost impossible to book an appointment. I’ve been trying for over a month with no success. Every time I call or check online, there are no available slots — even for basic health concerns like allergy management. It’s frustrating and worrying, especially for patients with ongoing health needs who are told to “try again next week” with no guarantee. The system simply doesn’t seem to have enough capacity after the merger. I understand demand is high, but patients deserve at least a reliable way to get support within a reasonable timeframe. I’ve already had allergy testing done, and need medication review and risk assessment. But the delay has left me with no support plan, even though I’m regularly exposed to known allergens. This isn’t safe.

recent_reviews.author: Tom Bould
recent_reviews.text: So time to review, I have been a patient at this GP for little over 6yrs. Dr S (Partner) is an excellent and caring practitioner hence I’ve given 2* not 1. However; During these 6yrs I have constantly been spoken to rudely by Dr. T (Partner). A little over a year ago he tried to blame me for aggressive behaviour which was ironic given it was him stood over me, pointing his finger towards me, firmly speaking, not allowing me to speak, undermining me when I could get a word in and even chasing me through to reception and berating me in front of other patients in a public area because I was asking reception for the complaints procedure. If only he’d listened to my concerns during the consultation. During a reflective period I came to the conclusion it would no longer be healthy to have consultations with this horrid practitioner and asked the practice manager to accommodate this. Within a week they had the audacity to send me a warning letter which I obviously challenged; driven by this unprofessional doctor. The outcome of my challenge was inconclusive and as such I asked for the letter sent to me to be struck off; this never transpired. This broke the camels back. I have now left the surgery and will have to travel to the doctors elsewhere unfortunately as I have ongoing health issues. I find it difficult to comprehend why when a patient challenges a doctor’s professionalism it then gets pinned back towards the patient. There are lots of papers about the power imbalance between these dynamics and they are trained to be aware of them. Clearly this was lost on this practitioner. Any attempt to react towards this genuine review from the surgery or have it removed should not be taken seriously as they will endeavour to uphold their already low status I am sure. I have deliberately removed the full names whilst typing this review for confidentiality reasons. I would seriously recommend to anyone able to please go elsewhere.

recent_reviews.author: Paula Ariel
recent_reviews.text: Doctors should keep up-to-date on medical facts and treatments, and unfortunately this doctor doesn't! After suffering sleepless nights due to menopause symptoms, and after a lot of research, I decided to ask the female doctor at this surgery for a prescription of Oestrogel. Her knowledge was extremely poor, and she said that she always recommended anti-depressants before trying any HRT! After a blood test to prove I was menopausal I had a face to face appointment. I explained to her that anti-depressants is not seen as a correct treatment for menopause any more, and that my mood was fine, just having hot sweats throughout the night. Her reply was that if I wanted any HRT I would need to see a professional at a hospital, but if I wanted treatment straight away she was happy to write a prescription for anti-depressants. Hospital appointment came through with a 12 month wait, so I moved to a practice in Cheadle, given the gel straight away, and now have no symptoms. recent_reviews.text: I would like to formally complain about the unacceptable and unprofessional behaviour of the reception staff. I attended the facility seeking urgent medical assistance for my mother, who was experiencing severe difficulty breathing and had a high temperature. When I asked whether a doctor could assess her condition, I was told that I was “joking” and that no doctor would see her because some had gone home and the remaining doctors did not have time. I fully understand that medical staff may be under pressure and that other patients require care; however, my mother’s condition was serious, and we were prepared to wait. At the very least, we expected to receive basic medical advice on what steps to take next. Instead, we were treated with complete disregard and a lack of empathy, which was extremely distressing given the circumstances. Such an attitude towards patients and their families is unacceptable and does not meet the standards of care and professionalism that should be expected.

recent_reviews.author: Andy Metcalf
recent_reviews.text: I am not a regular poster of reviews on google - nor I suspect are 90% of Portcullis Surgery patients. I am certain this means the google reviews do not reflect the typical patient experience of Portcullis Surgery. I am a 73 year old male and have been a patient at Portcullis for over 10 years (dr Beanland). I have had an array of health issues in that time, some serious, most less so, and I have used a lot of Portcullis’ many services.. I have always received responsive, professional and caring support from everyone that works there. Of course they (like the entire NHS) are under immense pressure, there are limits on what they can do, and sometimes issues arise. However, every time I have discussed concerns, politely, they always go the extra mile and ensure my needs are met. If you are disappointed or frustrated with your experience with Portcullis Surgery please try a polite email or phone call rather than posting negative comments and reviews - you will get better results personally, and the staff at an excellent practice, that we are lucky to have in Ludlow, will feel the appreciation they deserve.

Not at all a good start, I’ve already put a request to move back to my previous doctors although they are not much better atleast you only had to wait probably 10 or 15 minutes after your appointment time not 30 minutes and then another 30 to 45 minutes later, Dr Lees was running behind, but it didn’t stop her coffee time, like everyone else’s time didn’t matter, I shall not be going back to this shocking place

recent_reviews.author: dannyw919191
recent_reviews.text: No issues when I’ve actually been able to get an appointment. Unfortunately this is a nationwide issue at the moment and affects a lot of GPs. But how on earth am I meant to ring at set times each day and hope for the best when working full time?! Most of the time you can’t even wait in a queue or even request a callback as there’s too many people doing the same. The result, is “call 111” (the old slopey shoulder approach) who generally tell you to go to A&E, putting yet more pressure on A&E staff who should only be dealing with emergencies, not general appointments that should be dealt with by your GP. Total shambles of a system at the moment.

recent_reviews.author: Kerry Johnson
recent_reviews.text: Didnt have a problem with the surgery until recently since theyve changed their appointment system. Have to do a "triage" online and then a doctor will decide whether an appointment is needed. Not been feeling myself for some time, wanted to see a GP to talk to but recieve a text to say blood test referral at reception. Have blood tests, wanted an appointment to see Dr to talk about further symptoms face to face but then get a phone consultation 2 weeks after blood tests. Felt like I couldnt talk openly about problems as she was more focused on talking about tablets rather than an injection I used to have. Another week's passed by and im feeling worse now, but dont want to do triage again and end up with another telephone consultation or just told to have tests. One thing I hate due to severe anxiety is telephone calls, yet thats all they seem to offer now. Bring back the days of face to face appointments, where you could book them on the day.

recent_reviews.author: Sarah Louise
recent_reviews.text: Utterly appalling service that puts cost-cutting before patient care! This GP surgery has become a disgrace to the NHS and a source of constant frustration and disappointment for families like mine. Time and time again, patients, including children, are fobbed off and redirected to pharmacists, regardless of the nature of the issue. I’ve had to rely on a pharmacist for help more times than I can count, not because it was appropriate, but because the GP refused to engage. This is not the NHS my mother or grandmother relied on and not the one I expect my daughter to grow up with. Watching its rapid decline in recent years has not been subtle. We are witnessing a slow dismantling of a public service that once represented the very best of British values. Something must change. I pay for prescriptions for myself and my eldest son, but a young child should be receiving care, not being brushed aside because the surgery is trying to make ends meet under government pressure. It’s clear that patient care no longer comes first here. Budget cuts seem to have taken priority over even the most basic medical duty, to examine and treat a sick child. The NHS is in decline, and surgeries like this one are accelerating that decline by refusing to stand up for the people they are meant to serve. I will be raising this with my MP. Enough is enough.

recent_reviews.text: Where to begin with this place. Majority of the reception staff are rude and obnoxious with a horrible snooty attitude. The odds of seeing an actual Dr are slim. recent_reviews.author: Daniella Kay
recent_reviews.text: As a new patient at The Welcome Practice, there are several things I appreciate and a few important areas that I believe need improvement. I understand that the practice sees many patients daily and that the staff work very hard, but it’s important to share honest feedback so that patient care can continue to improve. Firstly, the punctuality of the GP practitioners needs urgent improvement. Patients should not be waiting long after their appointment time, especially vulnerable patients. Waiting more than 10 minutes past the scheduled time already feels too long — and during my first new patient appointment, I waited 45 minutes, which is unacceptable. While I understand that some appointments may occasionally run over, such long delays should not be a regular experience. Improving punctuality would greatly improve patient comfort, reassurance, and trust in the service. Secondly, the admin process needs to be more prompt and consistent. Whether it’s medications, sick notes, prescriptions, or other health issues, practitioners should make sure that patients are offered clear alternatives when something is unavailable or when we are unsure of our options. Communication is key, and patients need to feel fully informed. Ensuring that practitioners take time to understand and prioritise patients’ needs is extremely important, especially for those who are newly registered. I also feel the practice would benefit from maintaining a calm, supportive, and organised atmosphere. Every patient has different needs and copes differently, and the environment plays a huge part in making people feel safe, respected, and comfortable. On a very positive note, I want to highlight Amina at reception, who was exceptional. She was caring, helpful, and supportive throughout my registration process. She assisted me with setting up access to my medical records online, answered all my questions at reception, kept me updated about my appointments, and helped with my prescriptions. She is genuinely lovely, and the practice needs more receptionists like her — her kindness and professionalism truly stand out. Overall, I hope the practice takes this feedback seriously and works to improve punctuality, communication, and overall patient support. As patients, we have the right to share our honest experiences, and I believe these improvements would help transform the service into a true five-star experience, especially for new patients joining the practice. Because of the quality of my new patient consultation and the exceptional support from Amina at reception — I am giving this practice 2 out of 5 stars. These were the only reasons I did not give a lower rating. Without those two experiences, my review would have reflected much less. After looking at the clinic’s online reviews, I noticed that many other patients have also shared negative experiences, with a large number of one- and two-star ratings. This shows I am not the only person concerned about the standards and reputation of the practice. As a new patient leaving this review, I truly believe management needs to take these issues seriously and work on them urgently. Improving punctuality, communication, admin efficiency, and overall patient care is essential if the practice wants to rebuild trust and provide a service that meets a five-star standard. Thanks, Daniella Sandja

Improving punctuality would greatly improve patient comfort, reassurance, and trust in the service. Secondly, the admin process needs to be more prompt and consistent. Whether it’s medications, sick notes, prescriptions, or other health issues, practitioners should make sure that patients are offered clear alternatives when something is unavailable or when we are unsure of our options. Communication is key, and patients need to feel fully informed. Ensuring that practitioners take time to understand and prioritise patients’ needs is extremely important, especially for those who are newly registered. I also feel the practice would benefit from maintaining a calm, supportive, and organised atmosphere. Every patient has different needs and copes differently, and the environment plays a huge part in making people feel safe, respected, and comfortable. On a very positive note, I want to highlight Amina at reception, who was exceptional. She was caring, helpful, and supportive throughout my registration process. She assisted me with setting up access to my medical records online, answered all my questions at reception, kept me updated about my appointments, and helped with my prescriptions. She is genuinely lovely, and the practice needs more receptionists like her — her kindness and professionalism truly stand out. Overall, I hope the practice takes this feedback seriously and works to improve punctuality, communication, and overall patient support. As patients, we have the right to share our honest experiences, and I believe these improvements would help transform the service into a true five-star experience, especially for new patients joining the practice. Because of the quality of my new patient consultation and the exceptional support from Amina at reception — I am giving this practice 2 out of 5 stars. These were the only reasons I did not give a lower rating. Without those two experiences, my review would have reflected much less. After looking at the clinic’s online reviews, I noticed that many other patients have also shared negative experiences, with a large number of one- and two-star ratings. This shows I am not the only person concerned about the standards and reputation of the practice. As a new patient leaving this review, I truly believe management needs to take these issues seriously and work on them urgently. Improving punctuality, communication, admin efficiency, and overall patient care is essential if the practice wants to rebuild trust and provide a service that meets a five-star standard. Thanks, Daniella SandjaLike1 Share

recent_reviews.author: Ajith Rao Bairneni
recent_reviews.text: I’m very sad to say that I used to love the service at this surgery, but unfortunately, that’s no longer the case. The recent decision to remove the emergency clinic services feels like a step in the wrong direction. Replacing it with a triage process has made things more complicated and less responsive. When people feel unwell, they come to the clinic seeking help—not to be filtered through a system that delays care. Reception staff should be empowered to assess urgency and offer appointments accordingly. It’s also concerning that we now have only one receptionist actively assisting patients, while the other seat is occupied by someone doing admin work. If the role is administrative, it shouldn’t take up space meant for patient-facing support. That seat matters—especially for parents and vulnerable patients who need quick access and reassurance. I hope the management will reconsider these changes and restore the level of care and accessibility that once made this surgery so dependable.

recent_reviews.author: Libby Williamson
recent_reviews.text: This surgery is diabolical! Getting an appointment is next to impossible. You are constantly told to send in requests online and even though you get a quick response, half the time it seems they haven’t even read your request. They will do anything to not see you in person, happy to prescribe antibiotics without any tests just by looking at your record briefly and if you do get to speak to someone on the phone they are usually rude and make you feel like you are wasting their time. I contacted them today online to request to speak with a dr about some medications my urology and gynaecology specialists at Spire Hull have requested for me (as it had to resort to paying privately to actually be taken seriously and have any investigations done, as this surgery doesn’t see to care) I was told I could have a 10 minute appointment with a nurse practitioner, not the dr and the I would have to wait over a month. Just to discuss some medication which a consultant had already requested I have! I was also told it will take 2 weeks to get my prescription! Not wanting to wait over a month for a simple conversation I called the surgery, explained the situation and was told the dr would send a response online (again). Eventually they responded with a very rudely written note. Stating ‘I suggest you just book an appointment online and I have left a letter you you at reception for the blood tests your consultant needs.’ This surgery is quite possibly the rudest and least understanding of any surgery I have been registered with and make you feel like you are wasting their time. Looking into moving to a different surgery with hopefully much better care!

recent_reviews.text: Dr Adnan is amazing the best doctor I’ve met. We recently joined this surgery after being with Hall Green GP for four years, and it’s honestly like night and day. It had become almost impossible to get an appointment at our old GP, so we decided to change, and it’s been the best decision we’ve made. We’re now able to get same-day appointments with ease, which has made such a difference. I’m especially happy that the surgery caters well to the South Asian community. My mother doesn’t speak English very well, so it’s incredibly helpful that the staff can communicate with her properly. The doctors don’t rush you and really take their time. Dr Kamran is also great and has a lovely sense of humour. All the doctors we’ve seen are very knowledgeable and actually prescribe effective treatment, unlike our previous GP where it felt like we were never given anything helpful. My brother had a head infection for years that our old GP couldn’t resolve. This new surgery prescribed new creams that finally cleared the issue, which we’re so grateful for. The receptionists are also fantastic friendly, polite, and pleasant to speak to. They’re not moody or dismissive like at some other surgeries. It’s only been about a month since we joined, but so far the experience has been excellent. We really hope the surgery continues providing this high level of care. Thank you! 😊

recent_reviews.text: So, so very disappointed with this doctor's surgery. I found an unconscious girl who was very, very cold—so much so I thought she was dead. recent_reviews.author: Wendy Lapworth
recent_reviews.text: I moved back here to look after my elderly step sister in 2017. She was registered with James Fisher medical centre and was extremely happy with how they looked after her, so I was happy to register myself too. I was fortunate enough to get to know some of the doctors that visited the house. They were wonderful to her. I had an ongoing health issue which needed monitoring. I was blown away by the fantastic reception team, my first time meeting them. That has never changed, they care so much that has never faltered after all these years. I was taken ill and ended up in lCU fighting for my life. I did go to the doctors first by taxi and virtually collapsed in the car park. The whole reception team ran out to help me. A huge personal thank you to Jo. Moving on, problems with my heart have developed. When phoning reception saying l don't feel well can l book a call the reply is no, you need to see a doctor, then the doctor treats me or l get admittedl to hospital. This has happened 3 or 4 times all through the observations of that wonderful reception team. I would like to add, a new neighbour moved in 3 months ago and asked about doctors. I told him about James Fisher. He said he had 2 others and would visit all as he would know by the feel of the welcome. He chose James Fisher saying, " I walked in and was made to feel so welcome, no brainer".The nurses are fantastic too, yearly check ups, jabs, bloods, tests. I would like to say a special thank you to Doctor Dick, who takes all the time in the world to listen to me, never interrupting he works out the options to try to help me, I never feel rushed. That helps so much when you feel vulnerable. Thanking all af the other Doctors that have looked after me and responded to calling an ambulance when needed. I feel so very fortunate to be looked after by such a professional and caring practice. Thank you all from the bottom of my heart. Wishing you all a Happy Christmas and a wonderful New year for 2026.

recent_reviews.author: anne_is
recent_reviews.text: After five years I have recently had another test to see how my previously diagnosed osteoporosis is going. This time I only received a much limited response to my test results and so I need an appointment to discuss this further with the GP, Dr. Greaves who sent me the results letter. However trying to get an appointment to do so was problematic and distressing. The receptionist who rang me back in reponse to my call was dismissive, impatient, bordering on the rude and I felt unkind. She did not get why I would need to see the same doctor despite my trying to explain and I felt dismissed out of hand. No appointment was secured so I will have to try again next week. I do understand that sometimes continuity of doctor is not possible but is it necessary for the booking staff to respond in what I consider a decidedly unfriendly and unhelpful way? I think not. Dr. Greaves has always been very helpful and supportive in the past and I am at a loss to understand why this does not appear to be the norm with all staff members.

recent_reviews.author: Valeria R
recent_reviews.text: I have been with this practice for almost seven years now and I feel quite disappointed. Unless I use the eConsult it’s practically impossible to get any support from a GP. If I try to get a phone appointment the minimum wait time is about five weeks. For urgent same day appointments I have to call at 8 am but it’s impossible to get through, in 7 years I’ve never managed to secure one! Even when using the eConsult, the GPs usually just respond electronically, without a quick follow-up call and there’s no way to reply to their messages. This creates unnecessary back and forth (with wrong prescriptions) and feels very impersonal. I haven’t seen or even spoken to a GP in ages everything is done digitally. Even in the past, when I said I wanted to raise a complaint they would just reply digitally again, asking if I was sure I wanted to proceed. This creates yet another round of unnecessary back and forth and puts you off from submitting yet another eConsult just to confirm that, yes, I do want to make a formal complaint. Very disappointed

recent_reviews.author: T GA
recent_reviews.text: EDIT // update -- a warning for local folk I was forced to make a private doctor's appointment, at my own expense, after Wish Park actively prevented me from getting suitable help. The private doctor asked which surgery I was with and when I said Wish Park she replied "oh, NIGHTMARE". So happy to hear a highly respected doctor vindicate me. She was not surprised at all. Clearly Wish Park has a bad reputation with patients AND good doctors. The private doctor apologised on behalf of the NHS and my ghastly experience. Her advice was to leave the surgery! She would not gain any more financially by saying that, she was just a very kind, good doctor (rare!). That tells our community something very clearly. If you can go literally anywhere else, do. If you loved ones are at this surgery, get them out. You will avoid the big private bill I had to pay to be told what I already knew! --- original review --- This surgery is a danger to the public. The reception staff have dangerously high egos - led by a lady named Caroline. Their entire job is to make sure the patient never sees a doctor, and that if they can fatigue you enough to stop asking, they have done their job. Patient records are changed without consent. Incorrect information is noted down. Medical decisions are made by admin staff. This surgery could well become angels of death, by systematic failings -- if they haven't already. Patronising. Evasive. Ignorant. Arrogant. Who knows what the doctors are like, they are apparently, never available. The admin staff seem to spend their time: answering the (very telling amount) of negative online reviews here; pushing paper around; playing at being doctor; sending out excessive surveys (by texts, emails and if you ignore them, by post) and taking their salary home. The public want to pay for an NHS that is patient oriented, which focusses on care. Currently the public pays for their lifestyles. The NHS is broken.

recent_reviews.author: Kae
recent_reviews.text: If I could genuinely give this surgery 0 stars I would, if you're a woman in need of any sort of hormonal health help please steer clear of this place!! Some of the doctors and nurses (only some), are very sweet and kind people, and they deserve to work at a better place than this. I don't leave reviews very often, but I want other people to be warned about this surgery. I've been going here since I was a child, and over the years they have progressively gotten worse. For starters, I was told for an entire year I had been referred to a gynaecologist and was on a priority list; I was never even referred, and had to be officially referred by an out of hours doctors surgery. I went in for a pelvic exam once, and let's just say no precautions were taken to help discomfort and pain (although I had asked), and the doctor stopped the process due to the pain I was going through (I don't blame her for this, I blame whoever trained her for not showing her how to properly do it), she was also a student doctor without any supervision from a higher up doctor, girl please get out you deserve better. I also was on iron medication for severe anaemia which the doctors surgery said they were going to hospitalise me for and then changed their mind 3 times about the situation. I told them the medication was making me sick, and they didn't give me any alternative. I once called for an emergency repeat prescription for pain medication, to which the receptionist was not taking me seriously and would not give me an appointment, so like any normal person I got my mum to call (I was 19), when I called the receptionist back (which btw was after she was rude to my mum), she told me I "can't get mummy to call", I later called to get her name so I could report her for the way she had spoken to me and she argued with me the entire phone call!! I forgot her name now, but she's probably the same person everyone here is complaining about lol. At least she referred me to an out of hours doctors that was genuinely helpful, although she should probably go through more training and gain some social skills, and that's me putting it kindly. Oh and they also put me on birth control (POP) without telling me it intensifies (suspected) endometriosis pains, I had asked as I wanted my periods to stop completely due to the pain they were not helping me with - I wasn't aware of the side effects because they couldn't be bothered to tell me (except the basic "spotting" and "irregular bleeding", which they also didn't help with). Just to point out, all of these issues occurred from January 2024 to now, and I'm still in the same position I was back then (I'm only 20 now) I never reported any of this (although I very easily could have, and wanted to take action against the surgery multiple times), and although that's on me, I wouldn't have been taken seriously; this was proved by the way I was treated, so I kept my head down until I could leave. Anyways, I've officially moved doctors surgeries now and will be telling absolutely everyone to avoid this one at all costs, your 2.9 stars is generous considering how unprofessional the majority of you are.

recent_reviews.author: Claire Hayes-Williams
recent_reviews.text: If I could give zero stars I would. My 75 year old mum was previously a patient here but thankfully I have moved her elsewhere. The serious neglect she received from this surgery is unforgivable. She was extremely ill at home and called the doctors asking if she could have a telephone consultation with a doctor or for a home visit because she felt too ill to drive into the surgery because she couldn't stand up due to balance issues and she had a severe headache causing her to not be able to focus. She was told by the receptionist that her symptoms sounded like she had a virus so to stay at home and there was no doctor available to visit and to call if no better the next day. She called the next day and then when explaining her symptoms again she was told she may have vertigo by the receptionist… since when has it been acceptable for a receptionist to make a diagnosis?! This was then finally followed by a doctor calling her telling her that yes she thought she had vertigo too. She prescribed her tablets for vertigo and I went to get these for my mum from the rude pharmacists below 168 medical. When I dropped the tablets off to my mum I could see that she really wasn’t well and her balance issues worried me. The reception staff wouldn’t speak to me on the telephone so mum had to speak to them and again she explained her symptoms and they brushed it off as vertigo… no further message was passed on to any doctor. I stayed with mum all morning and by lunchtime I decided to call 111 as she had woken from a sleep and her headache was worse and her right eye had begun to droop slightly. A consultant called me and then late afternoon a doctor was sent from another surgery to see my mum. From my basic medical experience (I work as airline crew) I said to the on call doctor I feel this is a stroke and the doctor on call said that she was glad to have seen my mum face to face because she too thought that perhaps it may be a stroke and we should get mum to A&E. We had to get my mum down the stairs on her bum into my car (because she couldn’t stand due to balance issues) the ambulance we were told would be at least 6 hours and I was not willing to wait any longer. As soon as my mum finally received her scan it was confirmed she’d had a stroke… she’d in fact had 3 by this point and all because she’d been left unseen by her doctor at 168 Medical. She spent two weeks at Southmead Stroke Unit and I’m lucky she is still here. 168 Medical should be utterly ashamed of themselves for their complete lack of care and attention to the information patients are telling them. As I say I have moved my mum to another practice now and they have been amazing with her.

recent_reviews.author: Warren Werfelli
recent_reviews.text: If I could give this place -2 stars I would. Receptionist is appalling, rude and downright incompetent. The environment is grubby, dreary and not a nice place to be; furthermore most lift buttons are broke. I was wrongly diagnosed today by a “paramedic” who took 4 hours to have a GP sign my prescription, which I was told would take an hour to “prepare” the prescription (how is this guy qualified to operate as a GP and prescribe medicine) so I went for a second opinion in Broomfield A&E. The GP there gave me a correct diagnosis without the need for medication, as it was viral and not bacterial. The over whelming smell of pound land cologne on the paramedic was off putting and the tone of voice of the receptionist is cringe worthy. Reception require interpersonal training on how to deal with unwell people. (It’s simple - positive, constructive and actually care about your patients) I’m changing my GP ASAP! 5 star reviews on this forum are friends of family for sure because it’s an abhorrent service. 2024 update - Unfortunately, unless we go private we’re forced to use the same doctor surgery due to our location, so here we go again. Imagine calling at 08:01 and being 24th in the queue. Wait on the phone for 17min to get to number 14 and have the line drop. Call back and you are put to the back of the queue, 24 again. The system is archaic and honestly it’s unfair! 2025 update - The surgery has improved service and has now setup an online method to book appointments. The team get back to you quickly and call you promptly. It’s nice to see the system change and improve the service. Rating as improved!

recent_reviews.author: Temitope Alaka
recent_reviews.text: I appreciate Dr Fadaly for the way he breaks his diagnosis and plan of care down for easy understanding and engagement. He is thorough and caring in his approach and delivery. I wish all my relatives and friends could hear him for their understanding and clarity on what I am going through that does not look like me! You can imagine what dilemmas I present with that puzzles them day to day. I have learnt to manage my day to day experiences until sadly at times I really look like what I am going through! Dr Thayur and Dr Suresh, they are so empathetic and compassionate in their delivery of care , which makes me feel a partner in my care delivery. They as female doctors are so maternal and truly understanding of women’s issues and how it impacts every other aspect of my role and expectations. They are thorough and follow through. The Advanced Nurse Practitioners Dan,Debbie , the nursing and health care assistants are so knowledgeable and well skilled to handle all many health conditions as they are equally keen to practice and deliver research based care that is effective and efficient in promoting General health and wellbeing. I specifically acknowledge the administrative team - Julie,Abbie and others and especially the Practice manager Amanda for their exceptional service in keeping the GP practice one to be reckoned with in Primary Care. They truly help to keep me in health and safeguard my well being. I am a grateful patient! My physical, mental, social and spiritual health are in a stable balance. It takes a lot knowledge updating, skill practise, research engagement and self care for our GPs to keep in practice and be able to deliver care to patients with multiple and diverse conditions. Just think on this for a moment!

recent_reviews.author: Cj True colours
recent_reviews.text: I would strongly advise people not to sign up to this surgery. In my experience, the service has been extremely disappointing and stressful. I have waited over 20 minutes on the phone multiple times, only for the call to be disconnected without warning. It feels impossible to actually get through to speak to someone, and when you finally do, the response is often unhelpful and dismissive. The way patients are treated, especially those struggling with mental health, is deeply concerning. Instead of feeling supported or listened to, I felt rushed, unheard, and not taken seriously. Mental health issues require compassion and understanding, and unfortunately, that has not been my experience here. It can already be difficult to reach out for help, and being met with poor communication and lack of empathy only makes things worse. Overall, the organisation, communication, and patient care need serious improvement. Based on my experience, I cannot recommend this surgery to anyone seeking reliable or supportive medical care.

recent_reviews.text: Absolutely appalled at this GP surgery. I myself have worked as a patient coordinator in a GP surgery for over 6 years plus moving from Leamington Spa. I sent in registration from for me and my 23m daughter three weeks ago. Calling on the day I sent the registration requesting an emergency appt for my daughter due to being very unwell, I requested if her registration could be added on asap so she can see the GP ( something we have done at the go surgery I’ve worked at to help new patients who urgently need GP advice) it’s easy to do. I explained to the reception staff on the phone I’ve worked at GP surgery and we’ve sometimes registered young patients on the day by adding name onto emis slot so appt doesn’t go and then registered, once registered name is added correctly onto emis. Kay went onto say rudely well just because you’ve worked at GP surely it’s not like that here. Very rude and inconsiderate. Maybe management needs to provide some new training! I was advised this can’t be done so I took my daughter to out of hours. Called back for appt four days later and told my daughter still hadn’t been registered!! Apparently the registration form was with the manager. Called back Today three weeks later for an appt for my 22 month daughter and again advised she hadn’t been registered and I need to bring some proof ID. I had no call or information in those three weeks requesting ID. I know from working in a GP surgery where I’ve registered number of patients, the ID doesn’t need to be provided to register!!! Why not register my daughter and I can provide ID when I arrive for her appt. I’ve been trying non stop for three weeks. Absolutely appalling, looking at who I’ve been treated even before joining the practice, I can’t imagine how appalling the actual service is as a patient. I will be joining somewhere else. Be cautious about joining this practice
