recent_reviews.author: Keith Richardson's
recent_reviews.text: My wife has injured her back, she is in agony all day and isnt sleeping due to muscle spasms locking her back when she turns over in bed. Its been a week now so this morning, called Limes for an emergency appointment, only to be told she needed to fill in the online triage form. She completed the form straight away but heard nothing until lunchtime when she was informed a prescription of ibuprofen gel was at the pharmacy. She had already explained on the form she had been using the gel, plus over the counter meds but nothing was easing the pain, so rang the doctors back to explain this, at 1.45 she got a call to say the doctor wanted to examine her, but at this point she was due to go into work for 3pm bearing in mind she had already taken most of the day off for an appointment she wasnt offered earlier, and was unable to go in at that point. She then got a call back to say the doctor would issue a short course of painkillers. I went to pick up said painkillers and the pharmacy gave me ibriprofen gel. They had no other prescription for her authorised. So I went into Limes to ask where it was and was told a doctor at Blackwell was dealing with it. Receptionist said they'd chase it up, I went back to the pharmacy at 5.50pm, still no meds and my wife got a call to say the doctor wouldnt prescribe them as she is on another medication, noone had informed her of this earlier. She was then offered a physio appoinment which she declined as A: her back is too painful at the moment to enable her to do physio and B: by the time said appointment comes through, no doubt her back will have healed sufficiantly enough to not need it anyway. Total joke, trying to get this sorted from initial phone call at 8am until 6pm today, 2 phonecalls, 2 pharmacy visits and one physical trip in to Limes, to end up absolutely no better off than when we started. The practice was totally empty when I went in there, half a dozen doctors and staff doing absolutely nothing. This new triage system is supposed to eleviate stress and waiting times and prioritize those in need and yet all it really us, is an excuse for doctors to not have to see you. None of us want to go to the GP, if we request an appointment/medication, it is because we genuinely need it. My wifes medication can be taken alongside the painkillers she needed, for a short time, under medical supervision, so to just refuse and leave her in such pain is just unethical. Limes medical center standards have really dropped since merging with Blackwell and now this ridiculous triage system which means you will never actually get to see a GP when there is a genuine emergency, unless the practice chooses. We are constantly being told not to use A&E unless its unavoidable because they are overstretched and yet our GP services leave us with no choice. People will end up dying over this ridiculous situation and unfortunately it will take that before anything changes.
recent_reviews.raw_card_text: Keith Richardson's7 reviews · 2 photos2 weeks ago New My wife has injured her back, she is in agony all day and isnt sleeping due to muscle spasms locking her back when she turns over in bed. Its been a week now so this morning, called Limes for an emergency appointment, only to be told she needed to fill in the online triage form. She completed the form straight away but heard nothing until lunchtime when she was informed a prescription of ibuprofen gel was at the pharmacy. She had already explained on the form she had been using the gel, plus over the counter meds but nothing was easing the pain, so rang the doctors back to explain this, at 1.45 she got a call to say the doctor wanted to examine her, but at this point she was due to go into work for 3pm bearing in mind she had already taken most of the day off for an appointment she wasnt offered earlier, and was unable to go in at that point. She then got a call back to say the doctor would issue a short course of painkillers. I went to pick up said painkillers and the pharmacy gave me ibriprofen gel. They had no other prescription for her authorised. So I went into Limes to ask where it was and was told a doctor at Blackwell was dealing with it. Receptionist said they'd chase it up, I went back to the pharmacy at 5.50pm, still no meds and my wife got a call to say the doctor wouldnt prescribe them as she is on another medication, noone had informed her of this earlier. She was then offered a physio appoinment which she declined as A: her back is too painful at the moment to enable her to do physio and B: by the time said appointment comes through, no doubt her back will have healed sufficiantly enough to not need it anyway. Total joke, trying to get this sorted from initial phone call at 8am until 6pm today, 2 phonecalls, 2 pharmacy visits and one physical trip in to Limes, to end up absolutely no better off than when we started. The practice was totally empty when I went in there, half a dozen doctors and staff doing absolutely nothing. This new triage system is supposed to eleviate stress and waiting times and prioritize those in need and yet all it really us, is an excuse for doctors to not have to see you. None of us want to go to the GP, if we request an appointment/medication, it is because we genuinely need it. My wifes medication can be taken alongside the painkillers she needed, for a short time, under medical supervision, so to just refuse and leave her in such pain is just unethical. Limes medical center standards have really dropped since merging with Blackwell and now this ridiculous triage system which means you will never actually get to see a GP when there is a genuine emergency, unless the practice chooses. We are constantly being told not to use A&E unless its unavoidable because they are overstretched and yet our GP services leave us with no choice. recent_reviews.text: I wouldn't recommend this surgery, -Denied a house bound & disabled patient home visits from district nurses, thus delaying treatment for months and leading to a decline in health -GP incompetence with referrals, GP was meant to assess me for a diagnosis in 2023 and they didn't do this, which lead to a delay in diagnosis, treatment and a worsening of my mobility and pain -Took 7 years of advocacy to get a review of pain medication for chronic pain condition -using an advocacy service didn't help as advocate had same issues with GP -Many issues with them refusing to carry out referrals. They insisted ASD.ADHD can be self referred, which they can't. The UKpsych website even outlines this clearly and I sent this to them, still they refused to send this for ages, then they sent the referral wrong which meant a delay of 1yr for my ASD referral -Difficult to get through the phones -Argumentative and passive aggressive phone staff, it I a always polite to them but this doesn't make a difference -Hard to get an appointment thats not a month out -Even more challenging is dealing with rude/unhelpful receptionist who often try to argue -More difficulties having to advocate for yourself with Drs, I have found only 1 Dr at Limes to be supportive, helpful and proactive (but only after making a huge mistake in delaying treatment) will at least listen but most dismiss you if you are disabled/chronically ill which is incredibly ableist -GP leaving inaccurate notes -Even had the brilliant OT/Physio and gynaecology Dr's at Ripley write letters to my GP's advising them it's in their professional opinion that a diagnosis/treatment would be beneficial to me and still the GP refuses, delays, denies. -Didn't inform me of a diagnosis that was made in diabetes which is insane, you can die or lose a limb because of this. The incompetence is a major threat to patients health and quality of life. -I have had to quote NHS quidelines to them, as often the GP is wrong on these guidelines, it seems the practice operates on bureaucracy and admin over what is NHS guidelines or best for the patient. I even had a GP ask me to send them the link to NHS guidelines I was quoting and he STILL did the opposite of what was suggested and his decision was an admin one, not a medical one. -every diagnosis and treatment I have, has come off my own back, not a single one was from a GP trying to help. However i don't believe it will be better elsewhere and I think they should just do better for the sake of all of their patients. I have raised complaints, had other medical professions try to intervene, used advocacy services (who met the same frustrations and exhaustion I did), written to my MP and complained to the health ombudsman. Sadly it seems patient experience actually does not have any impact on how practices are run, just look at all the poor reviews on google which shows you they are overwhelmingly letting down patients across the board. I genuinely fear for those patients who can not advocate for themselves and who are without any support, as they will never get their basic needs met at this practice. If you do advocate for yourself you will be deemed difficult.

recent_reviews.author: Dominic Outhwaite
recent_reviews.text: Date: 04/02/2026 I had an appointment to see the doctor (I forgot his name) as my chest is tight (still tight as I am writing this), as I have severe asthma and it flares up when I have a cold and sore throat. I have been unwell since Saturday (today is Wednesday) and still feel no better (hence why i got an appointment). The doctor saw me and when I told him how I was feeling (tight chested and struggling to talk and could not walk much without feeling very tired and breathless), he took my oxygen stats (which i did tell him that im not a normal asthmatic as I dont wheeze, have a clear chest when you listen to it and have good oxygen stats) but still have a tight chest. After taking my stats he said that if I had a tight chest and struggling to breathe then my stats should be low, but because they are not it sounds like i could be having an anxiety attack?? I told the doctor im not anxious about anything and quite relaxed (other than being unwell and struggling to breathe and talk), then he said maybe ive been misdiagnosed with asthma (which is rubbish as ive had asthma and been in an out of hospital over 200 times with it)! Then he even accused me of maybe faking it! How dare he!!! Not once did he ask me about my history (which if he even looked or had access to my files he would of seen how many times ive been in hospital, how many tests ive had and had lung collapse in the past)! I will be looking at making a complaint against the negligence of this doctor, as he clearly couldn't be bothered to help me feel better (which is his job role)! Too many times ive seen (both through experience and reading on the news) where doctors dont do their jobs and the patien gets worse and either dies or nearly dies. To be struggling to breathe and barely having the energy or oxygen to talk and to be just treated this way is a disgrace and very dangerous (luckily im used to this with incompetent doctors who dont read my history so I dont panic). I will warn any asthmatic peerson to stay away from this surgery as they will treat you like a text book (when not all asthmatics are the same) and could seriously put your life in danger.

recent_reviews.author: Carol Robertson
recent_reviews.text: My son, a mature student who lives elsewhere is staying with us for a few weeks over the Christmas/new year period. He develiped a health issue on NY day for which we atrended the walk in centre( not helpful). He then saw a pharmacist the next day, also unhelpful. A week later the issue had become worse, so he tried to book a Dr appointment as a temporary patient. Instead of calling him and asking him to register as a temporary patient a member of the reception staff told him to return to the walk in centre or call 111 because 'it was not an acute issue'. It was indeed an acute issue, having developed since my son came to visit. Acute issue or not, he has a right to be seen as a temporary patient by a local gp if he is visiting family. He called back to request to register as a temporary patient and the member of staff refused point blank to allow him to register! Absolutely disgraceful behaviour and extremely unprofessional. No reception staff have the knowledge to decide whether or not someone needs to see a gp and anyone has the right to register as a temporary patient if they are staying somewhere for a few weeks, whether or not they are sick. It was not an issue worthy of A&E but did require treatment. Meanwhile my other son( another student) also had an issue of similar urgency. He called the surgery, was imnediately registered as a temporary patient and given a prescription for antibiotics. What is wrong with this place and these reception staff. The second response was correct but both people should have been seen and treated. I will reconsider whether or not we remain registered as patients here. Not even worthy of one star

recent_reviews.author: Dani Atanacković
recent_reviews.text: Not had a great experience with them in general. Usually takes around half an hour to get through to them on the phone. When you have an appointment, it's usually at least 20 minutes late even though the surgery is empty, and then I feel rushed to get out as quickly as possible. When you fill in the online form, they often respond with a negative reply with no way to respond without starting a new form. I had a blood test which required 4 tubes of blood to be taken, the phlebotomist got confused and only took one tube, then when I called they tried to say they had taken 4 when only one test was showing on the app. I had to go back two days later for more blood to be taken. Made a complaint to the practice managers and never received a reply. I had 1 random missed call to book an asthma test when I wasn't expecting it, called and they put a form in and said someone would get back to me by Thursday at 6.30pm, put a form through on Tuesday because no one had contacted me and they immediately said this isn't the correct route, call the surgery! I just asked the pharmacy if I could collect part of a prescription that I hadn't collected and they said to call the surgery and they could send a new prescription over because it has expired, called them and they said I have to write a letter and take it into them because they can't do it by phone and there's no option to do it online. Edited 17th March: Had an appointment booked before Christmas for a spirometry test, which they cancelled. Still waiting for a new appointment mid-March despite them saying I'm top of the list!

recent_reviews.text: AVOID AT ALL COSTS I called up at my 3 year old was very poorly for about 5 days, high fever, earache - was advised to contact pharmacy by the surgery - which i did. 2 different pharmacies. Was given some ear drops which after a further 2 days weren't helping. I tried for another appointment via 111. Dr prescribed antibiotics for a problem that didnt exist. On day 10 of fever, earaches and sleepless nights, I managed to get an appointment for my daughter. Upon arrival at the surgery I attempted to sign using the screen. Which wasnt working for me. I patiently waited for the one receptionist to finish her phone call - miss phoebe - which took ages. I explained the screen wasnt allowing me to sign in. To which she replied 'because youre 10 minutes late' I advised I'd been waiting for her to get off the phone and the phone call appeared to be long to which she responded '*scoff* well I need to answer the phone' I expressed my concern for my daughters health as she said the doctor may not see her due to me being late 🙃 She did not leave the reception. She spoke to someone within the reception area who I heard say 'hes not going to see her now is he' She came back to tell me my 3 year old will not be seen. As a concerned mother in desperate need of a solution I pleaded for a few minutes with the GP She continued to refuse - book another appointment she says. I asked for her manage She said FINE *scoff* Manager comes out. Low and behold. Further disrespect. She basically told me its not their problem Told me I was shouting when I certainly was not. In the end I left and called 111 who said the GP should be seeing you and an urgent request has been sent to them. I call the surgery. Its phoebe again. I explain the conversation with 111 and she refuses to listen. Speaks over me. 4 times I repeated the same thing knowing full well she had no interest in helping. Just heaps of ego to offload. When she realised she made a mistake She said Do you know I'm the one you shouted at earlier. Honestly. I was speechless. My concern was my daughters health. Phoebe's was, well, her pride and ego. Disgusting behaviour. I emailed the surgery asking for their complaints process the same day. 4 months later still no response. I sought advice from the official complaints routes. I will be taking the to higher authorities. Never had an issue until April. Very rude and disrespectful members of staff I had an unfortunate encounter with. The other receptionists are always so kind and caring. EDIT - surname of member of staff removed as was called by the surgery advising we are unable to include full names. Wasnt aware. Sorry

recent_reviews.author: Grisly White
recent_reviews.text: The care I've had from this practice over the last 3 1/2 years has been abysmal. Initially, I had a case of gout in my ankle - absolute agony. This went untreated for over 3 weeks. I was told I couldn't have the traditional medicine, so would need to attend the surgery for an appointment. I couldn't walk, lived on my own, and could not get there. As a result, no treatment as no alternatives were offered. Once the gout eased off, I had a different pain. The GP ignored my comments that this wasn't gout and continually sent me for the same tests, not believing me. In frustration, I paid to see a podiatrist, have an MRI scan, and see a specialist - costing me nearly £1000. The specialist said the problem was obvious - I had a cavity in my ankle joint which required surgery. Eventually, I had this done and recovered well. Since then, I've repeatedly been called in for blood tests that turned out to be unnecessary, and "annual reviews" that had taken place a few months earlier. Nevertheless, when I needed to see somebody, an appointment was impossible. I had horrendous back pain 2 months ago, and could hardly get out of bed for 2 weeks. It was the third instance in 3 months, but the worst by far. I completed the online questionnaire, but was refused a GP appointment. I was put on a waiting list for physio. After over 50 years under this practice, I've left. I no longer have faith in the staff or systems. Awful!!!

recent_reviews.author: Richard Mullaney
recent_reviews.text: Pre covid this was an excellent surgery and it was always possible to get an appointment either the same day or very shortly afterwards. Post Covid it’s incredibly difficult to get anything at all. The phone lines open at 8.30am and even if you ring at the moment they open you get the ‘we are experiencing a very high volume of calls…’. Whatever time of day or week you call this is what you get. The other day I was number 9 in the queue and it took 27 minutes to get to number 1. When my call was finally put through the phone just rang and rang. I hung up after another 10 minutes. The reason I was ringing is because they had failed to send the correct prescription down to the pharmacy. I need the medicine as a matter of urgency but the only way I can get it is to leave work to go there in person. I can’t understand why, 2 years after the pandemic the surgery hasn’t seemed to address the call waiting times. If there’s a high volume of calls at all times of the day/week then hire more staff?!? Patients are without doubt going without vital care because of the way things are.

recent_reviews.author: Jeremy Flurg
recent_reviews.text: The online form to book appointments is excellent, and they always seem to call really soon after you fill it out (like within an hour) to schedule an appointment - often the appointment is even the same day. Amazingly fast appointments, and the GPs are great. My one complaint is that every appointment I've had has been with a different GP, so I have to keep re-explaining my health issues. This is despite me using the "request a specific GP" part of the form, in which I normally request whoever I had an appointment with last. Personally, I would be happy to wait a few days to see the same GP every time rather than have immediate appointments with random GPs, but can't complain too much as the appointments really are so efficient. Bear in mind when reading all the negative reviews that people are generally only driven to review when they have a bad experience - they is not representative. This is a good GP surgery. (a lot of reviews complaining about receptionists - I personally have had no issues, and think this is a petty thing to complain about anyway. You're getting healthcare for free, be grateful lol)

recent_reviews.author: liberty traynor
recent_reviews.text: I have been with many GP practices over the years, had referrals to many specialists and even considered saving up thousands for private healthcare before joining market cross surgery. Dr Steel and Dr Elliott have worked with me for months now to diagnose some long standing chronic health issues I have suffered with for years and never had any help or treatment or even tests. For once in my life I have felt heard and my health been taken seriously, I’ve been referred for scans and treatments that other GP’s have laughed in my face for asking for. For years I was told my symptoms were all down to anxiety and hormones, and after just 6 months at this surgery I actually have solid diagnoses and treatment plans! As a woman it is often hard to be taken seriously in the medical field, and not once have I felt like I have to fight to be believed by these doctors. I couldn’t say a bad word about them. I’m always able to get an appointment either in advance or as an emergency and the care feels so much more collaborative, personal and understanding than anywhere else. These doctors and nurses (specifically Dr Elliott, Dr Steel and nurse Donna) know exactly what to say and how to help, they never rush you and never make you feel like an inconvenience. Thank you ❤️

Today I was seen by Samantha Williams, who didn’t bother introducing herself, so I’ve no idea what her actual role is. What I do know is that she made it very clear I was wasting her precious time with something as apparently “trivial” as an ear infection. It also seems Friday is not the day to see her — she looked annoyed, tired, and ready to go home, and she made sure I felt it. The whole place has this atmosphere of “we’re very busy and very important — you’re lucky we even looked at you.” Meanwhile I’m just a taxpayer asking for a basic medical issue to be solved, yet somehow the entire process makes you feel like a beggar. You ask for help, you follow the process, and after repeating yourself a few times you might eventually get seen by a practice nurse who can’t help you and then looks at you like you’re inconveniencing her. Overall: dismissive attitude, no clarity, no accountability, and no sense of patient care. The reviews speak for themselves — and unfortunately, I now understand why.

recent_reviews.author: Judy Cooper
recent_reviews.text: Having COPD and showing signs of chest infection I did a sputum test on Tuesday morning after seeing the copd nurse . I phoned for results on Thursday but was told they weren't back yet and a Dr will call if they find anything concerning. Thursday evening at 18mins past 6 I get a text message saying a Dr will phone tomorrow ( Friday evening ) between 6 and 8 . They phoned from tower house Ryde to tell me yes there is an infection and that I need antibiotics. They put the request into the pharmacy regents in east Cowes which I obviously couldn't get till the Saturday morning, adding another 36 hours of unnassary struggle to breath . What part of primary care allowes someone struggling for longer than nessassary ? Why could they not have text me or phoned on the Thursday evening and sent request to regents for antibiotics for the Friday morning . . Why make me or anyone else wait another 36 hours before being able to start treatment from the first initial text message . It's absolutely wrong and very badly run if they cannot sort their primary care team out properly leaving patients in ill health waiting for as I can see no apparent reason .

recent_reviews.author: Chloe G
recent_reviews.text: ⭐ 1 star — Dangerous handling of mental health care and lack of compassion My experience with East Cowes Medical Practice has been extremely distressing and unsafe. I contacted the surgery after my mental health significantly declined after coming off of tablets and was told by the mental health team to get in touch to restart my medication. Despite clearly explaining that I was struggling and deteriorating daily, the receptionist refused to book me a GP appointment and insisted on sending me through triage, this triage was actually never logged and I had to chase and ended up going through triage again! After over a week of waiting for a call from the mental health team as advised and promised, I found out I hadn’t even been referred to the correct team, I had been put through to get another triage team, who couldn’t help or give me the medication I needed. When I begged for an emergency GP appointment again, I was told that “mental health doesn’t count as an emergency” and advised to go to A&E, despite me explaining that I suffer from health anxiety and physically could not cope with that environment or even get there. I was then told to ring 111. This advice was completely inappropriate and showed a worrying lack of training or understanding of mental health. I rang 111, who called the doctors and requested I be seen as an emergency. I got a call back from the receptionist once again denying me this and claiming 111 had no power to do this - despite them telling me to go to 111. I called once more the next day and 111 once again sent a message and requested I be seen ASAP - I have still not heard back. I was repeatedly denied medication that I’ve been safely prescribed for years, and TWO NHS 111 request for a same-day GP callback was ignored. To make matters worse, one of my previous triage requests disappeared from their system entirely, which raises serious concerns about their record-keeping. The whole experience left me feeling dismissed, hopeless, and at risk. Mental health should be treated with the same urgency and respect as physical health, but East Cowes Medical has failed to meet even the most basic standards of care, compassion, and patient safety. Triage does not work and reception staff seriously need urgent training in mental health and how to talk to people.

recent_reviews.author: Elin R
recent_reviews.text: Had some truly shocking experiences at this practice in the last decade, to the point where I need therapy to deal with it. If you’re a woman they’re shockingly out of date with current research and treatments. Didn’t have a period for over one year many years ago, and was told you don’t really need one, despite guidance saying your period should be induced as you risk endometrial cancer otherwise. Had some tests done, but they referred me for the wrong type of ultrasound so the cysts on my ovaries weren’t picked up. Blood tests showed abnormal levels of certain hormones, and according to the Rotterdam criteria they had all they needed to diagnose me with PCOS. However, a certain GP who’s now retired lied to my face when I asked about the blood test results and told me they are normal, to just go on the pill to induce my period, despite me saying I can’t go on the pill due to the side effects and despite there being other ways to induce a period, and to come back when I want to have a baby. I didn’t find out about this until over ten years later, when I first looked at my records online. I believed for over a decade that I was healthy, but I wasn’t. Fast forward and I go back to them for the same issues, and now I get my diagnosis. But I get no offer of any treatment such as metformin, despite this being a fairly established treatment for PCOS. I get no referral for a face to face appointment with a gynaecologist or endocrinologist to discuss treatments and how I should manage my symptoms. I finally got a metformin prescription, but that’s only because the fertility specialist I saw recommended it to my GP. Again, metformin is not just to help fertility, it’s also to help various PCOS symptoms. I’m sad that even 10 years after being fobbed off and lied to I’m still treated as an incubator and like my symptoms aren’t worth treating for my own sake and health, my only value apparently lies in having babies, it’s only then it’s worth treating. Additionally, they aren’t following the NICE guidelines regarding inducing periods and offering OGTT to PCOS patients. Also had symptoms of adenomyosis and endometriosis but only got an IBS diagnosis instead. Again, it’s only thanks to the fertility specialist that I now have a laparoscopy coming up to finally investigate whether I have these conditions or not. Not just for fertility reasons but for my own wellbeing. Other than this I’ve had multiple other bad experience with this practice. Receptionists refusing to offer me appointments for potentially serious conditions including when I had light sensitivity and blurred vision, being prescribed medications incompatible with other medications and medical conditions I take and have, being gaslighted and being fobbed off ad infinitum. I can literally print the NICE guidelines and clinical studies and take with me backing up my claims and why I need certain referrals and treatments, and I’m still fobbed off. My clinical records are full of factual errors as well, and when I request them to change them I’m ignored. Tried to complain but got nowhere, didn’t even get an apology. My advice to any poor soul who ends up seeking treatment here is to record what’s said at all appointments and all phone calls to the receptionist. The staff at this practice repeatedly acts as if I’m lying about what truly happened, and you might need proof as they never believe what you say. If you’re denied treatment or referral, ask them to make a note in your records that they denied you and why. And lastly, just avoid being poor so that you can seek proper care privately. Ironically, despite this taking the pressure of the practice and the NHS in general, the staff at this practice appears to dislike it when patients go private, I guess they just want you to be miserable and under their power and control.

recent_reviews.author: Kayleigh Elise
recent_reviews.text: Today I witnessed something which truly disgusted me. This evening, a man was in the middle of the road outside budgens and was bleeding from his head. There was a few people helping him including the regular pharmacist at rowlands pharmacy- who had rushed outside to see if she could help, which she did. A lady came in to your surgery and asked if there was a doctor, paramedic or nurse who could attend to the man, who was not even a 30 second walk away in the middle of the road. Now you would expect any decent doctor to do the right thing and attend the scene (especially as I work in a local establishment and regularly hear how lazy and useless the clanfield doctors are) but no, this lady was told by your surgery that you are ‘not an emergency service’. Disgusting. The General Medical Council clearly states that a doctor must offer help when off-duty, if an emergency arises, yet your doctors and staff couldn’t even be bothered to attend when on duty!! This may seem like an over reaction to a small situation however I am simply appalled. The only information you were given was that there was a man bleeding from his head in the middle of the road. That should have sent alarm bells ringing, you had no idea what had happened to him. The ambulance took 15 minutes to get to him, the whole time he was lying in the road. What if he had been stabbed? What if he had been involved in a car accident? I am 100% certain that your doctors and medical professionals are more equipped to preserve a life than any randomer in the street. Whoever dismissed this incident, whether it have been a receptionist or a medical professional- should be disgusted with themselves.

recent_reviews.text: If I could give this surgery zero stars then I would. Two of the GP's at Magna group practice missed a severe and life altering injury. I was days from becoming paralyzed from the neck down. Luckily it was caught in time and I was able to have emergency spinal surgery at Northern General. Now I'm left with using a wheelchair, had to give up work, having to move home to use a wet room. If the GP's had caught it when I was telling them, I would have had a much better chance of recovery and wouldn't have been left with the aftermath of it not being caught early enough. Currently going through an official complaint and looking into negligence claim. Please be very cautious and make sure to self advocate where needed!

recent_reviews.author: Jo
recent_reviews.text: It says something about a practice when you're put off before you can even register. I was willing to register at this practice because of the location, even despite how outdated and run down it seemed, but was immediately discouraged when I met the reception staff. In all fairness, one lady I spoke to was perfectly helpful, but when I tried to hand in my registration forms, the second older woman was completely rude. It makes me beg the question why someone would take a role in a customer facing job when they have no compassion or social skills. You’d think that they would treat people with a little more understanding considering their position. I was treated as if I had ruined her entire life by entering the front door. Apparently, the practice was in training, and I should have known this even though there were no signs informing me so, and the door was open for people to walk in. I recommend you try a different practice if you’re looking. Unless you like being huffed at, and having people roll their eyes at you for even dreaming of wanting the help of the people who are supposed to be there to help you. I suppose I should be grateful that I was able to see what the experience would be like before I registered.

recent_reviews.author: fabrice ro
recent_reviews.text: One week ago I posted that review "I received a text message from my GP surgery asking me to call and arrange an appointment. Today I waited 55 minutes on the phone before someone finally answered. When I eventually got through, I was told there were no appointments available on Friday, which is my day off. The only option offered was a telephone appointment on Tuesday with a one-hour window between 10 and 11 a.m., which is difficult for anyone who works during the week. After waiting nearly an hour on the phone, it was very frustrating to find that there was so little flexibility. I eventually hung up out of frustration. The system for arranging appointments clearly needs improvement. What happened is unfortunately poor patient access management. I effectively encountered two structural problems: Inbound call bottleneck – 55-minute wait suggests the practice phone system or staffing is under capacity. Wide telephone windows – “10–11 am” blocks may be used to allow GPs to run late, but they create problems for patients working normal hours. Under NHS rules, GP practices must provide reasonable access to appointments. If you encounter similar situations you can: Make a complaint to the practice manager. Escalate to your regional NHS England patient complaints service." I removed the review following a positive reply "...I've checked our appointment system and we do have available appointments now on Friday 10th April, so please do let me know if you would like me to book this for you - complaints.kingfisher@nhs.net." I sent two emails and had no replies. My review will stay!

recent_reviews.author: Jade
recent_reviews.text: Disclaimer: This two-star review is given for some of the kind staff, like the receptionists and the physician, who were very kind and thorough; otherwise, I would’ve given a 1-star review. I was with this surgery for several years. At first, I didn't experience any issues. Still, after a while, the care given was no longer provided - doctors would not take my concerns seriously, or follow up on blood test results that I felt should have been investigated further. Instead, doctors would rush my appointment, referring me to other departments/professionals to deal with me, or telling me to go to A&E, which was pointless, as I was told the GP should handle it instead. Making new or follow up appointments were also difficult and inaccessible - calling up to make one was almost impossible due to long wait times, and the practice removed their online booking system too. At my last face-to-face appointment with a doctor, I was brought to tears after carefully writing down all my concerns, with evidence and my previous test results. I felt very ignored and frustrated with my ongoing health issues and not getting proper medical help from this practice. There was absolutely no empathy or sympathy from the doctor either, which made it worse. After the previous incident, I had 1 more medical appointment over the phone (as I was too upset ever to do another face-to-face), which was also inadequate. Consequently, I decided to move to another practice, which I'm very pleased to say is much better at listening to and caring for its patients. It should be embarrassing for them to hear that, within the first 2 appointments at my new practice, I've received proper medical interventions and support that Kingfisher didn't provide in the 5+ years I was a patient there.

recent_reviews.author: LeeLee A
recent_reviews.text: ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Outstanding GP Practice – Compassionate, Professional, and Truly Patient-Centred I can’t speak highly enough of this GP practice. From the moment you walk through the door, you’re treated with respect, empathy, and genuine care. Every member of the team – from the reception staff to the doctors and nurses – goes above and beyond to make you feel listened to and supported. Appointments are thorough, never rushed, and the GPs take the time to explain things clearly, involving you in every step of your care. I’ve always felt like a person, not just a number – and that makes all the difference, especially when facing ongoing or sensitive health concerns. The reception team deserves a special mention – they’re friendly, efficient, and incredibly accommodating. Whether it’s helping to find a convenient appointment, offering reassurance over the phone, or simply greeting you with a smile, their role in the patient experience cannot be overstated. It’s rare to find a practice where clinical excellence and genuine compassion go hand in hand, but this is exactly that kind of place. I feel extremely lucky to be registered here, and I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend them to anyone looking for a GP practice that truly cares. Lee Allsopp

recent_reviews.text: I had some very bad experiences at South Oxhey Surgery with two of the doctors there. So I moved surgeries, and now I'm on the prescription I needed, which I'm relieved about because the last couple of years have been challenging due to the symptoms. I would have given this surgery 2 stars, but the third one is the one of the doctors there, the nurses and other admin staff, who are actually competent.

recent_reviews.text: I never thought I'd be compelled to write a review about a Doctor's Surgery but here it is! All the staff on reception were bright, cheerful and welcoming and then there was the physiotherapist, Danny Parkinson! The consultation lasted 10-15 minutes and in that time, Danny explained in brilliant and simple detail, put my mind at rest and when I left, I genuinely felt better already, armed with new exercises and a concise understanding of what had gone wrong with my neck. Sometimes, being armed with knowledge, from a consumate professional, can go a long way in propelling you down the road of recovery. Thank you Danny and keep up that positivity for others. A true star!

recent_reviews.author: Rebecca Jones
recent_reviews.text: First time at this doctors surgery and feel very disappointed. I am 36 weeks pregnant and had to wait over 2 weeks to get an appointment. On the morning of my appointment I get a phone call asking me can I come in earlier due to the doctor cancling my original appointment to which I agreed. I attend the surgery earlier as requested to then be sat waiting for a good 45 minutes before even being seen. When I finally get called in and speak with the doctor I felt I was rushed through my appointment and not listened to. The doctor dismissed my issues and gave me little feedback or advice. The feedback that was given was very contradictory. The doctor told me to stop taking my antibiotics that had been perscribed by the hospital department pria and insted perscribed me a ibuprofen gel advising me to apply this 3 times a day. Once recieving this it was to my horror that I discover this medication is harmful to pregnant women and the unborn child. I repeatedly asked was the gel Ok to use while pregnant and this doctor said yes! Its just a good job that I had my whits about me and was clued up to not use this medication. It even specifically said on the box that it was not suitable for pregnant women and could cause serious harm to the unborn baby and mother. To me this is a serious and reckless negligence by the practioner. It comes to something when you can't even trust the professionals and get more information from Google! So far I have not had a great experience with the care system during this time of need while being 8 months pregnant and its a very sad and dire situation for anyone who needs care in this country. When ringing the practice to inform them about the gel not being suitable for pregnant women to use, as lovely as the women was who I spoke to I was advised to ring the pharmacy and was told its there job to check these things when passing on drugs to the public so in otherwords passing the book. I rang the pharmacy to who then asked me did my doctor know I was pregnant to which I confirmed yes they did. The pharmacy then asked were would i be applying the gel, I answered, the ankle..There response to this was it should be Ok to apply to the ankle and because your doctor has prescribed it knowing your pregnant it should be Ok. My thoughts to this was what does it matter which part of the body I am applying the gel to? Either way it is going to get into my blood stream and is specifically warned not to use when pregnant because of the risks and dangers it can cause to an unborn baby and the complications and risks in which it poses for mother and baby during birth. I refused to use the cream because of this to be told to ring back the surgery to inform the practice that I'm not comfortable in using the gel. The reception lady advised me to ring at 8am the following morning to see if I can get another appointment with another doctor. To say I am unhappy is an understatement. Always do your research and trust your own judgements would be my advice. I do not have much faith in this doctor after my experience today.

recent_reviews.text: The worst doctors to ever exist. This GP surgery is absolutely negligent and should be avoided at all costs. I repeatedly went to them with serious symptoms and genuine concerns, only to be dismissed, belittled, and told there was nothing wrong and that I was wasting their time. No proper investigations were done, and no effort was made to actually listen to me. Because this surgery failed to do their job, I was forced to seek private medical care myself. The lack of care, compassion, and basic medical responsibility shown here is shocking. If my concerns had been taken seriously sooner, my diagnosis could have happened earlier. No patient should ever be made to feel dismissed or ignored the way I was. Do not use this surgery. Your health and your life deserve better.

recent_reviews.author: Belinda Gill
recent_reviews.text: I have been registered with this surgery for years and the service has just gone from bad to worse. It is virtually impossible to get an appointment. When you finally manage to get through, you're either told there's nothing available for months or you're given a random nurse instead of being able to see a GP. There's no continuity of care and no sense that anyone actually listens. The reception system is a complete joke. One receptionist will say there are no appointments for two months, yet if you call the very next day and speak to someone else, suddenly there's one available the following week. That makes absolutely no sense. Either appointments exist or they don't - it shouldn't depend on who answers the phone. The prescription handling has been even worse. I rang about a prescription that needed approving and was told, "Oh yes, sorry, I've just sorted it now, it was a computer problem". The very next day, after messaging through the NHS app, I was told the prescription couldn't be issued at all. So which is it? That directly contradicts that I was told on the phone. Patients should not be told one thing one day and the complete opposite the next. There is a serious lack of consistency, transparency, and basic professionalism. After being with this surgery for 23 years, it's incredibly disappointing to feel dismissed and misled. Patients deserve honesty and proper access to care - not confusion and contradictions.

recent_reviews.text: Edit-Yes, CQC rated the Last inspection as good last year but patients have mixed reviews as online there is a rating of 3.4 only whereas surrounding practices have 4.5 out of 5 and so on. I did not ask for the overall surgery summary of ratings on your reply as that is irrelevant to me because that didn't solve the issue for me at the time. I appreciate the response from the team after my poor experience and data mix up that was made with another persons, however refusal of a print off is not something that should have happened when patients have no online access as I enquired on this with PALS. Receptionist can Not refuse you a consultation print off if you have no online access, which I never had at the time. She didn't care. Thank you for a reply. Surgery no longer provides print off consultations to ALL croft surgery patients. This change came into affect on 15.9.25 Informed by the receptionist. So alternatively, I requested an email of the consultation, which I never received. Receptionist said she's not free for the day, or tomorrow or the entire week to send it & couldn't give me a time frame despite surgery being empty & she literally was at the desk free. 1 woman said printer is down & another receptionist walked in moments later to tell me infact, they no longer provide access to ANY consultation print offs. Good luck with your rights, proving anything if you can't print off nothing. She also said "I won't be stamping anything" so any paperwork cannot be proven original, without a stamp for you or your loved ones. App doesn't let you print it & it wouldn't be of any value without a stamp from the surgery therefore can't be used for your records as you can't obtain it unless you request a SAR which is useless if you need regular new consultations printed off. Strongly recommend moving to a highly trained admin staff equipped with exceptional high people skills who actively help patients, value & prioritize them, pressing a print button or email send button is not exhausting for them! (Literally, there's 4 other surgeries who confirmed they don't mind giving you print offs nearby!) I did log the entire telephone call on my phone confirming- receptionist says No print offs are available as of 15.9.25 to ALL patients & No they haven't uploaded these changes on there website or sent out any text alerts to patients. Poor communication. Bizarre, I asked why the sudden change? Receptionist said Dr Gill told them to stop print offs as it caused her "inconvenience & was time consuming" (our basic right is time consuming!) I kept a log of this. Dr Gill is a great GP, and I find it hard to believe he said that... I don't believe he refused all registered patients at croft practice basic access at all to a simple consultantation. The receptionist flat out said it's time consuming for Her. Despite needing this. So due to my experience of the admins multiple errors & data mishandling, recieving wrong records in the past and no record of my own today, I'm Very thrilled to have left & I know of others who want the same. Thank you to the wonderful GP & nurses here, they are truly terrific. Ashame about receptionists who display no determination or respectful positive attitude in my experience, the rudeness is worth monitoring for your own sake, doubt they will improve. This is why I log Everything because they will become defensive instead of actually improving despite having multiple leave us "feedback texts" still on my phone. Today, I've left my feedback, today they were rude, today I never got a feedback text. Makes sense. Perhaps, review or be clear of your definition to "high standard quality care" as patients then expect this. Poor admin experience with patients reflects poorly on ones overall experience which in turn is a let down for patients & ratings of the practice itself, despite great GP & Nurses who can't be faulted, they are brilliant. Overall, join elsewhere your better off.

recent_reviews.author: Jo Chetwyn
recent_reviews.text: Very sorry to say I had to vote with my feet after almost 40 years and switch to an alternative surgery. Quality of care just wasn't good enough. Waited weeks for appointments and then invariably had to wait 45 to 60 minutes sat in the waiting room when the appointment day finally arrived. This wait is only added to by the GP having to walk to the waiting room and call patients then wait to escort them to room, the screen calling system in place pre Covid worked so much better but never returned. Felt rushed by some of the GPs when in consultation. Hospital test results not followed up, no follow up on symptoms. Reception seemed to frown upon using online form to request non urgent appointments but yet insisted on sending a form to my phone when I turned up at the surgery to request an appointment. Double dosage if HRT incorrectly supplied. Made an official complaint to the surgery manager and to be fair received a well considered and balanced response but this did not make up for the poor service that was continuing to decline, hence i registered elsewhere. Such a shame as the surgery itself is a nice environment and some of the GPs are lovely....they are in the minority though and badly let down by others. Last CQC review was in 2016 and rated the surgery GOOD....a lot has changed since then. Covid appears to have been the straw that broke the camel's back. A sad sign of the times!

recent_reviews.author: quanbing chen
recent_reviews.text: I am extremely disappointed with my recent experience contacting this GP practice. Today, after being advised by a doctor to book an appointment, I called the practice to do so. However, once again, the receptionist refused to book me in and dismissed my symptoms without allowing any clinical triage. This is particularly concerning given that I was refused to see GP early this week and later found in A&E to have a chest infection, severe iron deficiency, and abnormal liver function results. On two occasions, my symptoms were stereotyped as “flu/cold” and filtered out at reception level, despite clear red-flag symptoms. Reception staff are not clinicians, and repeated refusal to allow GP or nurse assessment represents a serious patient safety risk. Had I continued to follow the advice to self-manage, my condition could have worsened significantly. I am sharing this experience so that the practice can reflect on its triage procedures and ensure that patients with ongoing or worsening symptoms are not dismissed without appropriate clinical review.

recent_reviews.author: Chris Hester
recent_reviews.text: It’s disappointing that GP surgeries are not consistently held to the same high standard of care as the private sector. When I called the practice today to speak to a doctor, I explained that I was attending a funeral and would not be available until after 12pm. Despite this, I was interrupted twice by Lorraine, an “advanced practitioner”. I have been suffering from a sore throat for over two weeks. I also mentioned that I had recently had a tooth removed, but as soon as this was raised there seemed to be little interest in addressing the sore throat itself. Instead, the focus shifted to redirecting me back to the dentist, despite the dentist having already advised me to contact my GP. This felt like unnecessary deflection rather than an attempt to resolve the issue. I do not visit this practice often, but this experience left me feeling that my concerns were not taken seriously and that there was a lack of empathy and common sense in the handling of my call. Having since seen the reviews, it is unfortunate to note a pattern of similar experiences. This is particularly disappointing as there are some good GPs working at the practice who appear to be let down by inconsistent standards of care among some of the staff.

recent_reviews.author: Melissa Campbell
recent_reviews.text: This I have gallstones and have been in excruciating pain. I have 3 children under 2 and (twins and a daughter ) a 7 year old son. I pass out due to these attacks, vomit and can’t keep food down. I lay on the floor for 3 hours at a time. When my husband isn’t home I have to make sure my babies are safe at all times incase an attack happens. I have been to my GP multiple times, phoned 3 ambulances and been to A and E twice. I was in the ambulatory unit last week due to a gallbladder attack. I was left sitting alone for 2 hours. Had bloods taken ( done wrong ) and my arms are black and blue. No one spoke to me bar one lovley blonde nurse. No one communicated with me, then o get the surgeon who comes in and tells me the hospital is full of sick people and they can’t help me. I need my gallbladder removed for the safety of my children who I have to be healthy to look after. I highlight this over and over and no one cares. Also it is imperative to have communication skills and be caring in a hospital. I have been yet again sent home and ignored and left in pain with my children still in danger if I have another attack: it is utterly disgusting and shocking. And I could write another review about my grandmothers experience when she spent her last 8 days in A and E dep. Thankfully Margret Kerr was a very very good place with competent nurses. Also in response to below, I too was sent home in labour and had my daughter at the side of the road 12 hours later after being in 3x that week and told it was in my head. Disgusting !!

recent_reviews.author: Vui Nguyễn
recent_reviews.text: Dear Sir/Madam, I am writing to formally raise a serious concern regarding the maternity care my wife received at Borders General Hospital. My wife’s due date was on the 8th. On the 10th, she began experiencing clear signs of labour. She was already 4 cm dilated, had discharge with unusual colour, and was suffering from very painful and frequent contractions. Naturally, we were extremely worried and went to the hospital for examination and support. However, after being assessed, the nurses advised my wife to return home and wait another 3–4 days before coming back. We were not given a clear or sufficient explanation for this decision. Given that she was already past her due date, 4 cm dilated, and in significant pain, we felt this advice was unsafe and very concerning. Because we were not reassured and feared for the safety of both mother and baby, I decided to take my wife to a hospital in Edinburgh. Within one day of being admitted there, she safely delivered our baby. This outcome has left us confused and deeply concerned about the judgment and decision-making at Borders General Hospital. If we had followed the advice to wait several more days, I fear the consequences could have been serious. We are an Asian family, and while I sincerely hope that this situation was not influenced by discrimination, the lack of clear explanation and the dismissal of my wife’s condition has caused us to question whether we were treated fairly and with the same level of care as other patients. We are not writing this complaint to create conflict, but to seek clarity and accountability. We respectfully request a full explanation of why my wife was sent home despite being 4 cm dilated, past her due date, and in severe pain. We also hope the hospital will review its procedures to ensure that no other family experiences similar distress. We look forward to your response.

recent_reviews.text: I have never been so grateful to the hard work and effort the staff here make at the surgery. The pressure they must be under is intense. I like the fact that I can request prescriptions/alterations to my medication via the NHS Wales app which keeps the phone lines free for more important patients requiring more urgent care. You actually get a timely response and informed on when these requests have been passed over to a doctor for review not left hanging around wondering if your request is sat in a long admin queue. They have always been good to help me with my on going medical problems. They have never refused me an appointment if I have asked for one urgently. They do their best for telephone triage if they can. I fully support the use of the website "Klinik system" to be able to get alot of things done without having to jam up the phones when I need to make an appointment. (subject to availability). In my view this is great to enable the reception staff to keep phone lines free for others who might struggle with technical applications or for those who may want to discuss their requirements over the phone. Nobody enjoys being on hold. Sometimes the parking can be abit hit and miss but that does not reflect the standards of the practice. Inside the surgery it looks very clean and a safe distanced environment. Unfortunately not a great deal of privacy is available at reception to discuss anything as jthe waiting room chairs are immediately behind you so nothing can be discreet but I'd probably write it down if it was that personal and hand it over to them. Hand sanitiser in the main entrance has once or twice been empty which maybe just needs a closer eye on but thats my own personal preference. As a whole to date, I fully respect this surgery and its staff for the hard work and effort it provides it's patients and I do feel safe being with them. Please note all of my feedback is about the Caritas surgery at Coedpoeth only. I have never been to the Cefn Mawr branch to provide any feedback. Hope you found my review helpful and informative.

recent_reviews.author: Sarah Carr-Cave
recent_reviews.text: I have been with Erdington Brach of MMP since 2000. I have seen many positive changes within the practice that ensures people are seen based on their clinical condition. The online triage form has stopped the first person in the phone queue at 0800hrs getting appointments based on the position in the queue. The forms are triaged against clinical need so the right people are seen based on a clinical assessment. My GP is Dr Gonzalez & she has managed me over a 15 yr period through 3 emergency spinal surgeries & more recently a major brain surgery. Without her I would not be where I am today. She listens to you & as she knows how to manage me, starts mentioning options 6 months before needed so I feel I have shared control. I work as a senior nurse in the NHS & I have no plans to leave the practice especially when my GP truly knows me & we work together to keep me physically working with joint control. I have received exceptional care & would highly recommend the service.

recent_reviews.author: Jack Ford (Jack F)
recent_reviews.text: I recognise people’s issues with the surgery so I’d like to offer some advice. You need to learn how to use the systems and play the game. Firstly you request an appointment via a link which is triaged around 11 - so you don’t need to ring at 08:00 in the morning and queue. You can raise an appointment request before 11:00 and it will be reviewed. The link you get sent can be reused after 08:00 on any day - not before - so you don’t need to ring up for a link every time just reuse the old one - put details in the application. When calling the survey always be polite because being rude to the staff doesn’t help. The staff have always been very kind and caring to me and dealt with my queries. If you have a prescription query then don’t call in the morning, call after 11:00. The doctors have always been very pleasant to me and delivered. They have been very good with my children. Sometimes you don’t always see the same doctor by that’s the climate today, that’s just how things work. The paramedic is always lovely with the children I have. I have no issues, you just have to work appropriately with the surgery to get the result you want, if an appointment can be telephone then take the telephone. I am very content.

recent_reviews.author: Marria habib
recent_reviews.text: I’m three weeks postpartum after having a C-section, and I honestly feel completely let down by this GP surgery. My stitches have come apart and become infected, and even after explaining this clearly, I was still refused an appointment. I’ve just given birth — I’m in pain, I’m exhausted, and I’m scared that something serious could happen if I don’t get proper care. This isn’t the first time I’ve struggled to get help from this surgery, but this time it’s really taken a toll on my mental health. I’m already trying to cope with the emotions of being a new mum, and being ignored like this has pushed me to the point of feeling genuinely depressed and anxious. I feel like no one is listening or cares about what I’m going through. No new mother should have to beg for help, especially when she’s in pain and worried about an infection after surgery. I truly hope this practice starts treating postpartum women with more compassion and urgency because right now, it feels like they just don’t care.

recent_reviews.author: Beth Mitchell
recent_reviews.text: Had an appointment here today under Yorkshire street medical. Never felt so dismissed in all life. i have endometriosis which took my 13years to get diagnosed so i have been met with my fair trail with the NHS poor treatment of this condition. I am currently in a 6 nearly 7 week pain flare of my endometriosis and am on a long list of medications to try help manage my pain thus far none been successful. Today i was met with a very abrupt dr telling me she cant do anything for me, it's just a painful condition. I know that this is a painful lifelong condition and whilst it may be true that there is nothing else she can currently offer to help, abit of empathy wouldn't have gone a miss. She also said to "just wait for my specialist appointment in april as it's not that long". I said i can appreciate that it isn't too long to wait however when i have already been in unmanaged unbearable pain for 6 weeks it is another 6 weeks until this appointment thats a long time to be in pain. She responded with i have know women to wait months and months for an appointment for diagnosis. I responded with yes i have been waiting months and months for a follow-up appointment and i am already diagnosed. She shrugged and said oh... well the medication that your on should help your symptoms I responded it's not that's why I am here. I left very frustrated and upset with my treatment. I Will avoid going here like the plague in future.

recent_reviews.author: Helen Aston
recent_reviews.text: Caring, compassionate and supportive The new GP (Dr Mc) at Dill Hall is the most wonderful Doctor my mum has had caring for her. Mum has complex heath needs and in order to avoid hospital admission whilst acutely unwell, her GP and community team cared for her in her own home. This fully supported mums request and advance care plans. The GP has continued to follow up her care whilst in respite and has the patience of a saint. We as a family are forever grateful, he's a true Family Doctor, quite a rarity these days. The reception team are also amazing and very supportive. We recognise how busy demand on the service is, so it has been wonderful for mum to get the care and support she so desperately needs.

recent_reviews.author: Aisha Ahmed
recent_reviews.text: Trust my luck to get the rude and blunt receptionist AGAIN. Yesterday I spoke to my GP who told me he wasn’t going to give me any antibiotics for my throat infection/ tonsillitis (he can’t pin point what it is because they’re STILL not seeing people face to face). So last night we had some antibiotics delivered to our house which I was confused about as I was told I wasn’t getting any. I then rang the pharmacy and they told me my GP had prescribed them. I then rang the surgery this morning just to confirm they weren’t prescribed in error. I don’t want to be taking antibiotics or any medication if I’m not supposed to. The rude woman answered the phone sounding like she hated her job. I was halfway through explaining why I was calling when she interrupted me and asked for my name. She didn’t hear what I had to say entirely. I gave her all the relevant details. All she had to say was ‘if he has prescribed them then you’re meant to take them’. So I’m meant to take medication that I was told I didn’t need and that I shouldn’t be taking (as explained by my GP). This receptionist is so rude and the surgery is a joke. I am calling for my safety as sometimes mistakes are made so I was just trying to make sure I was okay to take them.

recent_reviews.author: Isaac Fihosy
recent_reviews.text: A very useless service overall. EDIT: AVOID THIS SURGERY Despite the reply from ‘Sarah’ under my review no one has reached out to me and the service has steadily decreased. Please be wary of one ‘Dr. Greeney” and the receptionist known as “Bo”. If you have serious ailments these two will prolong or exacerbate your situation. Both individuals show alarming levels of callousness indifference indicative of too much time without proper regulation from a central body. I was struck by a car, called in to the surgery for a referral to x-ray / mri after seeing ambulance services (I suffer agoraphobia and anxiety so was told by ambulance crews to contact my GP for an X-ray / MRI referral to avoid waiting in A&E where the condition would flare up) Upon calling I was bizarrely told a referral “wasn’t appropriate” by Greeney. Every other professional within the NHS that I’ve spoken to in the wake of that interaction has been baffled by Greeney’s statement which suggests the GP has perhaps gone too long without oversight and is exercising her ego based on personal feelings, this is a serious deviation from professionalism and will not be tolerated or go unanswered. In any situation this behaviour is unacceptable. For context I am struggling with health issues in the wake of losing my partner, the GP surgery know this, are aware I struggle to leave the house, suffer low mood, and feel it appropriate to pettily exercise their unchecked ego regarding matters that ought to be straight forward. I had been in excruciating pain and without sleep for days due to Greeney’s purposeful incompetence. My anger at useless practitioners like this was thus especially heightened. Fatigued, I called the surgery to again arrange an appointment for a referral to Brightons MSK (musculoskeletal) dept. An individual named Bo answered, began commenting uselessly on an appointment I’d missed months before, then childishly ignored my repeated requests to book an appointment, told me I could book online and abruptly hung up. These people have no place in a professional environment where their behaviour poses a health risk to service users. _______ Bar a few, tart, condescending staff at reception make booking a constant exercise in irritation; they’ve a complete inability to professionally engage with and address serious issues without frustrating patients in the process; After losing my partner I have never felt so let down by a service that claims to work for the betterment of public health. Just recently they referred me to a dentist for an exposed nerve in a cracked molar. The Dentist they referred me to asked for a referral from the GP, they vehemently refused but could not come up with a definitive reason why they wouldn’t help instead saying “we know it’s bad.. oh well”. These people need letting go and replaced with workers who are focussed on problem solving.

recent_reviews.author: Kelvin Wright
recent_reviews.text: I am appalled by Hoylake and Meols medical center's decision to charge my daughter £35 for a supporting letter confirming her epilepsy – a letter your practice has already provided to her in the past, for the exact same purpose: supporting her application for concessionary public travel. My daughter is a hardworking NHS nurse who lives with epilepsy, a condition that prevents her from driving and makes reliable, affordable public transport essential. Yet now, for what should be a simple matter of accessing existing records and reissuing a standard confirmation, you're demanding payment. This feels less like reasonable administration and more like opportunistic profiteering at the expense of a vulnerable patient who also happens to be a frontline healthcare worker.

recent_reviews.author: Melina Dale
recent_reviews.text: I’ve encountered my fair share of underwhelming healthcare in the UK, but Dr. Kahn really raised the bar—for how low the standard can go. For nearly two years, I’ve been losing weight and dealing with mysterious digestive issues (I’ll spare you the gory details). I went to Dr. Kahn expecting at least a conversation about my blood results. What I got instead? A cheerful dismissal because “everything looks normal.” His golden advice? “Eat more sugar” and, wait for it… “Try Yakult.” Yes, Yakult. The sugary supermarket yogurt drink with 20g of sugar per shot—suddenly elevated to probiotic gold in Dr. Kahn’s world. Apparently, that’s what decades of experience boils down to: pushing processed sugar drinks as gut health solutions. Needless to say, I left the appointment more baffled than helped. I chose to listen to my body (since my doctor clearly wasn’t interested) and sought a private second opinion. Lo and behold: diagnosed with H. pylori and a stuck-open ileocecal valve. Both real, treatable issues. Both completely ignored. What’s most disappointing? I explained how much this was affecting my life—and got absolutely nothing back but indifference. I’m not sure what’s worse: the lack of curiosity or the lack of care PS: the reception team is absolutely lovely and caring and deserve 5 stars.

recent_reviews.text: This practice since I've been there has got progressively worse. Ive had to resort to paying private each time I've needed help. Yesterday was the worst time by far as they trashed their code of: conduct, ethics and The Hypocratic Oath. They pretended I'd filled in forms to see a mental health worker yet they had previously rung me to say I had an appointment with a doctor. When I got there and disputed this. I got gaslighted. At a doctors? Can you see the oxymoron there? Really? Previous to this I'd had two ECG's. I never got the results until I asked for my records. Both were abnormal. I had to go private to see a cardiologist. He told The Limes to give me an 'eco.' They told me they won't because I had private health care. Anothrt oxymoron. I had one smear in 11 years. The nurse told me it was my fault because "I didnt like the staff." Another vacuous, idiotic, moribund comment more offensive than the smear test itself. I had a private MRi. They lost it but the best one by far is yesterday when I saw the doctor who wasn't a doctor. The person i was consulting with said (when i told them I was disabled) "What's wrong with you then?" That's like saying to someone whose gay "Are you sure your gay?" Or "Prove you are black." Its offensive, glib, ignorant and arrogant. They broke their own code of ethics lying and gaslighting me. Its so appalling I can harding believe it.

recent_reviews.text: I found a lump on my left thigh. I saw my GP for the results earlier this week, and, as is usual when I see him, he listens to me about my concerns, never makes me feel awkward, and calms and reassures me. I have faith in the doctors and staff there, especially the Doctor who has been looking after me since my diagnosis. Without his help I would not have been able to move forward.

recent_reviews.author: Gracie Hughes-Faulkner
recent_reviews.text: This is the worst GP surgery I have ever been registered at!!! If I could give 0 stars I would. On two occasions now I have been left to wait for an hour and a half in the waiting area to then be told I couldn’t be seen, in both instances I asked the admin assistants why it was taking so long multiple times and they assured me I was “next”. Most recently this was because someone had left a note on my profile stating that I “couldn’t attend” my appointment despite me turning up on time. The issues here are indicative of a much wider systematic problem within the NHS I’m aware, but these people have given up trying completely. When I was 8 months pregnant I requested a fit to fly letter, I was texted by the GP (Dr Bashir) to come into the practice to discuss this. After over an hour of waiting, I was told that he cannot supply fit to fly letters as per new guidelines but that he thought it would be better to tell me in person. A complete lack of awareness and bedside manner. Please avoid this place at all costs and just register somewhere else if you can.

recent_reviews.author: Andrew Richards
recent_reviews.text: Once again the NHS has saved my life. I cannot praise the doctors and staff at this clinic any higher. I recovered from sepsis a decade ago and when I needed urgent attention recently for a bacterial infection the response was instantaneous! I found that by calling the surgery at their allocated ‘urgent ‘ time a doctor was able to call me back asap, which was within a few minutes. I was then easily able to either send a photo over the phone or arrange to provide a sample to be tested, both by the staff and also by the hospital. Test results were very quickly released to me and the appropriate prescription for meds conveyed to my chosen pharmacy the same day. I’m now on the mend due to the swift action of these consummate professionals.Where time is of essence I feel reassured that the system operating here is first class. Thank you everyone!

recent_reviews.author: Nicola Hayward
recent_reviews.text: Two of my relatives have had to recently visit the surgery. One used the app to make an appointment and whilst on the first go they were not able to get a routine appointment they did the next morning and was seen 14 days later and had a very good consultation with the GP who was extremely thorough. Another relative rang as had a more urgent issue and was seen same day. They discussed in detail what could be treated and how, side effects greatly explained, information fully provided to make decisions. A clear time frame was laid out to manage expectations. A few days later when they contacted the surgery once again, admin staff were able to arrange a very specific fit note via the GP. We are grateful to the surgery who always have given all our family members the best care over the many years but especially in the last couple when things have changed and the demand is so high for GP’s.

recent_reviews.author: Abygail Jones
recent_reviews.text: I don't usually do reviews, but I am sick of the quality of service I receive from reception. One time I called I was met with 'yes?' and very rude and to-the-point attitude when I asked for the help I needed. I once dropped off a sample, was told by the doctor to call the next day, called back after lunch the day after and was told it was 48 hours for results. Called back the day after, after lunch and was told it was a week I'd be waiting (I was severely dehydrated and the results would have told me whether I'd need a hospital visit or not). Another time I had to drop off another sample, I was told to come in on the day if I could, managed to get off work early and come in at 5pm, was met at the desk by a child in a school uniform?? They told me matter of fact that it was 5pm, I questioned why this was relevant, I was told they don't take samples, I advised I was told to drop it off asap and this is the only time I can come in, they took it and I was told 48 hours. I called back 2 days later after lunch and queried this, was told it hadn't been tested yet, this was back in April and I'm still waiting for the results (lol). Earlier in the year, I was called despite not making an appointment, the doctor asked what I needed, I confusedly said I had no idea, I hadn't made an appointment, they then read out my full name and address, and asked if I had a throat infection, I said no, they said it must have been a mistake. So I took somebodies call? And they told me their ailment? Thank god it wasn't something very personal. I called this morning for a nurse, and was met with a very abrupt woman who asked what it was for, when I told her, she asked whether I'd done the relevant things doing needed before I make my visit, I said yes, she then asked my postcode and I must have gone in to quite a bad reception area, she then asked for my postode again, I tried to give her it, but she cut me off, she must have only heard HG4 because she responded with 'yes, everyone in the area has a HG4 postcode, I need the last part', I said (rather aggravated at this point, and also trying to move in to an area with better signal) I'd just given her it and tried to give her it again, only to be hung up on. People call for help and honestly, I'm sometimes anxious to call in case I'm met by unkind staff, which is mostly the case. I can't imagine being someone with severe anxiety, too afraid to call and get the help they need because the staff are so abrupt and unkind. It's unprofessional and rude.
