recent_reviews.author: Nick Dawson
recent_reviews.text: Service has recently gone downhill massively, which is a huge shame because through the lockdown and the pandemic they were fast and reliable. I'm not sure why service seems to have utterly collapsed recently when it managed to survive all that. Have recently had a doctor's appointment in which the doctor could not help me with a physical ailment, which is fine. But didn't elaborate as to why. Leaving the receptionist to do it themselves and play 20 questions in front of the entire reception, very embarrassing. It says a lot when the receptionist seems to know more than the doctor.... When I got in the car to leave I then realized this same doctor had printed off the wrong prescription for me to collect, just to really hammer home that this guy doesn't know what he's doing. All of this was a few days ago. TODAY however I've been waiting for a phone appointment for weeks regarding a simple medication change to one I've been on before, meaning the call itself should be pretty straightforward. However someone put this appointment down as a face-to-face appointment when I was told on the day I booked it that this would be a phone appointment, I rang up and spoke to the receptionist and now I've had to cancel my plans this afternoon because I MIGHT get a call back today...... To repeat what I said at the start this practice was very professional during the pandemic and I'm amazed that the service provided didn't seem to be effected at all during the lockdown. Why is it collapsing now? It's such a shame.

recent_reviews.author: Amanda
recent_reviews.text: I am a patient at Leiston surgery and have had just about enough of the way patients are treated. Last year I changed my address. In 2020 I was diagnosed with aggressive breast cancer. Had undergone chemo. Radiotherapy. And herceptine injections over the course of a year. Last year I was sent for my pathway mamogram in a van in the co op car park. I thought this was strange as I usually went to Norfolk and Norwich hospital and saw the Brest nurse if I had any concerns. I asked the nurse on the van if this was my pathway aftercare mamogram she asked me if I had had breast cancer. I said yes she said you shouldn’t be here and there was nothing in my record to say I was a breast cancer patient she told me to go back to your GP. When I did the doctor had no idea that I had had breast cancer. (Do these doctors read your medical file before they speak to you or make you ongoing appointments .) This morning I called the surgery saying my medication hadn’t been authorised. I had applied on line every month for the last 4 years with no problem. They told me they wouldn’t issue my medication as I needed to speak to a pharmacist. This medication is to prevent my breast cancer from returning and I will be on it for another 5 years. recent_reviews.author: Chris
recent_reviews.text: After waiting for appointments that are urgently required, patients are often sent away without proper help or support. The doctors frequently dismiss serious concerns, and you’re only allowed to discuss one issue per appointment, even if your problems are clearly related. I was left without proper care despite attending my appointment, and the staff refused to treat me due to lateness (due to access issues, I was 10 mins early on site). It is important to note that NHS-funded practices receive payment for each booked appointment regardless of whether the patient is seen or the issue is addressed. This creates a situation where practices are financially compensated even when patients do not receive the care they urgently need, which is a systemic flaw and not a one-off incident. Access is also a major problem: the car park is overcrowded, making it almost impossible to arrive on time, and there’s little understanding or flexibility when this happens. Overall, the service is disorganised, uncaring, and leaves patients feeling abandoned. This is a diabolical level of care, a surgery to be avoided at all costs. I would like to stress the urgency of my condition. An infected wound, particularly one showing signs of spreading or possible sepsis, can rapidly become life-threatening if left untreated. Despite the clear medical urgency and the unavoidable lateness of my arrival, the surgery showed little to no concern for my health or the potential severity of the infection. This lack of compassion and medical responsibility is deeply concerning and unacceptable in an NHS-funded practice.

recent_reviews.text: Update Feb 2026 I was genuinely surprised to see so many negative reviews about Apex Medical, as my experience has been completely different. I’ve never had any issues being seen when I need to. I use the e-consult process and always receive a response the same day, followed by an appointment when required. The system has worked smoothly for me every time. Just last week, I was seen by both a GP and a nurse, and today I had an appointment with the senior nurse practitioner. She really put my mind at ease, took the time to listen, and made me feel reassured about my concerns. The receptionists have also always been friendly and helpful, which makes a big difference. For me, the most important thing is getting the care you need when you need it and that’s exactly what I’ve experienced at Apex Medical. Jan 2025 Credit where it’s due here I could not have asked for more today. I had an e consult and was waiting on a prescription. I went to the surgery to pick this up but it was not ready, the lovely receptionist (Jane I think) went above and beyond as she knew I was going on holiday and waited for a doctor to be available to sign off the prescription. It would have been easy for them to simply tell me to come back, but she knew I needed the medication asap so went out of her way to ensure I got it. I know this surgery gets a lot of negative press but in recent months I’ve been very impressed - thanks again

recent_reviews.author: Sarath Sasan
recent_reviews.text: I am very disappointed with the way my blood test results were handled by this practice. I had blood tests done on 15 July 2025. Only recently, through the NHS App, I discovered that my cholesterol and creatinine levels were elevated. The healthcare professionals’ notes stated that I might require a statin and a repeat blood test within 4 weeks. Despite the potential health implications, I was never contacted by the practice about these abnormal results. This delay of several months in communicating important medical information is extremely concerning. When I called the surgery on 20 January 2026 to discuss this, the phone handler was very rude and told me, “You have to check your app regarding your results.” I found this response unacceptable and unprofessional. What makes this more frustrating is that your own website clearly states: “If your test results show that you need more tests or treatment, we will contact you.” This clearly did not happen in my case. I hope the practice takes this feedback seriously and improves both patient communication and staff attitude, as delays and poor communication around test results can have serious consequences for patient health.

recent_reviews.author: Karlie
recent_reviews.text: Hands down, the worst GP in the area. Do not register with this GP unless you want to be neglected and charged extortionate fees for disabled medical support. Extremely disappointed with this practice. I’ve been a patient here for over 10+ years and it just seems to get worse. The front desk workers are rude, cold and very insensitive. Communication is poor, follow-ups for mental health and chronic conditions are inconsistent, and appointments are often hard to get. Don’t even expect a timely responses to emails in matters of escalation or crisis. Recently, I was asked to pay £30 for a simple university support letter — an unfair and unreasonable fee, especially given my long-term medical condition and recent injury. This feels exploitative and shows a worrying lack of empathy for patients with ongoing health needs. I have never felt so ignored and mishandled, especially in the experience of health decline. Not a team you can rely upon - I hope to switch soon and hopefully receive better care and support. Overall, I cannot recommend this practice. Patients seeking reliable, supportive care should look elsewhere.

recent_reviews.text: The building is a bit tired, but there's always attentive service from the staff, especially the doctors. A disappointing update, considering how much I have appreciated the clinic over the years.

recent_reviews.author: Dave J
recent_reviews.text: My wife had an appointment with the nurse last week as she had a water infection, she took a water sample with her to save going backwards and forwards,the nurse dipped the sample and said (you have all sorts in here, I will give you some antibiotics it will be at the chemist by the time you drive there), when we got to the chemist no prescription was there so waited 20 minutes as the lady in the chemist was keeping refreshing the page looking for this prescription,my wife rang the doctors and asked about it and was told the doctor has to do the telephone appointments first before the prescriptions,so we went home and had to wait an hour before going back for this prescription, my point is why did the nurse say that it would be there when it was an hour and 20 minutes before she got it, I think the doctor should be signing the prescription off first so people can get them before the chemist shuts as it was a Friday teatime and the chemist is shut all weekend, this doctor has taken far too many patients on in my opinion and can’t keep up with the work load,I look forward to your response (that’s if I get one because it looks like you only respond to the 5 star reviews not the 1 star ones). Part two of this situation, My wife had arranged a telephone appointment on Friday for today Thursday 22/1/2026 between 11.30-12.00, the doctor rang at 10.40 and my wife missed the call by seconds and rang straight back and was told the doctor will ring her back today, no one rang my wife back so at 4.45pm she rang the doctors and was told that her telephone appointment was between 10.30 and 11.30 and really the doctor would like to see her face to face but they is no appointments till the 2/2/2026, so you only get one chance at the telephone appointment,if you don’t answer then you will have to make another appointment.well done (too many patients and not enough time comes to my mind). Part three of this situation. Thank you for finding the time to reply to my review, it’s a shame the doctor can’t find the time to ring my wife back. If a clinical decision was made that this situation had to be made face to face why didn’t the doctor ring again after my wife missed the call ????, let’s continue, so since the doctor didn’t ring back and there was no appointments until the 2/2/2026 my wife rang a private menopause clinic on Friday morning and was advised that she would need a blood pressure test before proceeding any further, so she went to HOGG chemist (which is a very good helpful chemist by the way) and had a blood pressure test that showed her blood pressure was 180/120 which is very high apparently, HOGGS rang my wife’s doctor straight away explained the situation,the doctors rang my wife at lunchtime and said come in at 4.10pm today, I took my wife for her appointment (she also took another water sample because she still wasn’t feeling well),the person my wife seen (Iam not sure if it was a nurse or just a lady in a green uniform) took my wifes blood pressure and it was 170/120, my wife was asked to go back to HOGGS chemist and ask for a monitor to keep an eye on her blood pressure, I DONT UNDERSTAND WHY THE DOCTORS DONT HAVE THESE MONITORS ????,when we got to the chemist the chemist said we don’t have one and imeary medical group knows we don’t have one,so he advised us to go to ASDA pharmacy which we did but the pharmacist was on a break till 5.00pm, when he came back he said he only has one monitor and it is out at the moment and didn’t understand why the doctor didn’t put my wife on some tablets straight away, my wife rang the doctors while with the ASDA pharmacist and explained what was going on,so now she has another appointment at the doctors tomorrow, and to top it all off we have a 27 year old son with severe autism and epilepsy (which the doctor knows fine well) as he is under the same doctor and he has to come with us, I look forward to your reply.

recent_reviews.author: Ana Pratt
recent_reviews.text: Went for a routine smear, appointment was after 5, I came few minutes early after leaving work 30 minutes early and being in traffic for 40 minutes. There were no other patients there but still had to wait 15 minutes. The issue was I really didn't have much time as I needed to get home and was getting more anxious with the wait. So after 10 minutes past my appointment time, I asked if they knew how long the wait will be, I was told Im the next one in, after 15 minutes and no clue when I'll be seen I said I'm sorry but I'll have to go as I can't wait longer, the receptionist just said ok. Then I asked if I can reschedule the appointment and as she was looking for next time slot, the nurse came out and called my name. While with the nurse, I was asked when was my last smear, I said couple of years ago I think and it would have been on my record. She said she can't see it as she is new to the surgery and she doesn't have access to anything historical. Then I said it would have been the routine smear so couple of years ago, then she said smears are done every 3 years in this country. I said ok. I have a foreign surname and I feel like there was an intentional point made there about being in this country. Then somehow she managed to find on the system when I had my last smear and she confirmed to me it was 3 years ago. I was explained other things in the course of that appointment and I did feel like every single explanation was made in a tone as if I come from somewhere they don't have running water. Awful experience, coming across and needing to deal with racism and prejudice while trying to do a routine appointment is not something anyone should be faced with. Leave your politics outside of doctors surgeries please!

recent_reviews.author: lindsay hull
recent_reviews.text: It’s not that I have had awful experiences every time that I have been to this practice but this morning really made me question their practices. I gave birth 2 weeks ago, and this morning spoke to the emergency midwife number as I suspected I had mastitis, they advised I will require antibiotics before it becomes more severe and said to call my doctors for an appointment. They said this should be a priority appointment. On calling the doctors, the receptionist was not at all empathetic to the situation, said there was no appointment today and nothing for another week. I was told to go to a walk in centre. Given that I have a 2 week old, breastfed baby, this seems like poor advice. She is currently vulnerable. We had to take her A&E last week where we were put in a separate room but ultimately my partner became ill a few days later. We have had to be cautious at home so that she does not catch it too. Thankfully, after speaking to the midwife team again, I was able to go to the maternity triage, which still resulted in a long wait but I needed antibiotics today. They commented that it was shocking that I didn’t get a doctors appointment for an infection which can worsen very quickly, and having a newborn baby to feed. I understand that receptionists have to ask what the issue is to ascertain whether the case is priority, and I feel in this situation the broader picture and health of a vulnerable newborn baby was not taken into account, which is very disappointing, it makes you question whether they view you as a human being, or just another call to get out the way. Please try better

recent_reviews.author: Kayleigh
recent_reviews.text: I wanted to leave feedback specifically for Dr Barber, because my experience with her was genuinely exceptional. I’ve had several difficult experiences at this surgery in the past, so I don’t usually feel confident or comfortable attending appointments or leaving positive reviews. Because of that, I feel it’s especially important to say how different my appointment with Dr Barber was. I saw Dr Barber because I’ve been struggling with my mental health, and I honestly can’t thank her enough. She was incredibly kind, patient, and genuinely easy to talk to. I felt listened to and taken seriously from the moment the appointment started, without any judgement or rushing. Dr Barber explained things clearly, showed real understanding, and made what could have been a very difficult conversation feel safe and manageable. I left the appointment feeling supported and reassured, which means a lot given how overwhelmed I’ve been feeling. She is exactly the kind of doctor you hope to see when you’re vulnerable — compassionate, thoughtful, and professional. I’m very grateful for the care she showed me. She is a true credit to this surgery and I hope she always gets the recognition she deserves within the field.

recent_reviews.author: Anita Nagy
recent_reviews.text: This GP does not even deserve 0 stars. The pain clinic sent a letter to the GP already in May, and again in December, asking where I should be referred because of my hip pain, but to this day no appointment has been arranged for me. It seems that they do not care at all that I am in pain. I requested an appointment by email. First, I was given a telephone appointment, then later I received a message saying that the appointment would be in the surgery. I went to reception to ask what kind of appointment I actually had, and they told me it was a telephone appointment at 4 pm. However, at 3 pm the doctor called me and told me to go at 4 pm to another surgery, which is located in the city. It seems that they do not know what they are doing. I told the doctor that my only question was whether they had already requested an appointment for me with MATS, and he said that he did not know what MATS was. How did he become a doctor if he does not know even this? The receptionists except for one new young man are rude and dismissive. I cannot believe that after so many negative reviews there is no authority that checks what is going on in this surgery?!

recent_reviews.author: Lauren Hatherley
recent_reviews.text: I've recently switched to this surgery after having been a patient of another local (and notoriously bad) practice and I am really pleased with the service so far. Using the online triage service is really easy, and I have received same day responses to my queries which really surprised me after having waited up to a week for even an acknowledgement from my last GP surgery. I was previously a patient with St Neots surgery over ten years ago, and it is nice to see that the practice is still responsive and efficient. Some of the same GPs are still working here, which I've taken as a good sign! Everyone I have had contact with, from the receptionist to the GP, has been really helpful, friendly, sensitive, and supportive.

recent_reviews.text: I have continuously had awful experiences with this GP, I would avoid it as much as possible. Apparently having several chronic pain conditions isn’t important enough to get seen for over 8 weeks. I have asked for help so many times in person, on the phone or through the electronic system to be pushed away each time. Calling up is a waste of time because they only offer you a same day appointment (some of us are managing health conditions around working a job) or they don’t offer you anything at all. I was told I would hear back for an appointment in 4 weeks. It has now been 5, and on calling today have been told it could be 8 weeks. No wonder people pay to go private, unfortunately I do not have that luxury.

recent_reviews.raw_card_text: Dean WhitfordLocal Guide · 48 reviews6 months ago Beyond belief how Lisson Grove operates! Only ever get appt to see practice nurse, waiting room always empty, terrible .Like Share Response from the owner 5 months agoDear Mr Whitford We are sorry to hear that you have felt unhappy with your experience at the practice. Unfortunately, we are not able to go into personal or specific details in an open forum, but the best way to resolve any specific concerns is to contact us directly so that we can look into them properly. For context, the practice operates a system called total triage. This means that every acute appointment request is reviewed by a senior clinician, usually the same day and often within two hours. The clinician decides the most appropriate way to address the issue, which might be by signposting elsewhere, giving advice, arranging a telephone consultation or booking a face-to-face appointment. Patients are directed to the most suitable member of the team, whether that is a GP, nurse or another specialist, so that the most complex cases are managed by the highest skilled staff while everyone can benefit from the skills of the most appropriate staff member. In your case it sounds as though the clinician felt your needs could be best managed by a nurse, which is why that appointment would have been offered. This approach helps ensure that as many patients as possible are seen promptly and appropriately. We do value feedback and would encourage you to get in touch with the practice directly if you would like us to review any specific concerns in more detail. Kind regards Chris (Practice Manager)

recent_reviews.author: Jo H
recent_reviews.text: Just shocking! I am not a patient here but my partner is. He rarely uses GP services but the last few months has needed to and it has been a very stressful experience for him. Fobbed off, no call backs, referrals not done, wrong details given on fit note. Econsults and online enquiries not even acknowledged, even by the practice manager. I note a review here from 2 years ago, stating their mental health care is awful. Nothing has changed. 22 days from econsult to telephone appointment, and that's ONLY after a phone call was made to the surgery. Website and phone messages state "the quickest way to contact us is via our website" Ha, what a joke! Receptionist only following guidelines but when someone calls reference their mental health to be told, "phone at 8am or call 111" when it's explained that this just stresses them out more is a real kick in the teeth. More needs to be done to prioritise mental health. In fact this surgery needs to improve ALL aspects of its operations. We all appreciate that the NHS is under a great deal of stress but all my partner has experienced is a real comedy of errors.

recent_reviews.author: Boxing Spectator
recent_reviews.text: A GP surgery that doesn’t process prescriptions for locals. 1 mile rule. Crazy. However it is obvious the surgery cares greatly about their reputation & the surgery itself is always trying to help.
recent_reviews.raw_card_text: Boxing Spectator11 reviewsEdited 4 months ago A GP surgery that doesn’t process prescriptions for locals. 1 mile rule. Crazy. However it is obvious the surgery cares greatly about their reputation & the surgery itself is always trying to help.Like Share Response from the owner 4 months agoThank you for taking the time to leave a review. It's extremely frustrating for us too, as we would love to dispense to all our patients who would like us to. Unfortunately, NHS regulations strictly limit which patients we are allowed to dispense to — only those who live more than one mile (as the crow flies) from a community pharmacy. We are audited every year to ensure we comply with these rules, and failing to do so could mean losing our dispensing licence altogether. We do feel a one-star review is an unfair reflection of the Surgery, as these regulations are set nationally and are not within our control. If you would like to discuss this further, please ask to speak with our Dispensary Manager or Patient Services Manager, who will be happy to explain the rules in more detail.

recent_reviews.author: Tiana Bishop
recent_reviews.text: November 2025 Brought my 19 month old daughter in yesterday for a severe allergic reaction (before we knew what it was) and was given a prescription allergy medication and was told to come back if symptoms get any worse. Ended up bringing her back down today because her lips had started to turn blue and we were turned away from the hospital. We were given a rushed appointment where I had to explain everything that had happened again and told to wait outside the room whilst two more patients were seen. I could then hear Dr Khan and the receptionists talking about us in the staff area 'that same baby is back that was here yesterday, she's really bad now, very blotchy' 'why on EARTH would you give her the same thing that gave her the reaction before??'. This really upset me, of course she was not intentionally given the same thing, we had no idea she even had any allergies and were just told to keep a food diary for the next 4 weeks to try and figure out what was causing it. I have never felt so belittled by medical professionals, the way they spoke about us within earshot (not quietly either) was blatantly unprofessional. I called my own mum crying and only then was I spoken to nicely by the staff. We'll be going straight to A&E if it happens again because the stress and embarrassment was beyond belief.

recent_reviews.author: Account User
recent_reviews.text: ABSOLUTE DISGRACE I have tried on several occasions to book appointments with this practice and not had success. I am complaining about their bookings process which has been implemented in recent years. For many years, patients were able to book an appointment at the reception desk as normal. However, when I tried to make an appointment last year, I was told I couldn't do it at the surgery, with the actual receptionist, only on their website, which is uncared for and outdated. I had a great battle to get an appointment last year. I tried to make an appointment today, I looked on the website but the system was not working. I went to the practice in person and asked the receptionist to book an appointment (this is a fairly normal and reasonable request, you'd certainly think so at a GP surgery). The receptionist refused to make me an appointment and said that it can only be booked online. At first she said it can only be booked ON THE DAY you want an appointment, which is absurd. She said that appointments cannot be booked on the reception desk, which begs the question of the point of having a reception desk, especially as there is a computer device in the porch now for patients to make the doctor aware that they've arrived. She then said that appointments can only be made online and between the hours of 08:00 and 11:00, just a three hour window! Patients may have busy lives to lead and family, work commitments and other such duties, it's careless and unreasonable to only allow booking ON THE DAY and only booked BEFORE 11:00. If it's an online portal, then there should be the option to make the booking at any time. It's appalling that I cannot book an appointment at the reception desk, that is what the reception is supposed to be there for. I've been with this surgery for my entire life and never had any problems making an appointment until they changed to this method. It's absurd. The whole desk was bordered up with a glass partition too, which can make communication difficult for the hard of hearing - not that the reception service would be of any use to those who can hear - as they can't/won't do anything! Appointments should be able to be booked at the reception desk.

recent_reviews.text: I saw Mei Jinghon re an awful cough I had. She checked me over and then checked with Dr Grant. It was decided antibiotics and an X ray. I didn't expect that. The next day Dr Grant rang to say something was picked up on my xray. She thought to do with my infection but asked me to book in for a scan. I was a bit shell shocked but managed to get an appointment at Walton hospital the very next day. The results came in and Dr Grant rang me and told me what she was going to do next. I want to thank them so much. recent_reviews.author: BINAYA KHADKA
recent_reviews.text: I have had one of the worst experiences with my GP. I’ve been dealing with a stomach issue for the past 50 days and have to call every single day at 8:00 AM to book an appointment. I’ve already visited the GP more than 15–16 times during this period, and on other days, I went to the hospital. The hospital advised me to contact my GP for an endoscopy, but the GP has only done blood tests (three times) and stool tests (twice) and prescribed medicines that haven’t worked. I have to take 3–4 painkillers per day just to get through the pain, but they still haven’t taken steps like arranging an endoscopy, which could actually help determine what’s wrong. What’s worse is that, according to the NHS app, they have recorded visits that never happened. Despite being in severe pain, I cannot get timely appointments. I’ve been unable to work because of this ongoing issue. When I called this morning at 9:00 AM, I waited over 20 minutes only to be told that all appointments for the day were gone. I asked if they could book me an appointment for tomorrow, but the receptionist abruptly hung up on me. This level of care is both disrespectful and unacceptable. Additionally, during my first visit, they handed me a form to fill out praising their services, which now feels completely inappropriate given the circumstances. I am writing this because I am in pain and deeply frustrated—50 days of suffering without proper treatment is far too much. Please if you can’t give treatment then don’t take the form of new comers at least they will go other GP and then can get treatment at time. Thank you

recent_reviews.author: Sharmarni Danials
recent_reviews.text: I’ve been with this surgery since 2013 and to be honest I found it okay.. maybe that’s because I didn’t go much. However, after being pregnant and giving birth I found out how ‘helpful’ they are. Let’s start with the receptionist - I wouldn’t say she’s rude but she has a tone. I remember when I asked a question about my babies vaccines and her response was very much well make a decision otherwise cancel the apt.. instead of actually reassuring me. During my pregnancy the doctors were very reluctant to help with medication - even when I was given it by midwife’s or I previously had it before with them. They didn’t want to do anything and always said to go back to the midwife. Meaning I had to drive from Anerley to Orpington and heavily pregnant! I went for my postpartum check up and the first person I saw was fine. However, the nurse who was meant to give my daughters vaccines was another issue. I explained I wasn’t sure and wanted more information. I actually repeated how concerned and nervous I was multiple times. Her response was can you decide what you want to do as other people are waiting. Her way of explaining and reassuring was telling me she had 3 kids and her brother took the vaccines and everyone died it. She repeated told me to hurry up - I even explained to her how poor her response was and walked out. To be quite honest I only stayed with the surgery for convenience and because there is one doctor (I know she partially owns the surgery or is a director there) and she’s lovely. Whenever I had an issue with my newborn she got an apt the same day. Otherwise, everyone else is a lost cause. Now I’m looking for a new surgery!

recent_reviews.author: gj
recent_reviews.text: It is not a good GP. First of all, unsurprisingly, the receptionists are incredibly rude, but this would be tolerable if getting an appointment wasn't like the hunger games, even with the app, which they claim appointments are available from at 6am (a complete lie). On a good day, appointments on the app are available at 8am. Today it was 8.21, and only 9 were available. By the time you book it sometimes, someone else has and you have to repeat the whole process and possibly experience the same thing again. If you CALL to get an appointment instead, by 8:05 you are the 49th person waiting. If by some chance, after the hour and a half it'll take you to get to the end of the queue, someone answers the phone, they'll tell you appointments are gone, try the app. But most of the time as it reaches the end of the call, it transfers you to another line that just rings and rings and then cuts off. You have sick and elderly patients who deserve more. – And this is just trying to get a telephone appointment. I can't even imagine what one must do to get a face to face. —————— After about 2 decades at this place, I finally moved in 2025. Much of the persistent issues I complained about there which were not addressed are now being managed elsewhere, albeit slowly. While grateful, I am extremely resentful about what could have been. The significant impact on my quality of life was preventable with a more proactive and escalated management plan by doctors. Do not bother with this place if you’re looking for care. They will waste years of your life.

recent_reviews.text: This time I have to give 0 star if I can. You have some very efficient and decent people working there,however that’s not the case with the lady who was on the reception on 26/01/26 at 8.10am. I had few interactions in the past with her which all went like yesterday’s one and previously decided it’s not worth my time to bother with her attitude,but just got enough of her. Whenever you go there to book appointment she is always making extra comments in a rude way or you tell her you need two appointments for your two sick children who are young and vulnerable with severe cough and she is rolling her eyes or like yesterday raising her eyebrows and telling me that’s not emergency and to seek pharmacist advice. Guess what they haven’t got stethoscope to hear child’s chest do they? Hence I’m coming to seek help from doctors. So every time the extra comments,the personal judging,the rolling of the eyes is completely unnecessary and rude. Not to mention she never wears her badge with her name facing the people like the other stuff there do. Always the face and the name of the badge are flipped towards her chest. Wonder why? Elderly lady with blond ish hair. Just got enough of her attitude. Sort it out please. We as a patients are there to seek help from professionals and most of the stuff fit the description but that one individual puts a stain on your establishment!

Thumbs up from me, I hope the review is removed

recent_reviews.author: Shelly Williams
recent_reviews.text: ** Warning** I’ve been complaining about the service of this GP practice, and now, without warning, they have decided to remove me from their GP list. Dr Mahfooth: he sits with a clinical mask on with every face-to-face appointment. I genuinely think he doesn’t care about patience, having to be prompted constantly for medication/referrals and medication reviews. Dr. Chung talks 100mph. She puts the phone down before the patient disconnects the telephone conversation. It’s clearly stated within the medical environment that gabapentin should NOT be prescribed to patients who have migraines, and she prescribes it to me!! Dr Lewis: In my opinion, he looked at me, which made me feel very weird. It’s like he was undressing me with his eyes. I came into the appointment with my boyfriend to make me feel safe, but on one occasion, I came alone to the appointment before I even sat down. He said, “Oh, you didn’t come with your boyfriend this time.” That was a weird comment, as I am the patient, not my boyfriend. Dr Calverley: apologising for ECG results not being shared with me after a few months is not acceptable because fast forward, I now have a heart condition. Dr. Gunatunga: From the first time I heard her voice, you could tell she cares about her patients. She has a slightly strict nature, but she is very medically informative. Assistant Practice Manager Helen: She does not honour anything she says. She’s more concerned about her staff calling in sick than the patient’s well-being. Practice manager: the most significant language barrier I’ve ever come across, she lies she waffles on and on, and she doesn’t have a clue about anything medically Secretary: You select that option, and you say hello, good morning, or good afternoon. The English woman says, "Yes, can I help you?" Telephone Manor is not their strong point. If you’re a woman of colour who speaks directly and is unafraid to challenge these medical professionals, this GP practice has a problem. I would not have been removed from the GP practice list if I were a non-ethnic individual.

Make that make sense!!🤦‍♀️ they had on Monday sent another item but I still had to ask for the other one. I ordered within plenty of time for chemist to receive and order what my child needs firstly before she ran out and secondly before christmas. They finally sent prescription late Monday so now im in the position of my child has ran out of medication again! And we don't know if they can get it before Christmas!!! Because of their negligence my child may end up in hospital over christmas/new year as that will be the only place I can get her medication. Will be looking for new doctors in the new year so my child os SAFE!!

recent_reviews.author: Margaret G
recent_reviews.text: Double check your medication: Been a patient for years and have received great treatment when needed. Lately I have had reason to question the prescribers {not the DRs} My latest issue was Friday 30th Jan 26. A simple request turned in to quite a serious matter. Requested a prescription online stating clearly which medication I required. Went to the pharmacy to pick it up. Luckily I checked and double checked the medication, it was incorrect. This lead to the receptionist {very helpful}, the prescriber and pharmacy all becoming involved. it culminated in me sitting in A&E all afternoon to get the correct medication. I fully understand the reason for not giving me what I had requested as apparently it was not in my record from the hospital, the bit I don't understand is why I was prescribed a medication I was already taking. Had I not checked the labels I could have easily been administering double doses of a drug I was supposed to be weaning off from. I would have written in about this matter but I had cause to write in last August re a different issue and I'm still awaiting a satisfactory response. I did receive an explanation quite quickly however it was not what I'd requested, again. Perhaps this review may re open lines of communication. As stated I'm happy with this surgery in general but it seems the fine details are not being observed which is where the problems usually lie.

recent_reviews.author: Douglas O
recent_reviews.text: I’ve been a patient here for over 10 years. The GPs are generally competent and provide good clinical care when you can access it. Unfortunately, the practice is severely let down by its administrative and support staff. Recurring Problems: Administrative errors are frequent - appointments booked for specific tests that then aren’t conducted, medication issues not properly managed, and a general lack of accountability when things go wrong. The real issue is how complaints are handled. Rather than addressing legitimate concerns professionally, the practice actively obstructs the complaints process. Reception staff are often dismissive or outright hostile when patients raise issues. Requests to speak with management are routinely refused, with patients told to “put it in writing” - even when reasonable adjustments are requested for disabilities. There’s a pattern of stonewalling until matters are escalated to NHS England, at which point the practice suddenly engages - but rarely accepts responsibility or makes meaningful changes. Bottom Line: If you have straightforward healthcare needs and don’t experience problems, you’ll probably be fine. But if something goes wrong, expect obstruction rather than resolution. The clinical staff deserve better support, and patients deserve basic professionalism.

recent_reviews.author: Richard Cumming-Bruce
recent_reviews.text: Dr Pankhurst is as good a GP as you could hope to find. Incredibly hard-working (she once rang me at 8.25pm) ; exceptionally organised (she ALWAYS sends me a reminder when I am due a test or appointment; caring; sympathetic; sensible; decisive and, above all, right whenever mshe has needed to be. My general health has dramatically improved since she started looking after me, about 15 years ago. She may have saved my life this year and certainly saved me an awful lot of grief, by picking up on my PSA in a blood test, when I had prostate cancer without any symptoms and sent me for an urgent MRI scan. My late wife would probably still be alive, if she had moved to Dr Pankhurst, rather than kept her old doctor. 5 stars isn't enough! I feel lucky to have her looking after me.

recent_reviews.author: Nick
recent_reviews.text: A true reflection of the poor management of surgeries across the country. Report below national average per 1000 and still can't allow access to appointments and within a reasonable time frame. A few Doctors there have an appalling attitude and bedside manners, one in particular is Dr Paul. She looks so depressed, blames everything on mental wellbeing or weight, refuses to even hear or consider questions about further investigation surrounding issues that have gone on for years, with no interest in helping the person she sees. The admin staff have the worse attitude of all. They clearly let people know of poor behaviour won't be accepted on the telephone line and within the surgery, but often times they speak so poorly to you, with condescending tones and with an attitude like they are doing you a favour not that they should be there to service their community. So many relations and friends have been fobbed off for years at this surgery and to mention a couple, one was fobbed off over 2 telephone appointments and pictures sent for that person the following day self admitted themselves to hospital, to a day later family was called in to do the 'say goodbye' visit. He thankfully and miraculously survived. Another, was presenting certain symptoms over a year, eventually after a hospital visit, these common precursors that were ignored by this practice, turned out to be Ovarian Cancer. There are quite a few more. Complaints have been made but CQC and PALS are more interested in protecting their own than the quality of care for its community.

recent_reviews.author: Dorothy Parker
recent_reviews.text: They have built a medical centre in Shifnal that must have cost £millions and there is no one in it. No doctors, (well I didn’t see one) no patients, no nurses just a receptionist and a filing clerk. Around 8.30 - 9 pm I phoned up for a prescription and the message said I was 17th in the queue but as an alternative, I could fill in a form online. I did both I press the button for a callback, and I filled the form in online. I received a message back to say they would be in touch with me with in 3 days. That is not a joke - that is actually the truth. (I know we don’t pay for the national health service but ‘christ’ you wouldn’t would you?) I decided to visit the surgery in person and the receptionist managed to Fast-track me and promised a call sometime that day. In the meantime I went to boots the chemist to try and help myself. The pharmacist there couldn’t help me And said I had to speak to the doctor. I went home to await the promised call which I did get. I gave my symptoms and was told I could collect a prescription at Boots the chemist in Shifnal that day. 12-30- 1pm I made my way back to Boots To collect the prescription but there was no prescription there. I then made my second trip to the surgery And asked the receptionist where the prescription was. She was very pleased to tell me that yes they had got the prescription ready and It was just waiting for the doctor to put his ‘finger on the button’. ‘’The exact phrase’ This was 45 minutes after the call when it was prescribed. recent_reviews.author: Naomi Summerscales
recent_reviews.text: In the past 2 weeks I have tried to get my son seen for 2 separate reasons. The first was a very large bump on his forehead, which resulted in an egg shaped lump. I walked him over immediately to see if I could get him seen by a nurse or doctor to check he was ok and was told that (despite I had no transport) I had to take him to A&E in Kingsbridge to get advice. They refused to let him see a doctor even for a quick once over. Then today, I called up and explained that he has sores all over his lips and mouth making it very painful and I wanted him to see a doctor and again they refused to let him be seen by a doctor. This time I was told we had to take him to Kingsbridge to see a pharmacist. When I said, “what if they just say he needs to see a doctor”, they said “well he can see one then”. If they could see his face they would understand why he needs a doctor - but they didn’t even ask for photos. This system is just passing the buck and as a member of the surgery it feels totally unfair that you can not see a local doctor but instead have to travel 20 mins into Kingsbridge to see a pharmacist. In terms of looking out for the local community this isn’t a good enough service. As a member of this surgery it feels like a lottery system as to whether you get to see an actual doctor or not. This is anxiety inducing. I’m very, very disappointed.

recent_reviews.text: I can’t believe how uninviting the pharmacy is at the surgery. The young lady stood talking to her colleague for 2 minutes whilst I was standing at the closed window, right in front of her, waiting to be helped. And to top it off they provide you with a sarcastic “well you have a nice day” when you are walking out. I find there a severe lack of customer service and frankly the people managing the surgery could not be asked to correct the issue with basic customer service. The response from those managing the surgery tells it all. Never addressing the points raised, excuses, and failing to address there is a lack of customer service. Also interesting that all pharmacies can have an opened counter. The key is customers should be the first priority and the other jobs secondary. There are always 2 to 3 people in the pharmacy so this should not be an issue. To be clear the window is always closed!

recent_reviews.text: I have nothing but praise for the practice. OK the wait to see a Dr in person can be long. But it's been like this since COVID and it is the same everywhere. Funding has not kept up with the amount of patients to be seen and for the first time that I can remember, there are G.P's without jobs because the practices can't fund taking them on. If your problem is urgent getting sn appointment on the day is possible as long as you ring early. At the very least you get a phone call and follow up. Having faced some challenges with my health this year I can say the whole team stepped up and did their jobs with kindness, concern and professionalism.

recent_reviews.author: Lesley Wynter
recent_reviews.text: Consistently good levels of care & timely interaction should be the default for Health Centres, not my experience here. I initially received a high standard of care & concern, but that fast petered out into being advised of a month's wait to see a GP at the practice. I did not require a personal appointment, merely an adjustment in pain medication, to give an update in my condition & to ensure that my Fit Notes for my employer were concurrent. Literally a 5 minute telecom. Had I been a person with diminished capacity/lack of knowledge, I would have been left unattended for an unacceptably long period - that is dangerous practice. The doctors I have seen or managed to speak to have been clearly under duress. The reception staff are usually pleasant. I sent an email to the Practice Manager raising my concerns; all I got in return was a generic email. The difference between how quickly one used to be able to see a doctor circa 2000-2015 compared to now is shocking.

recent_reviews.author: Martin Reviews
recent_reviews.text: Goodcare Practice is very local to me, and as a disabled person with stroke and seizure conditions, access to a reliable GP surgery is essential. Unfortunately, my experience has been consistently poor and, at times, dangerous. For months, my physiotherapist requested that an updated discharge letter be uploaded to my NHS records so other consultants could access my medical information. The letter was ignored repeatedly. It was sent by post, delivered in person, emailed multiple times, and discussed directly with the Principal GP, who agreed to upload it — yet it still never happened. In total, the same letter was sent nine times. Shortly after, I tried to order my seizure medication via the NHS App and was blocked due to a supposed medication review. I contacted the practice and was told the app was “wrong” and that I wasn’t due a review. I was then told to email the practice. After several days with no response, I called again and was told I had used the “wrong” email address and that there is a separate email specifically for medication issues — something I had never been informed of. I emailed again and was told to wait 48 hours. By this point, my seizure medication had been blocked for five days. I began experiencing small seizures, and due to the risk of a serious or fatal seizure, I was forced to attend emergency services. No patient — especially one with life-threatening conditions — should be put in this position. The administration is disorganised, communication is unclear, and critical medication access was mishandled. Reception staff appear to act as gatekeepers without urgency, and management oversight feels severely lacking. This practice’s failures directly endangered my health. I would strongly urge anyone who relies on timely medication or coordinated care to think very carefully before depending on Goodcare Practice. Off to the hospital .

recent_reviews.author: Randa Imlahi
recent_reviews.text: I am writing to express my deep disappointment and frustration regarding an appalling experience I recently had with Dr. Zaman at your practice. I have been a registered patient with this GP for over 10 years, and I have always valued the care I received — until this incident, which has completely shattered my trust. I attended an appointment solely to support my sister, who was the patient that day. It was not my appointment, and Dr. Zaman is not even my assigned doctor. During the consultation, I asked a polite and reasonable question regarding my sister’s condition. In response, Dr. Zaman spoke to me in a rude, disrespectful, and dismissive manner that left both of us shocked. To make matters even worse, I later discovered that I had been removed from the GP practice entirely — without any discussion, justification, or chance to explain myself. This decision is completely unjustified, especially given that I was not even the patient in the consultation. I did nothing wrong, and yet I have been treated as though I had. I have repeatedly tried to speak to someone higher up about this issue and have requested to speak with Dr. Razak, but no one has responded. Instead, I have been falsely accused, ignored, and denied the basic fairness of being heard. This entire experience has been deeply upsetting and distressing, and it is unacceptable that a long-term patient should be treated in such a disrespectful and discriminatory manner. I am now struggling to find healthcare because of this completely unfair removal, and I find it heartbreaking that this is how your practice chooses to treat loyal patients. I am demanding that this matter be taken seriously and that a formal investigation be opened immediately. I expect a written explanation and apology, as well as reinstatement as a patient at the practice. I look forward to a prompt response.

recent_reviews.author: Rida Ahmed (Italiano El Masry)
recent_reviews.text: Golborne Medical Centre is, without a doubt, the best GP practice I have experienced in my time living in the UK. From the moment you step in, the welcoming atmosphere created by the reception team sets a wonderful tone for your visit. The staff are polite, attentive, and always ready to assist, making sure every patient feels comfortable and well-informed. The nurses and medical professionals show exceptional dedication and care, taking the time to listen and explain matters clearly. The doctors are not only experts in their field but also exhibit a rare empathy and understanding, treating each person with the dignity they deserve. The holistic approach to both physical and mental health at this centre is truly commendable. It is a privilege being registered with such a dedicated team, and I am so grateful for the outstanding service and care provided.

recent_reviews.author: Ms S
recent_reviews.text: Since changing to this GP practice, my experience has been very disappointing. I have had ongoing health issues, including asthma and a bladder problem that has lasted over three years. Despite attending multiple hospital appointments, there has been no proper GP follow-up, and my last appointment was over a year ago. Every winter I need my blue inhaler regularly, yet each month I face problems and delays when requesting it, even though this is a long-standing and well-documented condition. It feels like I have to argue just to receive basic medication. Overall, communication is poor, concerns are not taken seriously, and continuity of care is lacking. I do not feel supported or listened to as a patient.

recent_reviews.author: Dave
recent_reviews.text: I would give no stars if that were possible. I contacted the surgery to arrange an appointment to have stitches removed and was spoken to in an extremely rude and unprofessional manner by a male receptionist. When asked when I would like the appointment, I replied “as soon as possible.” In response, I was spoken to sharply and told that I could not call and expect an appointment the same day. I calmly explained that I was not expecting a same-day appointment and was simply answering the question I had been asked. Despite this, the receptionist continued to speak in a dismissive and condescending way, using phrases such as “say no more,” which I found wholly inappropriate and unprofessional in a healthcare setting. After eventually offering me an appointment for two days later, the receptionist ended the call abruptly the moment I confirmed, without any courtesy or confirmation. This forced me to call back, wait a further 10 minutes, and speak to another receptionist to ensure the appointment had actually been booked. In contrast, the second receptionist was polite, professional, and helpful, which only highlighted how unacceptable the first interaction was. I was also informed that calls are recorded, and I sincerely hope management listens to this call, as the behaviour displayed was entirely unsuitable for someone dealing with patients. People contact their GP surgery because they need medical care and support, not to be spoken to rudely or treated with impatience and disrespect. I will be submitting a formal complaint, as this level of conduct should not be tolerated in a healthcare environment.

recent_reviews.author: Helen Stokes
recent_reviews.text: I want to be honest I’m critical old school but young still:) if I’m desperate I get appointments. Jot all staff are great that’s true it looks like you have forced some to be there. However the physio is exceptional the doctors don’t just tend to hand you any old thing. Some are genuinely interested in how you are feeling I’ve had that on more than one occasion. I’ve had much worse surgeries in bilston such as bilson health centre. Often things can be out and f the person on the desks control. That’s why I’ve never got angry with them. They don’t get paid enough. Your health isn’t worth the stress with that and I get stressed easily very easy. The only thing I can advise is message them phone or arrive on same day before 8 am they have always tried their best with me and that’s the receptionists across all the surgeries not one or two each one has always tried to get an appointment so it’s not like they would know me personally I guess I’m trying to say. I can only suggest this. Times are changing we no longer get family doctors. They see loads a day. Yes I agree they get paid enough. One doctor though actually made me think differently he pointed out a truth. Last year not even year ago I was in hospital passed out with blood pressure of 200. Ended up in icu. Always known blood pressure issues so hospital should kept me in they sent me home as I woke up told me it was stress. My doctor pointed out I couldn’t have had a panic attack whilst unconscious that that’s what’s known as a symptomatic heart attack. It made sense I don’t remember much but I know I wernt panicking as I was only at 111 I though I had a water infection and was weekend.they told me go see my doctor and as my doctor rightly pointed out. How can I monitor your blood p24 hours I can’t come home with you. I can’t xray you. I can’t send blood test to reception and get back within hour . I can only do so much. In all honesty they changed over years of the way I thought. I thought that’s right he has a point. Sometimes though I get it it’s easier to blame who’s in front of you. Unfortunately when they refer you or it’s something out of their control it becomes a complaint. This isn’t a lecture please don’t think this. However I made me think when he put it like this to me. Also it don’t help when people don’t cancel appointments. That could be used for you. Just like you get the arrogant people who won’t move out the way when an ambulance has its siren on “. That’s a second that could save someone. I guess it’s a new way looking at things

recent_reviews.text: Pocklington Group Practice has to be the best doctors that I have ever been to. Me and my family moved to the area 16 months ago and the process of joining the surgery was so easy. I have a lot of different health problems so I see a lot of different doctors and nurses and they are all so nice and friendly and I never feel rushed when am in with any of the doctors or nurses they really do take there time to make sure that needs have been met. AND LETS NOT FORGET ABOUT ALL THE STAFF IN THE DISPENSARY. Let me tell you all You are all AMAZING AND SO KIND HEARTED💖 All the hard work you do is incredible, they are always there to make sure your repeat prescriptions are done on time and it’s always service with a big smile from all of them. They get to know you as a person not just a patient and sometimes I think they get forgotten about because we don’t get to see how hard and dedicate they are to all the patients behind there dispensary door. Thank you to all the incredible staff once again keep doing what you always seem to do and you won’t go far wrong. From Donna Fitzpatrick x

recent_reviews.author: Ann Stevenson
recent_reviews.text: I’ve only been offered a routine telephone appointment with a GP in several weeks to discuss a probable posterior fossa brain cyst identified incidentally on an MRI scan for another condition. I’ve been waiting for the surgery to get back to me, as they stated they hadn’t received a letter from my consultant despite me receiving a copy of this over a week ago. This will be 4weeks after finding out about the neurological anomaly on my brain scan and experiencing worsening symptoms relating to this. I’m beside myself with anxiety and feel badly let down by the surgery. The receptionist was very blunt and insensitive on the phone both when offering the appointment and when I called to request an appointment with a GP with this information a few weeks ago. I wouldn’t recommend this surgery at all.

recent_reviews.text: My mother in law called the practice in August of this year to arrange a phone consultation with the mental health nurse as this is what she asked for, she was then passed on to the community link worker which was not what my mother in law asked for as she had previously dealt with said link worker who was very unhelpful , & decided to cancel her appointment with the link worker as she wasn’t what my mother was looking for to confide in. My mother in law then called the practice again to arrange a phone call in September to speak with the mental health nurse who within a couple of weeks decided she would cancel my mother in laws appointment without my mother in laws knowing or permission. She found this out after waiting all day on the arranged appointment day for said phone call & it took for my mother in law to contact the practice & find out from a hopeless receptionist that the mental health nurse had cancelled her phone call. Avoid this practice at all costs they shun you whilst at your lowest & pick & choose whose mentally or physically suffering enough to entertain.

recent_reviews.text: Every recent interaction with them, they've messed it up. ADHD diagnosis, they tell me I missed an appointment they never informed me of and mixed up my records with a woman with cancer, only noticing once they're on the phone with me and audibly reading the words "Ovarian cancer". This is on top of telling me they'd referred me and not even done that. Ear infection, prescribed Doxycycline until the infection became immune to it, presumably because they didn't check the record before prescribing more. Taking blood, told me it'd be fine I had doxycycline and later on assumed I'd need an MRI scan for fatty liver because of it. Absolute mess, writing this review because all this has happened and got some cheek on the phone because I was a little passive-aggressive about waiting more than half a year for an ADHD diagnosis due to aforementioned incompetence.

recent_reviews.author: Chris Wicks
recent_reviews.text: We are so grateful for the kind, sympathetic and very helpful response from the surgery today. My wife became ill during our tour in Scotland. We extended our stay in Pittenweem for her to recover. Finally we needed a GP appointment. The reception staff were really helpful and we were given an appointment with the Doctor at Elie. A most helpful consultation followed. It gave us reassurance and a prescription for medication. I dare say we were fortunate to find a quiet winters day to present the problem and the response was brilliant. A big thank you. Of course at other times the wonderful NHS Scotland services are under great pressure and patience is necessary, bravo to everyone involved.

recent_reviews.author: Neelam S
recent_reviews.text: This is not the first issue I’ve had with this practice. There appears to be a recurring pattern of disregarding my clear request to see a doctor. When I recently called for an appointment, I explicitly asked to see a doctor. Chloe (receptionist) attempted to book me with a physician associate instead and implied they were effectively the same as a doctor, stating they “do the same thing.” That is misleading. Doctors and physician associates do not have the same training, qualifications, or prescribing authority. I should not have to argue repeatedly just to secure the type of appointment I asked for in the first place. I was then told I was being rude simply for asserting my request. Patients have the right to be given accurate information and to request an appointment with a doctor without being pressured or misled. This ongoing issue needs to be addressed.

recent_reviews.author: Lakshmi Periyasamy
recent_reviews.text: I have been registered with two different GP practices before, in different places, but I can honestly say this one has been the best experience for me. From the moment I joined, I noticed a real difference in the way the practice is run and how patients are cared for.Whenever I call, the staff do their very best to arrange an appointment for me, and they are always polite and supportive. That itself makes a huge difference, as I feel that my concerns are taken seriously and that I am being looked after. My GP, Dr. Machado, is truly outstanding. He listens with patience, explains everything clearly, and gives practical advice that I can follow. What I value the most is his positive and reassuring approach , h e never rushes me, and his kind words and encouragement give me real confidence in managing my health. From my personal experience, the care and support I have received here are far better than what I had before. I feel very fortunate to be registered with this practice and to have Dr. Machado as my GP. I would strongly recommend this practice to anyone looking for excellent, patient-centred care.

recent_reviews.author: Shreena Bahara
recent_reviews.text: I am writing to express my extreme dissatisfaction with the service provided by this practice, which I can only describe as completely unacceptable and the worst I have encountered in West Brom. The telephone lines are consistently unavailable, ringing out throughout the day. I have personally witnessed my partner repeatedly attempting to call with no success. He had a scheduled telephone appointment with Dr Haruna at 2:00pm. Despite this, no call was received until 5:15pm — two and a half hours late. When Dr Haruna eventually called, the same issue that occurred earlier that morning happened again: we could not hear her due to problems with the phone line. An alternative contact number was provided immediately and we were advised she would call back within 30 minutes. No return call was received. We then contacted the practice ourselves, only to be told that Dr Haruna had already gone home. This is completely unacceptable. A patient was left without a consultation after waiting all day, despite doing everything possible to engage with the appointment. I am absolutely disgusted by the level of patient care and what I consider to be negligence towards patients. In addition, the attitude of the front-of-house staff is consistently rude and unprofessional, and entirely inappropriate for a patient-facing role. Due to the seriousness of these concerns, I will be making an official complaint to the CCG. This practice urgently needs to address its communication systems, staff conduct, and overall approach to patient care.

recent_reviews.author: Laura Wyglendacz
recent_reviews.text: I have left this GP practice because of their inability to address my request for reasonable adjustments in a timely and professional manner. Receptionists and practice manager seemed to find it very difficult to communicate with each other and with me about my straightforward request for a conversation, which I had to make 4 times in the space of 8 weeks. By the time I finally received a voicemail from the manager, I had lost faith in their ability to handle basic tasks (it is a legal requirement to respond to requests for reasonable adjustments per Equality Act 2010) like this so have gone elsewhere. The nurses were great. Aimee was so good when I had a cervical smear a couple of months postpartum and with a history of pain. Some of the doctors were good, but others created a stressful and rushed environment during appointments, and I was always having to ask them to slow down and not interrupt me. Dr Catriona was always kind and patient whilst being straightforward and honest, thank you. I hope I can find a better run surgery elsewhere, which has a competent and modern approach to running a service and provides access to healthcare in an environment suited to my disabilities that I am entitled to. My request (if I had been able to make it) was simply to have the very bright artificial lighting turned down or off during consultations, and for Doctors to be made aware to slow down, let me structure the appointment the way it made sense to me, and not interrupt so I had time to listen, process and respond to questions and suggestions during appointments. I left more than one appointment without my issue being resolved because I was so overwhelmed, rushed, upset and frustrated and it caused distress over days on several occasions.

recent_reviews.author: Preservation Fitness Personal Trainer. Bristol.
recent_reviews.text: 1 Star – A System Focused on Managing Pain, Not Fixing It In 2014, I went to my GP with upper back pain and tingling in my arms. I was a self-employed carpenter with 20 years in the trade. My body was my livelihood. What followed was nearly a decade of chronic pain — and a treatment pathway that focused almost entirely on symptom management. The default response was painkillers. When those didn’t work, stronger painkillers. Then steroid injections. At no point was I given a long-term, structured rehabilitation plan focused on correcting posture, muscular imbalance, or movement dysfunction — despite this clearly being a musculoskeletal issue. I don’t believe the individuals I saw lacked care. The problem felt systemic. The protocol seems built around managing pain quickly and cheaply in the short term, rather than investing in proper rehabilitation that could prevent long-term suffering. Eventually, scans showed rotator cuff tendon impingements, tendinopathies, and C7 foraminal cervical stenosis. Yet even with clear findings, the approach didn’t shift toward comprehensive rehabilitation. Over time, I lost my ability to work. I had to give up my 20-year career as a carpenter because the pain became unmanageable. Years of medication also left me with ongoing stomach problems that I still deal with today. What troubles me most is this: musculoskeletal conditions are often treatable with structured, progressive rehabilitation. But GPs are general practitioners — they are not trained rehabilitation specialists. Without deeper biomechanical assessment, issues like postural dysfunction and muscle imbalance can be missed entirely. Out of desperation, I retrained and studied rehabilitation myself. Through targeted strength training, correcting movement patterns, and addressing long-standing imbalances, I rebuilt my body. Today, I am no longer living in chronic upper body pain. That tells me the issue wasn’t that my condition was untreatable — it was that the system wasn’t set up to treat it properly. My hope is that musculoskeletal protocols within the NHS evolve to prioritise early, structured rehabilitation over long-term reliance on medication and injections. It would save careers. It would save quality of life. And in the long run, it would likely save public money too. No one should lose their livelihood because the system defaults to managing symptoms instead of correcting causes. If you’re living with ongoing upper back pain, shoulder pain, or tingling in your arms — and you feel like you’re only being offered temporary fixes — please don’t wait ten years like I did. Chronic pain is not something you just have to “manage.” In many cases, it can be understood, addressed, and improved through proper assessment, structured rehabilitation, and correcting muscular imbalances. At Preservation Fitness Bristol, my mission is simple: To help hardworking people rebuild their bodies properly — not just mask symptoms. I understand what it feels like to lose your strength, your confidence, and your livelihood because of pain. That’s why my approach focuses on: Identifying the root cause Correcting posture and movement dysfunction Rebuilding strength progressively Providing ongoing support and guidance If you’re ready to take control of your recovery instead of relying solely on pain relief, reach out. Don’t let chronic pain define the next decade of your life.

recent_reviews.author: Sam Jayne
recent_reviews.text: Terrible GP practice, possibly one of the worse in cambridge. Previously I had a shared care agreement with a private consultant to access my ADHD meds. There has been zero to none empathy about how their restrictive surgery practices seriously impact the quality of individuals health and well being. Since joining the surgery, which incidentally is dictated by your address you cannot just sign up anywhere. My health and well being has been seriously compromised by the surgeries refusal to prescribe me urgent repeat prescription. I am asthmatic and I have been diagnosed as asthmatic for 50 years. I have routinely been prescribed Ventolin Inhalers for the past 50 years with additional prednisolone when needed. Without the correct inhalers I could have an asthma attack and die. This surgery had repeatedly refused to prescribe life or death medication. I was told that it was my fault that I had missed an appointment that was necessary to prescribe routine medication. I had explained to them that without my ADHD medication I forget everything, including appointments, meetings and other responsibilities, including the completion daily tasks to look after my basic needs. There is no acknowledgement or empathy regarding the fact I am seriously depressed because my ADHD medication is necessary to elevate my dopamine levels and balance my moods. There is ZERO empathy from reception staff or my GP Dr Hakker. I have repeatedly expressed how important it is for me to have the correct asthma medication and explained that I could die without the correct medication but I still have to wait weeks for an appointment that I may or may not remember. In the meantime I could die from an Asthma attack.

recent_reviews.author: Sarah Martin
recent_reviews.text: Now, I can't say all the receptionists are unprofessional and rude here, I do believe there are some professional people working there, but I did have the unpleasant experience of encountering a rather abrupt, unhelpful, unpleasant, unkind, loud, argumentative, unempthetic receptionist. It was an extremely unpleasant experience on my part. I was only asking for some clarification and some help over appointment issues. The receptionist in question seemed to be becoming rather frustrated with me even though I was just asking normal, general questions, she then gave me unsolicited advice about how I should manage my families appointments. I am a healthcare professional myself, and I work in a busy hospital environment, there would be a variety of complaints against me if I spoke to my patients in the same manner. I believe some further professional training would not go amiss here, especially considering the amount of complaining reviews here that target the same subject, as a general manager of a practice, you should be taking these quite seriously. This kind of experience makes all the staff look terrible. Fortunately, the health care assistant helping me that day at my actual appointment was very polite, she bent over backwards to help me after my appointment, and she explained why some of the letters were on the system yet. I think it's quite important as a practice that you should look into this matter, patient care is very important, people need to feel like they're being heard, and their issues are important, to encounter such an unpleasant front of house staff member, it's very disheartening towards the trust. I really suggest there are some consequences to these actions, and that some staff members cannot go around treating patients as if they are below them or a nuisance.

recent_reviews.author: J S
recent_reviews.text: Where to start. I have been a patent here for a number of years and there are a couple of really great doctors here, Dr. Butcher and Dr. Arkley are a real credit to their profession. The dispensary team are also really lovely, the lady who used to work at boots is so proficient and friendly, and the other lady is also very helpful and caring. They are a joy to deal with. However, this is all over shadowed by the abject horror of the reception team. To get access to any of the above, you have to navigate a gauntlet of toxic, ill informed, entitled and bullying reception staff. They frequently give out completely incorrect information and then blame the patients, there is zero accountability for mistakes made and the practice manager is evasive and unaccountable. There is one particularly bad receptionist (mentioned in other reviews) who is so hostile and bullying that I can’t for the life of me work out how she continues to be employed in a care giving role. I recently was refused an appointment for an issue that she said wasn’t their responsibility. After 2 months of this saga and 3 refused appointment requests, I had to screenshot the nhs website to prove it was in fact their responsibility. I was then reluctantly given an appointment, with no apology or explanation. I was sent a letter about a change in the service recently and when I phoned up, the receptionist asked who had told me about this change as they wouldn’t have said that. She then did an abrupt 180 when I told her it was a letter from them. I actually feel sick with anxiety at having to make an appointment and I tent to suffer with ailments until they are intolerable, just to avoid having to go through the utter hell of talking to the reception staff or battling with Anima. I have been in tears on numerous occasions just trying to access basic medical care. This bullying, rude and medically ill informed team needs addressing as a matter of urgency. I have been reluctant to write a review for fear of the repercussions next time I have to phone, but then I realised there is literally no way they could be any more hostile and unpleasant that they currently are. The anima appointment system is also completely redundant and if you have job you basically can’t ever use it as it’s only open at for 15 mins in the morning when you are driving to work. There is no alternative to this as the reception team refuse to help if you are unable to use anima. It is such a shame that a good clinical team is being overshadowed so catastrophically by a handful of people who are so unpleasant.

recent_reviews.text: So disappointed. One star is a star too much. Saw the very unhelpful Dr Huggins yesterday. I wanted to discuss my adhd. My active mind is keeping me awake at night and I’m getting about 3.5 hours sleep a night. Dr Huggins spoke over me and told me I was here to discuss sleep issues. He told me in a loud voice and brusque manner that if I needed to discuss my mental health I needed a different appointment. I pointed out calmly that my neurodivergence wasn’t a mental health issue and I didn’t appreciate him raising his voice or being rude. I also added if I did have wellbeing issues then his attitude was neither helpful or kind. Dr Huggins then stated if I wasn’t there to discuss sleep I could leave, if I didn’t like how he spoke to me I could leave. So I left. I’d waited 3 weeks for that very unhelpful interaction. Maybe Dr Huggins doesn’t know much about neurodivergence, maybe he’s forgotten that he is supposed to to be supportive and helpful. Whatever his reasons, there is no place for aggressive behaviour, raising your voice and being condescendingly rude. Dr Huggins needs refresher training or observations to evaluate his aptitude for the role he is handsomely paid for. At least I know who to avoid in future. A small win!
