recent_reviews.author: Khalifa Aaliyah
recent_reviews.text: The attitudes of the receptionists are horrendous, the only helpful and nice receptionist is the tall blonde one. She actually listens, whereas the rest think they're higher than what they are and feel they can speak down to you. They're dismissive and cut you off before you can even explain your situation and then they wonder why they find themselves having to ask you again what's wrong, if you don't like your job get a new one! And if you'd listen in the first instance it wouldn't take you twice the time to sort issues out. I explained on the phone the day prior that I needed needles to administer my insulin and requested an emergency prescription because they hadn't bothered to update my repeat prescription online when the hospital had advised them to almost 2 weeks ago, I explained everything clearly on the phone what I needed and that it's the needles specifically for the insulin. I'm a high risk pregnancy and I've had several hypos within the last 2 weeks and so it could genuinely be a matter of life or death if I don't have the appropriate prescription! I was assured that the FULL prescription would be available for me to collect, it wasn't! They didn't give me needles. When trying to correct THEIR error, the receptionist had the nerve to tell me not to get frustrated even though I wasn't I was simply trying to explain myself but she wouldn't stop cutting me off to allow me to explain! Then told me there's nothing she can do and that I'll just have to try to get an appointment tomorrow. It's not my fault they're incompetent and don't know the difference between lancets for testing blood sugar levels and the screw-in needles for insulin. She said well the doctor can't do anything if it's not on the repeat prescription list. They were instructed in the beginning of March to update it by the hospital! Why is vital information not being processed when it's received from the hospital!? Stop acting like the patients are an inconvenience when your job is public facing. Some of the doctors are incredibly rude and dismissive too. The majority of the staff are in dire need of retraining and personality transplants. I've seen the way the receptionists have spoken to vulnerable patients in the past too, absolute disgrace! I'm only still there because my GP actually gets things done otherwise I'd have switched long ago!

Absolutely appalling place.

recent_reviews.author: Ignacio IK
recent_reviews.text: I have to say the reception staff at this surgery are extremely rude and unnecessarily difficult to deal with. Once you finally get to speak with a doctor, everything is fine — professional, respectful, no issues at all. But with reception, it feels like they want to act as if they are the doctors themselves, questioning and interfering far beyond their role. My message to them is simple: stick to your job — answering calls and booking appointments. Do not overstep your limits. Another serious issue is the inconsistent way patients are treated. When members of the Asian community come in and speak with the reception staff in their own language, suddenly the service becomes excellent, polite, and helpful. Why is this not the same for everyone? Reception staff must treat all patients equally and professionally, regardless of who they are. The reception team needs proper training in respect, professionalism, and equality. And if they cannot provide that, they should be replaced with staff who can.

recent_reviews.author: Greg Ward
recent_reviews.text: My wife and I regularly talk about how lucky we are to have this medical practice as our local GP clinic. Dr Patel could well be the hardest working GP in the NHS; on a couple of occasions we've received calls at 7pm or 8pm ensuring he got back to us as he cleared his hefty backlog of calls for the day, given his nature to listen and give you time to discuss your issues. Dr Jha is also incredibly thorough and meticulous, reading her notes BEFORE your appointment, knowing your issues in detail, and even recounting previous discussions from 12 months prior. Both excellent technical doctors with a real personal touch and genuine care and empathy. Finally, Charles does a fantastic job on reception, always doing his absolute best to find you some availability, with a smile.

recent_reviews.author: Liam Day
recent_reviews.text: Incredibly frustrating administrative barriers to basic care. I had a clinically agreed-upon follow-up clearly documented on my file by the GP. When I tried to book it, the practice refused and insisted I submit a brand new eConsult instead. eConsult is a triage tool for new issues, not a hurdle to block pre-agreed follow-ups. Even after the receptionist confirmed my review was on the system, they refused to book it. Forcing patients to jump through arbitrary administrative hoops for established, documented issues is obstructive and poor continuity of care. It feels like the practice is more interested in deflecting patients and mediating their own 'quick wins' rather than providing genuine medical attention. After having to constantly challenge and correct their illogical policies, I am seriously considering moving to a new practice.

recent_reviews.author: Gregory Smith
recent_reviews.text: This used to be an exemplary medical practice where all staff were helpful and caring. Something has happened to change this. The reception staff, nurses, phlebotomist are all still the charming, polite and caring people they always have been. However, the doctors and paramedics go out of their way to never actually see patients. They come over as arrogant and far too precious to show any empathy or care. Personally I feel very let-down by the lack of care and interest shown by the doctors/paramedics. They put up barriers that prevent patients from getting the care they need. The first barrier is the so-called triage form; firstly this asks you to describe the problem, only allowing you to focus on one problem, if you have a number of related health issues, there is no way to describe these. This section basically asks you to diagnose yourself. The second section asks you about how long the problem has been ongoing, far enough, but you can’t help feeling there’s a ‘catch’ to this question. If you put down a short time that gives the doctors the chance to say “let’s see how it progresses then”, if you put down a long time that gives them the opportunity to say “well, you've put up with it for this long, why are you bothering me now?” Actually they won’t say this because they go out of their way to never speak to patients, much preferring to send a text to which you cannot reply. Start again and describe the problem (one only). The next question asks what you have done to help yourself, fair enough, but if you are having to rely on a self-diagnosis, you could have got it all wrong. The next question asks if there’s anything you’re particularly worried about OF COURSE THERE IS OTHERWISE I WOULDN’T BE FILLING OUT THIS STUPID FORM. The final question asks how you would like them to help. So you've been asked to diagnose yourself and now they want you to prescribe your treatment. I would like someone at the practice to explain why they are so adverse to actually seeing patients, other practices in the area, which are just as busy, go out of their way to see patients. The best you can hope for from Neetside is a phone call if you’re lucky. It is invidious to mention doctors by name but there is one who takes great delight in telling you how clever he is, howmuch he knows, how important he is and giving you irrelevant information (I had to listen to how African tribes people are treated for anaemia – hello, this is Bude not Namibia. If you are offered an appointment with this particular doctor set a side a considerable length of time, for two reasons: the fist is that he thinks there is nothing wrong in keeping patients waiting an hour beyond their appointment time, the second is that before he’ll do anything for you he has to tell you how important he is, how much he knows and irrelevant information (I really didn’t need to know his wife is vegan) A very sad decline in standards from what used to be the best doctor’s practice for miles around. I Suggest you stay at home ask Dr Google or AI what’s wrong, the treatment you need and get well again, quickly!

Terrible, terrible service that made my sister feel really small and was just nasty.

recent_reviews.author: Robert Bache
recent_reviews.text: Arrived latish Friday afternoon with an eye condition. The Receptionist took details and referred me to Kate, the Paramedic. I did not even manage to sit down in the waiting room when I was called to see Kate. She examined my eye and called Dr. Richard Coates who in turn called Dr. Simon Mathieson. Within minutes of arriving I was seen by 2 doctors who referred me for a phone consultation with the eye clinic. Within 20 minutes of arriving home they phoned and prescribed Chloramphenicol. The following morning I went to the Chemist to get some but they could not dispense it as a proper prescription was required. I went to A&E at the North Devon Hospital and within an hour I had the medication. The NHS at its best. Thank You.

recent_reviews.author: Aaron Godwin
recent_reviews.text: Just to start by saying that I have never left a review for anywhere else before. I joined the surgery around summer last year. Ive had issues with my health for the past 4+ years and have understood that the NHS is under strain and has long waiting times etc. Unfortunately, over the past 8/9 months, my health issues have got substantially worse and I then joined the surgery. From the start I struggled with the online booking system but thats okay. It seems when you need an emergency appointment, it is almost impossible to get one. I recently rang up to try and get an appointment and was told that I would get a call back. When I did get the call back I was told that it is not urgent (even though I have been badgering the surgery for the past 8/9 months) and I have to wait for a future appointment, which is a month wait for a phone call appointment! They send links for appointments that have nothing available etc. I have been missing work/lost my social life/cancelled holidays/dont feel safe to drive all due to the way I have been feeling, so to be told that its not urgent is really great. I have also contacted privately to try and get through to somebody but this has come to nothing. I would be okay with this if it was worth the wait. On the handful of occasions I have managed to get in, there have been a few times when I have left feeling like Im not listened to, fobbed off, spoken to very patronisingly or told to make a diary. This has been nurses and receptionist as well. Ive only managed to get 1 set of blood tests in all this time! No other tests have been done. No referrals sent off (even though it was promised). I will give credit to one doctor - Kathryn Hayman. She is the only one who has ordered tests and actually listened etc but the wait to get back in to see her is too long! I thought I might be the only one who feels like this but after seeing other reviews I'm clearly not! I understand that all GPs/nurses are all under pressure, but if things were done properly early on then there wouldnt be people coming back so much.

recent_reviews.author: Sherry Holloway
recent_reviews.text: Being subjected to the endless repetitive random holding messages while waiting in the phone call queue makes you feel even more ill than you already are. Admin staff must be insufficient given there are only one or two in the call queue but yet you have to wait ages for your call to be answered. Worse still is making sick patients listen to a long list of sicknesses they don’t have and inappropriate messages like urging you to download the app is awful. Especially the dire threats and even the tone of the man’s voice if patients abuse staff - which most decent people would not do anyway. The holding message asks for dignity and respect for staff. What about dignity and respect for your patients? Why subject them to a barrage of unnecessary messages when they need to call? No one calls their doctor unless they have to so why do this to them? “Have you considered visiting your local pharmacy? Have ear ache? shingles? string of diseases/illnesses? please contact your local pharmacy, download the app, in fact, do anything but just get off the phone and stop bothering us” - that’s the message the surgery is giving out. Being forced to listen to a barrage of messages smacks of disrespect to ill patients and makes them feel much worse.

recent_reviews.author: A C
recent_reviews.text: The 1 star reviews are so right here. This is our family surgery due to it's location and changing to a new surgery seems impossible due to wait lists. I've had consistent negative experiences with the receptionist, they are incredibly rude, dismissive, blunt and just awful to deal with. At the end of the call you actually don't want to make an appointment as they treat you like a total nuisance. The interaction is much more stressful than it needs to be and instead of feeling supported you are left spoken down to as though you are inconveniencing them. I don't understand how these receptionists can get away with being so rude and unhelpful. Kindness is free! I hope they take the feedback from these reviews seriously. Totally understand someone may be having a bad day, the current state of the NHS, all the reasons under the sun, but as a place centred around care, how can you be made to feel so unwelcome. Extremely disheartening. To end on a positive note, the handful of times I have managed to see a GP they have been helpful and nice. Just need to get past the awful receptionists. Good luck to everyone having to call them. Hopefully the new online system replaces the calls and no one will need to deal with the surgery receptionists again! Regarding the new online system, the info about this is the 2min voice recorded message about the new service, details are minimal, basically google the surgery's name. Don't expect anything via post or email or anything even though the changes are huge and for the better.

Our team works hard to make as many appointments available as possible, but at present the demand for GP appointments is higher than the capacity we have. If you have concerns about the wider issue of appointment availability, we kindly suggest raising this with your local MP. recent_reviews.author: Tony Evans
recent_reviews.text: I have been so pleased with the high quality of care and service during the last 3 years of attending the Stanton Surgery. However, the very poor level of service provided by the dispensary this morning was jaw dropping! I arrived at the dispensary this morning to collect my prescription only to find it was closed for the day for staff training. Obviously staff need time for training but I had run out of my medication. I asked the surgery receptionist whether I could have my medication and was told to come back tomorrow. I wasn’t happy with her response so I asked to see the practice manager. After 5 minutes the dispensary manager appeared with my medication. When I asked her why I wasn’t notified of a planned closure day I was abruptly rebuked by her and told I should have collected the medication earlier. As I tried to suggest the surgery should notify users of the dispensary she retorted that I’d got my medication now and turned away from me and walked into the dispensary wearing a sly smile. I was left gob smacked at the complete lack of customer service I received from the receptionist and the dispensary manager. Hopefully any future training should focus on providing an acceptable quality of customer service. In the mean time I’ll be looking at other options to obtain my medication.

recent_reviews.author: S Thompson
recent_reviews.text: Unfortunately, like many others who have shared their reviews of this practice - we have had a shocking experience with the receptionist of this clinic. Today, my husband tried to drop off a stool sample for our 5 yr old daughter who has been very ill for 4 days. Unbeknown to us - the walk in clinic we took her to on Saturday was in a different borough to phoenix and so while they had advised us that her notes would be updated and we could simply drop off the sample, it turns out the notes were in the post. Rather than trying to understand the situation or show any empathy, the receptionist was dismissive, told him she could do nothing and basically told him to leave and fill out a form. Despite the rudeness, when he told me what had happened I filled out the form and returned to the clinic two hours later and unfortunately was met by the same receptionist who also cut me off mid sentence and told me she couldn’t take the sample and repeated her stock response of fill in a form. I politely told her I understood but that I had filled in said form. She told me to leave and wait till the doctor responded. I explained that I had a sick daughter at home and a full time job so going backwards and forwards was unhelpful. Begrudgingly She checked the system for me and found the doctor has responded - she then proceeded to berate me for not having told her about the response from the doctor. When I advised I hadn’t received a text she said - exact words- ‘well I’m not a mind reader’. When I asked her to not be so rude she offered to get her manager which I gladly accepted. She then launched a verbal tyrade about the problems I was causing, stormed out of reception, brought her manager back and proceeded to tell her, loudly, infront of other patients that I had demanded she take my daughters stool sample. I calmly explained to her manager what had actually transpired and her manager apologised for her behaviour. While the manager was very respectful and helpful, the situation was clearly not a surprise to her and now having read the other reviews I can see why. Perhaps she was having a bad day, perhaps she is having many bad days but I do not understand why anyone would do that job who possesses not an ounce of helpfulness or compassion. To the managers of the practice, I will raise this formally with you - although it seems you have done nothing with the previous feedback. To prospective patients, if you would like to be shown any level of respect at a time when you probably need it the most, do not waste your time here. There are plenty more clinics that understand the care in healthcare.

I had been worried about my lump for a long time - it had grown considerably in the past months, but was advised that it would be impossible for it to be removed on the NHS - and even if I get a referral, the waiting time for a specialist consultant would be months. When my GP (Vine Hall Surgery in Molesey) suggested Thorkhill Surgery and Dr Teresa Mitchell, little did I know that my lump would be gone within a week. I am so impressed by Dr Mitchell, the way she reassured me and subsequently removed my lump - I couldn't believe it! I just want to express my gratitude to Dr Mitchell (and her assistant) for everything they do and in this instance - for restoring my respect and belief in the NHS.

recent_reviews.text: Only became a patient at this GP recently after my move to Oakham. My previous GP back in Northamptonshire was absolutely abysmal. So I have to say, these guys do seem pretty on the ball. Perhaps I’m just not used to having my phone call answered in less than two hours, or being able to get a blood test booked in within 6 weeks. A big fan of their online service as well; both the telephone line and online services are available throughout the day, which is a positive change for me! We can’t all be available to contact at 8am. My first experience here was for a blood test yesterday, followed by some further contact today. recent_reviews.author: David Parker
recent_reviews.text: Following tooth surgery on 17/7 I developed continuing pain in the lower jaw and mouth. After 2weeks I returned to the dentist. No dental cause could be found. I went to an orthodontist. An adjustment was made to a denture which proved ineffective. I was advised to speak with a doctor. I made application but was refused a consultation. I was told to contact a dentist despite already explaining that I had done so. The pain continued and I made a second application to see a doctor with further explanation. A consultation was again refused. I returned to my orthodontist and had a new denture made for no reason other than experiment. The pain continued. I am unable to sleep or eat. I had no alternative but to apply a third time to the clinic for help. I have received a reply saying that a doctor will consider the application and contact me in two weeks. 2.7 on reviews exaggerates the care on offer at Oakham Clinic. 13/9 As addendum. Strep throat caused further problem and difficulties in swallowing. I visited Sarah the pharmacist at Boots adjacent to the clinic. What a difference. Sarah was understanding, sympathetic and as busily efficient as ever. After basic examination I was given antibiotics and hope for some relief. Thank you Sarah 5*.

recent_reviews.text: The new booking system is useless. My mum tried to book an appointment and the next available was in 10 days. They said if is not suitable to ring 111. If you keep this new system we have to change GP
recent_reviews.raw_card_text: Ancuta Tamba12 reviews2 months ago The new booking system is useless. My mum tried to book an appointment and the next available was in 10 days. They said if is not suitable to ring 111. If you keep this new system we have to change GPLike Share Response from the owner 2 months agoI'm sorry you've not got on with our new appointment system. Since 1.10.25 GP surgeries have been contractually bound by the government to have an online consultation method in some form or other. When researching our options, the benefits of Rapid Health were that there was a consistent approach made across triage decisions, and an emphasis on prioritising 'health need' rather than 'health want' i.e. a same or next day appointment is offered to those who medically need it rather than because you want it sooner. More routine requests will be offered appointments further in the future, but the waits for these e.g. 10 days in your case is still much sooner than what we had to offer for routine appointments prior to this system (often 28days plus). Try us again when you next have need to and you will find the appointment on offer will depend on the urgency and medical need of the problem.

recent_reviews.text: I had a very disappointing experience at Hyde Park Surgery. I attended the surgery simply to request a stamp on my child’s school application form. My daughter is already registered at the practice, and the doctor had agreed to sign and stamp the form. However, the reception staff and the manager then demanded £40 just for a surgery stamp, which I found unreasonable and unacceptable. To make matters worse, the original application form was destroyed without my consent or any prior communication, causing unnecessary stress and delay to my child’s school application. Throughout this process, the attitude of the staff was rude and unprofessional, and the matter was treated as a major issue despite being a very simple request. The lack of clear communication and courtesy was extremely disappointing. Overall, this was a very poor experience, and I would expect much better professionalism, transparency, and respect from a GP surgery.

I was then told to scan a QR code, but again, this was communicated in a manner that felt disrespectful. I understand staff may be busy, but the way patients are spoken to makes a big difference. A little courtesy and professionalism would go a long way in making people feel welcome, especially when registering for the first time.

recent_reviews.author: Arthur Voit
recent_reviews.text: We came to the UK with a certain level of scepticism about free healthcare and general practice overall. However, our experience at this clinic completely changed our perspective. We were genuinely impressed by how quickly everything was arranged — the appointment was scheduled within just two days, and the level of professionalism and knowledge demonstrated by the specialists was outstanding. I have Type 1 diabetes, and during the visit I received a full assessment and was prescribed all the necessary medications, sensors, and supplies on the same day. Everything was provided completely free of charge, and I was able to collect it immediately from a nearby pharmacy. Honestly, I was shocked — in the best possible way. Special thanks to Dr. Matharu for the attentive, professional, and genuinely caring approach. Highly recommend this clinic to anyone looking for efficient and high-quality medical care in the UK.

recent_reviews.author: Rina Begum
recent_reviews.text: Formal Complaint – Ongoing Negligence, Poor Management and Lack of Compassion I requested to be seen three days ago explaining I was in severe pain from an ongoing issue and requested a female GP for personal and medical comfort reasons. This was clearly stated in my booking request. I arrived early for my 9:45 appointment on 10/10/25, waited over 20 minutes, and only after I asked what was happening was I told my appointment had been made with a male GP despite my clear request. The receptionist said the GP who triaged it didn’t tell them, and when I asked why no one checked my notes, she said there was a lot of writing to read and it’s small. That response alone says everything about the standards here. It’s astonishing that basic duties like reading patient notes are treated as optional. There are serious reasons women may refuse male doctors – religion, trauma, or safety – all ignored through sheer carelessness. They then rebooked me for 2:20 PM the same day after their own mistake. I mistakenly thought it was 2:30 PM and arrived slightly late, only to be cancelled on instantly. So it’s fine for them to waste patients’ time and mess up bookings, but the moment you’re confused because of their errors, you’re punished for it. I left in pain and requested my scan results to take elsewhere. I’d had a scan on 25th September, told results would be ready in two weeks. Yet they booked me for a results appointment on 20th October – nearly a month later – despite my worsening pain and repeated requests. I asked for a female GP because I’ve had years of male doctors dismissing symptoms later proven serious. For many women, this isn’t preference, it’s about safety and dignity. The so-called apology I received was half-hearted and clearly rehearsed, more about getting me out of the way than taking accountability. This isn’t an isolated incident. Reception staff constantly mishandle bookings and patient details, once signing me in under another patient’s name, leading to wasted appointments. The recall nurses are just as unprofessional. Despite me asking them not to call, they continued repeatedly. One recall nurse even said, “You know you can just say you don’t want the appointment instead of saying you’ll call back,” and hung up on me mid-sentence, during a time I was already managing a health crisis for a family member. That kind of disrespect is beyond unprofessional. And Nurse Lucy – for nearly a year she told me to keep buying and using the same medication that didn’t work. I spent a fortune following her advice while my condition worsened. I told her it was ruining my life and mental health and begged her to investigate further – she ignored me. A private doctor later confirmed the treatment was completely inappropriate and should have been stopped long ago. Nurse Lucy also claimed she’d do a referral, which I later discovered she couldn’t, and she simply didn’t escalate it to a GP. I had to chase it myself. That’s not a misunderstanding, it’s outright negligence. This practice is a disgrace, poorly managed, disorganised, and devoid of compassion. Notes aren’t read, patients in pain are ignored, and mistakes are constant. Yet to be treated with basic humanity, you have to go private. It’s interesting how the NHS, despite being funded by taxpayers, continuously fails people while private care does the very basics right. If you’re considering registering here, don’t. You’ll have your time wasted, your health ignored, and your requests dismissed by staff who treat you like an inconvenience. The ethics and professionalism here are in the ground. I’ll give credit where it’s due, Dr Mona and Dr Gujral have been the only compassionate doctors I’ve ever dealt with at this practice. Talent wasted in such an environment. I’m certain I’m not the first to go through this, nor the last. I held off complaining because I believe in giving people grace, but this place is a complete failure of ethics, management, and basic decency. A shameful waste of taxpayers money. I will make sure to take this complaint as far as possible.

recent_reviews.text: I’d like to express my appreciation for Cathy and the excellent service she provides. recent_reviews.text: Just registered with this practice as my previous practice in Tynemouth who I was only with last couple of years was the worst practice I’ve ever used. In one short phone call my previous concerns were dealt with immediately within minutes of registering.. The staff I’ve met so far and also spoken to on phone have been exceptional and very helpful and I feel reassured again to have found a good surgery, plus there is plenty of parking onsite and nearby if car park full, and it’s very easy to find just off main road.

recent_reviews.text: Go elsewhere if your looking for a new GP surgery. I've tried calling to arrange an appointment to be told they now only offer same day appointments and you have to call at 08.30 the same day, this is absolutely useless to someone like myself who has a Mon-Fri 08:00-17:30 job. The receptionist had no empathy and provided no guidanceor advice of what I can do to get an appointment, she was just a cold monotone voice repeating the same thing "we dont do appointments anymore unless you come in at 08.30 to see if we have any same day appointments". I used to recommend this doctors to everyone, but the last few years it's gone down hill. From Dr's rushing you out the door and not taking time to find out what is wrong to receptionists that ignore the ringing phone (which I have watched them do many times) or when they do answer have 0 empathy skills and may as well be an automated robot. The new proccess seriously needs to be reviewed as this is not accessible to working people at all. People who work need an appointment to get authorisation to be off work to attend the doctors. Some compasion and empathy training would also be a welcome change.

recent_reviews.author: Charlotte Ashley-China
recent_reviews.text: I've been to the surgery a few times recently for various issues, not just myself, but for my baby. I've rarely needed to attend the doctor's until I got pregnant. I have to say, whether it has been for same-day appointments for my baby who has had a chest infection, an ear infection and tonsillitis (all in her first year) she has always been seen - following two incorrect diagnoses from A&E I might add!! I've attended for myself and have always been able see a suitable member of staff. I feel the surgery has much better reception staff now as well (didn't used to be the case!) and I've noticed an improvement especially in the last 2 years! Definitely worth reviewing because all NHS staff need to hear it when they're doing a good job.
